This document replaces, rather than patches, the rejected Stage 2 addendum. It
defines the narrow physical and transaction contract that may be implemented
only after focused reviews and a fresh full adversarial review issue GO on one
exact hash of this file.

This candidate does **not** authorize:

- authoring or applying migration 028;
- changing the packaged schema attestor or its readiness latch;
- enabling a browser-capture route, Chrome extension capability, DOM access,
  browser-capture intent, grant, upload, or link-only action;
- provider authorization or manual-enrichment execution;
- access to a live YouTube target in development, test, lab, or production;
- production browser capture or held-transcript processing;
- a native SQLite fork, client-cache restriction, backup-engine replacement,
  production operating-system containment layer, or any new/general-purpose
  external product or recovery control plane. This does not forbid the
  purpose-limited existing service-keystore/provisioner protocol used only for
  tombstone signing reservations, their bounded service-private signing-action
  records, monotonic per-key issuance/horizon maxima, key-retention floors,
  cleanup pins, sealed database-zero proofs, exact tombstone-key retirement
  control/barriers plus their exclusive controller/operation records and
  nonexportable owner capabilities, the symmetric runtime-only
  ordinary/controller-authority/channel/resume projection, its byte-exact
  tuple-binding hash and cold-start materialization, and atomic same-channel
  forward/reverse role reclassification plus compare-and-resume,
  nonrollbackable receipt count/head plus global candidate/
  hash indexes, authenticated chained receipts that are the durable key-ID
  nonreuse records, and the
  immutable per-store metadata-integrity keys used only for those receipts,
  plus the per-store startup/recovery controller latch used only for the
  service-linearizable admission/fence handoff;
  the stable authority-store locator;
  pending origin/restore reservations; authenticated origin,
  restore-disposition, and active-publication receipts; the nonrollbackable
  authority register/history plus generation/epoch allocation; gated database-
  hash/identity compare-and-swap; epoch promotion; and authority-marker

  general operator/product/browser/provider/manual-enrichment/database-query/
  backup-browse/recovery API. The evidence-only disposable AC13 guest is not

- touching a shared, lab, or production database.

Offline SQL authoring and disposable-database implementation tests become

## 2. Governing sources and explicit reconciliations

The final DOM-capture and held-manual-enrichment planning packages remain the
product authority:

- `docs/plans/youtube-dom-capture/2026-07-22_ai_brain_youtube_dom_capture_prd_v2_final.md`
- `docs/plans/youtube-dom-capture/2026-07-22_ai_brain_youtube_dom_capture_implementation_plan_v2_final.md`
- `docs/plans/youtube-item-recovery-enrichment/2026-07-22_ai_brain_item_recovery_manual_enrichment_prd_v2_final.md`
- `docs/plans/youtube-item-recovery-enrichment/2026-07-22_ai_brain_item_recovery_manual_enrichment_implementation_plan_v2_final.md`
- `docs/plans/youtube-item-recovery-enrichment/2026-07-22_manual_enrichment_v2_requirement_traceability.md`

Current protected-main schema and runtime behavior control where those plans
refer to an obsolete migration number or an object that does not yet exist.
This addendum makes six narrow reconciliations that require review as part of
its GO:

1. The coordinated migration sequence is now:
   `028_youtube_browser_transcript.sql`,
   `029_manual_transcript_enrichment_expand.sql`, and
   `030_manual_transcript_enrichment_contract.sql`.
2. Automatic recovery currently uses
   `youtube_innertube_timedtext`. No existing policy method, rights basis, or
   source kind truthfully classifies that unrestricted path. Migration 028
   therefore records an immutable recovery-apply receipt and attempt but
   creates no `capture_policy_decisions`, `transcript_sources`, or
   `transcript_segments` row for automatic recovery. A later reviewed policy
   decision is required before that path may persist a policy-bound source.
3. Migration 028 stores an opaque `hold_generation_id` for a synthetic held
   attachment. It does not create integer enrichment-generation allocators,
   current-applied generation pointers, manual jobs, runs, attempts, usage, or
   release authority. Migration 029 owns that complete graph. Before any 029
   status action, authorization, release, claim, dispatch, or apply, it must
   bind each 028 `hold_generation_id` one-to-one to exactly one positive,
   never-reused held enrichment generation at the same item, source, and
   content revision.
4. Migration 028 uses the existing source `text_sha256`, ordered segment
   indexes, per-segment hashes, and `provenance_json`. It does not invent an
   aggregate `integrity_sha256` or integrity-version contract. Before any 029
   status action, authorization, release, claim, dispatch, or apply, migration
   029 must freeze, persist, and recompute the reviewed
   `transcript-integrity-v1` aggregate and exact provider-body hash at GET,
   POST, claim, dispatch, and apply.
5. Current automatic recovery writes a pre-upgrade snapshot and any provider
   capture artifacts after its database body commit. That split filesystem
   write is the R-032 crash window. Migration 028 replaces future recovery
   artifact creation with the atomic database attempt and receipt; it neither
   creates a new recovery artifact nor deletes an existing artifact. This is a
   reviewed behavior change, not an accidental omission.
6. The final plans require per-item operational detail to disappear with the
   item. Migration 028 therefore makes extension, recovery, capture-artifact
   caller, artifact-operation, and other item-owned detail cascade with the
   item. The sole narrow post-delete exception is a deletion-ID-scoped
   cleanup authority/outbox containing only the minimum root-relative
   filesystem manifest and identity data needed to finish an already
   committed deletion. It is unavailable to ordinary readers, logs, exports,
   diagnostics, and backups as a product record, grants no item or content
   authority, and is atomically removed immediately after durable cleanup.
   Only bounded content-free keyed-authenticator tombstones remain after that
   removal.

The content-revision rule follows the final implementation ADR: every SQL
statement that names `body` in an `UPDATE OF body` event advances the revision
exactly once, including a byte-identical assignment.

## 3. Stage boundary

### 3.1 Migration 028 owns

Migration 028 and its transition binary may own only:

- the current-frontier and migration-runner safety changes needed to apply 028
  exactly once;
- immutable CSPRNG 128-bit item-instance identities, live uniqueness, and item
  content revisions;
- transaction-ephemeral body-revision authority used only to make each body
  statement advance its revision exactly once;
- revision, exact provider-input fingerprint, hashed-claim, and lease fields
  on current async queues;
- truthful policy/source enum expansion for a future browser-visible
  transcript;
- exact item ownership across policy, source, and segment rows;
- one-active-source enforcement;
- an inert processing hold and inert extension-request ledger;
- bounded content-free caller-request and deletion-request tombstones that
  prevent replay resurrection after item deletion;
- an immutable receipt-only automatic-recovery success record;
- an atomic R-032 recovery apply/finalize transaction;
- held-item and stale-result fences across all current body-derived workers;
- a fixture-only internal attachment harness using packaged synthetic data;
- the exact inherited NotebookLM backup scrub and the owned backup
  publication, recovery, and shared-lock hardening frozen in section 6.1,
  without replacing the backup engine;
- recoverable, idempotent cleanup of existing capture-artifact files during
  explicit item deletion, including item-owned cross-process artifact-write
  caller bindings/operations, a purpose-limited durable deletion cleanup
  authority/outbox, bounded anti-replay tombstones, and provisioned-root
  durability;
- exact schema capability attestation, claimant containment, compatibility
  refusal, and forward-recovery evidence.

### 3.2 Migration 028 does not own

The following remain deferred:

- Stage 3 and Stage 4 extension build flavors, permissions, DOM extractors,
  browser routes, link-only routes, inspect/confirm flow, intent/grant/handoff,
  private-lab identity, and live-target authorization;
- migration 029 processing decisions, accepted authorization snapshots,
  authorization context, integer enrichment generations, manual-enrichment
  receipts, runs, attempts, provider usage, handling terms, interactive worker
  lanes, release mutations, and dual-write transition;
- migration 030 strict contraction, removal of old states or columns,
  compatibility-view retirement, and rollback-binary retirement;
- migration-029/manual-enrichment provider dispatch, digest generation,
  semantic indexing, UI authorization, partial-success handling, retry,
  provider drift handling, and semantic-reader cutover;
- any stronger deletion deadline, backup sanitization beyond the inherited
  NotebookLM scrub and section-6.1 publication/recovery protocol,
  client-storage policy, native runtime, or host-containment proposal.

## 4. Non-negotiable preservation invariants

1. Existing weak YouTube and YouTube Short items retain automatic-recovery
   eligibility. Existing pending, running-drained-before-migration,
   retryable, manual-needed, ignored, and done job history is preserved.
2. Only an item explicitly marked
   `extraction_method='browser_link_only_v1'` is excluded from automatic
   recovery. Migration 028 does not assign that marker.
3. An active transcript source or processing hold prevents automatic recovery
   from claiming, dispatching, or applying. Historical source conflicts stop
   migration preflight; the migration never guesses which source wins.
4. Existing paste, upload, official-caption, owned-media, URL capture,
   export, print, share, NotebookLM, Recall, search, and ordinary item-read
   behavior remains available. No ordinary item receives lab-only
   restrictions.
5. Production browser capture and manual processing remain denied in code
   before request-body or item-body access. Schema capability, flags,
   manifests, environment aliases, or stored rows cannot override that denial.
   Existing automatic transcript recovery and ordinary production processing
   remain positive controls and are not covered by this restricted-work
   denial.
6. A held live source remains usable until `source_delete_by` unless the user
   explicitly deletes the item. Routine backup neither purges nor mutates the
   live graph.
7. Explicit item deletion removes the live item-root graph. A backup retained
   before deletion may continue to contain the old bytes until ordinary
   configured pruning; migration 028 makes no immediate backup-erasure claim.
   Every detailed per-item operational row cascades with that graph. The
   deletion-ID-scoped cleanup authority/outbox is not retained product
   history: it survives only to complete post-commit filesystem cleanup and
   durable `done+tombstone` publication, remains through verified signing
   promotion, and is removed only by the later sealed ack transaction.
8. Existing capture-artifact rows and files are not rewritten or removed by
   recovery. Automatic recovery creates no new capture-artifact file or row.
   Explicit item deletion still removes existing artifact rows and files
   through the recoverable cleanup contract in section 10.
9. Raw claim tokens, transcript text, URLs, titles, provider payloads, and raw
   provider errors do not enter receipts or diagnostic evidence.
10. `items` is not rebuilt. Existing item values, `batch_id` bytes, workflow
    foreign keys, indexes, and unrelated triggers are preserved.
11. D-015 remains authoritative. A browser-transcript hold blocks source/body
    recovery, enrichment, batch, generic embedding, and any claimant whose
    input separation is unproved. It is not a blanket ban on an independently
    authorized standard-mode manual note. `manual-transcript-lab` starts no
    note-index worker, and a recovery-created note remains AI-off.
12. Every S28 item has one immutable CSPRNG 128-bit `item_instance_id`.
    Uniqueness is required among live items, allocation collision retries are
    bounded, and no permanent deleted-instance accumulator exists. Every
    queued and non-queued writer, artifact operation, deletion request, input
    fingerprint, and mutation preimage binds the exact current instance and
    revision before dispatch or mutation; a public ID plus revision is never
    sufficient stale-work authority.
13. Every caller request has an explicit authority interval no longer than
    86,400,000 milliseconds. After item deletion, its only durable replay
    memory is a content-free keyed-authenticator tombstone. Caller-request
    tombstones use
    `block_until=max(authority_expires_at,deleted_at)+300_000`, where
    `deleted_at` is the initial deletion transaction's one bound database
    clock. The final deletion-request tombstone uses
    `block_until=max(authority_expires_at,completion_clock)+300_000`, where
    the one sealed frozen `completion_clock` is also bound to `completed_at`,
    the signing action, HMAC, DML, and trigger. Safe-integer overflow refuses
    the transaction, and cleanup requires a fresh database clock strictly
    greater than `block_until`. Expiry never authorizes new work; after the
    bounded terminal-reconciliation window an old replay is rejected by
    authority expiry independently of the exact-current-instance fence, and
    a request carrying a deleted instance is independently rejected when a
    current item exists with another instance.

- The exact file

  has SHA-256
  `75229da2ded0817318ac04657c3330555ed93d74c78b019d6cbcd56c7e69a4c7`,
  and its independently recomputed canonical S27 descriptor has SHA-256
  `f75352b79274ebc9a7e4a68204e0a41a043a16d5fb21aae7805787c2638cc83a`.
- Its executable verifier has SHA-256
  `decf2cc79c14b82b6f85e5f18408a94533891e19a958faefa5ca64469e584210`
  and the command
  `node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/implementation/fixtures/verify-stage2-s27-schema-manifest.mjs`
  returns `status=ok`. Before executable imports it verifies the exact source
  commit and source blobs, launch flags and injection environment, Node
  executable, root package and lock bytes, resolved JavaScript entries,
  complete executed package trees, `better_sqlite3.node`, and the resolved
  platform `vec0.dylib`. After loading only those attested bytes it verifies
  the external non-system shared-object envelope, SQLite source ID and compile
  options, sqlite-vec version/function/module registries and scalar-plus-vec0
  KNN golden behavior, every raw 001..027 migration byte, the 29-row ledger,
  schema/object hashes, `quick_check`, and zero FK violations.

Before the read-only database preflight, a dedicated content-free provisioning
command must create or validate the configured capture-artifact root. It
resolves and validates every existing ancestor, rejects symlinks and
non-directories, creates only the absent final root component with mode
`0700`, and records the canonical realpath/device/inode fingerprint used
below. On every successful invocation—including when the final component
already exists after a prior crash—it opens and fsyncs that exact root,
fsyncs its containing parent, and then revalidates the root and parent
identities before returning. The command is idempotent and performs no
database DML. S28 activation never lazily creates the root. An unavailable
directory-sync primitive or changed root identity is a refusal. The native
Buffer-valued canonical realpath must fatally decode as UTF-8 and
byte-for-byte re-encode to the same Buffer; an invalid or lossy root path is
unsupported. `artifact-root-v1` always frames those exact validated Buffer
bytes, never a separately normalized path string. The executed
provisioner failpoints must equal the `root_provision` registry and cover
crashes between `mkdir`, root fsync, parent fsync, and final identity
revalidation. Disposable tests receive their own provisioned temporary root.

### 5.2 Quiescence and integrity

- Capture, transcript recovery, realtime enrichment, batch enrichment,
  embedding, and note-index writers are stopped.
- No transcript, enrichment, embedding, or note-index job is `running`; no
  claimed-by identity, claim-token hash, or unexpired lease remains. Expired
  claims must be reconciled by the pre-028 binary before writers stop; the
  migration never guesses their outcome.
- No enrichment job or item is `batched`. Item and job enrichment states agree.
  Every non-null historical batch value is either a valid legacy provider ID
  or a canonical resolved `opaque-v1` binding as defined in section 9.4; no
  unresolved `opaque-reservation-v1:` value, malformed reserved-prefix value,
  or item/job/binding mismatch exists.
- `PRAGMA quick_check` returns exactly `ok`.
- `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` returns zero rows. A nonzero historical baseline is
  not grandfathered.
- No item has more than one active transcript source.
- `items.id`, `capture_artifacts.id`, and `note_index_jobs.item_id` each have
  SQLite storage class `text`, nonzero UTF-8 byte length, fatal UTF-8
  decode/re-encode equality, and zero nulls. Ordinary SQLite `TEXT PRIMARY
  KEY` does not imply `NOT NULL`; null or BLOB identities are explicit
  refusals, never rows that migration 028 repairs or silently omits.
- Before DDL, preflight enumerates every existing database-owned scalar input
  that migration 028 will place in the section-7.10 deletion rowsets: owning
  item, capture-artifact, transcript/enrichment/embedding/note-job, and
  transcript-attempt projections. It applies the identical typed scalar
  validator in frozen post-migration column order. Columns not yet present use
  only their prescribed null/default/backfill class; random item-instance
  values are validated after generation and are not predicted. REAL, unsafe
  integer, invalid or non-roundtripping TEXT, unsupported storage class,
  missing/extra column, or descriptor/order drift refuses. The newly created
  extension-request, artifact-request, and artifact-operation rowsets must be
  empty. This pass validates historical inputs only; it does not claim to
  compute a component requiring future deletion ID, deletion time, or
  generated instance values. After DDL/backfill, the locked validation-only
  exact component pass in section 8.3 covers the actual owning items,
  extension requests, capture artifacts, artifact requests/operations,
  generic jobs, and transcript attempts. Permissive historical non-STRICT
  storage is never grandfathered into an undeletable S28 item.
- Every source-bound policy has a non-null owner exactly equal to the source's
  item. A null or mismatched owner is an explicit preflight refusal requiring
  separately reviewed cleanup.
- Every segment's item matches its source's item.
- Every transcript attempt's item matches its job's item.
- Every non-null `last_attempt_id` resolves to the same job and item.
- Segment indexes are unique and nonnegative per source, and stored
  `segment_count` agrees with the persisted segment count for sources that
  already have segment rows.
- The exact vector audit reports `safeToEnableWriters=true`: no
  chunk-without-bridge, bridge-without-chunk, bridge-without-vector,
  vector-without-bridge, duplicate-rowid, dimension, or high-water anomaly is
  present. Repair is a separate reviewed operation, never an implicit part of
  migration 028.
- Every capture-artifact path is either a validated root-relative path or a
  legacy path that resolves inside the configured capture-artifact root.
  Every owning item ID used as an artifact-directory component is exactly 24
  lowercase hexadecimal characters.
  Validated canonical relative-path bytes are unique globally, owned by the
  row's exact item
  directory, and do not alias another row by path or filesystem identity.
  Unresolvable, absolute-outside-root, traversal, duplicate, cross-item,
  symlinked, or hard-linked paths refuse migration and deletion until
  separately reconciled.
- The exact section-7.10 deletion manifest for every existing item is within
  all seven frozen admission limits. Migration refuses an item at any `+1`
  boundary; it does not activate S28 with an item that the bounded deletion
  protocol could never remove.
- The provisioned artifact root exists with the exact recorded realpath,
  device, inode, ownership, and mode. Preflight is read-only and never creates
  or repairs it.

### 5.3 Preservation snapshot

Before rehearsal, capture content-free evidence for:

- row counts for every rebuilt or referenced table;
- stable hashes of non-content key/state projections;
- every item index and trigger SQL string;
- policy, source, and segment index/trigger SQL strings;
- foreign-key manifests and actions;
- `sqlite_sequence` high-water values for every AUTOINCREMENT table;
- the exact weak-item eligibility projection and existing transcript-job
  projection;
- the item-ID/created-at projection used only to prove one unique
  migration-backfilled instance per existing row, without predicting the
  random values;
- the exact set and bytes of all non-null `items.batch_id` values;
- the artifact-root identity and canonical capture-artifact row/path/file
  identity projection plus the frozen legacy absolute-to-relative mapping used
  by section 7.10.
- the exact historical deletion-rowset scalar projection, including each
  SQLite storage-class tag and the frozen post-migration physical
  table/column order.

The snapshot produces a content-free token over those projections. After the
migration runner obtains its writer lock, it recomputes and compares that token
and every mutable quiescence/integrity predicate before executing any DDL.

A fresh ordinary backup must be created and verified. Backup verification must
not alter the live database. The migration must first pass against a
production-shaped disposable copy of that backup.

## 6. Migration application and schema attestation

### 6.1 Runner transaction

The migration runner must:

1. capture the entry values of `foreign_keys` and `legacy_alter_table`, set
   `foreign_keys=OFF` and `legacy_alter_table=ON` before beginning the
   transaction, and reject a read-only or otherwise incompatible connection;
2. acquire the SQLite writer lock with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` before ledger-table
   creation, legacy hash-column addition, or legacy hash backfill;
3. create or upgrade the ledger, re-read it, and perform any legacy hash
   backfill inside that same uncommitted transaction;
4. re-run every mutable preflight predicate and compare the preservation token
   under that same lock;
5. reject an already-recorded filename whose stored hash differs;
6. execute an unseen migration and insert its exact filename/hash ledger row
   in that same transaction;
7. commit the ledger bootstrap, schema, and migration row together, or roll
   all three back;
8. make a second exact run a no-op;
9. restore `foreign_keys` and `legacy_alter_table` to their entry values after
   commit or rollback on every success and failure path.

Every supported writable connection attached to the authoritative active S28
database—including the ordinary singleton, migration command, transition
connection, forward-recovery artifact, and any connection that may close
last—comes only from one reviewed active-database connection factory. Before
that factory exposes the handle or permits any write, it attests
`journal_mode=WAL`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `recursive_triggers=ON`,
`trusted_schema=OFF`, `secure_delete=ON`, `synchronous=FULL`,
`ignore_check_constraints=OFF`, `wal_autocheckpoint=0`, and the target
platform's reviewed SQLite full-sync settings (`fullfsync=ON` and
`checkpoint_fullfsync=ON` on Darwin). `secure_delete=ON` is attested before
migration 028 can create or use a cleanup outbox or `item_delete_permits`
table and on every later S28
writer; `FAST`, zero, an unknown numeric/text result, or later PRAGMA drift
closes the handle. The first-layer native connection role also installs an
authorizer before any schema prepare or application SQL. It rejects every
attempt to set or change `foreign_keys`, `recursive_triggers`,
`trusted_schema`, `secure_delete`, or `ignore_check_constraints`, and the
wrapper reattests all five
values before and after every prepared statement and at transaction
commit/rollback. The dedicated stopped-writer migration role may use its
declared pre-activation `foreign_keys=OFF` window only for the exact migration
statement inventory; no application or root-item DML is admitted in that
window. A writable
active-S28 handle that cannot prove every value is closed and never joins the
application pool. A supported diagnostic or backup-source handle is opened
genuinely read-only, sets `query_only=ON`, and is never a checkpoint owner.
`synchronous=NORMAL` remains permitted only for B27/S27 operation or a
disposable negative-control clone, never for a connection attached to the
active S28 database.

The backup controller first acquires the active database's exclusive
source-generation barrier, stops new writer/checkpoint and attached read-
snapshot admission, and gives every existing writer, cleanup worker,
transaction, ordinary/diagnostic/backup reader, attached handle, and read mark
exactly one monotonic 60,000-ms deadline to drain and close. The deadline
begins when admission closes; zero-handle/read-mark proof at or before
equality is accepted, and the first observation after equality refuses.
Timeout creates no candidate, releases no partial output, and emits only content-free
`backup_deferred_privacy_window` count/age/state telemetry plus an operator
incident. While the barrier remains held, the centralized checkpoint
coordinator completes and fsyncs a FULL checkpoint followed by TRUNCATE,
requires no busy writer/frame, and proves the source `-wal` is absent or
zero-length and no rollback journal is live. Only then may the controller open
the sole exact backup-source read handle/snapshot below; no other reader is
admitted while it exists. On success or pre-candidate refusal, that handle is
closed first, the barrier is released, and only the attested active-database
factory recreates fresh pooled readers.

The exact backup-source handle then opens one explicit SQLite read snapshot
and holds that same snapshot transaction through the last logically
reconstructed row; it never advances or silently reopens the snapshot. For
S28, before destination creation, a count query in that same snapshot must
prove exactly zero `item_artifact_cleanup_jobs` rows and exactly zero
`item_delete_permits` rows. It also proves that the checked sum of the exact
`item_request_tombstones` and `item_deletion_request_tombstones` counts is at
most `RESTORE_TOMBSTONE_MAX=65,536`; those two counts are bound into the
authenticated internal package descriptor but are never emitted by backup
listing or catalog APIs. The same snapshot reads the exact all-valid authority
marker, requires it to equal the currently verified external active record,
and binds the marker tuple plus complete active-record SHA-256 into that
internal descriptor. Any nonzero transient relation, over-cap tombstone
sum, missing-table-under-S28, unreadable, changed-snapshot, or indeterminate result
closes the snapshot and fails content-free before a private candidate, hidden
publication directory, listing result, or final basename exists.

Raw/page-level backup is forbidden, including the SQLite online-backup API,
filesystem copy/reflink, `VACUUM INTO` from the source, serialization of the
source file, or copying a source WAL/journal/freelist page. Instead the
descriptor-generated sanitized-image builder `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` creates a
zero-length private
destination, installs the exact attested schema with `secure_delete=ON`, and
streams only logically live rows from that held source snapshot in frozen
relation/primary-key order through exact typed column encoders. Virtual-table
and shadow content is rebuilt only through its descriptor-declared logical
source route; indexes and triggers are created from the descriptor, never
copied as source pages. The destination transaction and source snapshot stay
open through the last row/count/hash check and commit together or the
destination is destroyed. S27 follows its own exact descriptor route and has
no cleanup-outbox relation; it may not pretend to be S28 to bypass the gate.

The two five-field tombstone tables are permitted inside a whole-database
snapshot because they are bounded content-free replay guards. Backup
catalogs, filenames, intents, logs, and indexes never separately surface or
join them. Key retirement does not retain keys solely for an offline backup.
Supported restore instead requires the authenticated, nonrollbackable
restore-epoch publication barrier below before any item or endpoint is
visible. If that barrier or its external keystore proof is unavailable, the
backup is unsupported/unrestorable and fails closed; Stage 2 makes no
unconditional restore-availability claim.

A snapshot opened before an item deletion is truthfully a pre-delete backup
and may contain that then-live item under normal backup retention. A deletion
committed before snapshot admission defers new backup creation only while its
detailed cleanup outbox remains. A stuck outbox blocks backup indefinitely
with bounded content-free retry plus an operator incident alert until cleanup
or separately authorized manual resolution; the controller never weakens the
zero-row gate. This is a database-only backup contract and makes no claim that
artifact files are complete or restorable from the database backup.

Cleanup retry for a nonterminal/poisoned outbox uses database time and exact
delay `min(900000,1000*2^min(attempts,10))` milliseconds; equality admits the
next attempt and earlier clocks skip it without increment. The backup
controller performs at most one 60-second drain attempt per invocation and
does not hot-loop the poisoned row. Its alert contains only outbox count,
oldest age, attempts bucket, and closed stable error code—never deletion/item
ID, path, manifest, or authenticator—and repeats no more often than once per
15 minutes. Manual remediation requires a separately reviewed cleanup
authority that either completes the same identity/fsync/tombstone protocol or
keeps the gate blocked; direct outbox deletion and backup-gate override are
forbidden.

The volatile reconstruction stage has its own crash contract before any
content-bearing candidate exists. The descriptor freezes a dedicated private
stage parent, expected device/UID/GID/mode, and run-directory grammar
`.stage2-backup-scrub-<43-base64url-run-id>`. That same run ID deterministically
selects hidden publication directory
`.ai-brain-sanitized-backup-v1-<43-base64url-run-id>`; no independent hidden
nonce is drawn. While holding the same maintenance lock used for publication,
the controller creates the empty run directory with exact private owner/mode
0700 and the platform-frozen empty-directory link semantics (exactly two on
the supported Linux/Darwin filesystems), verifies the stage parent's baseline
link count increased by exactly one, and parent-fsyncs. It then constructs
content-free ordered no-LF JSON `stage2-backup-scrub-run-intent-v1`, at most
2,048 bytes, with keys
exactly
`domain,run_id,source_schema_manifest_sha256,
source_authority_marker_sha256,candidate_basename,
hidden_publication_basename,destination_final_basename,sqlite_source_id,
sqlite_compile_options_sha256,candidate_sha256,candidate_size,
candidate_device,candidate_inode,candidate_parsed_page_map_sha256,
candidate_package_descriptor_sha256,status`.
Candidate basename is exact `candidate.sqlite`, hidden basename is the
deterministic name above, hashes/run ID use their closed grammars, and the
destination final basename uses the publication grammar below. Initial
candidate proof fields are all JSON null and status is `building`; the only
other valid pairing has all six proof fields present and status
`candidate_validated`. Candidate hash, parsed-page-map hash, and package-
descriptor hash are 64 lowercase hexadecimal; size/device/inode are canonical
uint64 decimal JSON strings. `candidate_parsed_page_map_sha256` is exactly the
already-defined full parsed-page-map hash emitted by
`stage2-backup-physical-sanitization-v1`, and
`candidate_package_descriptor_sha256` is SHA-256 of the complete canonical
authenticated immutable package-descriptor bytes containing the exact page/
profile/cache facts. A mixed null/present tuple or status mismatch refuses.
The intent is
written to run-local `intent.json.tmp` with
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, exact owner/mode 0600/link-count-one;
file-fsynced; atomically renamed to `intent.json`; run-directory-fsynced; and
reopened/fstat/hash-verified. Candidate creation is forbidden until that
initial intent is complete and durable. The private stage is mode-0700,
single-controller and lock-excluded; Stage 2 assumes host-root integrity and
treats offline injection by that identity as out of protocol rather than
granting cleanup authority from a basename alone.

Before a next backup, backup listing, prune, restore, or stage construction,
the lock holder validates the stage parent and performs a mutation-free
two-phase sentinel scan. Phase one observes at most two stage-parent child
entries: exact `{}` or one validated matching run directory is accepted; a
second entry or any nonmatching entry refuses unchanged. Phase two observes
at most seven children of that one run directory: zero through six unique
accepted names is supported and the seventh refuses unchanged. No cleanup
occurs until both complete scans and every retained path/descriptor identity,
device, UID/GID, mode, type, size, and link-count check finishes. The only
child names are
`intent.json.tmp`, `intent.json`, `candidate.sqlite`, and the candidate's
exact `-journal`, `-wal`, and `-shm` suffixes. Intent/temp size is
`0..2,048`, candidate size is `0..1,073,741,824`, WAL and journal size are
each `0..2,147,483,648`, and SHM size is `0..67,108,864`; all are checked
uint64 values before any read or unlink. An unknown name, alias, over-cap
scan/file, symlink, wrong metadata/device, unexpected directory link count,
or identity drift preserves everything and fences.

After the normal close/file-fsync/physical proof at immutable failpoint 14,
the controller constructs the same ordered intent with exact candidate
hash/size/device/inode, parsed-page-map hash, package-descriptor hash, and
status `candidate_validated`. It replaces `intent.json` only through
O_EXCL `intent.json.tmp`, temp fsync, atomic rename, run-directory fsync, and
reopen/fstat/hash verification. Hidden-directory creation or copy is
forbidden until all five replacement durability/reopen steps succeed. This
candidate seal exists solely to bind
destination handoff and cleanup; it never authorizes pre-hidden resume. Any
process crash before the deterministic hidden publication directory becomes
visible takes cleanup-only recovery: the held SQLite source snapshot and
scrub clock are not reconstructable, so startup never reopens, resumes, or
recreates that candidate. It safely destroys the entire owned run and a
future invocation reacquires the source barrier, captures a fresh snapshot
and clock, and chooses a fresh run ID.

If a deterministic hidden directory may have become visible, destination
recovery runs first. Once hidden recovery converges, exact hidden-absent plus
final-absent means destroy the stage and permit only a future fresh run.
Hidden-absent plus final-present is publication-complete only when the final
basename equals the run intent, the candidate seal is exact, the completed
backup validator passes, and final hash/size equal the seal (and the stage
candidate too when still present); then stage cleanup proceeds. A different,
unsafe, unvalidated, or mismatching final preserves/fences. This also handles
final-only handoff after the hidden directory has already been removed.

Safe stage destruction closes every handle; requires each present child to
be unaliased, capped, ordinary, exact-owner/mode/device, and link count one;
and unlinks in exact order `candidate.sqlite-shm`,
`candidate.sqlite-wal`, `candidate.sqlite-journal`, `candidate.sqlite`,
`intent.json.tmp`, `intent.json`. Partial or valid-hot journal bytes are
destroyable because the candidate is unpublished; no hot journal is replayed.
The controller fsyncs the run directory after every present unlink, proves
zero children, requires its exact directory link semantics, rmdirs it, fsyncs
the stage parent, reproves the stage parent's exact descriptor-bound baseline
link count, and repeats both sentinel scans to exact `{}`. Empty,
temp-only, intent-only, and already-partially-cleaned prefixes follow that
same suffix of the order; candidate/sidecar without a complete durable
initial intent remains quarantined as an impossible unauthorized prefix.

The separately hash-pinned registry-embedded
`stage2-backup-private-stage-operations-v1` submanifest has these exact 34
ordered operation IDs:
`private_stage_parent_scan,private_stage_run_mkdir,
private_stage_run_parent_fsync,private_stage_intent_temp_create,
private_stage_intent_temp_write_complete,
private_stage_intent_temp_fsync,private_stage_intent_rename,
private_stage_intent_dir_fsync,private_stage_intent_reopen,
private_stage_candidate_create,private_stage_candidate_close,
private_stage_candidate_seal_temp_create,
private_stage_candidate_seal_temp_write_complete,
private_stage_candidate_seal_temp_fsync,
private_stage_candidate_seal_rename,private_stage_candidate_seal_dir_fsync,
private_stage_candidate_seal_reopen,private_stage_destination_recovery,
private_stage_final_classify,private_stage_unlink_shm,
private_stage_fsync_after_shm,private_stage_unlink_wal,
private_stage_fsync_after_wal,private_stage_unlink_journal,
private_stage_fsync_after_journal,private_stage_unlink_candidate,
private_stage_fsync_after_candidate,private_stage_unlink_intent_tmp,
private_stage_fsync_after_intent_tmp,private_stage_unlink_intent,
private_stage_fsync_after_intent,private_stage_rmdir,
private_stage_stage_parent_fsync,private_stage_second_scan`.
Before/after each ID yields exactly 68 coordinates, each governed by the exact
`cleanup_only_fresh_run|destination_recover_then_cleanup|
publication_complete_then_cleanup|preserve_fence` disposition. It mutates
every scan cap, file cap, directory link count, identity, seal field, final
comparison, cleanup prefix, and second-pass result. This is an additional
private-stage crash submatrix; it does not add, remove, or rename any of the
24 runtime `isolated_backup_scrub` failpoints and does not alter the existing
45-ID AC13/AC17 base-operation formulas. No next operation proceeds until
the private-stage submatrix oracle and second two-phase scan both accept.
The registry top-level `private_stage_operation_registry` is the
machine-readable authority. It stores operation IDs, edges, all 68
operation-major before/after coordinate objects, coordinate count, and the
four ordered state/disposition records. Schema version is integer 1,
coordinate order is exact `operation_major_before_after`, and the ordered
platform bindings are exactly Linux S2-AC-13 under
`stage2-ac13-qemu-tcg-vm-v2` then Darwin S2-AC-17 under
`stage2-backup-darwin-fixture-v1`. Each binding names its existing
case-evidence path, exact existing evidence fields `registry_sha256` and
`assertion_manifest_sha256`, and assertion source `child_event`. Linux binds
the existing assertion `S2-AC-13/backup_transition_contract`; Darwin binds
the existing assertion `S2-AC-17/darwin.case_contract`. Each may emit its
single aggregate PASS only after all 68 coordinates validate in registry
order. Thus the existing 31-field/no-extra-key evidence schema and existing
71-record assertion manifest bind the registry object and its complete
coordinate result without introducing either an impossible evidence object
or unfrozen per-coordinate assertion IDs.
SHA-256 of compact
`JSON.stringify` for platform bindings, operation IDs, coordinates, and
disposition rules is respectively
`d7b06556946ac7970519908b6546a8082ade5bcab3db179fcfc9b2043c9d8d26`,
`d4a17f5a377d77a7a8f758e1107c759bd2ba13047e85bed1f1ee99842c3e6d0e`,
`8763950808783ac3b0d8f0962fcc5564fb2dbd6ef844f5f691156be815a7b167`,
and
`cd65b1be35f1933beb819bddbd35272fa14c116daa3d45a809501e77104710d3`.
Its `authority_sha256` is
`e4218fc4206ca5df6171aec062b55910f204950779a8fec977009f88ac750571`,
SHA-256 over the 7,647-byte compact `JSON.stringify` object containing every
preceding registry field in file order and excluding only
`authority_sha256`; field/order/count/hash drift refuses.

The sole exception is the fresh logically reconstructed sanitized candidate,
never a raw copy, never the configured active database, and never attached to
any active-S28 connection. It is created under the existing attested
single-owner volatile staging boundary and opened by a separate reviewed
`isolated_backup_scrub` factory with exactly one handle, no concurrent
reader/writer, `journal_mode=DELETE`, `foreign_keys=ON`,
`synchronous=FULL`, memory-only temporary storage, secure deletion, and the
target full-sync settings. The sole SQL-visible application function is the
same exact constant `brain_s28_bridge_present()` tripwire; no write, durable,
artifact, delete, role, arm, consume, or active function is registered. The
native authorizer admits exactly two writable no-tail prepared roles on this
isolated handle: the descriptor-hashed NotebookLM snapshot-scrub `UPDATE`,
bound to its exact database-clock parameter/type/value and expected
matched/change count, and the descriptor-hashed bare `VACUUM`. It also admits
exactly three non-authorizing read-only roles: one single-row
`isolated_scrub_clock_read`, one descriptor-complete ordered preimage proof,
and one descriptor-complete ordered postimage proof. The clock role executes
only exact no-tail
`SELECT CAST(unixepoch('subsec')*1000 AS INTEGER)`, requires one safe-integer
row followed by `SQLITE_DONE`, and its result is the sole `now` binding to the
update. The pre/post roles may only read the declared candidate relations in
frozen primary-key order and must reproduce the expected row counts, mapping
digests, and zero-payload result; they grant no DML. Each role permits one
prepare/step-to-completion/finalize sequence, and the closed order is
`clock_read -> preproof -> scrub_update -> postproof -> vacuum -> physical
parse`. It rejects every other prepare, binding, action/source trace,
table/column, statement cache, reordered/repeated phase, reprepare drift, or
active-database role. The one captured `now` value is used for every
occurrence in the fixed `UPDATE`. The predicate matches exactly a row whose
original `payload_title`, `payload_text`, or `payload_url` is non-null.
`payload_url` is a present nullable column in both S27 and S28. Every
right-hand side below is evaluated from that row's original preimage:

1. when `phase='pre_create'` and `create_dispatched_at IS NULL`, set
   `state='expired'`, `phase='terminal'`,
   `safe_reason='backup_snapshot_omitted'`, and
   `completed_at=COALESCE(old.completed_at,now)`;
2. when `state IN ('sending','leased')` and
   `phase IN ('create','reconcile')`, set `state='reconciling'` and
   `phase='reconcile'`, while leaving `safe_reason` and `completed_at`
   unchanged;
3. when `state='leased'` and `phase='poll'`, set `state='processing'` and
   `phase='poll'`, while leaving `safe_reason` and `completed_at` unchanged;
4. otherwise leave `state`, `phase`, `safe_reason`, and `completed_at`
   unchanged.

For every matched row, the statement sets `payload_title`, `payload_text`, and
the nullable `payload_url` to null,
`snapshot_purge_at=MIN(old.snapshot_purge_at,now)`,
`snapshot_purged_at=COALESCE(old.snapshot_purged_at,now)`,
`lease_token_hash=NULL`, `lease_until=NULL`, and
`updated_at=MAX(old.updated_at,now)`. Every other column retains its exact
SQLite storage class and bytes. The fixed statement therefore touches only
`notebooklm_export_requests.state,phase,safe_reason,payload_title,payload_text,
payload_url,snapshot_purge_at,snapshot_purged_at,completed_at,lease_token_hash,
lease_until,updated_at` under the exact predicate that at least one payload
field is non-null. No other table, column, statement, parameter tuple, or
function-backed authority receives candidate DML authority. Before that first
candidate DML, a genuinely read-only candidate
check proves
exactly zero `item_artifact_cleanup_jobs` and `item_delete_permits` rows for
S28 and independently proves that the two tombstone counts and their checked
combined value at or below 65,536 equal the held source-snapshot/package
values. Its authority marker must byte/numerically equal the source/package
tuple and is never scrubbed or regenerated during backup; a nonzero transient
relation, over-cap or unequal tombstone count, marker drift, or
indeterminate result destroys/refuses the unpublished candidate as
`backup_deferred_privacy_window`. The scrub transaction captures the exact
matched-row count and
verifies, before VACUUM, that it equals both the frozen preimage set and exact
postimage set; it proves the complete mapping above for each matched row and
byte/storage-class equality for every other column and every unmatched row.
After VACUUM it again proves zero non-null payload fields, exactly zero
cleanup-outbox and transient-permit rows, and the unchanged two tombstone
counts with combined value at most 65,536. The descriptor-bound
`stage2-backup-physical-sanitization-v1` validator then parses the complete
candidate file, not SQL query output alone. It requires `secure_delete=ON`,
`freelist_count=0`, zero-cell/no-overflow `item_artifact_cleanup_jobs` and
`item_delete_permits` b-trees, every page reachable exactly once from
the declared live schema/table/index graph, every freeblock/unallocated
payload region zero-filled, and no WAL, shared-memory, rollback-journal, or
unreferenced overflow bytes. Schema SQL may contain the table/column names,
but no deletion ID, statement nonce, command blob/map, item ID/instance,
request fingerprint, authenticator, authority restore epoch, expiry/deletion
clock, relative path, device/inode, manifest JSON/hash, state/error, or
timestamp payload can exist in a live outbox/permit cell or unreachable
candidate bytes. The
validator hashes the entire parsed page map and refuses before publication on
one nonzero unreachable byte, freelist page, unknown page role, or structural
drift. It closes and genuinely read-only reopens the candidate, recomputes the
whole-file hash/size, and binds the exact SQLite source ID, compile options,
page size, reserved-byte count, auto-vacuum mode, text encoding, and
secure-delete profile already frozen by the selected binary/schema manifest.
The only supported Stage 2 backup/restore page profile is exactly
`page_size=4,096` bytes and `reserved_bytes=0`. Before any candidate may be
published, listed, or selected, this same closed-file validator freezes
`sanitized_page_count` in `1..262,144`, maximum b-tree depth, and the checked
equalities
`sanitized_database_size_bytes = sanitized_page_count * 4,096` and
`restore_disposition_cache_pages =
sanitized_page_count + 2*maximum_btree_depth + 512`. It requires every
b-tree depth to be in `1..sanitized_page_count`, so the hard maxima are
1,073,741,824 file bytes, 786,944 cache pages, and 3,223,322,624 cache bytes;
all additions and multiplications use checked nonnegative safe-integer
arithmetic. The authenticated immutable package descriptor records the exact
page size/count, maximum depth, file bytes, computed cache pages, and cache
bytes. Restore must rederive exact equality rather than trust those fields.
Page-count equality at 262,144 under the supported 4,096-byte profile is
publishable; 262,145, one byte/page less than an asserted equality, overflow,
or formula/profile drift refuses before publication and therefore cannot
enter backup listing.
Raw-byte fixtures on every supported SQLite build seed distinct maximum-width
values in every outbox field plus unique maximum-size command-map/statement-
nonce canaries in the transient permit and complete maximum-row shapes across
page, cell, overflow, freeblock, and stream-chunk boundaries; delete through
the production command path with `cache_spill=OFF`; checkpoint/TRUNCATE the
source WAL; reconstruct and VACUUM the fresh image; and prove none of those
byte strings or unique prefixes occurs outside the permitted schema text in
the closed image, page cache after role teardown, or any sidecar.
They crash/reopen at every reconstruction, destination-commit, VACUUM,
checkpoint, close, physical-parse, fsync, hidden-copy, and publication edge
and require either no publishable candidate or the same complete proof. The
observed SQLite-3.49.2/WAL/secure-delete sentinel success is only a
feasibility vector, not a substitute for that build/profile matrix. Any
version/compile/profile drift, ambiguous page ownership, or missing
conformance fixture fails publication; row-count zero or VACUUM alone is never
accepted as physical proof. Restored-worker
tests prove that a pre-create row is terminal and cannot dispatch,
create/reconcile rows are claimable as `reconciling`, poll rows are claimable
as `processing`, every terminal/other row retains its declared state, and
duplicate-safe marker, alias, and idempotency bindings remain intact.

Publication uses an owned recovery protocol under the destination parent, not
an unrecorded rename. The one persistent shared maintenance lock is
`<destination parent>/.backup-offsite.lock`; in production that is exactly
`/opt/brain/data/backups/.backup-offsite.lock`. Production has three
root-controlled provisioning marker paths:

- `/opt/brain/scripts/.backup-offsite-lock-bootstrap-clean-v1`;
- `/opt/brain/scripts/.backup-offsite-lock-bootstrap-b27-v1`;
- `/opt/brain/scripts/.backup-offsite-lock-provisioned-v1`.

All marker paths, marker staging paths, the `/opt/brain/scripts` control
parent, and every existing ancestor must be nonsymlink and
path/descriptor-identity-stable; the production control parent is exactly
`root:brain-data:0750`. A visible marker is an ordinary regular file owned
`root:root`, mode `0600`, link count one, and contains exact canonical
`stage2-backup-provisioning-intent-v1` bytes. That record has keys exactly
`domain,route,shared_run_binding_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,
platform_descriptor_sha256,base_commit,s27_descriptor_sha256,
admission_manifest_sha256,tool_transition_manifest_sha256`. Domain is exactly
`stage2-backup-provisioning-intent-v1`; route is exactly `clean|b27`;
`platform` is exactly `linux`; and the shared binding, aggregation binding,
selected Linux descriptor, commit, S27 descriptor, admission manifest, and
transition manifest bind the one pre-run platform transaction. The compact
ASCII JSON plus LF is 1..768 bytes and is read through a 769-byte cap. The
selected bootstrap and later provisioned marker contain byte-identical intent
records. A retry whose package, route, commit, S27 descriptor, admission
manifest, or transition manifest differs preserves and refuses.

A marker is never exposed by writing its final pathname. For marker role
`bootstrap-clean|bootstrap-b27|provisioned`, the sole staging basename is
`.stage2-backup-marker-<role>-<sha256(intent-bytes)>.tmp`. A root worker with
effective UID/GID `root:root`, `umask 0177`, and requested mode `0600`
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`-creates that temp with final metadata already
visible, writes the complete intent, fsyncs and genuinely read-only reverifies
it, then makes one same-filesystem no-replace hard link to the fixed marker
path and fsyncs the control parent. It next unlinks the temp and fsyncs the
control parent again, leaving the final marker at link count one. Recovery
accepts only: no name; one safe temp whose bytes are an exact prefix of the
current intent and whose name already commits its full intent hash; a complete
temp at link count one; the complete temp/final same-inode pair at link count
two; or the exact final at link count one. It durably removes a partial temp,
completes a valid link/cleanup prefix, or re-fsyncs an already-complete marker
and parent. A second temp, alternate hash, unsafe metadata, different inode,
different bytes, extra link, or both route bootstraps preserves and refuses.
Thus marker visibility is atomic and no partial file can be reinterpreted by
a later package.

With all marker and marker-temp names absent, production may begin in exactly
one of two descriptor-bound states. The existing-B27 route must match the
checked-in `stage2-b27-backup-upgrade-v1` manifest named by the pre-run
post-SQL Linux platform descriptor. Its controller retains exact inherited open-file
descriptions for `/run/brain-release.lock` and
`/run/brain-release-tools.lock`. The first excludes current-main
`activate-release.sh` and `switch-release.sh`; the second excludes current-main
tool-set staging and promotion. Neither lock is claimed to exclude the
current-main `remote_install_backup_tools` path, because that path does not
take either lock. B27 is therefore supported only in the descriptor-attested
single-actor legacy-entrypoint maintenance window: before admission, every
manifest-listed legacy deploy/installer process and descendant is absent and
drained, no independent legacy root invocation may begin until provisioned is
durable, and every repository-controlled launcher is stopped. This is an
explicit operational precondition, not a fictitious lock guarantee or a
production OS-containment claim. A preexisting legacy process refuses
admission. An out-of-protocol privileged actor that launches old bytes after
the frozen drain violates host integrity and receives no concurrency or
recovery claim.

The B27 controller validates and acquires the existing backup-lock open-file
description before publishing its bootstrap intent, then retains all three
open-file descriptions through entrypoint transition, consumer revalidation,
provisioned-marker completion, and descendant drain. The fresh route has no
legacy release state and must match the checked-in
`stage2-backup-clean-host-v1` absence manifest: exact provisioned
`/opt/brain/data` and control-parent identities; absent destination parent,
lock, database, release activation, durable/active tool targets, all three
marker paths and staging prefixes, backup artifacts, and publication residue;
and every named consumer absent or stopped-and-drained. The independently
derived unit inventory includes the cron daemon controlling
`brain-backup.cron`, every timer/path/service publisher, and every application
worker. A stopped-and-drained unit is inactive, has no
activating/deactivating/reloading state, and has an empty
descriptor-attested systemd cgroup; disabling or masking alone never
qualifies. All controls remain stopped-and-drained until provisioned is
durable and the selected bootstrap is durably absent. Any other markerless
state refuses without mutation.

The checked-in `stage2-backup-tool-transition-v1` manifest named by the same
descriptor supplies the one shared production target/source inventory. It has
top-level keys exactly
`domain,base_commit,s27_descriptor_sha256,tool_files`. The nonempty
`tool_files` array has 1..64 entries ordered first by
`kind=legacy_entrypoint|ordinary` in that order and then by unsigned-byte
canonical target path; target paths are unique. Every target is a strict
descendant (never equal to or an ancestor) of one explicitly admitted tool
parent, which may be the control parent. No target is equal to or a
component-prefix/descendant of the backup parent, lock, marker paths, another
target, another entry's staging temp, or a source locator. Every target
basename avoids all reserved marker/tool/publication/intent basenames, and the derived
`.stage2-backup-tool-<index>-<new_sha256>.tmp` path is unique and cannot equal
any target or other derived temp. The manifest has at most 64 distinct target
parents. Each entry has keys exactly
`path,kind,source,b27_old_artifact,new_artifact`. `source` has keys exactly
`role,locator_kind,locator,sha256,packaging_scope`; its role is exactly
`backup_tool/<three-decimal-index>/source`, its SHA equals
`new_artifact.sha256`, and it equals one required binary-artifact role in
every applicable case. Production sources have
`packaging_scope=production`; disposable Darwin sources are
`evidence_only`. `b27_old_artifact` is JSON null when protected main requires
that path absent; otherwise it and the always-nonnull `new_artifact` have keys
exactly `sha256,uid,gid,mode,type,size,link_count`. The clean route requires
every target absent at admission and permits only absent-or-new prefixes. The
B27 route permits only the listed old-or-new prefixes, treating null old as
required absence. Every B27 `legacy_entrypoints` record is one-to-one with a
`kind=legacy_entrypoint` transition entry and supplies its exact old process
matcher; there is no separate unnamed old-state inventory.

All production manifests and marker intents use the section-12 canonical JSON
and locator rules. Arrays are bounded as stated or at 256, have no duplicate,
and use their declared unsigned-byte ordering. A production absolute path is
1..1024 ASCII bytes, normalized, nonsymlink at every required existing
component, and contains no empty, `.`, `..`, backslash, NUL, control, or glob
component. `base_commit` is exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal; every SHA-256 is
exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal. `uid`, `gid`, `size`, and `link_count` are
JSON strings matching `0|[1-9][0-9]*` and denoting
`0..18446744073709551615`; `mode` is a JSON string matching `[0-7]{4}`;
`type` is exactly `regular|directory`. Artifact records require
`type=regular` and `link_count="1"`.

`stage2-b27-backup-upgrade-v1` has top-level keys exactly
`domain,base_commit,s27_descriptor_sha256,release_lock,release_tools_lock,
backup_parent,backup_lock,process_scan,staging_prefixes,consumer_units,
legacy_entrypoints`.
`release_lock`, `release_tools_lock`, and `backup_lock` have keys exactly
`path,uid,gid,mode,type,size,link_count`; `backup_parent` has keys exactly
`path,uid,gid,mode,type`. Each legacy entry has keys exactly
`path,sha256,process_matchers,required_state`; matchers are 1..16 unique
records in unsigned-byte canonical order with keys exactly
`kind,executable_path,executable_sha256,script_path,script_sha256,argv_prefix,
systemd_unit,cgroup_path`. `kind` is exactly
`native_executable|interpreter_script|systemd_unit`; inapplicable fields are
JSON null; nonnull paths/hashes use the exact production path/SHA rules;
`argv_prefix` is null or 1..32 exact printable-ASCII strings of 0..512 bytes;
and nonnull unit/cgroup values identify the exact stopped launcher and
descriptor-attested cgroup. Native matching binds the reopened executable
device/inode/path/hash, interpreter matching additionally binds the script
path/hash and argv prefix, and unit matching binds the exact unit/cgroup.
For every legacy entry, `path,sha256` equal the one-to-one transition entry's
`path,b27_old_artifact.sha256`. At least one matcher directly binds those same
bytes: a native matcher has equal executable path/hash; an interpreter matcher
has equal script path/hash; and a unit matcher's descriptor-attested
`ExecStart` resolves to one of those two exact bindings. A matcher that names
only an unrelated interpreter, executable, unit, or cgroup cannot satisfy the
entry.
`required_state` is exactly `absent_and_drained`.
`process_scan` has keys exactly
`identity_mode,pid_limit,argv_bytes_per_process,cgroup_bytes_per_process,
passes`, with values `pidfd_starttime`, `32768`, `65536`, `4096`, and `2`.
Failure to open a pidfd and bind the same kernel start time for every examined
live process refuses; there is no weaker fallback mode.
`stage2-backup-clean-host-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,base_paths,absent_paths,absent_prefixes,consumer_units`; each base record has keys
exactly `path,uid,gid,mode,type`, and each absent-path entry is a canonical
absolute exact pathname. `absent_prefixes` has 1..128 unique records in
unsigned-byte `(parent,prefix)` order with keys exactly
`parent,basename_prefix,scan_limit`; parent is an exact admitted directory,
the prefix is 1..128 printable-ASCII basename bytes with no slash, and
`scan_limit` is exactly `4096`. Admission streams at most 4,097 entries per
declared parent, refuses on the 4,097th, and requires zero prefix matches; a
prefix is never reinterpreted as an ordinary absent absolute pathname. In both
manifests each consumer entry has keys exactly
`name,required_state`, with `required_state` exactly
`absent|disabled_stopped_drained|masked_stopped_drained`. The domain of each
manifest equals its filename without `.json`. Clean `absent_paths` includes
every production transition target and all three exact marker paths;
`absent_prefixes` includes every marker/tool staging prefix. B27 legacy
entries and old transition artifacts are
one-to-one. The shared binding, aggregation binding, selected Linux platform
descriptor, and applicable `fixture_sha256` bind all three files. AC13
independently derives the complete current-main
path/unit/legacy-process inventory and fails on any omitted, extra, stale,
reordered, scalar-type, enum, or cross-manifest mismatch.

B27 `staging_prefixes` uses the identical 1..128 record schema and contains
the same complete derived marker/tool prefix set. Markerless B27 admission
requires zero matches. Selected-route recovery repeats every bounded parent
scan before mutation and permits only the one exact protocol-safe
current-role/current-index temp already named by the active intent and
transition hash; an alternate hash, stale index, second match, malformed
prefix-bearing basename, 4,097th entry, or unscanned target parent preserves
and refuses. The clean route applies the same bounded recovery rule after its
bootstrap intent exists.

The B27 admission scanner examines at most 32,769 numeric `/proc` entries and
refuses on the 32,769th. With every declared launcher already stopped, it
opens and hash-verifies each candidate executable and script, binds PID plus
kernel start time plus its pidfd, parses bounded exact argv
and cgroup membership, walks the bounded parent/start-time graph, and requires
zero matching process or descendant. It then repeats a complete scan and
requires the same zero result; PID disappearance, reuse, unreadable identity,
argv/cgroup truncation, namespace drift, or a late match refuses. These typed
matchers close repository-controlled old entrypoints; a privileged actor
executing copied or renamed unlisted bytes during the declared maintenance
window remains the explicit host-integrity violation stated above.

After full admission, the selected bootstrap intent is published through the
staged no-replace protocol above. In the clean route, the reviewed worker runs
as `brain:brain-data` with exact `umask 0007` and creates
`/opt/brain/data/backups` by one no-replacement `mkdir` with requested mode
`2770`. The already-setgid `brain-data` data root and requested mode make the
first visible directory exactly `brain:brain-data:2770`; the worker fsyncs
`/opt/brain/data` and revalidates both identities and metadata. An exact
existing parent is the only accepted clean retry shape; there is no
post-create `chown` or `chmod`. The B27 route never creates or repairs the
parent.

Only the exact clean bootstrap intent with both other markers absent may
authorize a missing lock. The production worker runs as `brain:brain-data`
with exact `umask 0007` and opens the final component read-write with
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, requested mode `0660`; the setgid parent supplies
GID `brain-data`, so the first visible inode is already an ordinary regular
file owned `brain:brain-data`, mode `0660`, size zero, and link count one. The
disposable helper uses its declared UID/GID, exact `umask 0077`, and requested
mode `0600`. No path performs post-create `chown`, `chmod`, unlink,
replacement, or metadata repair. B27 selected with a missing or drifting lock
always preserves and refuses.

For both a clean-created and B27-existing lock, the controller
`lstat`-validates, opens read-write with `O_NOFOLLOW`, and requires exact
device/inode and metadata equality through `fstat`. It acquires an exclusive
kernel `flock` on that opened descriptor, repeats every route, intent, lock,
consumer, destination-parent, and ancestor proof, then fsyncs the lock
descriptor and destination parent while still holding the lock. B27 performs
this acquisition before publishing its bootstrap intent; clean performs it
after durable parent/lock creation. The operation matrix freezes those two
scenario orders explicitly.

Target tools are published in manifest order. For index `000..T-1`, the exact
source locator is reopened and hash/size/identity-verified before destination
mutation. A descriptor-bound worker uses the target artifact's final effective
UID/GID, exact `umask 0000`, the target's exact requested final mode, and
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` to create only
`.stage2-backup-tool-<index>-<new_sha256>.tmp`; owner/group/mode are therefore
correct at first visibility and are never repaired. It writes only an exact
prefix of source bytes, completes the bytes, fsyncs and genuinely read-only
reverifies the ordinary link-count-one temp, then atomically renames it over
only the route-exact old target or into the route-exact absent target and
fsyncs the containing directory.

A retry accepts only the exact route prefix plus either no temp or the one
current-index temp. A safe temp must have the exact committed name,
type/owner/group/mode/link-one identity, size in `0..new_artifact.size`, and
bytes equal to that exact source prefix; it is unlinked and its directory
fsynced before restaging. A symlink, extra temp, wrong identity, nonprefix
byte, oversized temp, out-of-order new target, third target state, or
target/temp ambiguity preserves and refuses. Before advancing past any target
already observed exact-new—including a crash after rename but before the
original parent fsync—recovery reopens and read-only reverifies the target,
fsyncs the file, fsyncs its containing directory, and revalidates it. Thus
every accepted new prefix is made durably authoritative on every retry. After
every entry, all earlier targets are exact new and durably re-fsynced, the
current temp is absent, and all later targets remain exact route input.

Only after all target tools are exact new, every legacy entrypoint is the
Stage-2-aware new artifact, the descriptor-attested legacy process inventory
is still absent/drained, every old nonnull creator hash is absent, every
null-old B27 path and clean input path has transitioned to new, systemd has
reloaded the exact unit files while controls remain stopped-and-drained, and
all retained lock/parent proofs have repeated may the controller publish the
byte-identical provisioned intent through the staged no-replace marker
protocol. It then unlinks only the selected bootstrap marker and fsyncs the
control parent. A crash may leave only the selected bootstrap, that bootstrap
plus provisioned, or provisioned only; retry accepts them only when both
records byte-equal the current intent and completes forward. Provisioned-only
is normal state. Both bootstraps, wrong/malformed/mismatched intent bytes,
provisioned-without-lock, or lock/consumer/tool drift are preserved refusals.
Once provisioned exists—and always before S28 activation—no repository path
may create, recreate, replace, unlink, `chown`, or `chmod` the lock.
Concurrent supported controllers converge through the route-intent no-replace
publication, exact parent/lock `EEXIST` validation, retained route-specific
outer locks, and the same backup-lock open-file description.

Stage 2 claims and validates the POSIX file type, UID, GID, mode, size, link
count, device, and inode fields named above. An ACL, xattr, mount-policy, or
same-inode metadata model outside those fields is a separately provisioned
host-integrity precondition, not an unbounded Stage 2 inspection claim.

Production Linux resolves only the descriptor-attested system `flock`
executable and applies it to the already-open inherited descriptor; it never
asks `flock` to reopen the path. S2-AC-13 is accepted only from the
descriptor-bound acceptance supervisor after one exact
`stage2-ac13-qemu-tcg-vm-v2` disposable VM has completed, its effective
runtime envelope has matched, and every owned host artifact has been
destroyed. A container, chroot, host execution, KVM/device passthrough, or
alternate VM profile refuses. Root and real `brain:brain-data` identities and
the production absolute paths exercised by AC13 exist only inside the guest.
The VM is evidence-only and grants no production containment authority.

The selected pre-run Linux platform descriptor's canonical
`stage2-ac13-qemu-inputs-v1` manifest has
keys exactly
`domain,launcher,runtime,runtime_dependencies,base_image,firmware,
image_build_manifest,system_flock,launch_config,expected_runtime_envelope`.
Every scalar artifact record has keys exactly
`role,locator_kind,locator,sha256,packaging_scope`; all use
`packaging_scope=evidence_only` and map one-to-one to the corresponding AC13
binary role. The scalar roles are exactly `ac13/launcher`,
`ac13/qemu_runtime`, `ac13/base_image`, `ac13/firmware`,
`ac13/image_build_manifest`, `ac13/system_flock`, `ac13/launch_config`, and
`ac13/runtime_envelope_expected`. `runtime_dependencies` has 1..256
role-unique entries in unsigned-byte role order and equals the independently
regenerated complete effective dynamic loader, shared-object, and
loadable-module closure for the reopened runtime, including system-resolved
bytes. Its roles are exactly
`ac13/runtime_dependency/<three-decimal-index>` for indices `000..R-1`.
Omission, extra dependency, loader/search-path drift, or a runtime/input hash
mismatch refuses before spawn.

`image_build_manifest` resolves to canonical
`stage2-ac13-networkless-image-build-v1` bytes. That manifest has keys exactly
`domain,architecture,source_commit,network_policy,environment,build_inputs,
steps,guest_entries,system_flock,output`; domain and architecture are exactly
`stage2-ac13-networkless-image-build-v1` and `x86_64`; `source_commit` equals
the shared binding and both platform descriptors' common commit. `network_policy` has keys exactly
`namespace,loopback_state,denied_socket_families,dns,proxy_environment` and
values `new_private`, `down`,
`["AF_INET","AF_INET6","AF_NETLINK","AF_PACKET","AF_VSOCK"]`, `none`, and
`[]`. Build execution occurs in that new network namespace after verifying
loopback down, no other interface, an empty resolver configuration, and no
proxy variable; the builder's syscall filter rejects every listed family.
Any interface, route, resolver, proxy, socket-connect attempt, downloaded
byte, or ambient package-manager/cache input refuses.

The image-build record has `locator_kind=repository_path` and exact locator
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/implementation/fixtures/stage2-ac13-networkless-image-build-v1.json`.
The top-level system-`flock` record has
`locator_kind=guest_image_path` and exact locator
`ac13/base_image:/usr/bin/flock`; its role/hash equal the nested
`system_flock.path,system_flock.sha256` binding below.

`environment` is exactly
`["HOME=/nonexistent","LANG=C","LC_ALL=C","PATH=/nonexistent",
"SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0","TZ=UTC"]`. `build_inputs` has `I` entries, where
`1 <= I <= 128`, in three-decimal index order. Each has keys exactly
`index,kind,artifact`; `index` is `000..I-1`; `kind` is exactly
`builder_executable|builder_dependency|recipe|source`; and `artifact` uses the
scalar artifact schema, role
`ac13/image_build_input/<three-decimal-index>`, and
`packaging_scope=evidence_only`. At least one input is
`builder_executable`, every executed or opened builder/recipe/source byte is
represented exactly once, and the independently regenerated executable,
dynamic-loader, shared-object, recipe-import, and source-open closure equals
this ordered array.

`steps` has 1..256 entries in exact execution order with keys exactly
`index,executable_role,arguments,input_roles,output_paths`. Index is
three-decimal and contiguous; executable and input roles reference
`build_inputs`; `arguments` has 1..64 printable-ASCII strings of 0..1,024
bytes; and `output_paths` has 1..256 unique canonical absolute guest paths in
unsigned-byte order. No shell, ambient executable resolution, dynamic
download, undeclared input, device passthrough, host share, or nondeterministic
timestamp source is permitted. The validator independently repeats the build
from only those reopened inputs under the exact network/environment policy and
requires byte-identical output.

`guest_entries` has 1..65,536 entries in canonical absolute-path byte order,
each with keys exactly
`path,type,sha256,link_target,uid,gid,mode,size,link_count,source_role`.
Paths are normalized absolute guest paths with the section-12 component rules;
scalar metadata uses the section-6.1 bounds; and type is exactly
`regular|directory|symlink`. For `regular`, SHA is nonnull, link target is
null, link count is `"1"`, and source role references one build input. For
`directory`, SHA, link target, and source role are null and size is the
canonical extracted directory size. For `symlink`, SHA is over the exact
printable-ASCII link-target bytes, link target is a normalized guest path,
source role references one build input, and size is its exact byte length.
Device, socket, FIFO, hard-linked, multiply-linked, unlisted, or unsupported
inodes refuse. The array is the complete independently extracted image inode
inventory; every entry and all metadata equal exactly.
`system_flock` has keys exactly
`path,sha256,interpreter_path,runtime_dependency_paths`; path is the exact
guest executable path, SHA equals the top-level `system_flock` artifact,
`interpreter_path` is a canonical guest path or null, and the 0..128 unique
runtime-dependency paths are unsigned-byte sorted. The executable,
interpreter, and complete independently derived guest loader/shared-object
closure each equal one `guest_entries` regular-file entry; no ambient guest
byte is accepted.
`output` has keys exactly
`role,sha256,size,format,standalone,backing_depth`; role/hash equal the
top-level `base_image`, size is a canonical uint64 decimal string, format is
`qcow2`, `standalone=true`, and `backing_depth="0"`.

The base image contains no `/opt/brain` before the fixture builder creates the
descriptor-bound clean or B27 state. Before any guest child exists, the
preflight validator independently reopens the manifest, launcher,
runtime/version, runtime closure, firmware, every image-build input, rebuilt
standalone image, extracted system `flock` closure, launch config, and expected
envelope and requires every nested role/hash and the descriptor static
`qemu_inputs` hash to close. It does not read or require the not-yet-created
per-case binary-artifact manifest or its isolation record.

The canonical launch artifact is `stage2-ac13-qemu-launch-config-v2`, with
keys exactly
`domain,profile,architecture,accelerator,machine_type,cpu_model,outer_euid,
outer_egid,outer_capabilities,working_directory,umask,environment,rlimits,
io_limits,inherited_descriptors,launcher_start_gate,configured_devices,
host_shares,host_devices,network,monitor,qmp,runtime_socket,start_paused,
qmp_protocol,
expected_runtime_envelope_role,expected_runtime_envelope_sha256,arguments,
expanded_arguments_sha256`. Domain and profile are respectively
`stage2-ac13-qemu-launch-config-v2` and
`stage2-ac13-qemu-tcg-vm-v2`; architecture, accelerator, and CPU model are
exactly `x86_64`, `tcg`, and `max`. `machine_type` is the one concrete
versioned `pc-q35-X.Y` name in the expected-envelope artifact and materialized
argv; the alias `q35`, `X.Y` notation, and every unresolved placeholder are
forbidden in persisted bytes. Outer IDs are nonzero safe integers;
`outer_capabilities`, `host_shares`, and `host_devices` are empty arrays.
`working_directory` is literal `descriptor_attested_private_stage`; `umask`
is `"0077"`; `environment` is exactly
`["HOME=/nonexistent","LANG=C","LC_ALL=C","TMPDIR=."]`; and `rlimits` has
keys exactly `core_bytes,file_bytes,nofile,processes` with values
`"0","8589934592","32","64"`. `io_limits` has keys exactly
`serial_bytes,serial_frame_bytes,serial_events,diagnostic_stderr_bytes,
qmp_bytes,qmp_message_bytes,qmp_messages` and canonical decimal-string values
`"8388608","4096","10000","8388608","8388608","1048576","10000"`.
Serial is the same uint32-big-endian length plus 1..4,096-byte canonical event
payload framing used by the outer assertion channel; QMP uses its JSON message
bound and raw aggregate bound; stderr is raw bounded bytes. Equality passes;
the first excess byte/frame/event/message irreversibly fails, triggers
supervisor cleanup, and forwards no assertion.

Before spawn, the supervisor creates one
`AF_UNIX,SOCK_STREAM|SOCK_CLOEXEC` socketpair. It retains the controller
endpoint outside the killable launcher/QEMU process group, duplicates only
the peer to descriptor 5, and creates no pathname, listener, TCP/VSOCK
endpoint, or discoverable runtime socket. `inherited_descriptors` is exactly
six descriptor-ordered records with keys `fd,role,access`:
`[0,stdin_null,read]`, `[1,serial_events,write]`,
`[2,diagnostic_stderr,write]`, `[3,firmware,read]`,
`[4,writable_root,read_write]`, and
`[5,qmp_private_peer,read_write]`. Every other descriptor is closed or
close-on-exec. A runtime descriptor scan permits the one identity-attested
connected socket at role `qmp_private_peer`; every other pathname, socket,
device, or backend not represented by the expected envelope refuses.
Expected/observed/QMP/receipt artifacts contain semantic roles and descriptor
numbers only, never a staging, executable, socket, or other raw host path.

`launcher_start_gate` has keys exactly
`kind,child_fd,parent_death_signal,release_octet,closed_before_exec` and values
`pipe`, `6`, `SIGKILL`, `"01"`, and `true`. Descriptor 6 exists only in the
pre-exec launcher: after fork the child sets `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG=SIGKILL`,
verifies its parent is still the recorded supervisor, enters its new process
group, and blocks on exactly one `0x01` octet. EOF, another octet, parent
identity drift, or signal-setup failure exits without opening the root or
executing QEMU. The supervisor publishes the durable root runtime authority
defined below before writing that octet. The child closes descriptor 6 before
exec, so the QEMU descriptor set remains exactly 0..5.

`configured_devices` is exactly
`["virtio-blk-pci:stage2_root","isa-serial:stdio"]`; it names only explicit
frontends, not the full effective versioned-q35 topology. Network and HMP
monitor are `none`; QMP is `private_inherited_socketpair`; runtime socket is
`none`; and `start_paused=true`. `qmp_protocol` has keys exactly
`domain,transport,child_fd,start_state,request_id_start,request_timeout_ms,
total_byte_cap,inspection_plan` and scalar values
`stage2-ac13-qmp-protocol-v1`, `af_unix_stream_socketpair`, `5`, `paused`,
