`1`, `10000`, and `8388608`. `inspection_plan` is the canonical
`stage2-ac13-qmp-inspection-v1` record defined below, not a free string.

`arguments` is the fully materialized ordered array:
`["-nodefaults","-no-user-config","-no-reboot","-display","none","-S",
"-machine","<machine_type>,accel=tcg","-cpu","max","-smp",
"cpus=2,sockets=1,cores=2,threads=1","-m","4096",
"-nic","none","-monitor","none","-serial","stdio","-chardev",
"socket,id=stage2_qmp,fd=5","-mon",
"chardev=stage2_qmp,mode=control,pretty=off","-sandbox",
"on,obsolete=deny,elevateprivileges=deny,spawn=deny,resourcecontrol=deny",
"-bios","/dev/fd/3","-blockdev",
"driver=file,node-name=stage2_root_file,filename=/dev/fd/4,aio=threads,cache.direct=on,cache.no-flush=off","-blockdev",
"driver=qcow2,node-name=stage2_root,file=stage2_root_file,read-only=off",
"-device","virtio-blk-pci,drive=stage2_root,id=stage2_root"]`.
Here `<machine_type>` is specification notation only: persisted bytes contain
the already-validated concrete field value. `/dev/fd/3` and `/dev/fd/4` are
descriptor pseudopaths, not host locators.
`expanded_arguments_sha256` hashes exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify(arguments)` bytes. The launcher directly execs the
descriptor-attested absolute runtime after clearing the ambient environment,
setting the exact cwd/umask/limits, and installing only those six
descriptions; it invokes no shell.

QEMU starts paused. The canonical `stage2-ac13-qmp-inspection-v1` plan has
keys exactly
`domain,capabilities_request,fixed_query_order,qom_walk,lifecycle,
event_policy`. Domain is exact. `capabilities_request` has keys exactly
`execute,arguments` and is exactly
`{"execute":"qmp_capabilities","arguments":{}}`. `fixed_query_order` is
exactly
`["query-qmp-schema","query-version","query-target",
"query-current-machine","query-kvm","query-status","query-cpus-fast",
"query-pci","query-block","query-named-block-nodes","query-chardev",
"query-fdsets","query-mice","query-display-options","query-vnc","query-tpm",
"query-audiodevs"]`. Every fixed query uses exact empty arguments and occurs
once in that order in each `pre_start` and `pre_destroy` inspection.
`query-status` must return `paused` in both.

`qom_walk` has keys exactly
`root,traversal,child_type_prefix,result_sort,max_nodes,max_depth,
max_path_bytes,max_cumulative_path_bytes`. Its values are `/machine`,
`breadth_first`, `child<`, `name_then_type`, `"4096"`, `"64"`, `"4096"`,
and `"1048576"`. The root is queried first; each `qom-list` reply is sorted by
unsigned-byte `(name,type)`; only a type beginning `child<` enqueues the
canonical child path; and the FIFO is processed in that order. A duplicate,
cycle, empty/`.`/`..`/slash-bearing child name, link traversal, unwalkable
child, bound equality excess, or path/cumulative-byte excess refuses.
`lifecycle` is exactly
`[{"phase":"run","execute":"cont","arguments":{}},
{"phase":"quiesce","execute":"stop","arguments":{}},
{"phase":"destroy","execute":"quit","arguments":{}}]`.
The supervisor sends `cont` only after the first inspection and guest-start
authority, sends `stop` only after the exact terminal serial attestation,
performs the complete second inspection only after STOP and paused status,
and sends `quit` only after that comparison passes.

`event_policy` is exactly
`[{"phase":"greeting_through_pre_start","events":[]},
{"phase":"cont_through_terminal_attestation","events":["RESUME"]},
{"phase":"stop_through_pre_destroy","events":["STOP"]},
{"phase":"quit_through_eof","events":["SHUTDOWN"]}]`.
Each named event occurs exactly once in its phase; its QMP timestamp is
validated as a safe nonnegative pair but excluded from the normalized
envelope; every other event, wrong phase, duplicate, omission, or event after
EOF refuses. Request IDs are consecutive safe integers beginning at 1:
capabilities first, then each pre-start fixed query, the breadth-first QOM
requests, `cont`, `stop`, each pre-destroy fixed query, the second
breadth-first QOM requests, and `quit`. Every response has exactly the matching
ID, no request is outstanding when the next phase begins, and every error
response refuses.

The canonical QMP-schema projection recursively retains every parsed key and
value. At every depth it inserts object keys in unsigned-byte key order.
Every nested array—including `features`, `members`, `variants`, `values`, and
scalar arrays—is canonicalized element-first and then sorted by the unsigned
bytes of each element's exact no-LF `JSON.stringify` result; duplicate
canonical nested-array elements refuse. The top-level schema array is the
single comparator exception: after recursively canonicalizing each element,
it sorts by the unsigned-byte lexicographic pair `(meta-type,name)`, first
`meta-type` and then `name`, and requires both fields to be nonempty strings
and every pair to be unique. A missing or differently typed tuple field
refuses. There is no version-dependent declared-key or wire-order fallback,
and an omitted, extra, duplicate, or differently typed key remains in the
projection and changes its hash. The raw transcript is binary
`stage2-ac13-qmp-transcript-v1`: exact ASCII
`stage2-ac13-qmp-transcript-v1`, one `0x00`, then zero or more frames
`direction:u8,kind:u8,sequence:u64be,length:u32be,payload`. Direction is
`0x01` supervisor-to-QEMU or `0x02` QEMU-to-supervisor; kind is respectively
`0x01` greeting, `0x02` request, `0x03` success reply, `0x04` error reply, or
`0x05` event. The closed direction/kind matrix permits only requests from
supervisor to QEMU and greeting, success/error replies, and events from QEMU
to supervisor; every other pair refuses. Sequence begins at zero and
increments by one; length is
1..1,048,576; and payload is the exact single raw QMP JSON message including
its exact two-byte `0x0d 0x0a` terminator. The parser rejects a duplicate JSON key,
non-ASCII byte, alternate terminator, extra whitespace outside the JSON value,
trailing byte, direction/kind mismatch, wrong ID, or plan/event mismatch.
Total framed bytes and frame count are respectively at most 8,388,608 and
10,000. `qmp_transcript_sha256` hashes these complete binary bytes.

The checked-in `stage2-ac13-qemu-runtime-envelope-expected-v1` artifact has
keys exactly
`domain,profile,runtime_sha256,qemu_version,machine_type,
inspection_plan_sha256,
qmp_schema_sha256,normalization,runtime_envelope,runtime_envelope_sha256,
guest_attestation,guest_attestation_sha256`. Domain/profile are exact; runtime
hash equals `ac13/qemu_runtime`; machine type is one concrete supported
versioned name; `inspection_plan_sha256` hashes exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify(qmp_protocol.inspection_plan)` bytes;
normalization is `stage2-ac13-qemu-envelope-projection-v1`; and both hash
fields cover exact no-LF `JSON.stringify` bytes of their named records.
`qemu_version` has keys exactly `major,minor,micro,package`; the first three
are canonical uint64 decimal strings and package is 1..128 printable ASCII
bytes fixed by the reopened runtime.
`runtime_envelope` has keys exactly
`machine,cpu_topology,pci_devices,qom_devices,block_nodes,block_edges,
block_frontends,chardevs,host_descriptor_classes`. `machine` has keys exactly
`type,accelerator,cpu_model,smp_cpus,memory_bytes`; numeric values are
canonical uint64 decimal strings. Every array is bounded at 4,096,
duplicate-free, and unsigned-byte sorted by canonical no-LF entry JSON.
`cpu_topology` has keys exactly
`sockets,cores_per_socket,threads_per_core,total_cpus,cpus`; its first four
values are respectively `"1","2","1","2"`. `cpus` has exactly two records,
in numeric `cpu_index` order, with keys exactly
`cpu_index,socket_id,core_id,thread_id,qom_path`; every numeric field is a
canonical uint64 decimal string, socket/thread are `"0"`, core/index are
`"0"` then `"1"`, and qom path is the exact normalized path returned by the
complete QOM walk. Host thread IDs are deliberately excluded as nondeterministic.
PCI records have keys exactly
`bus,slot,function,class,vendor,device,subsystem_vendor,subsystem_device,
qdev_id`. `bus`, `slot`, and `function` are canonical uint64 decimal strings
in `0..255`, `0..31`, and `0..7`; `class` is exactly six lowercase
hexadecimal; `vendor` and `device` are exactly four lowercase hexadecimal;
the two subsystem values are either both null or both exactly four lowercase
hexadecimal; and `qdev_id` is 0..128 printable ASCII bytes. QOM records have
keys exactly `path,type,parent`; `path` is a normalized absolute QOM path of
1..4,096 bytes, `type` is 1..256 printable ASCII bytes, and `parent` is null
exactly for `/machine` and otherwise is the exact normalized parent path.
They are the complete structural `/machine` traversal, including implicit
chipset devices.

`block_nodes` is exactly
`[{"node_name":"stage2_root","driver":"qcow2","read_only":false,
"encrypted":false,"host_role":null},
{"node_name":"stage2_root_file","driver":"file","read_only":false,
"encrypted":false,"host_role":"writable_root"}]`
in canonical entry order. `block_edges` is exactly
`[{"parent":"stage2_root","child":"stage2_root_file","role":"file"}]`;
no `backing`, data-file, filter, throttling, secret, or other edge exists.
`block_frontends` is exactly
`[{"device":"","qdev_id":"stage2_root","root_node":"stage2_root",
"read_only":false}]`. The projection is regenerated jointly from
`query-block`, `query-named-block-nodes`, and the descriptor identity scan;
the file node alone maps to descriptor 4 and the qcow2 node has backing depth
zero. An omitted protocol node, auto-generated/alternate node name, extra
node/edge/frontend, filename-derived identity, or collapsed graph refuses.
`chardevs` is exactly
`[{"label":"serial0","kind":"stdio","host_role":"serial_events",
"frontend_open":true},{"label":"stage2_qmp","kind":"socket",
"host_role":"qmp_private_peer","frontend_open":true}]`. Host-descriptor
records have keys exactly `kind,access,role,count`; `kind` is exactly
`regular_file|character_device|connected_unix_stream|pipe|eventfd|eventpoll|
memfd|signalfd|timerfd`, `access` is exactly `read|write|read_write`, and
`count` is a canonical uint64 decimal string in `1..32`. The expected-envelope
array itself is the finite role domain: every role is a unique 1..128-byte
printable-ASCII semantic name already present in that checked-in array, and
no rule-based new role is admitted. The known descriptions map exactly to
`stdin_null`, `serial_events`, `diagnostic_stderr`, `firmware`,
`writable_root`, and `qmp_private_peer`; anonymous runtime descriptions are
aggregated only by their exact expected semantic role/kind/access tuple. Any
other class, role, access, or count refuses.

`guest_attestation` has keys exactly
`pci_devices_sha256,block_devices,network_interfaces,serial_channels`; it
requires the runtime PCI records with only `qdev_id` removed, in the same
canonical order. `pci_devices_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-ac13-guest-pci-devices-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact UTF-8 no-LF
`JSON.stringify` bytes of that guest PCI projection. `block_devices` is
exactly one record
with keys `name,bus,driver,read_only,root`, bus/driver are
`virtio|virtio_blk`, read-only is false, root is true, and name is the one
exact guest name frozen by the image. `network_interfaces` is exactly
`[{"name":"lo","kind":"loopback","up":true}]`. `serial_channels` is exactly
`[{"name":"ttyS0","kind":"isa_serial","framing":
"uint32be_canonical_json","max_frame_bytes":"4096",
"max_events":"10000"}]`. No nested record has an extra key and no envelope
field contains a raw host path. The guest emits this exact record in its one
terminal serial event; the outer validator independently recomputes every
field from the preceding bounded guest events.

The raw serial artifact `ac13/serial_transcript` is the exact descriptor-1
byte stream: zero or more frames `length:u32be,payload`, with length 1..4,096
and payload exact ASCII compact JSON without LF. Every payload has keys
exactly `domain,sequence,kind,payload`; domain is
`stage2-ac13-serial-event-v1`, sequence begins at zero and increments by one,
kind is `guest_observation|assertion|terminal_attestation`, and only the final
event is terminal. Guest observations occur first in fixed
`pci_device,block_device,network_interface,serial_channel` order and canonical
record order; their payload has keys exactly `observation_kind,value`, where
`observation_kind` is one of those four literals. For `pci_device`, `value`
has keys exactly
`bus,slot,function,class,vendor,device,subsystem_vendor,subsystem_device` and
there is exactly one event for every runtime PCI record after removing
`qdev_id`, in that same canonical order. For `block_device`, `value` has keys
exactly `name,bus,driver,read_only,root` and exactly the one frozen
`block_devices` record is emitted. For `network_interface`, `value` has keys
exactly `name,kind,up` and exactly the one frozen `network_interfaces` record
is emitted. For `serial_channel`, `value` has keys exactly
`name,kind,framing,max_frame_bytes,max_events` and exactly the one frozen
`serial_channels` record is emitted. Thus the observation count is exactly
the guest PCI projection length plus three; a missing, extra, duplicate,
wrong-kind, wrong-record, or zero-cardinality substitution refuses.
Assertions then occur in manifest order. For `assertion`,
payload has keys exactly `assertion_id,status`;
`assertion_id` is the next exact AC13 assertion-manifest ID and status is
`PASS|FAIL`. Assertion events occur in manifest order without omission,
duplicate, or post-failure PASS. For `terminal_attestation`, payload has keys
exactly
`case_id,status,assertion_count,assertion_ids_sha256,guest_attestation,
guest_attestation_sha256`; case is `S2-AC-13`; status is `success|failure`;
count is the canonical uint64 decimal number of preceding assertion events;
ID hash covers exact no-LF `JSON.stringify` of their ordered IDs; and the
guest record/hash use the exact expected schema above. Exactly one terminal
event follows all assertions and is the last byte-bearing frame. Success
requires every preceding status PASS, exact manifest ID/count/hash equality,
terminal status success, and exact guest attestation; failure forwards no
assertion.
The raw `ac13/diagnostic_stderr` artifact is the exact descriptor-2 stream,
bounded at 8,388,608 bytes; successful AC13 requires it empty and therefore
requires the SHA-256 of zero bytes. The QMP, serial, diagnostic-stderr, and
observed-envelope phase artifacts use bounded `evidence_blob` storage and
must pass the pre-journal state-4 gate defined below; “before case evidence”
alone is not sufficient durability.

The generated
`stage2-ac13-qemu-runtime-envelope-observed-v1` artifact has keys exactly
`domain,profile,instance_id,writable_root_id,launch_config_sha256,
expected_runtime_envelope_sha256,inspection_plan_sha256,
qmp_transcript_sha256,qmp_schema_sha256,root_runtime_authority_sha256,
pre_start,pre_start_sha256,pre_destroy,pre_destroy_sha256,guest_attestation,
guest_attestation_sha256,serial_raw_bytes,serial_payload_bytes,
serial_event_count,serial_max_frame_bytes,serial_transcript_sha256,
diagnostic_stderr_bytes,diagnostic_stderr_sha256,qmp_bytes,
qmp_message_count,qmp_max_message_bytes,match_result`. Byte, frame, event, and
message counters are canonical uint64 decimal strings within `io_limits`;
`serial_raw_bytes` includes every four-byte length, payload bytes exclude
lengths, max frame is the observed maximum or `"0"` for no frame, and hashes
cover exact raw artifacts. Both snapshots use the expected runtime-envelope
schema; both hashes equal
`runtime_envelope_sha256`; guest bytes/hash equal
`guest_attestation_sha256`; inspection and authority hashes equal the reopened
launch/root-authority artifacts; and `match_result=exact`.

Before `cont`, the supervisor combines the paused QMP projection with the
outer executable/argv/environment/cwd/credential/capability/rlimit/descriptor
scan and requires exact expected-envelope equality. A missing command,
unexpected QMP error/event, cap/deadline breach, unmapped filename/socket,
unexpected backend, or nonexact comparison refuses without starting a vCPU.
After the guest emits its exact terminal serial attestation, the supervisor
sends `stop`, requires the STOP event and paused status, repeats the structural
and outer inspection, requires the same envelope, sends `quit`, and
drains/reaps the process group. The private QMP endpoint is never exposed to
the guest. Implementation must first verify the pinned runtime's exact
versioned machine name, connected-socketpair chardev syntax, QMP command
schemas/event order, descriptor-pseudopath identity behavior, and
stop/cont/quit behavior; those verified exact choices are then frozen in the
input manifest. If the pinned runtime cannot implement this exact profile,
AC13 and Stage 2 are NO-GO pending a newly reviewed contract amendment. No
fallback, `-drive`/fdset/alternate-blockdev substitution, alternate monitor
frontend, or alias is silently accepted.

Before any writable root, the supervisor completes a 4,096/4,097 bounded scan
of its private staging parent and requires zero names matching any of
`.stage2-ac13-root-<uuid>-<64hex>.qcow2` or
`.stage2-ac13-root-intent-<64hex>.json`,
`.stage2-ac13-root-intent-<64hex>.json.tmp`,
`.stage2-ac13-root-authority-<64hex>.json`, or
`.stage2-ac13-root-authority-<64hex>.json.tmp`,
`.stage2-ac13-root-destruction-journal-<64hex>.json`, or
`.stage2-ac13-root-destruction-journal-<64hex>.json.tmp`; a prefix-bearing
malformed name also refuses. It then chooses unique canonical `instance_id` and
`writable_root_id`, builds canonical `stage2-ac13-root-intent-v1` bytes with
keys exactly
`domain,shared_run_binding_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,
platform_descriptor_sha256,instance_id,writable_root_id,root_basename,uid,gid,
mode,base_image_sha256`. Platform is exactly `linux`; all four federation
fields equal the reopened platform context. UID/GID equal launch-config outer EUID/EGID
and mode is `"0600"`. For intent hash `H`, final and temp basenames are exactly
`.stage2-ac13-root-intent-H.json` and
`.stage2-ac13-root-intent-H.json.tmp`. The supervisor uses `umask 0177` and
requested mode `0600`; both names, whenever present, are ordinary
outer-UID/GID files with those exact bytes and expected link count under the
first-visible-final-metadata temp/write/file-fsync/read-only-verify/
no-replace-link/parent-fsync/temp-unlink/parent-fsync protocol. Only a durable
link-count-one final intent authorizes publication of the same canonical bytes
under section-12 evidence role `ac13/root_intent`. That content-addressed blob
is completed and reopened under the exact evidence-blob protocol before root
creation; its hash equals `root_intent_sha256`. Recovery from an exact external
intent with a missing safe blob completes only that exact blob first, while
unsafe blob metadata preserves the external intent and refuses. Only the
external final plus the reopened blob authorizes creation of its root basename.

The root is `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` first-visible mode `0600`, a complete
byte-for-byte private copy of the standalone base image—never a backing-file
overlay—then file/parent-fsynced and read-only hash/size/identity-verified.
`qemu-img`, a backing path, shared-write reflink, alternate constructor, or
sparse-byte ambiguity refuses.

After the complete root is reverified, the supervisor forks the gated launcher
described above. Before releasing its gate or allowing any root read/write, it
builds canonical `stage2-ac13-root-runtime-authority-v1` bytes with keys
exactly
`domain,shared_run_binding_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,
platform_descriptor_sha256,root_intent_sha256,instance_id,writable_root_id,
root_basename,root_device,root_inode,root_uid,root_gid,root_mode,
root_link_count,boot_id_sha256,leader_pid,leader_start_time,process_group_id,
launcher_sha256,runtime_sha256,state`. Domain and the exact Linux federation
tuple are exact; all
hash/ID/basename fields cross-bind reopened inputs; root identity fields equal
the still-open descriptor and use canonical uint64 decimal strings; boot ID
hashes the exact Linux boot-ID bytes; PID, kernel start time, and process-group
ID are nonzero canonical uint64 decimal strings; executable hashes equal the
preflight inputs; and state is exactly `armed`. The child is still blocked,
has not execed, and has performed no root I/O when these bytes are created.

For authority hash `A`, final and temp basenames are exactly
`.stage2-ac13-root-authority-A.json` and
`.stage2-ac13-root-authority-A.json.tmp`. They use the same exact
outer-UID/GID, `umask 0177`, mode-`0600`, link-count-one publication protocol
as the root intent. It reopens the final byte-identically, then immediately
durably stores and reopens the same canonical bytes at the section-12
`evidence_blob` path for role
`ac13/root_runtime_authority`; the authority final remains durable until that
blob publication completes, so every blob crash prefix remains recoverable
from authoritative bytes. An authority final without its exact intent/root, a
launcher that passed the gate first, or a root identity change refuses and
terminates the gated process. Both the external authority final and reopened
authority blob are required before the supervisor releases the one-byte gate;
publication failure terminates the still-gated process.

Startup recovery scans at most 4,097 parent entries and 65 matching
intent/root/authority/journal/temp names before mutation. It initially
classifies every name read-only. Only a trusted `setup_replay` coordinate may
complete or durably remove a safe intent/authority temp prefix under its exact
protocol. A journal candidate enters `journal_publication_repair` only when
its complete bytes already parse as the one canonical, semantically valid
initial journal for the surviving authority/root state. An empty, partial,
noncanonical, unsafe, or semantically invalid journal candidate is preserved
byte-for-byte and returns `prejournal_fail_closed`; it is never completed,
truncated, unlinked, or synthesized.
An exact final intent with no root and no authority is an intent-only cleanup
shape. An intent plus ordinary link-count-one expected-owner/mode root but no
authority is recoverable only when size is no greater than the base and bytes
equal that exact base prefix; this is the pre-arm copy-prefix shape. Neither
shape may remove the intent or root directly. Only a trusted `setup_replay`
coordinate may classify either as its known killed setup attempt, publish the
exact destruction journal below to freeze the intent hash and any pre-unlink
root identity, complete idempotent cleanup, run recovery twice, and then start
a fresh transaction. On ordinary startup the same journal-less names are
preserved byte-for-byte and return `prejournal_fail_closed`; no journal is
synthesized from ambient residue.

An exact intent/root/authority triple enters armed recovery. The supervisor
performs the B27 32,768/32,769 bounded PID/start-time/pidfd scan, additionally
binding boot ID and process-group ID. It terminates the exact live leader and
all same-group descendants, scans at most 1,025 descriptors per process and
refuses on the 1,025th, waits/reaps where parentage permits, repeats the
complete process scan, and requires zero group members and zero descriptors
whose device/inode equal the authority root. Only then may it unlink the exact
authority-bound ordinary link-count-one root inode regardless of post-arm
bytes or size within `file_bytes`, and only through the durable destruction
journal state machine below. No armed root, authority, or intent unlink is
legal before that journal is reopened. PID reuse,
unreadable identity, extra group member, open root descriptor, root
device/inode/owner/mode/link drift, or alternate bytes in either control file
preserves and refuses. Authority without exact intent/root, root without
intent, extra, alternate-hash, or unbound state also preserves and refuses.
Only a trusted `setup_replay` coordinate may reconcile a journal-less
deterministic pre-gate prefix and then run recovery twice before a fresh
transaction. On ordinary startup, any intent/root/authority state without complete
canonical initial-journal bytes is the exact `prejournal_fail_closed`
preserve/refuse state. One exact complete journal or complete legal journal
candidate authorizes only the publication-repair/idempotent continuation
defined next.

The acceptance supervisor—not the killable launcher or QEMU—is the sole root
destructor, journal owner, and receipt writer. A root transaction begins only
after the canonical intent bytes and root plan are frozen as
`reached_phase=root_planned`; an earlier preflight failure creates no root
name, journal, or destruction receipt. For every root-transaction outcome,
including intent-publication failure, intent-only setup, a pre-arm copy prefix,
and an armed runtime, it freezes the exact reached-phase/nullability shape.
After any required runtime-group termination/drain and QEMU-access closure,
but before owned-root revalidation or initial-journal creation, the
supervisor materializes every nonnull phase-artifact preimage named by the
future journal: exact raw QMP transcript, raw serial transcript, diagnostic
stderr, and—when `observed_runtime_envelope_sha256` is nonnull—the exact
canonical observed-envelope bytes. It publishes each under its declared role
through the global evidence-blob protocol, reaches state 4, reopens and
independently reparses it, and requires its hash and all counters/projections
to equal the frozen in-memory fields. The initial journal is forbidden until
that entire applicable set is durable. A hard death anywhere inside this
gate remains `prejournal_fail_closed`; its private coordinate sandbox may
contain only the global protocol's exact blob prefixes and the outer harness
disposes them without accepting package output. A complete journal on restart
must find every nonnull referenced artifact as a safe, exact state-4 final and
reopen/reparse it; absence, candidate-only state, unsafe metadata, or byte/hash
drift preserves and refuses rather than reconstructing bytes from a hash.

After that artifact gate and owned-root revalidation/hash, but before the
first root, authority, or intent unlink, the supervisor publishes canonical
`stage2-ac13-root-destruction-journal-v1` bytes. The keys are exactly
`domain,phase,journal_id,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,profile,
instance_id,writable_root_id,outcome,termination_reason,reached_phase,
guest_status,runtime_termination,launch_config_sha256,expanded_arguments_sha256,
expected_runtime_envelope_sha256,observed_runtime_envelope_sha256,
qmp_transcript_sha256,serial_transcript_sha256,diagnostic_stderr_sha256,
root_intent_sha256,root_runtime_authority_sha256,root_state,
pre_unlink_device,pre_unlink_inode,pre_unlink_size,pre_unlink_sha256,
descendant_count,unlink_result,parent_fsync_result,post_lstat_errno,
authority_unlink_result,intent_unlink_result,post_scan_entry_count,
post_scan_match_count,cleanup_started_at,finished_at`. `journal_id` is a fresh
64-lowercase-hex content-free nonce. Its final and only temp basenames are
exactly `.stage2-ac13-root-destruction-journal-<journal_id>.json` and that
basename plus `.tmp`; both use the intent's outer UID/GID, `umask 0177`,
mode `0600`, ordinary-file/no-symlink/link-count-one constraints.

Initial journal `phase=destruction_armed`; it freezes every pre-unlink fact,
all phase-reached hashes and nullable values used by the receipt, a truthful
UTC-millisecond `cleanup_started_at`, and the already-zero descendant count.
All five cleanup-result fields, both post-scan counts, and `finished_at` are
null. Initial publication uses the exact temp/O_EXCL/write/file-fsync/
read-only-reverify/no-replace-link/parent-fsync/temp-unlink/parent-fsync
protocol. Only that durable, reopened journal authorizes the first destructive
unlink. The state machine then unlinks only the journal-bound root inode,
fsyncs the parent, proves `lstat=ENOENT`, reopens and validates the already
durable authority evidence blob when armed, removes the matching authority,
removes the matching intent, and performs a bounded scan that permits exactly
this journal and no root, authority, intent, or other journal match.

Only after those actions succeed does the supervisor advance the same journal
to `phase=cleanup_complete`. It preserves every frozen field, fills the exact
cleanup results and post-scan counts, and sets `finished_at` to the actual UTC
millisecond completion time, which is not earlier than `cleanup_started_at`.
The advance creates the exact `.json.tmp` with `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, writes,
file-fsyncs, and read-only-reverifies the unique legal successor, reopens and
revalidates the armed final, atomically renames the temp over that exact final,
and fsyncs the parent. A crash may leave only the armed final, or the armed
final plus a complete legal successor temp; recovery reexecutes idempotent
cleanup before completing the advance. A completed final plus an identical
temp removes/fsyncs the temp. Any other temp, phase regression, changed frozen
field, unsafe metadata, or alternate journal preserves and refuses.

The completed journal bytes are then durably stored and reopened under
section 12 role `ac13/root_destruction_journal` using the exact evidence-blob
protocol. Their SHA-256 is the receipt's
`root_destruction_journal_sha256`; the journal contains no receipt or binary
manifest hash, so the graph is acyclic. Startup recovery accepts an exact
journal even when its bound root, authority, or intent is already absent:
`destruction_armed` replays only the journal-authorized idempotent remaining
cleanup, advances the journal, and publishes its blob; `cleanup_complete`
reopens the blob and proceeds to the receipt. A surviving unbound inode or
control file, or a mismatch against a surviving bound name, still preserves
and refuses.

The canonical `stage2-ac13-vm-destruction-receipt-v2` has keys exactly
`domain,profile,instance_id,writable_root_id,outcome,termination_reason,
reached_phase,guest_status,runtime_termination,launch_config_sha256,
expanded_arguments_sha256,expected_runtime_envelope_sha256,
observed_runtime_envelope_sha256,qmp_transcript_sha256,serial_transcript_sha256,
diagnostic_stderr_sha256,root_intent_sha256,root_runtime_authority_sha256,
root_destruction_journal_sha256,root_state,pre_unlink_device,pre_unlink_inode,
pre_unlink_size,pre_unlink_sha256,descendant_count,unlink_result,
parent_fsync_result,post_lstat_errno,authority_unlink_result,
intent_unlink_result,post_scan_entry_count,post_scan_match_count,
cleanup_started_at,finished_at`. Every field other than the journal hash is
copied byte-for-byte from the reopened `cleanup_complete` journal.
`outcome=success|failure`; `termination_reason` is exactly
`success|intent_publication_failure|root_intent_blob_failure|
root_copy_failure|spawn_failure|authority_publication_failure|
authority_blob_failure|launcher_gate_failure|qmp_protocol_failure|
envelope_mismatch|guest_failure|timeout|supervisor_signal|runtime_exit|
runtime_signal`; and `reached_phase` is exactly
`root_planned|intent_published|intent_blob_persisted|root_copying|root_ready|
capture_opened|launcher_gated|authority_published|authority_blob_persisted|
gate_released|runtime_started|pre_start_verified|guest_terminal|
pre_destroy_verified|runtime_drained` in that order. The complete allowed
reason/phase relation is:

- `success` requires `outcome=success`, `runtime_drained`, guest status zero,
  runtime exit zero, and the nonnull exact observed envelope;
- every other reason requires `outcome=failure`;
- `intent_publication_failure`, `root_intent_blob_failure`,
  `authority_publication_failure`, `authority_blob_failure`, and
  `launcher_gate_failure` require respectively `root_planned`,
  `intent_published`, `launcher_gated`, `authority_published`, and
  `authority_blob_persisted`;
- `root_copy_failure` requires
  `intent_blob_persisted|root_copying`;
- `spawn_failure` requires `root_ready|capture_opened|gate_released`;
- `qmp_protocol_failure` requires
  `runtime_started|pre_start_verified|guest_terminal|pre_destroy_verified`;
  its last two phases require guest status zero;
- `envelope_mismatch` has exactly two tuples:
  `runtime_started` with null guest status for the pre-start comparison, or
  `guest_terminal` with guest status zero for the pre-destroy comparison;
- `guest_failure` requires `guest_terminal` and guest status one;
- `timeout` requires
  `capture_opened|launcher_gated|authority_published|
  authority_blob_persisted|gate_released|runtime_started|pre_start_verified|
  guest_terminal|pre_destroy_verified`; a terminal-or-later timeout has guest
  status zero;
- a handled `supervisor_signal` may preserve any exact phase reached while the
  supervisor still owns the in-memory transaction; the hard-death
  pre-journal coordinates are governed separately below and create no
  receipt; and
- `runtime_exit` and `runtime_signal` require respectively an
  `exit` or `signal` runtime termination and one of
  `runtime_started|pre_start_verified|guest_terminal|pre_destroy_verified|
  runtime_drained`; a terminal-or-later tuple has guest status zero.

`guest_status` is null before `guest_terminal` and afterward is exactly safe
integer zero for guest success or one only for `guest_failure`.
`runtime_termination` has keys `kind,value` and is exactly one of
`{"kind":"not_started","value":null}`,
`{"kind":"exit","value":<safe integer 0..255>}`, or
`{"kind":"signal","value":<safe integer 1..64>}`. `root_state` is exactly
`not_created|copying|ready|armed`. The launch-config, expanded-argument,
expected-envelope, and root-intent hashes are always nonnull. Authority hash
is nonnull exactly from `authority_published`; QMP, serial, and stderr hashes
are nonnull exactly from `capture_opened`, including hashes of empty captures;
the observed-envelope hash is nonnull exactly from `pre_destroy_verified`.
Runtime termination is `not_started` before `runtime_started` and the exact
exit or signal afterward; `runtime_exit` cannot carry a signal and
`runtime_signal` cannot carry an exit. Root state is `not_created` through
`intent_blob_persisted`, `copying` at `root_copying`, `ready` from
`root_ready` through `launcher_gated`, and `armed` from
`authority_published`. Pre-unlink identity/size/hash fields are null only with
`not_created` and otherwise use the exact uint64/hash formats. Cleanup results are
`not_needed|ok`; authority unlink is `ok` exactly with `armed` and
`not_needed` otherwise; root unlink is `ok` exactly with
`copying|ready|armed`; intent unlink is `ok` exactly from
`intent_published`; parent fsync is `ok` exactly when any of those three
unlinks is `ok` and `not_needed` otherwise; `post_lstat_errno=ENOENT`;
`post_scan_entry_count` is a canonical uint64 decimal string in `1..4096`;
descendant count is `"0"`; and `post_scan_match_count` is explicitly the
unexpected-match count after excluding the one current journal, so it is
`"0"` although that journal is included in `post_scan_entry_count`. Both
timestamps are UTC RFC3339 with millisecond precision. A receipt claiming a
zero post-scan entry count is rejected by an explicit tuple vector because
the current journal still occupies one counted entry.

Before publishing receipt hash `H`, whose exact bytes are at most 65,536, the
supervisor applies the global four-state evidence-blob classifier to only
final `H` and candidate `.H.tmp`. The receipt-specific reconcile operation
verifies the candidate absent, removes one safe candidate-only prefix, or
validates/file-and-parent-fsyncs the complete same-inode link-count-two pair
and removes only its candidate. A different-inode pair, extra link, unsafe
metadata, oversize/nonprefix byte, or other receipt-like name preserves and
refuses. Reconcile-or-verify-absent and an unconditional blob-parent fsync are
separate ordered operations and crash coordinates; the latter runs whether
or not this invocation performed the unlink. It then freshly revalidates the
exact state-4 final or publishes state 1 through the global evidence-blob
protocol under role `ac13/root_destruction_receipt`. The
external destruction journal remains until the receipt final and blob parent
are durable; it is unlinked last, its parent is fsynced, and a final
4,096/4,097 scan requires zero root, intent, authority, journal, or temp
matches. A failure receipt proves cleanup only and never grants PASS.
Buffered assertions are forwarded only for `outcome=success`, exact
guest/runtime status zero, two exact envelope comparisons, complete armed-root
destruction, durable authority/intent removal, exact raw-stream validation,
and a validator-accepted receipt.

A Darwin disposable S2-AC-17 run, where a system `flock` executable is
absent, executes only the immutable capsule-prebuilt test adapter that calls
`flock(2)` on an inherited descriptor. Its source, compiler
executable/hash/version, exact flags, prebuilt bytes, comparison-only noexec
runtime rebuild, and immutable syscall self-test are bound by the selected
Darwin descriptor and per-case binary manifest under the exact roles defined
in section 12. That fixture is never
packaged or accepted in production; AC17 refuses on a non-Darwin runner or a
missing/mismatched adapter. Each platform case has its own command, package
binding, assertion set, and evidence file; neither can stand in for the other.
An in-process Node scheduler delegates through the reviewed
descriptor-attested adapter and does not pretend Node core supplies `flock`.

AC17 never consumes either production admission manifest. Its checked-in
`stage2-backup-darwin-fixture-v1` template has keys exactly
`domain,root_token,identity_policy,control_relative_path,
destination_relative_path,tool_files`;
domain is exactly `stage2-backup-darwin-fixture-v1`; `root_token` is exactly
`${STAGE2_AC17_PRIVATE_ROOT}`; `identity_policy` is exactly
`current_process_identity`. Both relative parent paths and each tool
relative path are 1..512 printable-ASCII bytes, normalized nonempty
slash-separated strings with no absolute prefix, backslash, empty, `.`, or
`..` component. Control and destination parents are component-disjoint:
neither is equal to or a component-prefix of the other. Every tool is strictly
beneath the control parent, cannot equal or contain either parent, and cannot
use a reserved marker, lock, marker-temp, tool-temp, publication, intent, or
destruction-receipt basename. `tool_files` has 1..16 entries in unique
relative-path byte order; no two tool paths are equal or component-prefix
related, and no tool path can equal another tool's derived staging-temp path.
Each entry has keys exactly
`relative_path,source,new_artifact`. `source` uses the section-12 artifact
entry schema, role `backup_tool/<three-decimal-index>/source`, and
`packaging_scope=evidence_only`; its SHA equals `new_artifact.sha256`.
`new_artifact` uses keys exactly
`sha256,mode,type,size,link_count`, requires `type=regular` and
`link_count="1"`, and uses the section-6.1 scalar bounds; UID/GID are
deliberately absent from the host-independent template.

Before creating a private root, the descriptor-bound acceptance supervisor
streams at most 4,097 entries from its attested temporary parent and retains
at most 65 names matching either
`.stage2-ac17-root-<uuid>-<64hex>` or
`.stage2-ac17-root-intent-<64hex>.json` or
`.stage2-ac17-root-intent-<64hex>.json.tmp` or
`.stage2-ac17-root-destruction-journal-<64hex>.json` or
`.stage2-ac17-root-destruction-journal-<64hex>.json.tmp`; the 4,097th total or
65th match refuses. A prefix-bearing malformed name also refuses. It
classifies every exact prior intent/journal prefix before choosing new IDs.
Only a trusted `setup_replay` coordinate may reconcile a journal-less
deterministic pre-fixture prefix and then run recovery twice before a fresh
transaction. On ordinary startup, root/intent state without complete
canonical initial-journal bytes is the exact `prejournal_fail_closed`
preserve/refuse state. A complete legal journal candidate may be repaired;
an exact final journal may be resumed. No cleanup entry, root, or intent is
removed before that journal is durable and reopened. A missing cleanup manifest, unsafe root
metadata, unlisted entry, hash/path mismatch, alternate intent, or unbound root
is preserved and refuses. One exact existing journal is resumed only under
that same journal-bound protocol. Every resumable branch runs recovery twice
and requires zero global root/intent/journal matches.

The supervisor chooses a unique lowercase RFC4122 root ID and 64-hex nonce and
expands `${STAGE2_AC17_PRIVATE_ROOT}` to the canonical absent path
`.stage2-ac17-root-<uuid>-<nonce>` only at a whole-component boundary. Before
that path exists it computes in memory canonical
`stage2-backup-darwin-expanded-v1` bytes
with keys exactly
`domain,template_sha256,root_plan,control_parent,destination_parent,lock_file,
markers,tool_files`; domain is exact. `root_plan`, `control_parent`, and
`destination_parent` each have keys exactly `path,uid,gid,mode,type`; every
UID/GID equals the attested current process identity, every type is
`directory`, every mode is `"0700"`, and paths are the exact component-safe
template expansions. These records freeze required first-visible metadata;
they do not falsely claim a pre-create inode. `lock_file` has keys exactly
`path,uid,gid,mode,type,size,link_count`; its exact destination child requires
mode `"0600"`, type `regular`, size `"0"`, and link count `"1"`. `markers`
has exactly `bootstrap_clean,bootstrap_b27,provisioned` records in that order,
each with keys `role,path,uid,gid,mode,type`, exact control-parent basenames,
mode `"0600"`, and type `regular`.

Each expanded tool record has keys exactly `path,source,new_artifact`, is a
one-to-one whole-component expansion of its template entry, uses the same
source/artifact bytes, and remains beneath the control parent. Expanded
`new_artifact` has keys exactly
`sha256,uid,gid,mode,type,size,link_count`; UID/GID equal the attested current
identity and no entry may request another identity. The canonical expanded
manifest hash is the disposable provisioning intent's
`tool_transition_manifest_sha256`, and the template hash is that intent's
`admission_manifest_sha256`; neither blob is written yet. For any later blob
hash `H`, the only temp and final paths are
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/qa/stage2/runs/<package_run_id>/platforms/darwin/blobs/.H.tmp`
and the sibling `H`. The current-identity supervisor uses the exact global
section-12 evidence-blob publication/recovery protocol, including serialized
candidate ownership, all four legal name states, same-inode link-count-two
pair recovery, unconditional post-reconciliation parent fsync, and final
read-only revalidation. No AC17-specific fallback or alternate blob name is
admitted.

After the expanded hash fixes the complete canonical provisioning-intent bytes
and every deterministic scenario name, the supervisor computes canonical
`stage2-ac17-cleanup-manifest-v1` bytes with keys exactly
`domain,expanded_manifest_sha256,provisioning_intent_sha256,entries`.
`provisioning_intent_sha256` hashes the fully computed canonical provisioning
intent and can never name the later root intent. Its 1..8,192 role-free
entries have keys exactly
`path,kind,action,required_prestate,required_end_state` and contain every path
the run may create beneath or equal the planned root—including the 4,097
sentinel entries, marker/tool temps, markers, tools, lock, destination
publications/residue, control/destination parents, and root—exactly once in
strict leaf-first processing order. Durable evidence blobs and the external
root-intent names are outside this cleanup-target set and use their own exact
protocols.
`kind=regular|directory`;
`action=unlink_if_present|rmdir_if_empty|verify_absent`;
`required_prestate=present|absent|present_or_absent`; and
`required_end_state=absent`. The generator proves the bound before any child.
`unlink_if_present` and `rmdir_if_empty` require
`required_prestate=present_or_absent`; `verify_absent` requires
`required_prestate=absent`. Thus an already-processed prefix remains legal
after supervisor death. Every entry is beneath or equals the planned root, the
root is last, and no operation may create an unlisted name. At this point the
expanded, provisioning-intent, cleanup, and root-intent bytes and hashes are
complete in memory, but no root-specific evidence blob or private-root inode
exists.

The supervisor next publishes a canonical `stage2-ac17-root-intent-v1`
outside the absent root. Its keys are exactly
`domain,shared_run_binding_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,
platform_descriptor_sha256,template_sha256,expanded_manifest_sha256,
cleanup_manifest_sha256,root_basename,uid,gid,mode`; the federation fields
equal the exact reopened Darwin platform context, all hashes and current
identity are exact, and mode is `"0700"`. The final basename is
`.stage2-ac17-root-intent-<sha256(intent-bytes)>.json` and its only staging
basename is the same string plus `.tmp`. The current-identity supervisor uses
`umask 0177` and requested mode `0600`; temp and final are ordinary
current-UID/GID mode-`0600` files with expected link count under the exact
first-visible-final-metadata temp/write/file-fsync/read-only-verify/
no-replace-link/parent-fsync/temp-unlink/parent-fsync protocol. The same
canonical bytes and hashes let recovery deterministically regenerate every
missing root-specific blob from the checked-in template, shared and
aggregation bindings, selected Darwin descriptor, root basename, and exact
generators without consulting an ambient path.

Only after the external root-intent final is durable and reopened does the
supervisor durably publish and reopen, in order, roles
`ac17/expanded_manifest`, `ac17/provisioning_intent`,
`ac17/cleanup_manifest`, and `ac17/root_intent`
under the exact section-12 evidence-blob protocol. Within the live transaction,
publication failure may retry only the exact current bytes before any root
mutation. After supervisor death, a crash after intent publication but before
all four finals may be regenerated/completed only by the outer harness's
trusted `setup_replay` coordinate: it regenerates byte-identical bytes, checks
the intent hashes, completes only the missing exact blobs, performs the
journal-authorized cleanup and two recovery passes, and then uses a fresh
transaction. Ordinary startup preserves every journal-less intent/blob prefix
and returns `prejournal_fail_closed`; it never regenerates or completes a
missing blob from ambient residue. The provisioning-intent blob hash must
equal the cleanup manifest's `provisioning_intent_sha256`. A root-specific blob final without the exact
external intent or its journal/receipt-bound recovery authority is invalid
orphan evidence and fails preflight; this ordering therefore leaves no
unrecoverable pre-intent blob prefix. Only the durable external intent plus
all four reopened blob finals authorizes one `O_EXCL`/no-replacement root
`mkdir` with exact `umask 0077` and requested mode `0700`. If `mkdir`
returns success, the supervisor immediately opens the exact new directory,
requires exact path/descriptor identity, and binds its device/inode before
admitting any receipt-capable phase. Identity-proof failure preserves and
refuses with no journal, receipt, evidence, or PASS. Only after identity is
bound does it freeze `reached_phase=root_created_unverified`; it then
performs the root-parent fsync and repeats the identity proof. Parent-fsync
failure retains the bound unverified tuple for journal-authorized cleanup;
post-fsync identity failure preserves and refuses with no receipt. Only both
successes advance in memory to `reached_phase=root_created`. The control
parent is then created the same way.
A control-parent `mkdir` failure that created no name remains at
`root_created`. After a successful control-parent `mkdir`, the supervisor
immediately opens it and requires exact path/descriptor identity before
admitting any receipt-capable phase. Identity-proof failure preserves and
refuses with no journal, receipt, evidence, or PASS. Only after identity is
bound does it freeze `control_parent_created_unverified`, device, and inode;
it then fsyncs the containing parent and repeats the identity proof. Only
their success advances to `control_parent_created`; parent-fsync failure
retains the bound unverified tuple for journal-authorized cleanup. Thus expanded/cleanup plans and durable recovery
authority exist before the first private-root mutation.

The disposable route publishes the canonical clean bootstrap/provisioned
intent beneath its private control parent, requires the B27 marker and every
unexpected marker/tool temp absent, permits absent-to-new tool prefixes, and
never names or touches `/opt/brain`, either `/run/brain-release*.lock`, or a
production B27 state. It executes the complete scrub, publication, lock, and
operation-matrix proof under the exact expanded plan.

For every outcome, including compiler or blob failure before any cleanup
manifest or root exists, the supervisor first freezes the exact
reached-phase/nullability shape. After normal tests or any child failure it
drains descendants; when a cleanup manifest exists, it then makes one
nonmutating pass over the frozen leaf-first entries, validates every required
prestate, and freezes the exact number of present entries. Before the first
`unlink` or `rmdir`—or immediately for a no-cleanup shape—it publishes
canonical `stage2-ac17-root-destruction-journal-v1` bytes with keys exactly
`domain,phase,journal_id,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,outcome,
termination_reason,reached_phase,template_sha256,expanded_manifest_sha256,
cleanup_manifest_sha256,root_intent_sha256,root_state,root_device,root_inode,
control_parent_device,control_parent_inode,initial_present_entry_count,
processed_entry_count,root_remove_result,
parent_fsync_result,post_lstat_errno,intent_unlink_result,
post_scan_entry_count,post_scan_match_count,descendant_count,
cleanup_started_at,finished_at`. `journal_id` is a fresh
64-lowercase-hex content-free nonce; final and only temp basenames are exactly
`.stage2-ac17-root-destruction-journal-<journal_id>.json` and that basename
plus `.tmp`. Both are ordinary current-UID/GID, mode-`0600`,
link-count-one files created with `umask 0177` and no symlink.

Initial journal `phase=destruction_armed`. It freezes every phase-reached hash,
root and control-parent identity/nullability facts, exact initial-present count when a cleanup
manifest exists, already-zero descendant count, and truthful UTC-millisecond
`cleanup_started_at`. Processed/result/post-scan fields and `finished_at` are
null. It uses the exact temp/O_EXCL/write/file-fsync/read-only-reverify/
no-replace-link/parent-fsync/temp-unlink/parent-fsync protocol. Only the
durable reopened journal authorizes cleanup mutation. The supervisor then
revalidates the exact journal-bound root device/inode before any cleanup
entry equal to or beneath that root and revalidates the exact journal-bound
control-parent device/inode before its mandatory cleanup entry whenever
those fields are nonnull, processes every
cleanup entry idempotently, fsyncs every containing directory,
removes the root, fsyncs the attested temporary parent, proves root
`lstat=ENOENT`, unlinks the exact root intent, fsyncs the parent, and performs
a bounded scan permitting exactly this journal and no root, intent, other
journal, or temp match.

After cleanup, the supervisor advances the same journal to
`phase=cleanup_complete`, preserving every frozen field, filling the exact
processed/results/post-scan fields, and setting `finished_at` to the actual
UTC-millisecond completion time, not earlier than `cleanup_started_at`. The
advance uses the exact journal `.json.tmp`, `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, complete
write/file-fsync/read-only verification, armed-final reread, atomic rename
over that exact final, and parent fsync. An armed final plus a complete legal
successor temp resumes idempotent cleanup before the rename; a completed final
plus an identical temp removes/fsyncs the temp. Changed frozen fields, phase
regression, unsafe metadata, or any alternate journal preserves and refuses.
The completed bytes are then durably stored and reopened under role
`ac17/root_destruction_journal` using the evidence-blob protocol.

Canonical `stage2-ac17-root-destruction-receipt-v2` has keys exactly
`domain,outcome,termination_reason,reached_phase,template_sha256,
expanded_manifest_sha256,cleanup_manifest_sha256,root_intent_sha256,
root_destruction_journal_sha256,root_state,root_device,root_inode,
control_parent_device,control_parent_inode,initial_present_entry_count,
processed_entry_count,root_remove_result,
parent_fsync_result,post_lstat_errno,intent_unlink_result,
post_scan_entry_count,post_scan_match_count,descendant_count,
cleanup_started_at,finished_at`. All fields except the completed-journal hash
copy byte-for-byte from that reopened journal. The journal contains no receipt
or binary-manifest hash, so hashing is acyclic. Outcome is `success|failure`;
`termination_reason` is exactly
`success|compiler_failure|expanded_manifest_failure|cleanup_manifest_failure|
intent_publication_failure|expanded_manifest_blob_failure|
provisioning_intent_blob_failure|cleanup_manifest_blob_failure|
root_intent_blob_failure|root_creation_failure|
control_parent_creation_failure|child_failure|timeout|supervisor_signal`.
`success` requires `outcome=success`,
`reached_phase=fixture_started`, and the exact created-root/full-cleanup tuple
below; every other reason requires `outcome=failure`. `reached_phase` is exactly
`template_only|expanded_computed|cleanup_computed|intent_published|
expanded_persisted|provisioning_intent_persisted|cleanup_persisted|
root_intent_persisted|root_created_unverified|root_created|
control_parent_created_unverified|control_parent_created|fixture_started`.
Template hash is always nonnull; expanded, cleanup, and intent hashes become
nonnull exactly at `expanded_computed`, `cleanup_computed`, and
`intent_published`, respectively, and remain so.
Compiler/expanded-computation failure pairs with `template_only`;
cleanup-computation failure with `expanded_computed`; intent-publication
failure with `cleanup_computed`; expanded, provisioning, cleanup, and
root-intent blob failures respectively with `intent_published`,
`expanded_persisted`, `provisioning_intent_persisted`, and
`cleanup_persisted`; root-creation failure requires
`root_intent_persisted|root_created_unverified`, where the former means the
no-replace `mkdir` created no root and the latter means it created the exact
identity-bound root but its parent fsync failed; identity-proof failure before
or after that fsync preserves/refuses with no receipt;
`control_parent_creation_failure` requires
`root_created|control_parent_created_unverified`, where the former means its
`mkdir` created no control parent and the latter means the exact parent was
identity-bound but its containing-parent fsync failed; identity-proof failure
before the unverified phase preserves/refuses with no receipt. Child
failure requires `control_parent_created|fixture_started`; and a handled
timeout or signal preserves the exact last phase reached while the supervisor
remains alive. A hard-death pre-journal coordinate is governed separately
below and creates no receipt.

`root_state=not_planned|not_created|created`. `template_only` requires
`not_planned`; `expanded_computed|cleanup_computed|intent_published|
expanded_persisted|provisioning_intent_persisted|cleanup_persisted|
root_intent_persisted` require `not_created`; and
`root_created_unverified|root_created|control_parent_created_unverified|
control_parent_created|fixture_started` require `created`.
Device/inode are nonnull canonical uint64 decimal strings exactly with
`created` and null otherwise. Control-parent device/inode are nonnull canonical
uint64 decimal strings exactly at
`control_parent_created_unverified|control_parent_created|fixture_started`
and null at every earlier phase; cleanup revalidates that exact identity before
its mandatory entry. `initial_present_entry_count` is null at
`template_only|expanded_computed`, exactly `"0"` from `cleanup_computed`
through `root_intent_persisted`, exactly `"1"` at
`root_created_unverified|root_created`, exactly `"2"` at
`control_parent_created_unverified|control_parent_created`, and a canonical
uint64 decimal string in `2..E` at `fixture_started`, where `E` is the
cleanup-entry count and root/control parent are mandatory distinct entries.
Processed count is `"0"` when cleanup
hash is null and otherwise equals the exact cleanup-entry count.

`root_remove_result`, `parent_fsync_result`, and `intent_unlink_result` are
`not_needed|ok`. Root removal is `ok` exactly at
`root_created_unverified|root_created|control_parent_created_unverified|
control_parent_created|fixture_started` and `not_needed` otherwise; intent
unlink is `ok` exactly at or after `intent_published`; parent fsync is `ok`
exactly when either operation is `ok` and `not_needed` otherwise.
`post_lstat_errno` is null with `not_planned` and `ENOENT` otherwise.
Post-scan count is a canonical uint64 decimal string in
`1..4096`; descendant count is `"0"`; and `post_scan_match_count` is
explicitly the unexpected-match count after excluding the one current
journal, so it is `"0"` while that journal remains included in the entry
count. Both times are UTC RFC3339 with millisecond precision. A zero
post-scan entry count is an explicit rejection vector because the current
journal remains counted. Thus a pre-root
compiler, blob, or intent failure has one valid receipt shape without
inventing an inode or successful removal. The sole success tuple additionally
requires initial-present count in `2..E`, processed count exactly `E`, root
removal, parent fsync, and intent unlink all `ok`,
`post_lstat_errno=ENOENT`, and descendant and unexpected-match counts both
`"0"`.

Before publishing receipt hash `H`, whose exact bytes are at most 65,536, the
supervisor applies the global four-state evidence-blob classifier to only
final `H` and candidate `.H.tmp`. The receipt-specific reconcile operation
verifies the candidate absent, removes one safe candidate-only prefix, or
validates/file-and-parent-fsyncs the complete same-inode link-count-two pair
and removes only its candidate. A different-inode pair, extra link, unsafe
metadata, oversize/nonprefix byte, or other receipt-like name preserves and
refuses. Reconcile-or-verify-absent and an unconditional blob-parent fsync are
separate ordered operations and crash coordinates; the latter runs whether
or not this invocation performed the unlink. It then freshly revalidates the
exact state-4 final or publishes state 1 through the global protocol.
The receipt is then persisted as role `ac17/root_destruction_receipt` under
the exact evidence-blob protocol. The external journal remains until receipt
final and blob parent are durable; it is unlinked last, its parent fsynced,
and a final 4,096/4,097 scan requires zero root, intent, journal, or temp
matches.

The acceptance supervisor owns the root, root intent, journal, and cleanup
plan outside the killable fixture process group. Partial setup, compiler
failure, child nonzero, timeout, injected controller/worker/launcher death,
and normal completion enter this bounded state machine only while the
supervisor remains alive or complete canonical initial-journal bytes exist.
Every reviewed
negative case must end with root and root intent absent before its expected
nonzero result, except the exact hard-death fail-closed coordinates whose
private sandbox is disposed only by the outer harness. If the supervisor
itself dies after complete journal bytes exist, publication repair or an
armed journal replays only the exact idempotent remainder and a completed
journal reconstructs the exact receipt before any new run. Earlier hard death
creates no receipt and preserves. Identity or cleanup failure emits no
PASS/evidence and preserves the suspect state for inspection. Only after the wrapper
independently validates the cleanup manifest, journal, receipt, final zero
scan, and descendant absence may it finalize AC17 artifacts or forward PASS.

One reviewed controller owns the opened lock description. The acquisition
helper may inherit that descriptor only to call `flock(2)`; `flock --close`,
path-reopening command mode, an independently opened description, and any
unreviewed duplicate are forbidden. `LOCK_UN` is forbidden on every reference
from successful acquisition through final release; release occurs only by
closing references. The controller creates one reviewed, descendant-tracked
mutating process group and retains its descriptor throughout the critical
section. Every process capable of persistent mutation inherits that same
open-file description before it can mutate and must retain its reference until
it can no longer mutate. Every unrelated child receives the descriptor closed
or close-on-exec. Daemonization, double-fork escape, unreviewed exec, closing a
holder before its mutation-capable descendants have exited, and mutation by a
nonholder are forbidden. The descriptor-bound descendant-control adapter
tracks, waits for, and if necessary terminates and drains the complete
mutating process group before the controller closes its reference. If the
controller dies while any worker or grandchild lives, each still-capable
mutator's inherited reference retains exclusion until that complete tree
exits. If a worker dies first, the controller retains exclusion through
recovery and cleanup. If both controller and worker die while a mutating
grandchild remains, that grandchild's inherited reference still blocks
reacquisition until its last close. The kernel releases the lock only when the
last reference to that locked open-file description closes; there is no PID,
token, lease, age, stale-owner, or PID-reuse cleanup decision.

Every publisher, backup listing, prune, restore, startup-recovery entry point,
and backup-tool installer holds that exact descriptor lock across recovery,
its complete operation, ordered cleanup, and descendant drain. The canonical
production publication owner/group is always `brain:brain-data`, independent
of the entry-point EUID. A root publisher keeps the lock in its controller and
delegates persistent namespace mutation to the reviewed
`brain:brain-data` worker, passing the exact already-open source-candidate and
lock descriptions; it never creates root-owned publication residue. A root
restore or installer validates and may recover `brain:brain-data` residue
while retaining the same lock. Disposable fixtures use their declared current
UID/GID.

Two publishers serialize. Lock acquisition or pre-mutation current
path/descriptor/ancestor identity, symlink, ownership, mode, size, link-count,
platform-adapter, or inheritance failure refuses without publication,
recovery, listing, pruning, restore, or tool-install mutation. A descendant-
drain failure after mutation withholds success, retains the controller's lock
reference, blocks all competing consumers, and invokes the exact reviewed
terminate/drain path; it does not falsely claim that prior mutation did not
occur. The pre/post identity proof detects replacement before or during
acquisition; a completed same-metadata offline replacement while no repository
holder exists is an out-of-protocol host-integrity event and is not claimed
detectable without protected external inode attestation. Tests cover exact
fresh/B27 admission and marker states; concurrent and interrupted parent/lock
bootstrap, acquisition, lock-file/parent fsync, durable tool transition, and
marker completion; two concurrent publishers; controller-only and worker-only
death; a live worker after controller death; controller-plus-worker death with
a live mutating grandchild; an unrelated leaked-descriptor descendant;
explicit `LOCK_UN` refusal; daemon/double-fork and nonholder-mutation refusal;
drain failure after mutation; whole-tree death and last-close release;
PID-reuse irrelevance; acquisition-time path/inode replacement;
symlink/mode/owner/size/link-count/ancestor drift; the split Linux AC13 and
Darwin AC17 adapters; `brain`-owned crash residue recovered by root restore
and installer; a root entry point producing only `brain:brain-data` residue
that a later `brain` publisher recovers; direct root-owned-residue refusal;
and exclusion of listing, pruning, restore, recovery, and installer work.

While holding the lock, recovery performs a two-phase bounded scan. Phase one
uses streaming directory reads to inspect at most 4,097 total
destination-parent entries and at most 65 names with the owned hidden-
publication prefix, retaining the exact names and identity/metadata records
for at most 64 valid owned directories. It completes that full sentinel scan
and validates every retained entry before any cleanup or new-publication
mutation. The 4,097th total entry, 65th matching name, or any late malformed,
unowned, symlinked, wrong-mode, cross-device, identity-drifted, or otherwise
invalid entry refuses with every name and identity unchanged. Only after phase
one accepts may phase two process at most the retained 64 directories. Thus
4,096 total and 64 matching entries are accepted bounds whose `+1` cases are
observed but never processed.

After the scrub transaction, bare VACUUM, zero-payload check, exact zero
`item_artifact_cleanup_jobs` and `item_delete_permits` rows for S28, exact physical-sanitization
validator PASS, `quick_check`, zero foreign-key violations, candidate close,
and proof that no `-wal`,
`-shm`, or `-journal` sidecar exists, the controller `lstat`s the exact
candidate path inside the attested private stage. It freezes device, inode,
size, UID, GID, mode, and link count; requires the stage-attested expected
owner/group/mode, an ordinary nonsymlink regular file, and link count one; then
opens that same path read-write with `O_NOFOLLOW`. `fstat` must equal the
frozen path identity and metadata. The controller fsyncs that descriptor,
repeats path/descriptor identity validation, and keeps the same descriptor
open through the copy. A symlink, path substitution, nonregular file, hard
link, wrong owner/mode, or device/inode/size drift refuses before any hidden
file is created. Negative evidence performs every such replacement between
close, `lstat`, open, fsync, and copy.

Only after those checks does the publisher create one private hidden directory
at the run-intent's exact deterministic basename, which matches
`^\.ai-brain-sanitized-backup-v1-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$`, no replacement, expected
owner/group (`brain:brain-data` in production), and the same filesystem device
as the destination parent. Any other nonce or basename, even one matching the
grammar, refuses. The worker uses exact `umask 0077` and requested
mode `0700`. On the production Linux and AC13 mode-`2770` parent, setgid
inheritance intentionally makes the first visible hidden directory mode
`2700`; on the declared non-setgid disposable AC17 parent it is mode `0700`.
Those are the only environment-specific expected hidden modes. No post-create
`chown`/`chmod` repair is permitted. The publisher immediately fsyncs the
destination parent and revalidates the parent and hidden-directory identities
and metadata before copying a candidate.

The persistent worker copies bytes only from that already-open source
descriptor—never by reopening the staging path—through an
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` descriptor to hidden `sanitized.sqlite`, expected
publication owner/group, requested mode `0600`, under the same worker's exact
`umask 0077`. A root controller passes that exact source descriptor to its
`brain:brain-data` worker. The newly visible candidate must already have exact
final metadata; no `chown`/`chmod` repair is permitted. After copy, the source
descriptor must still match the frozen identity before close. The publisher
computes the hidden file's exact SHA-256, size, device, and inode; requires
link count one; fsyncs the file and hidden directory; and opens that hidden
file genuinely read-only to reverify the exact hash/size, zero forbidden
payloads, exact zero cleanup-outbox and transient-permit rows for S28,
`quick_check='ok'`, and zero
foreign-key violations.

Only then may it create hidden `intent.json` with
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, expected publication owner/group, mode `0600`,
and the same exact worker `umask 0077`, with no post-create metadata repair;
write and fsync the record; and fsync the hidden directory. Until both fsyncs
complete, a visible empty or partial intent grants no link or final-path
authority and is handled only by the pre-link recovery branch below. Complete
intent bytes are exact compact UTF-8 JSON with one trailing LF and keys in this
order:
`domain,version,final_basename,candidate_sha256,candidate_size,
candidate_device,candidate_inode`. `domain` is exactly
`sanitized-backup-publication-intent-v1`, `version` is integer `1`,
`final_basename` is a fatal-roundtripping UTF-8 basename that matches
`^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}_[0-9]{6}_[0-9]{3}_[a-f0-9]{12}\.sqlite$`,
contains no path separator, and is neither `.` nor `..`; the hash is 64
lowercase hexadecimal, and size/device/inode are canonical unsigned-decimal
strings in `0..18446744073709551615`. The complete record is at most 334 bytes
including its trailing LF; the parser reads at most 335 bytes and treats a
335th byte as invalid without reading further. It contains no absolute path,
title, URL, body, payload, or other content. Because an absent final is never
relinked during recovery, the intent binds only that final basename and the
hidden candidate identity; it is not claimed to bind the hidden-directory
nonce or parent identity and grants no authority to republish.

Publication is one same-filesystem no-replace hard link from hidden
`sanitized.sqlite` to the requested final basename. The final and hidden names
must then identify the same regular-file device/inode and expected size, with
link count exactly two at both names. The publisher fsyncs the final file,
opens it genuinely read-only and reverifies the exact hash/size, zero
forbidden payloads, exact zero cleanup-outbox and transient-permit rows for S28,
`quick_check='ok'`, and zero foreign-key violations, then
fsyncs the destination parent. Only after all of those steps is publication
complete. Cleanup then unlinks hidden `sanitized.sqlite`, requires the final
to retain the same identity with link count exactly one, fsyncs the hidden directory,
unlinks `intent.json` last, fsyncs the hidden directory again, removes that
now-empty hidden directory, and fsyncs the destination parent. Removing the
intent before final verification and parent fsync is forbidden.

Before any new publication and before backup listing, pruning, or restore may
proceed, recovery repeats the same streaming 4,096-total/64-matching bounded
scan while holding the same opened-descriptor `flock`. Namespace access uses
the frozen Node path-based protocol, not `openat`, `linkat`, `unlinkat`, or a
directory-FD-relative child path. It retains an opened destination-parent
descriptor only for identity comparison and fsync, constructs each child from
the already-validated canonical parent string plus one validated basename,
and before and after every path-based `lstat`, `open`, `link`, `unlink`, or
`rmdir` repeats the complete ancestor/parent and affected-component
device/inode/type/UID/GID/mode/link-count proof; after a removal, the required
component result is exact absence plus the declared retained-link state
instead of a nonexistent identity. Every opened file uses `O_NOFOLLOW` where
available and must `fstat`-match its immediately preceding path proof. A
mismatch refuses or preserves according to the branch below; Stage 2 does not
claim resistance to an external host actor racing the gap between those path
operations.

Before any completed S28 final may enter backup listing, pruning selection, or
restore, its genuinely read-only validator independently reproves exact zero
`item_artifact_cleanup_jobs` and `item_delete_permits` rows, the exact two
tombstone counts with checked combined value at most 65,536, and the
package-bound 4,096-byte page profile, page count at most 262,144, maximum
b-tree depth, file-size equality, and restore-cache formula above. Restore
repeats every proof after copy and before exposing the restored database.
These checks do not enumerate, join, or expose tombstones in backup catalog
output.

A supported restore first authenticates the immutable backup package,
descriptor, closed-file hash, physical-sanitization result, source
five-field authority marker, and source active-authority-record hash. It
resolves the destination through the descriptor-bound
`authority_store_locator` and requires the package marker's
`authority_logical_store_id` to equal that selected logical store. The
service must find the package's exact source active-record bytes/hash in that
same store's retained predecessor chain and cross-equal its generation/event/
epoch/origin tuple to the package marker. A valid package from another store,
an unretained/invented source record, or a marker/record mismatch refuses
before reservation or copy even if every database page and package MAC is
otherwise valid.

The service then performs a create-once compare-and-reserve against the exact
current revision-3 active-record hash. It allocates `N+1`, a fresh
32-CSPRNG-byte lowercase-hexadecimal authority event ID and
`authority_restore_epoch`, and constructs authenticated compact ordered no-LF
JSON `stage2-backup-restore-reservation-v1` bytes, at most 4,096 bytes, with
keys exactly
`domain,authority_store_locator,logical_store_id,
expected_predecessor_active_record_sha256,restore_generation,
authority_event_id,authority_restore_epoch,source_package_sha256,
source_authority_record_sha256,source_authority_marker_sha256,
schema_manifest_sha256,active_database_basename,candidate_basename,
target_state,authentication_algorithm,authentication_key_id,authenticator`.
The candidate basename is exactly
`.stage2-active-candidate-<authority_event_id>.sqlite`; target state is
`replace_predecessor` when the active name identifies the exact current
predecessor or `restore_absent` when the active name and all its sidecars are
absent. The MAC uses the same logical-store key, ASCII domain
`stage2-backup-restore-reservation-authenticator-v1`, `0x00`, and section-7.5
frames for every prior field. The service validates all standard ID/hash/
uint64/basename grammars, the source-store chain proof, unit generation
increment, and the namespace attestation before durably storing the
reservation in its one nonrollbackable pending-restore slot. It returns only
after persistence; timeout is resolved by reread. At most one pending origin
or restore exists for the locator/store, identical replay is a reread, and a
different tuple conflicts. A pending reservation cannot be abandoned or
replaced by a later generation.

That pending service state closes every new active-database admission. The
coordinator retains an exclusive restore-publication barrier and uses one
monotonic 60,000-ms budget to quiesce every already-open item/read endpoint,
reader, writer, worker, request, checkpoint owner, and possibly-last-closing
handle. Equality is accepted; the first observation after equality records
`restore_admission_drain_timeout`, leaves the reservation durable, and starts
one exact 5,000-ms termination phase: stop listeners, cancel registered
requests/workers, call `sqlite3_interrupt` on every registered handle, and
require handle-close plus worker/request EOF. Equality is accepted. If those
proofs still fail, the supervisor terminates the old service process and must
observe process exit plus closure of every inherited endpoint/handle FD
before a recovery launcher may claim the barrier. Until that proof the
barrier is explicitly unavailable, an old in-flight endpoint may still be
terminating, and no candidate copy, revision 1, restore DML, or claim of
exclusive/no-endpoint state is permitted. For `replace_predecessor`, after
exclusive closure it performs FULL then TRUNCATE
with zero busy/frame results, closes the final handle, proves zero read marks/
handles, and applies the exact safe sidecar cleanup plus main/parent fsync and
identity reproof. For `restore_absent`, it proves the active name, WAL, SHM,
rollback journal, hot journal, and temp sidecars all absent before and after
the drain. A damaged or mismatching existing target is never treated as
absent and remains fenced/quarantine-only. Restart finds the pending
reservation through the stable locator, re-closes admissions, and resumes
this same drain; crash injection brackets reservation persistence, admission
closure, every drain observation, checkpoint, close, sidecar operation, and
fsync.

Only after the drain succeeds does the coordinator materialize the
authenticated package database directly at the reservation's exact
same-parent candidate basename. The destination is created with
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, active-database owner, mode 0600, parent device,
and link count one; bytes come only from the still-open/hash-verified
immutable package file. It fsyncs the complete candidate and active parent,
then genuinely read-only reopens/fstats/hashes the path and proves exact
package file length/hash, descriptor schema/profile, source marker,
path/descriptor device+inode identity, and absence of candidate sidecars.
Before revision 1, an absent candidate is recreated; a safe link-count-one
candidate with exact name/owner/mode/device, ordinary nonsymlink type, no
alias/sidecar/control/receipt/record, and size from zero through the exact
package length may be unlinked, parent-fsynced, and recreated from the
retained package whenever it does not pass the complete validator. This
includes a full-length hash-mismatching image left by a crash after the last
write but before file fsync. A complete valid candidate resumes in place.
Any extra link/name, sidecar, wrong metadata/device, overlength file,
target-state drift, service-state conflict, or missing package remains gated.
The
reservation and immutable package remain retained across every crash.

Only after that closed-candidate proof does the service atomically consume the
pending reservation by comparing the unchanged predecessor revision-3 hash
and publishing one authenticated
`stage2-active-database-authority-v1` record with keys exactly
`domain,logical_store_id,authority_event_id,restore_generation,
record_revision,authority_origin,authority_restore_epoch,
activation_database_sha256,database_device,database_inode,
schema_manifest_sha256,source_package_sha256,
predecessor_active_record_sha256,status,
authentication_algorithm,authentication_key_id,authenticator`; generation is
previous plus one, `record_revision=1`, the epoch and authority event ID have never
appeared, the database
identity/hash is that exact reserved candidate, origin is `backup_restore`,
source package and predecessor fields equal the reservation, and status is
exactly `restore_gated`. Its device/inode must remain unchanged through
tombstone disposition, DELETE-to-WAL conversion, revision 2, active-target
rename, and revision 3; only the two specified whole-file hashes change.
Before any restore-only mutation, the candidate requires exactly zero
`item_artifact_cleanup_jobs` and `item_delete_permits` rows; a nonempty permit
is never resumed or consumed and rejects the package as impossible
transaction residue. The exact two tombstone counts must equal the
