Create the transaction-transient command authority relation:

```text
item_delete_permits
permit_id                     TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
                              COLLATE BINARY, exactly 26 lowercase RFC4648
                              base32 characters with canonical final bits
commit_blocker                TEXT NOT NULL CHECK exact
                              stage2-item-delete-permit-must-be-consumed-v1
deletion_id                   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
                              exactly 43 base64url characters
item_id                       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
item_instance_id              TEXT NOT NULL exact 32 lowercase hexadecimal
command_blob                  TEXT NOT NULL, exact 1..1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes
vector_snapshot_count         INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative safe integer
vector_snapshot_sha256        TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
vector_purge_state            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK prepared|vectors_purged
vector_purged_count           INTEGER NULL nonnegative safe integer
vector_purge_receipt_sha256   TEXT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
created_at                    INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative database time
FOREIGN KEY (commit_blocker) REFERENCES item_delete_permits(permit_id)
  DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
```

Every `permit_id` is the canonical unpadded lowercase RFC4648 base32 encoding
of exactly 16 CSPRNG bytes; decode/re-encode equality and the final-bit rule
make it exactly 26 ASCII characters in `[a-z2-7]`. The BINARY primary key plus
that 26-byte CHECK makes it disjoint from the fixed 45-byte
`commit_blocker` sentinel. No row can therefore satisfy its deferred self-FK.
A permit may exist only inside the one dedicated deletion transaction. Its
initial `prepared` shape requires both purge-result fields null. The sole
allowed update is exact top-level `prepared -> vectors_purged` after the
native vector-purge proof; it sets `vector_purged_count` equal to
`vector_snapshot_count` and stores the expected receipt. The receipt is
SHA-256 under ASCII domain `stage2-item-vector-purge-receipt-v1` and
section-7.5 framing over permit ID, deletion ID, statement nonce, item ID,
item instance, canonical decimal snapshot/purged count, and snapshot digest.
The later command trigger must retain and prove the marked permit before
returning; the immediately next `outbox_commit_dml` proof trigger must delete
it before that statement returns. Any early deletion or surviving permit
makes the phase or COMMIT fail under pinned `foreign_keys=ON`, independently
of host cleanup.

Direct generic insert/read/update/delete, REPLACE, UPSERT, and trigger access
are denied by the native authorizer. The only top-level permit writes are the
one exact insert under `permit_insert` and the one exact
`prepared -> vectors_purged` mark under `permit_mark`; the command-view and
`items` triggers may only read the matching proven permit under their frozen
source names, and only the `outbox_commit_dml` built-in proof trigger may
delete it. Every other update/delete is rejected, and pre-conflict guards
prevent victim replacement.
The exact self-FK acceptance negative uses the same supported SQLite build and
a fresh disposable database containing the byte-identical generated S28
schema before any product handle is published. The evidence harness begins
one immediate transaction, inserts one otherwise valid permit directly,
attempts COMMIT, requires `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY`, executes and verifies
explicit ROLLBACK, and proves the permit count is zero. That pre-publication
evidence route is not present in the production binary, connection-role set,
or authorizer trace and grants no application bypass.
The pinned-runtime staged-purge feasibility variant inserts the same
impossible prepared permit, performs the exact bounded sequence of fresh
per-row top-level vec0 deletes under `trusted_schema=OFF`, attempts early
COMMIT, requires
`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY` with the transaction still open, explicitly
rolls back, and proves both the vector and ordinary graph byte-semantically
restored and the permit absent.

Create the main-schema zero-row view
`item_delete_commands(command_blob)` as one typed-null projection under
`WHERE 0`. It has exactly one `INSTEAD OF INSERT` trigger and no update/delete
route. `command_blob` is exact compact no-LF canonical JSON with a top-level
array `[domain,permit_id,deletion_header,tombstone_map]`; `domain` is
`stage2-item-delete-command-v1`, `permit_id` is the fresh ID above,
`deletion_header` is the descriptor-frozen positional array containing every
permit-bound detailed-request, cleanup-outbox, item/instance/revision,
manifest/vector/snapshot, authority, clock, count, and hash scalar. It
contains the exact `manifest_json` TEXT value once and no second
variable-size blob. `tombstone_map` is an array of 0..1,024 entries. Each
entry is an exact
nine-TEXT-value positional array in this order:

```text
request_class_domain
caller_request_id
authority_expires_at canonical decimal
authority_restore_epoch
canonical_request_commitment
terminal_code exactly item_deleted
deleted_at canonical decimal
block_until canonical decimal
request_authenticator
```

The only variable-size semantic envelope is this one `command_blob`; the
permit insert/mark bind only descriptor-fixed scalar projections of those
same decoded bytes. Its maximum is closed arithmetically before deletion can
be admitted:

- raw compact `manifest_json` is at most 262,144 UTF-8 bytes;
- canonical `JSON.stringify(deletion_header)` with that one manifest value
  replaced by the empty JSON string is at most 65,536 UTF-8 bytes;
- embedding any valid compact JSON manifest of `M` bytes as that JSON string
  adds at most `2*M` bytes over the empty-string form, because only existing
  quote and backslash bytes acquire one additional escape byte. Therefore the
  complete header is at most
  `65,536 + 2*262,144 = 589,824` bytes;
- the longest request-class domain is the 36-byte
  `capture-artifact-request-manifest-v1`; the other eight values are bounded
  at 43, 16, 64, 64, 12, 16, 16, and 64 ASCII bytes. With eighteen quote
  bytes, eight commas, and two brackets, one map entry is at most 359 bytes.
  The maximum 1,024-entry map is therefore exactly bounded by
  `2 + 1,023 + 1,024*359 = 368,641` bytes; and
- the top-level wrapper outside the already-counted header and map is exactly
  64 bytes: 31 for the quoted 29-byte domain, 28 for the quoted 26-byte permit
  ID, two brackets, and three commas. Thus every worst-case command is at most
  `64 + 589,824 + 368,641 = 958,529` bytes, leaving 90,047 bytes below the
  1,048,576-byte transport cap.

The host independently constructs and measures the raw manifest, empty-
manifest header, full header, map, and final command and refuses any
individual bound or formula mismatch before command DML. The SQL trigger
independently enforces the raw-manifest, header, map-entry/map-count, and total
byte bounds after the outer storage-class/total-byte gate. Equality at every
declared bound passes and each `+1`, escape-expansion, maximum-map plus
maximum-manifest, and maximum-nonmanifest-header vector refuses before the
inner root delete. Future artifact admission and migration preflight use the
same 262,144-byte raw-manifest and header-envelope projection, so the accepted
tree cannot later become undeletable solely because this transport is too
small.

The map is unsigned-byte ordered and unique by
`(request_class_domain,caller_request_id)`. The host fatal-parses and
byte-reencodes the complete value before binding it. The SQL trigger
first requires SQLite storage class TEXT and the byte cap before any JSON
parse, then independently requires strict `json_valid(X,1)`, exact compact
`json(X)` equality, exact top/header/entry fixed arities and JSON types, ASCII
canonical domains/hashes/IDs, canonical decimal integer strings, all field
grammars and checked clock arithmetic, map count `0..1024`, strict
unsigned-byte adjacent order, no duplicate typed key, exact per-class counts,
and relational equality in both directions using only built-in SQL and
`json_each`/`json_extract`. The selected SQLite source ID, JSON1 compile
profile, and canonicalization/error semantics are manifest-pinned and tested;
version drift refuses rather than silently reparsing.

The raw `command_blob` bytes and internal `permit_id` are deliberately
excluded from every request fingerprint, HMAC preimage, deletion component
hash, and durable identity comparison. Only the decoded typed values, the
independently frozen component hashes, and the relational two-way equality
authorize the step; no security decision compares two raw JSON encodings.
The blob is transaction-only transport and is never logged, exported,
returned, backed up, or retained after the command.

Before the command-view insert, the exact native-role route inserts the
`prepared` permit and performs the vector phase at top level because
sqlite-vec 0.1.9's `vec0` module is not
`SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS` and is unsafe from schema triggers under
`trusted_schema=OFF`. The frozen pre-proof bytewise-orders every exact
`(chunk_id,canonical-rowid)` pair for the item, requires the ordinary
`chunks`/`chunks_rowid` graph and joined `chunks_vec` presence to be two-way
complete for the target set: every target chunk has exactly one bridge, that
bridge's rowid has exactly one supported-dimension vec0 member, target chunk
IDs and rowids are unique, and no bridge for a target chunk is extra or
missing. It makes no unscoped claim about a virtual-table row that cannot be
attributed to this item. Each snapshot record is exactly the chunk ID's 24
lowercase-ASCII bytes followed by its positive signed-64 rowid encoded as
eight-byte unsigned big-endian, for exactly 32 bytes. The records are ordered
by unsigned chunk-ID bytes and then numeric rowid. The exact digest is
SHA-256 over ASCII `stage2-item-vector-snapshot-v1`, one `0x00`, the
section-7.5 unsigned-count frame, then the ordered fixed 32-byte records with
no per-record delimiter or alternate text encoding. Count zero hashes exactly
the domain, separator, and canonical zero-count frame with no record bytes.
The host preproof, native postproof, permit/command value, and fixtures use
that one preimage. Under `vector_purge_dml`, `N=0` executes no delete. For
`N>0`, the native role walks the frozen ordered snapshot and executes exactly
one fresh hard-coded no-tail
`DELETE FROM chunks_vec WHERE rowid=?` per canonical ordinal, binding only
that record's rowid. Each step returns `SQLITE_DONE` with
`sqlite3_changes64()=1` and is finalized before the next ordinal; no statement
is cached, reset, rebound, range-selected, or reached from schema SQL. The
role retains the running checked sum and next expected ordinal, and the
midpoint coordinate is executable immediately after the finalized
`ceil(N/2)` statement. Exact top-level post-proof requires the checked change
sum equal the frozen snapshot count, zero matching vec0 rows, unchanged
ordinary snapshot rows, and the same item/instance/command tuple. Only then
may `permit_mark` store the exact count/receipt and change
`prepared -> vectors_purged`.

The separate per-item vector-graph cap is `V_MAX=4,096`. For each item,
`chunks`, `chunks_rowid` bridges owned by those chunks, and corresponding
`chunks_vec` rowids must form one exact one-to-one set of 0..4,096 elements;
a missing member, duplicate target chunk/rowid, dimension/high-water anomaly,
class mismatch, or 4,097th element refuses. Independently, every S28
`chunks.id` must have SQLite storage class TEXT and be exactly 24 UTF-8 bytes,
all lowercase ASCII hexadecimal: the locked migration preflight requires
`typeof(id)='text'`, `length(id)=24`,
`length(CAST(id AS BLOB))=24`, and
`id NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*'` for every existing row before DDL or activation.
The generated S28 built-in `BEFORE INSERT ON chunks` guard repeats those four
predicates, and `BEFORE UPDATE OF id ON chunks` unconditionally refuses;
every future repository chunk creator generates exactly 12 CSPRNG bytes and
lowercase-hex encodes them before the guarded insert. Thus no post-migration
path can create a wider snapshot key.

Migration-028 locked preflight proves both the ID grammar and complete bounded
vector graph before DDL/activation. Every later chunk/vector admission holds
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, projects the resulting one-to-one set, and accepts equality
but rejects `V_MAX+1` or a malformed ID before any ordinary or virtual-table
DML. Deletion enumerates with `LIMIT 4097`, uses the same equality proof, and
stores only the exact count and ordered-set digest in the command/permit; its
maximum encoded snapshot is exactly `4,096*32=131,072` bytes. The bounded row
list remains mutable process memory and is zeroized after transaction
resolution. Descriptor cache arithmetic includes that exact 131,072-byte
record array, its same-size sort workspace, fixed digest state, and the
descriptor-bounded vec0/SQLite working pages; it contains no
maximum-width/unbounded TEXT term. Acceptance covers 0, 4,095, 4,096, and
4,097 rows; 24-byte equality plus 23/25-byte, uppercase, nonhex, BLOB, invalid
UTF-8, and update attempts; every target-set one-sided anomaly; and rollback
after the 4,096-statement bounded per-row top-level purge.

The command-view trigger never reads or writes `chunks_vec`. It requires
exactly one already-existing `vectors_purged` permit whose command bytes,
item/instance, vector count/hash/receipt, deletion ID, and statement nonce
equal the parsed header, then issues the exact inner
`DELETE FROM items WHERE id=<header item> AND
item_instance_id=<header instance>`. The descriptor has exactly one
`BEFORE DELETE ON items` authority trigger. It refuses
`delete_permit_missing` unless one permit row's globally unique
deletion ID and statement nonce byte-equal the complete command header and
current locked item; it proves the map and the locked detailed
source rows are two-way equal on every tuple field, inserts exactly one
detailed deletion request and prepared outbox, inserts caller tombstones with
two set-based `INSERT ... SELECT` joins through `json_each`, proves the
ordinary target chunk/bridge graph still has the permit-bound count, valid
24-byte IDs, unique target IDs/rowids, and exact one-to-one built-in
relational shape, and rereads every inserted shape while leaving that one
permit present through the cascade. SQL does not recompute or compare the
snapshot digest: exact digest/set equality is owned by the immediately prior
native `vector_postproof`, and the still-held writer lock plus closed role
machine permits only `permit_mark` then this command with no intervening
application statement. Back in the view trigger after the cascade, the
immediately checked inner-delete count is one; it proves the item and detailed
request absent, the exact marked permit still present, the outbox exact and
`prepared`, and the inserted tombstone set two-way equal to the map with exact
per-class and union counts. The command-view step then returns
`SQLITE_DONE` and is finalized.

Only the next `outbox_commit_dml` phase may run. Its one hard-coded guarded
UPDATE binds the same deletion ID, statement nonce, transaction clock, root
fingerprint, manifest hash, `state='prepared'`, and null `committed_at`; its
SET list is exactly `state='committed',committed_at=:transaction_clock`.
The exact built-in `AFTER UPDATE OF state ON item_artifact_cleanup_jobs`
proof trigger matches the retained permit, reproves the complete post-cascade
graph and two-way command-map/tombstone equality, deletes exactly that permit,
and proves the committed outbox plus zero-permit final shape. The update must
change one row, return `SQLITE_DONE`, and be finalized before COMMIT.
Any missing, extra, duplicate, altered, reordered, over-cap, parse, insert,
vector receipt/snapshot, cascade, outbox, or final-set mismatch raises inside
its guarded phase and rolls the entire transaction back, including
the earlier bounded per-row top-level vec0 deletes and permit writes.

During that item-delete command, the SQL-only authority trigger inserts exactly one
tombstone for every detailed extension or artifact caller request before those
rows cascade. `deleted_at` is the transaction's one database-clock value.
For each source request,
`block_until = max(authority_expires_at,deleted_at) + 300_000`, with checked
safe-integer arithmetic. While the tombstone exists, replay first looks up the
random `caller_request_id`: an exact authenticator returns only
`terminal_code='item_deleted'`; a mismatch returns
`caller_request_id_mismatch`; neither path reads an item or starts work.
Expiry cannot authorize new work.

For each item instance, `extension_capture_requests` may contain at most 1,024
live detailed caller rows, `item_artifact_write_requests` may independently
contain at most 1,024, and their combined set may contain at most 1,024. The
combined bound is still asserted explicitly rather than being inferred from
the two class bounds. Before migration 028 performs any DDL, its locked
preflight counts each class and the union for every existing item instance
and refuses the entire migration on a 1,025th class row, a 1,025th combined
row, an unreadable count, or a mismatched instance; the clean/S27 transition
expects exact zero because both classes are new, and any re-entry or
transition-gated preexisting staging relation must pass the same complete
per-item preflight before mutation or latch publication. Every later caller
admission, under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, counts the extension class, artifact
class, and union through their leading item/instance indexes. A new extension
row requires extension count `<1024` and union count `<1024`; a new artifact
row requires artifact count `<1024` and union count `<1024`. Otherwise it
returns stable `item_request_retention_limit_exceeded` before row, child,
provider, or filesystem work.

The S27-to-S28 runner acquires `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on the main database before
that first count and retains the same transaction through bounded preflight,
DDL, descriptor verification, and migration-ledger insert; no deferred
transaction or legacy writer may race a successful count. Its executable
assertion uses a named TEMP STRICT guard/CHECK plus per-item, per-class, and
combined index scans with `LIMIT 1025`, so the observed sentinel is bounded
and a 1,025th row aborts and rolls back guard, DDL, and ledger together.
Top-level `RAISE()` remains forbidden. The current raw-SQL/default-deferred
runner is incompatible until replaced by this exact capability.

Deletion command construction loads the complete locked combined child set,
bounded at 1,024, only after the current tombstone-key signing reservation and
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The two descriptor-frozen set-based inserts run in the
single parent `BEFORE DELETE` trigger, never a host loop, stateful UDF, or
child-trigger ordering dependency. The final SQL proof requires the exact
locked source tuple set, canonical command-map tuple set, and inserted
tombstone tuple set to be equal with zero missing or extra entries; it also
requires the two inserted counts to equal their locked per-class source
counts, their sum to equal the locked union count, and every count to be in
`0..1024`. Tests cover per-class and combined 1,023/1,024/1,025 boundaries,
migration refusal before DDL, map omission/addition/duplicate/reorder/type/
authenticator changes, surviving-permit commit failure, rollback/retry, and
trigger-order permutations on the actual adapter.

Updates are rejected. Freeze
`idx_item_request_tombstones_janitor(block_until,caller_request_id)`. One
janitor batch reads one fresh database clock `N` and executes the exact
equivalent of
`DELETE ... WHERE caller_request_id IN (SELECT caller_request_id ... WHERE
block_until < :N ORDER BY block_until,caller_request_id LIMIT 256)`, with the
inner index forced/verified by the descriptor and `changes()` in `0..256`.
Equality remains blocked; no unordered, offset, caller-sized, or larger batch
is accepted. The sole clock-read exception is the exact exclusive
`tombstone_key_retirement_controller_v1` owner with a matching
`caller_tombstone_drain` operation: while its cross-equal `draining` barrier
excludes ordinary janitors and producers, the operation-bound native role
binds the barrier's immutable `frozen_database_clock` as `N` to this identical
statement and repeats observer-classified batches until a zero result. No
other or stale owner may supply, cache, or reuse a janitor clock. Once the tombstone is absent,
the original authority is necessarily expired; the replay is rejected on that
fact even if an exact item precondition is supplied, and a later live item
with another instance independently fails the expected-current-instance
check. Tests exercise those two predicates independently, the equality and
`+1` cleanup boundary, 255/256/257 ordering, `K_MAX`/`K_MAX+1`,
rotation/capacity, key loss, all-32 masked execution, an exact dummy-slot HMAC
match that still refuses, request-class substitution, ID
collision, HMAC mismatch, response loss, delayed replay, retirement-barrier
producer/janitor refusal, crash/replay after every batch outcome, and absence
from every read/log/export surface.

The receipt insert guard also proves the bound attempt has null source ID,
artifact IDs, error code, error message, and status code.

- `(job_id,attempt_number)`;

`result_fingerprint` is SHA-256 over the fixed
`youtube-recovery-result-v1` domain and a fixed-order sequence of normalized
provider, body hash, title, author, source URL, capture quality, extraction
method, extraction version, warning, duration, published time, thumbnail URL,
description, transcript language, generated flag, translated flag, and
transcript character count. Framing is exact: domain bytes, one `0x00`, then
for each field a four-byte unsigned big-endian byte length followed by UTF-8
bytes; null uses length `0xffffffff`; integers use base-10 ASCII with no plus
or leading zero; Booleans use `0` or `1`. Null and empty are distinct. The
implementation freezes one shared encoder plus independent test vectors before
this receipt can be treated as authority.

The normalized strings are exactly the validated values handed to the item
update, without an additional trim or Unicode normalization. `body_sha256` is

`transcript_chars` is JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit `body.length`, preserving
current behavior; generated/translated are null or exact Boolean; duration and
published time are null or safe nonnegative base-10 integers. Tests mutate
every field and cover null versus empty.

The receipt deliberately has no policy-decision or transcript-source column.
It cannot falsely classify `youtube_innertube_timedtext` as an approved
caption source. It stores no transcript text, URL, title, provider payload, or

All updates are rejected. Direct receipt deletion while its item exists is
rejected. Job or attempt deletion cannot orphan or silently remove it.
Item-root cascade is allowed and tested.

`job_id` is the durable crash-reconciliation key. Before any new claim or
provider call, and first inside apply, the worker looks up a receipt by job ID
and proves the job is done, `last_attempt_id` equals the receipt attempt, the

revision, and the committed body hash matches. A complete match returns the
durable terminal result
without the lost raw token; any partial or mismatched graph is an integrity
failure. The claim hash remains the same-process apply identity, not the only
post-crash lookup capability.

### 7.10 Capture-artifact write operations and deletion cleanup

Migration 028 adds a unique index on
`capture_artifacts(relative_path)`. Preflight
has already rejected bytewise, normalized, cross-item, and filesystem-identity
aliases and frozen an exact absolute-to-relative mapping for every historical
row whose `relative_path` is null. Under the migration writer lock, recompute
that mapping, populate every null `relative_path`, preserve the legacy
absolute `path` bytes for B27 reads, and verify the mapping token before
creating the unique index. S28 activation requires every row to have one
canonical root-relative path. Every new row uses that indexed key and leaves
the legacy absolute `path` column null. New capture-artifact inserts require a
matching write operation below, all row identity/path/result fields are
immutable, and direct row deletion while the item exists is rejected unless
the sealed item-delete permit is active.

Legacy absolute-path backfill is rejection-only canonicalization, never a
repairing normalization. For each row whose `relative_path` is null, frozen
preflight reads `typeof(path)` and `CAST(path AS BLOB)`, requires
`typeof(path)='text'`, a nonempty absolute path, fatal UTF-8 decode, and
byte-for-byte equality after UTF-8 re-encode, and requires `item_id` to be
exactly 24 lowercase hexadecimal. Let `R` be the provisioner-attested
canonical root returned by `realpathSync.native` with `encoding:'buffer'`,
with no trailing slash, and `P` the untouched stored path BLOB. `P` must
byte-equal `R || 0x2f || Q`; `resolve`, normalization, case folding, and
Unicode normalization never make a path acceptable. `Q` must be nonempty
valid UTF-8, use only `0x2f` as separator, contain no empty, dot, dot-dot, NUL,
backslash, or control-byte component, begin with the row's exact item ID, and
contain a nonempty suffix after that component.

The walker starts at `R`, uses Buffer-valued `readdirSync` plus `lstatSync`,
and requires every `Q` component to have exactly one bytewise-equal directory
entry. Every ancestor is a directory, no component is a symlink, the leaf is
a regular file with link count one, and
`realpathSync.native(P,{encoding:'buffer'})` byte-equals `P`. Its exact bytes,
size, and SHA-256 must equal every corresponding non-null stored row value.
Across every artifact row, canonical relative bytes and present
device/inode pairs are each globally unique. The canonical `relative_path`
is fatal UTF-8 decode of `Q` without transformation. A failed predicate,
including an alternate case/Unicode spelling accepted only by the filesystem,
lexical alias, root-prefix sibling, traversal, symlink, hard link, duplicate
identity, out-of-root path, or first-component/item mismatch, refuses
migration.

For a historical row whose `relative_path` is already non-null, frozen
preflight separately reads `typeof(relative_path)` and
`CAST(relative_path AS BLOB)`, requires storage class exactly `text`,
nonempty bytes, fatal UTF-8 decode/re-encode equality, and then applies the
same `/`-component, item-owner, exact-dirent, no-symlink, uniqueness, and
row/hash/size rules to those untouched bytes. A valid-UTF-8 BLOB in the
TEXT-affinity column is still rejected. A row-only missing file is allowed
only for this already-relative form when `write_status` is `failed` or
`skipped`: existing ancestors must pass, the first absent component
classifies the remaining suffix absent without creating or following
anything, and row content hash/size are null. If legacy `path` is also
non-null, `typeof(path)` must be `text`, its fatal-roundtripped untouched BLOB
must be exactly `R || 0x2f || relative_path_bytes`, and neither stored column
is rewritten.

The preservation token includes
`capture-artifact-legacy-path-map-v1`, framed under section 7.5 over the root
fingerprint, canonical decimal row count, and, in artifact-ID UTF-8 byte
order, each artifact ID, item ID, untouched nullable path BLOB, canonical
relative-path bytes, root fingerprint, nullable canonical device, inode,
size, link count, and content SHA-256. Under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, recomputation
must match; each backfill is an exact CAS on ID, null relative path,
`typeof(path)='text'`, and unchanged path BLOB with `changes()=1`; then all
path BLOBs and derived keys are reread and verified before the unique index.
Already-relative rows use an exact locked reread of storage class and BLOB
bytes against the frozen token; no coercing comparison is accepted.
Evidence stores only hashes, never absolute paths. Independent vectors cover
valid nested paths; root-prefix sibling and root itself; double separator,
dot/dot-dot, and trailing separator; invalid UTF-8, NUL, control, and
backslash; wrong item component; case/Unicode dirent alias; ancestor/leaf
symlink; non-directory ancestor; nonregular leaf; hard link; duplicate
relative key and device/inode; changed root identity or old path bytes;
row-order permutation; BLOB-in-TEXT-affinity storage, CAS/reread mismatch;
same-inode/same-size content mutation;
stored hash/size mismatch; row-only absence; and post-backfill old-path
mutation.

Create an item-owned detailed caller binding:

```text
item_artifact_write_requests
caller_request_id             TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, 43 base64url characters
item_id                       TEXT NOT NULL
expected_item_instance_id     TEXT NOT NULL exact 32 lowercase hexadecimal
expected_content_revision     INTEGER NOT NULL positive
expected_item_mutation_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal

state                         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK active|recovering|terminal
lease_epoch                   INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative

lease_last_renewed_at          INTEGER NULL nonnegative
lease_expires_at              INTEGER NULL nonnegative

authority_expires_at          INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative

authority_key_id              TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
authority_authenticator       TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal

```

It has the composite
`(item_id,expected_item_instance_id) -> items(id,item_instance_id) ON DELETE
CASCADE`. It exists only while the owning item exists; after item deletion,
bounded replay uses section 7.8's caller-request tombstone and no detailed
caller row survives. `caller_request_id` is unpadded base64url for 32 CSPRNG
bytes, is not derived from an item, job, path, or content field, and is
globally collision-checked against `extension_capture_requests` and
`item_request_tombstones`. `created_at` is one database clock.
The five authority fields byte-semantically equal the section-7.7 envelope:
`created_at=authority_created_at`; the committed requested TTL is positive,
no greater than 86,400,000 milliseconds, and equals
`authority_expires_at-created_at`; and the key ID/authenticator verify under
the retained authority key. Authority expiry cannot be renewed or extended.

`artifact_manifest_sha256` uses the section-7.5 length framing under domain
`capture-artifact-request-manifest-v1`. It frames, in order, caller request
ID, public item ID, immutable item instance, expected content revision,
expected mutation fingerprint, artifact-root fingerprint, canonical decimal
artifact count, canonical decimal requested authority TTL milliseconds, then exactly the
contiguous indexes `0..artifact_count-1`.
Each index frames its operation ID, artifact ID, canonical decimal index,
kind, nullable content type, deterministic final relative path, deterministic
staged relative path, expected byte SHA-256, canonical decimal expected size,
and truncation Boolean. Raw `suggested_filename` is not independently
authoritative after safe filename derivation; a retry is equivalent only when
all frozen derived fields—including both paths—are identical. Independent
vectors change each field, order, null/empty value, filename-derived extension,
and path component. A retry must present the same caller request, item,
instance, and manifest or fail `caller_request_id_mismatch`.

The initial request guard requires exactly `artifact_count` child operations
with those contiguous indexes and byte-identical manifest fields. Every child
must equal the parent's single expected revision, mutation fingerprint, and
root tuple; mixed child authority is impossible. For a new request, all
pending operations are inserted first and the parent is inserted last in the
same transaction; their request foreign key is deferred only until that
commit, so the parent guard can validate the complete exact set without an
assembling state. Active, recovering, and terminal guards recheck the same
count and set. `active|recovering -> terminal` occurs only after every derived
operation is terminal. Sealed item deletion validates the complete child set,
requires no live writer, inserts the exact content-free caller tombstone, and
then cascades the parent and children without a retained snapshot.
Caller request ID, item, item instance, expected revision, mutation
fingerprint, root fingerprint, request-manifest hash, count, and created time
and every authority-envelope field are immutable. Result/completion fields and terminal
states change only through the named sealed transitions.

Shape checks require:

- `active` or `recovering` has positive lease epoch, non-null token/renewal/
  expiry, null result/completed fields, and the exact
  original child count/set;
- `terminal` has non-null result/completed, null token/lease fields, and the
  exact original child count/set.

The request owner lease closes the pending-operation race. The initial FULL
transaction inserts the parent as `active` with epoch one, a fresh 256-bit
process-memory owner token hash, and the database-clock ten-minute lease.
The caller retains the raw token; it is never persisted or logged. Every
operation claim, renewal, identity commit, finalization, and handoff to the
next index matches that current parent token/state and atomically renews the
parent using the same database time. A request lease may never expire before
an active child lease; each child claim/renew transaction sets both expiries
to the same value and shape guards require the parent expiry to be at least
the maximum active-child expiry. The one-third boundary is scheduling-only:
the owner should attempt renewal then, but missing that schedule does not
revoke an otherwise valid lease before its nominal expiry. A renewal that
fails because the item/root/request tuple, token, epoch, or authority changed
makes that worker inert immediately. Every mutating use still requires a
successful current-token check at a database clock strictly before nominal
lease expiry; equality is expired.

No pending scan is legal while the request is `active` with a current lease,
while any writing/reconciling child has a current later-or-equal lease, or
merely because another process starts. At `now_ms >= lease_expires_at`, one
immediate CAS may change `active|recovering -> recovering`, increment the
epoch, install a fresh recovery token/lease, and prove no active child has
later authority. Only that exact recovery token may reconcile an expired
active child or terminalize pending children, in index order, while renewing
the request lease. A crashed recovery owner is itself taken over only at
equality/expiry. The former caller token can no longer claim, renew,
finalize, or hand off. Thus the first post-request-commit interval and every
gap between multi-artifact operations remain leased, while payload-free
startup recovery eventually fails or quarantines every remainder.

`authority_expires_at` is an independent hard ceiling on the whole caller
request. Every new child claim, parent or child renewal, stage creation,
write continuation, hard-link publication, successful finalization, sibling
handoff, pending recovery decision, and caller-result reconciliation requires
one database clock strictly less than both the applicable lease expiry and
`authority_expires_at`; equality is expired. No renewal may set a lease beyond
that authority ceiling. At or after authority expiry, recovery may only take
over to stop a writer, remove an exact proved owned stage/final residue, fsync,
and terminalize pending or active work with existing stable
`item_authority_lost`; it may not create a file, publish a final name, commit a
successful capture row, hand off to another child, or return the prior
detailed result as current authority. Tests pause at every claim/renew/write/
publication/finalization/recovery boundary at expiry equality and one
millisecond before it.

Add the nonpartial parent key
`(caller_request_id,item_id,expected_item_instance_id,
expected_content_revision,expected_item_mutation_fingerprint,
artifact_root_fingerprint)`.

Create an item-owned detailed operation record:

```text
item_artifact_write_operations
operation_id                 TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, 43 base64url characters
artifact_id                  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, exact 24 lowercase hexadecimal
caller_request_id            TEXT NOT NULL
artifact_index               INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
item_id                      TEXT NOT NULL
expected_item_instance_id    TEXT NOT NULL exact 32 lowercase hexadecimal
expected_content_revision    INTEGER NOT NULL positive
expected_item_mutation_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
kind                         TEXT NOT NULL, 1..128 UTF-8 bytes with no controls
relative_path                TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
staged_relative_path         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
artifact_root_fingerprint    TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
content_type                 TEXT NULL, otherwise 1..255 UTF-8 bytes with no controls
expected_sha256              TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
expected_size_bytes          INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative and within kind cap
truncated                    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK 0|1
state                        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK pending|writing|reconciling|committed|failed|quarantined
lease_epoch                  INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative; pending=0, active positive
claim_token_hash             TEXT NULL UNIQUE exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
lease_last_renewed_at         INTEGER NULL nonnegative
lease_expires_at             INTEGER NULL nonnegative
directory_device             TEXT NULL canonical unsigned decimal integer
directory_inode              TEXT NULL canonical unsigned decimal integer
stage_device                 TEXT NULL canonical unsigned decimal integer
stage_inode                  TEXT NULL canonical unsigned decimal integer
final_device                 TEXT NULL canonical unsigned decimal integer
final_inode                  TEXT NULL canonical unsigned decimal integer
quarantine_shape_sha256      TEXT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
last_error_code              TEXT NULL exact 1..64-byte ASCII
                             [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}; closed enum below
terminal_scan_epoch          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 nonnegative
terminal_scan_completed_at   INTEGER NULL nonnegative
created_at                   INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
updated_at                   INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
completed_at                 INTEGER NULL nonnegative
```

The tuple `(caller_request_id,item_id,expected_item_instance_id,
expected_content_revision,expected_item_mutation_fingerprint,
artifact_root_fingerprint)` references the matching item-owned request parent
with `ON DELETE CASCADE DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`, and
`(caller_request_id,artifact_index)` is unique.
That composite request-parent foreign key is the operation's sole cascade
path. The parent in turn has the one composite
`(item_id,expected_item_instance_id) -> items(id,item_instance_id) ON DELETE
CASCADE` relationship. The operation repeats the exact item tuple only so the
parent FK closes its authority; it has no second direct FK to `items`.
Missing, cross-item, or noncurrent-instance operations are relationally
impossible, and cascade order is unambiguous.

`operation_id` is the caller request's per-artifact idempotency key and is
allocated and durably carried through the request parent before the low-level
writer's first call. More precisely, it is unpadded base64url SHA-256 under domain
`capture-artifact-operation-v1` using the section-7.5 framing over caller
request ID and canonical decimal artifact index. The low-level writer never
invents an unrelated ID.
`artifact_id` is the first 24 lowercase hexadecimal
characters of SHA-256 over domain `capture-artifact-id-v1`, one `0x00`, and
the exact operation-ID bytes, so it is deterministically recoverable. Every
existing caller allocates one random `caller_request_id` from 32 CSPRNG bytes
and durably stores or carries it in its owning job, update receipt, Telegram
update, HTTP idempotency envelope, or client request before artifact work.
The request row freezes every derived operation before any file. The static
caller inventory and response-loss tests fail if a callsite can omit or
regenerate the request or operation ID. The same in-authority retry must reuse
the caller request, operation ID, expected item instance/revision, and mutation
fingerprint.

The stage path is exactly
`<safe-item-id>/.stage-<operation_id>.part`. The final path is the existing
safe artifact filename under that exact item directory.
`<safe-item-id>` is the exact item ID only when it is 24 lowercase hexadecimal
characters; a new artifact write for any other item ID fails before operation
insert and requires a separately reviewed path migration. Both paths are
stored before any file exists. A terminal operation row remains until
item-root deletion, so response-loss lookup and every deterministic late-file
scan remain possible while the item exists. Every lookup first compares the
stored or caller-carried item instance before consulting a public item ID.
After deletion only the bounded keyed-authenticator tombstone may answer the
caller request, and it never creates a new operation.

A committed row has matching non-null final identity, null
claim/lease/error/quarantine hash, and one exact `capture_artifacts` row. A
failed row has null claim/lease/final identity/quarantine hash, a stable error
code, and one exact `capture_artifacts.write_status='failed'` row with null
content hash/size and no file; its `error_message` is that bounded code, never
an OS message or absolute path. A quarantined row has null claim/lease, a
stable error code, a canonical content-free `quarantine_shape_sha256`, no
capture-artifact row, and preserves every unproved namespace entry. All three
terminal states begin with terminal scan epoch zero and null scan time; later
sealed scans may change only those diagnostic scan fields and `updated_at`.
The closed operation-error enum is
`content_size_mismatch|content_sha256_mismatch|owned_stage_io_failure|
owned_publication_io_failure|item_authority_lost|lease_authority_lost|
writer_lost_before_claim|
alien_namespace_entry|namespace_identity_mismatch|namespace_unsafe_type|
artifact_root_mismatch|deletion_limit_exceeded`. A `failed` row accepts only
the first seven codes; a `quarantined` row accepts only the final five; pending,
writing, reconciling, and committed rows require null. Every repository path
uses this exact first-match reduction over all predicates observable at the
current transition:

1. `namespace_unsafe_type`: either deterministic name has an unsupported or
   unsafe filesystem type;
2. `alien_namespace_entry`: a present deterministic name has no exact owned
   operation identity;
3. `namespace_identity_mismatch`: an expected owned name has identity,
   metadata, link-count, or path/descriptor drift;
4. `artifact_root_mismatch`: the provisioned artifact-root identity differs;
5. `deletion_limit_exceeded`: the exact conservative deletion projection is
   outside a frozen bound;
6. `item_authority_lost`: item absence or instance, revision, mutation
   fingerprint, cleanup, or other item-authority drift;
7. `lease_authority_lost`: token, epoch, state, or expiry no longer grants the
   attempted mutation;
8. `writer_lost_before_claim`: the expired parent owner left a pending
   operation with both deterministic names absent and every item/root
   predicate otherwise unchanged;
9. `content_size_mismatch`;
10. `content_sha256_mismatch`;
11. `owned_stage_io_failure`: a mapped I/O failure before final publication;
12. `owned_publication_io_failure`: a mapped I/O failure at or after final
    publication.

The first true applicable predicate supplies the one persisted code and its
declared failed/quarantined state; later predicates cannot replace it.
Platform errors are mapped by operation phase only to the two semantic I/O
codes after the preceding predicates have been evaluated. Independent
negatives mutate every code/state pair, every reachable simultaneous-predicate
combination and precedence edge, and reject empty, 65-byte, uppercase,
hyphenated, control, non-ASCII, unknown, raw
errno/exception/SQLite/OS-message, absolute-path, and filename-derived values;
the capture-artifact `error_message` must byte-equal the accepted stable code.
The shape
hash uses section-7.5 framing under domain
`capture-artifact-quarantine-shape-v1` over operation ID, immutable item
instance, and root fingerprint, followed by exactly two fixed slots in order:
stage then final. Each slot frames role, its deterministic relative path,
present Boolean, type, and nullable canonical unsigned-decimal device, inode,
size, and link count. The exhaustive type enum is
`absent|regular|directory|symlink|fifo|socket|character_device|block_device|other`;
`present=false` requires `type='absent'` and every scalar null, while a
present slot forbids `absent` and carries every `lstat` scalar. Thus one hash
binds simultaneous alien stage and final entries rather than selecting one.
It contains no absolute path or bytes. Independent vectors cover every pair
of absent/present roles, every type, null/value distinctions, maximum-width
scalars, and order changes. Pending rows have epoch zero and null
claim/lease/directory/stage/final/quarantine/error/completion fields with no
capture-artifact row and terminal scan epoch zero/time null.
Writing/reconciling rows have a fresh 256-bit token hash,
positive epoch/database-clock lease fields, null
final/quarantine/error/completion/terminal-scan-time fields, terminal scan
epoch zero, and no capture-artifact row. A
writing row before its identity CAS has a null stage pair; afterward it has the
exact non-null pair. A reconciling row preserves whichever reviewed
pre/post-identity shape it took over.

Operation ID, artifact ID, item, item instance/revision/mutation fingerprint,
metadata, paths, root, expected bytes, and created time are immutable. The
only updates are:

- one `pending -> writing` CAS that installs the first epoch/token/lease after
  rechecking item/root/path authority;
- one sealed `pending -> quarantined` transition if an alien namespace entry
  appears after the request/pending-operation commit but before the first
  writer claim;
- one sealed `pending -> failed` startup/abandonment transition after proving
  both deterministic names absent, or the paired quarantined transition when
  either name is an alien shape;
- exact current-token renewal;
- one `writing -> writing` current-token/epoch CAS that preserves an already
  validated directory pair or changes its exact expected-absent pair to the
  just-created non-null pair, changes the null stage pair to the just-observed
  non-null pair, updates `updated_at`, and runs only under the exact native
  stage prepared role after the stage-parent fsync;
- expired epoch-incrementing takeover to `reconciling`; and
- one current-token, sealed reconciliation/finalization transition to
  `committed`, `failed`, or `quarantined` with its exact row/file shape; and
- one sealed terminal-scan self-transition that preserves every terminal
  state/authority/result column, increments `terminal_scan_epoch` by one,
  records database time, and updates `updated_at` only after the proved
  residual validation/fsync sequence.

The identity CAS cannot repeat or change a non-null identity. Committed,
failed, and quarantined are terminal except for that named diagnostic
self-transition. Terminal-scan fields are excluded from request/result
authority and cannot change through any other statement. Direct operation
deletion while its item exists is rejected; only the sealed item-root cascade
removes it.
Capture-artifact insert guards match the operation's artifact/item/kind/path/
content-type/truncation fields and permit `write_status='ok'` only in the
finalization transaction or `failed` only in owned-file reconciliation.
Quarantine never fabricates a capture-artifact row. Ordinary, UPSERT, and
every REPLACE conflict path is covered by section 6.2.

The last terminal operation in a caller request also stores the canonical
content-free result-manifest hash and changes the request
`active|recovering -> terminal` in the same fixed outer operation transition
and its built-in relational trigger chain under the exact native artifact
prepared role/source trace, accepting `recovering -> terminal`
for the exact recovery token and clearing every request token/lease field.
`result_manifest_sha256` uses
section-7.5 framing under domain `capture-artifact-result-manifest-v1` over
caller request ID, item ID, immutable instance, the parent's exact
`artifact_manifest_sha256`, and artifact count, followed by every contiguous
artifact index. Each terminal
entry frames index, operation ID, artifact ID, terminal state, both relative
paths, root fingerprint, kind, nullable content type, expected hash/size,
truncation, nullable final device/inode, nullable stable error code, nullable
quarantine-shape hash, and the exact nullable capture-row
write-status/hash/size projection. Field order and null framing are fixed and
independently vectored. Diagnostic `terminal_scan_epoch`,
`terminal_scan_completed_at`, and the scan-only `updated_at` change are
explicitly excluded from this result manifest, the request manifest, and every
operation authority key; a later terminal scan therefore cannot alter a
retained terminal result. Startup may perform that pure database reduction
only through the named sealed terminal-scan outer statement after verifying
the exact operation count/set and every operation is terminal. An
`active|recovering` parent must first be owned by the exact expired-request
recovery epoch/token, and the trigger changes it to `terminal` and clears that
lease. An already-terminal parent is read-only request authority: its
operation scan uses only the exact native terminal-scan prepared role,
binding/row-count contract, and authorizer trace and
cannot update the parent. Neither path creates or retries file work. Direct
request update/delete is rejected.

The write lease is ten minutes. Claim and renewal use the database-clock,
strict-before-expiry, equality-to-reconciler, scheduling-only one-third
renewal attempt,
safe-integer, epoch, token, item, item instance/revision/mutation fingerprint,
root, path, state, and cleanup-row rules from
section 9.5. Those predicates also require the exact current item instance,
content revision, and recomputed mutation fingerprint. An expired `writing`
or `reconciling` operation is taken over by
an immediate-transaction CAS that increments `lease_epoch`, installs a fresh
token, and commits `state='reconciling'`. Missing the scheduling attempt alone
does not revoke before nominal expiry; a failed renewal makes the old worker
inert, and equality at nominal expiry rejects. A stale writer can neither
renew nor finalize. A partial unique index permits at most one
`writing|reconciling` operation per item, matching the current sequential
writer and serializing first-directory creation.

Supported S28 writers preserve deletability as an admission invariant. Before
any new request/operation insert, the same FULL immediate transaction
recomputes the exact current deletion manifest and adds a worst-case
reservation for every existing and proposed nonterminal operation. That
reservation includes the item directory when absent, both the deterministic
staged and final relative-path entries, both directory-entry and
cumulative-relative-path-byte contributions, and the expected file size for
each potentially present name. The conservative byte projection therefore
uses checked arithmetic to add two manifest entries, evaluates each path's
depth and UTF-8 byte length, adds both path lengths to the cumulative-path
bound, and adds exactly `2 * expected_size` to the file-byte bound. No
same-inode assumption, observed partial size, or absent counterpart may reduce
either reservation.

The projected compact-manifest size is the maximum of the exact compact JSON
for every owned legal namespace shape: stage-only partial, stage-only
complete, final-only post-publication, and the transient post-link
both-name shape. Each projection uses the exact entry key order and maximum-
width legal device, inode, size, link-count, hash, source, presence, and
artifact-ID scalar placeholders; it never estimates with an average row size.
Equivalently, the generic reservation adds the sum of two maximum-width legal
compact-manifest file objects. An already-present exact entry replaces its
corresponding reserved slot instead of being counted twice, but every absent
reserved slot and both path byte strings remain represented. Operation
identity/path uniqueness makes reservations non-overlapping.

The resulting projection must remain at or below all seven section-7.10
deletion limits. Equality is accepted and every `+1` case refuses before
request DML or file creation. A terminal owned failure proven to have both
names absent releases both reservations. A committed operation counts the
exact final row/file shape. A quarantined operation counts every exact staged
and final slot that remains present and may terminalize only when the
resulting exact manifest still satisfies every limit. A newly discovered
alien external entry that would produce `+1` is a host-integrity quarantine:
it is preserved, blocks deletion and new artifact admission, and is not
accepted as a supported invariant. Migration preflight establishes the same
worst-case invariant for historical items. Evidence injects crashes in the
middle of stage writing and immediately after final linking at every equality
and `+1` boundary.

Before the first per-artifact step, one FULL-durable immediate transaction
rechecks every deterministic stage/final name, reconciles an existing request
or inserts every derived `pending` operation followed by its item-owned parent,
freezes the exact request manifest/count/authority tuple, and commits the
parent's initial owner epoch/token/lease. A preexisting
target or stage name refuses before any request/operation insert with stable
`path_collision_preflight` and zero namespace mutation. A terminal request
never starts new work and replays from its item-owned parent and terminal
child rows while its authority remains current. After item deletion all of
those rows are absent; only an exact, in-window section-7.8 tombstone may
return `item_deleted`, and it cannot recreate work or disclose the former
result manifest.

Every repository capture-artifact writer uses this order:

1. In one immediate transaction, change the exact `pending` operation to
   `writing` with its first epoch/token/lease after proving the item
   instance/revision/mutation fingerprint, provisioned root,
   permanent path uniqueness across every backfilled artifact row and
   operation, no other `writing|reconciling` item operation, absent cleanup
   row, absent deterministic stage/final names, and the exact current
   parent-owner token/lease. The same commit renews that parent lease. A
   post-freeze alien name is
   preserved and seals the pending operation as `quarantined`. If the item directory already
   exists, record its validated regular-directory device/inode; otherwise
   record the exact expected-absent shape. This and every later transaction
   uses the FULL-durable connection.
2. In a second immediate transaction, recheck the token/lease/root/path and
   item authority; create or validate the exact item directory with the
   root-attested path semantics in section 6.4 and mode `0700`; then create the
   stage with
   `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` mode `0600` while the SQLite writer lock is
   held. Fsync the artifact root if the item directory was created, then fsync
   the item directory to make the stage entry durable. Only after those syncs
   install the exact native stage prepared role and execute the exact
   null-to-identity CAS;
   commit the recorded directory and regular-file device/inode identities.
   An abrupt stop before that FULL identity commit leaves a durable operation
   with the exact expected-absent identity shape and only an absent or
   deterministic empty-directory/zero-byte-stage namespace shape. No
   namespace entry is created after releasing a database lock that did not
   authorize it.
3. Write only through that open descriptor, enforce the exact cap, renew while
   the same item instance/revision/mutation remains current, verify the
   expected SHA-256/size, and `fsync` the file. Losing the name, item authority,
   or lease makes the writer close the descriptor and stop.
4. In one final immediate transaction, recheck the complete operation and
   freeze the exact native finalize prepared role/bindings/counts; re-`lstat`
   the stage without following links;
   verify identity/hash/size; and publish with a same-directory hard-link
   operation that fails if the final name exists. Unlink the stage, verify the
   final regular file has the same device/inode and link count one, and
   `fsync` the item directory. Only then execute the fixed outer operation
   transition to `committed`; its built-in relational trigger chain inserts
   the exact capture-artifact row, clears claim/lease, terminalizes the request
   when applicable, and commits as one SQLite statement under the frozen
   authorizer trace.

The filesystem actions in steps 2 and 4 are synchronous and contain no
`await` while the immediate transaction owns the SQLite writer lock. A second
writer or reconciler therefore serializes before any namespace mutation.
Hard-link publication is the reviewed no-clobber primitive; a target that
cannot supply its semantics refuses S28 artifact capability before caller
request/operation insert.
All existing ancestors and the root are identity-checked before and after the
path-based link/unlink sequence under the narrowed threat model in section
6.4.

An expired-operation reconciler first commits the takeover CAS. Its next
immediate transaction, again with synchronous filesystem calls under the
writer lock, validates the exact root, item-directory identity, operation,
deterministic names, stored item instance/revision/mutation, stage identity, or
the exact absent/empty pre-identity crash shape, and expected final
hash/size/identity. It removes only proved operation-owned stage/final names,
fsyncs the item directory and artifact root when directory membership changed,
installs the exact native reconciliation prepared role/bindings/counts, and
executes the fixed outer operation transition to `failed`; its built-in
relational trigger chain inserts the exact stable failed capture-artifact row,
clears claim/lease, terminalizes the request when applicable, and commits as
one SQLite statement under the frozen authorizer trace. Crash replay of
`reconciling` repeats absence checks idempotently. Both deterministic names
present as regular files with the stored stage device/inode, identical
expected hash/size, the same device/inode, and link count exactly two on both
names is the owned `after_final_link`/before-stage-unlink crash shape.
Reconciliation unlinks the stage, verifies that the remaining final retains
the stored identity with link count one, unlinks the final, fsyncs the item
directory, proves both absent, and only then may terminalize the operation as
failed. Crashes after either unlink replay through
`artifact_write_reconcile_after_stage_unlink` and
`artifact_write_reconcile_after_final_unlink`; the hard-link pair can never be
committed as a quarantine or passed to deletion admission. A missing post-identity stage plus a final
file with the stored stage device/inode, expected hash/size, and link count one
is the owned post-stage-unlink/pre-database-commit crash shape;
reconciliation removes that proved final, fsyncs, and fails the operation. A
missing post-identity stage without that proved final, a partial file that
does not prove the exact owned removable shape, or any alien stage/final shape
is preserved and transitioned through the exact native reconciliation role to
`quarantined` with its canonical shape hash and no capture-artifact row.

Startup recovery scans use the same durable connection and require no caller
resubmission or payload bytes. Pending scans and terminal scans that must
reduce an `active|recovering` parent first own the exact expired request
through the recovery CAS above; an unexpired active request or live sibling
operation is not scan-eligible. A `pending` scan selects one operation under
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, matches and renews that parent recovery epoch/token,
verifies the frozen request/count, item instance, root, and deterministic
names, and uses the sealed reconcile outer transition. Exact
absence of both names creates the stable failed capture row with
`writer_lost_before_claim` (or
`item_authority_lost` when the still-owning item drifted);
an alien name produces the canonical quarantined terminal shape instead.
This terminalizes every never-claimed remainder after owner expiry, including
later operations in a multi-artifact request whose item authority drifted.
A healthy owner remains protected before its first operation and throughout
earlier-sibling processing; two-process tests pause at both gaps.

A terminal scan selects one operation under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; it never
installs a persisted claim or lease on the sealed terminal row. It revalidates
the item instance, root and deterministic paths, performs every owned residual
unlink and directory fsync synchronously while retaining the writer lock,
then installs the exact native terminal-scan prepared role and executes the
named state-preserving update before commit. If its parent is
`active|recovering`, the frozen role/bindings also match and renew the exact
recovery epoch/token and may run the same-step pure request-terminal reduction
when all children are terminal. If its parent is already `terminal`, no
request column may change. That legal outer DML increments only the
operation's diagnostic scan epoch/time and `updated_at`; its exact one-row
outer change and dependent change counts must match the native observer. A
committed final file is validated and
preserved; a failed operation's exact proved residual is removed; a
quarantined shape is validated and preserved. The historical
`artifact_write_terminal_scan_*` failpoint names cover both pending-to-terminal
and already-terminal startup scan paths. No startup scan mutates an alien
shape or races an item-deletion manifest. Recovery creates no operation
because it creates no artifact.

The executed artifact-write failpoints must equal the thirty names in the
`artifact_write` registry. Tests cross operation/identity commit, midpoint
write, renewal/takeover equality, no-replace publication, file and directory
fsync, row/operation commit, response loss, every reconciliation/quarantine/
terminal-scan boundary, pending-commit process loss without caller replay, and
paused-writer races. Preinsert collision produces no operation; an owned
failure produces one stable failed row and no file; an alien shape produces
one durable quarantine and preserves the file. A committed operation replays
by `operation_id` without another row or file.

Admission evidence independently places both the staged and final path/entry/
byte/compact-object contribution at equality and `+1` for every one of the
seven limits, then stops at `artifact_write_mid_stage_write` and
`artifact_write_after_final_link`. The latter must replay through
`artifact_write_reconcile_after_stage_unlink` and
`artifact_write_reconcile_after_final_unlink`, remove the owned link pair, and
never terminalize it as quarantine. Safe within-limit quarantine substitution
is distinct from an unsafe or over-limit alien host-integrity refusal.

Create an item-owned detailed deletion request:

```text
item_deletion_requests
deletion_id                  TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, 43 base64url characters
item_id                      TEXT NOT NULL
item_instance_id             TEXT NOT NULL exact 32 lowercase hexadecimal
expected_content_revision    INTEGER NOT NULL positive
request_fingerprint          TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
request_authenticator        TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
request_authenticator_key_id TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
authority_created_at         INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
authority_expires_at         INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
authority_restore_epoch      TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
authority_key_id             TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
authority_authenticator      TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
artifact_root_fingerprint    TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
manifest_sha256              TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
```

`deletion_id` is unpadded base64url for 32 CSPRNG bytes. Before issuing a new
deletion envelope, the service checks the candidate against live
`item_deletion_requests`, `item_artifact_cleanup_jobs`, and
`item_deletion_request_tombstones`. It draws at most eight candidates; a
collision retries, while exhaustion returns stable
`deletion_id_allocation_exhausted` with no envelope release, permit, row,
filesystem mutation, or partial deletion. Intentional reuse of the selected
ID by that same request's trigger-created detailed row and outbox is required,
not a collision. There is no historical ID accumulator.

The five authority fields exactly equal the verified section-7.7 envelope.
The committed requested TTL is positive, no greater than 86,400,000
milliseconds, and equals
`authority_expires_at-authority_created_at`; fresh admission uses a database
clock at or after creation and strictly before expiry. Expiry cannot authorize
a new deletion.

The composite
`(item_id,item_instance_id) -> items(id,item_instance_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
is mandatory. The detailed request exists only inside the accepted item graph and
cascades in the same outer item delete as every other detailed per-item row.
It never survives the item commit. Its exact cleanup-reconciliation
authenticator, tombstone key ID, expiry, deletion clock, root-relative cleanup
identity/manifest, and cleanup state enter the purpose-limited outbox through
the same permit-matched SQL trigger chain before the cascade. The detailed request
has no committed or completed lifecycle; the `BEFORE DELETE` trigger inserts
and validates it and the item-root cascade removes it within the one outer
`sqlite3_step`.

`request_fingerprint` uses the section-7.5 framing under domain
`item-deletion-request-v1` over deletion ID, public item ID, immutable item
instance, expected content revision, authority-created and authority-expiry
clocks, canonical requested authority TTL, root fingerprint, manifest hash,
exact caller-tombstone projection
hash, item-owned artifact-request/operation snapshot hash, and exact
generic-claim/batch snapshot hash. `authority_key_id` and
`authority_authenticator` are the issuance fields. `request_authenticator` is
the internal HMAC-SHA-256 cleanup-reconciliation authenticator over ASCII
domain `stage2-deletion-cleanup-authenticator-v1`, one `0x00`, then
section-7.5 frames for request class `item-deletion-request-v1`, deletion ID,
authority expiry, authority restore epoch, this exact fingerprint, and the
transaction's exact deletion clock. It is not the eventual five-field
deletion-tombstone authenticator, whose terminal code and final horizon do not
yet exist. `request_authenticator_key_id` identifies the current tombstone key
used by the permit's precomputed cleanup value; no key bytes or generic
signing function enter SQL.

Direct insert, update, or deletion is rejected. The SQL-only
`BEFORE DELETE ON items` trigger reached through the exact command view and
transactional permit is the only insert path, and the item-root cascade under
that exact command is the sole deletion path. Pre-conflict guards reject every
UPSERT or REPLACE collision before victim mutation. Tests cover direct
mutation, trigger misuse, conflict algorithms, recursive triggers on/off,
cascade rollback, and full disappearance after commit; no test or guard
creates a deleted-instance exclusion set.

Create the sole durable terminal deletion replay record:

```text
item_deletion_request_tombstones
deletion_id                  TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
                             exactly 43 base64url characters
request_authenticator        TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
terminal_code                TEXT NOT NULL CHECK deleted
deleted_at                   INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
block_until                  INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
```

The tombstone has no public item ID, raw item instance, revision, root, path,
manifest, content, provider, deterministic item hash, or other per-item field.
It has no application read, log, export, or analytics surface and is never
separately cataloged, joined, indexed, or surfaced by backup manifests; it may
exist only inside the authenticated whole-database image.
The final cleanup path first acquires a bounded current tombstone-key signing
reservation with `purpose='finalization_commit'` and only then enters
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; acquisition uses its own monotonic 5,000-ms
equality-accepted deadline. A refused BEGIN releases the reservation only
through `delete_reservation_bundle_v1` after the exact phase-scoped
`begin_refused` tuple, exact held parent plus empty action array,
preimage/no-tombstone proof, and zero permit/database mutation; timeout or
lost response requires the exact both-present/both-absent reread. Any other
BEGIN outcome retains the reservation and fence for four-way or closed-image
recovery. The already-held capability acquires no keystore mutex while the
writer lock is held. Under that lock the route revalidates the complete
namespace and outbox cleanup authenticator, removes only the proved empty
nested/item directories, fsyncs every containing directory through the root,
and retains the writer lock throughout. It then executes the exact no-tail
read-only `final_completion_clock_read` statement
`SELECT unixepoch() * 1000 AS completion_clock` under a sealed native role.
It must yield exactly one row/one column with SQLite storage class INTEGER,
a nonnegative safe-integer value, then `SQLITE_DONE` and one successful
finalize. That value is frozen once as `completion_clock`; a repeated read,
REAL/TEXT/null value, extra row/column, overflow, alternate clock expression,
or statement/role drift refuses before HMAC use. The route computes
`block_until = max(authority_expires_at,completion_clock) + 300_000` with
checked safe-integer arithmetic, and precomputes a new
`stage2-request-tombstone-authenticator-v1` HMAC over request class
`item-deletion-request-v1`, deletion ID, authority expiry, authority restore
epoch, the exact outbox request fingerprint authenticated by that cleanup
authenticator, exact terminal code `deleted`, copied
`deleted_at`, and final `block_until`. Before returning that HMAC, the service
persists the reservation's one exact `block_until` signing-action record.

The sealed finalization trigger inserts that new authenticator and copied
deletion clock into the five-field tombstone only after proving the outbox
owns exactly one reserved capacity slot. The outer `cleaning -> done`
statement binds the same frozen `completion_clock` and sets
`completed_at=:completion_clock`; the trigger byte-compares that INTEGER
through `NEW.completed_at` and performs no second clock read. The signing
action, DML binding, retained outbox, `block_until`, and tombstone must all
reproduce the same scalar. The transition removes the capacity reservation,
the trigger inserts the tombstone into the same capacity unit, proves the
full capacity sum is unchanged, and keeps
the exact durable `done` outbox as the final-promotion/ack witness; it never
copies the outbox's distinct cleanup authenticator into the tombstone. The
first FULL commit uses the exact four-way outcome classification. Rollback
restores `cleaning`, zeroizes the precomputed value, and atomically deletes
the final held reservation plus its exact one-action prefix through
`delete_reservation_bundle_v1` only after exact preimage proof and the
both-present/both-absent timeout rule. Committed or indeterminate outcome
retains the reservation and gate and enters startup recovery.
Acceptance mutates the bound clock by minus one and plus one, changes its
storage class, overflows the horizon addition, attempts a second read, and
crashes after durable action append but before DML; every case either rolls
back and atomically deletes the exact reservation bundle or resumes from the
same bound action without inventing another clock.

After definitive commit and SQLite writer-lock release, the service verifies
the exact `done+tombstone` tuple and final action, atomically raises the final
`selected_key_id` retention to `block_until`, changes only the final
reservation `held -> promoted`, and writes its
`action_sha256` as SHA-256 over ASCII domain
`stage2-tombstone-signing-promotion-v1`, one `0x00`, then section-7.5 frames
for purpose, reservation ID, deletion ID, selected key ID, cleanup key ID,
the exact `stage2-deletion-cleanup-outbox-row-v1` hash of the `done` row,
`signing_actions_sha256`, tombstone authenticator, and canonical decimal
final `block_until`, in that exact order. The
old `(logical_store_id,deletion_id,request_authenticator_key_id)` cleanup pin
remains installed through final promotion and until the atomic
`delete_finalization_authority_v1` operation, including when it names a
different key.

While that exact `done` row still supplies the complete promotion preimage,
the controller rereads the promoted parent/action, final-key retention floor,
old cleanup pin, and `done+tombstone`, then executes or reconciles
`delete_finalization_authority_v1`. Only its exact all-absent result followed
by an unchanged database reread may establish `ack_ready`.

A second sealed FULL ack transaction is the final mutation. It is entered
with no keystore mutation held and only from exact `ack_ready`; it rereads the
byte/storage-class-exact `done` outbox and five-field tombstone and deletes
only that `done` outbox. It arms `transaction_outcome_observer_v1` before
BEGIN. An exact `begin_refused` retains `ack_ready`, performs no rollback or
service-store mutation, and enters bounded retry. After successful BEGIN, a
manifested `commit_not_attempted` sentinel remains set through every
pre-COMMIT failure. Such a failure applies the exact observer classifier and
may be only `open|rolled_back|indeterminate`; `committed` is impossible
without a raw COMMIT `SQLITE_DONE`. `open` alone executes the one hard-coded
rollback and must become the exact `rolled_back` tuple. `rolled_back`
prepares no SQL, retains `ack_ready` plus `done+tombstone`, and resumes the ack
transaction after closed-image proof. `committed`, including raw COMMIT `SQLITE_DONE`
followed by finalize or driver error, never rolls back; it closes/reopens and
proves `done` absent, the tombstone unchanged, no old cleanup pin, no
reservation/actions, and the same internal constant-time matching-key
retention proof, establishing exact `ack_committed` before response.
`indeterminate` prepares no SQL, closes and quarantines, and performs no
database or service-store mutation until
closed-image reconciliation proves either exact `ack_ready` with
`done+tombstone` present, which resumes ack, or exact `ack_committed` with
`done` absent, which may respond. Any other shape is startup class 8.

A crash at any promotion, atomic finalization-authority deletion, ack, or
response edge resumes the exact startup matrix below; no endpoint, same-ID
recreation, backup, restore, janitor, rotation, or new deletion is admitted
first. Only after finalization authority is absent and the ack commit has
removed the outbox may an in-window replay return
`terminal_code='deleted'`; an authenticator mismatch is
`deletion_id_mismatch` and starts no work.

Freeze
`idx_item_deletion_request_tombstones_janitor(block_until,deletion_id)`.
The bounded janitor uses one fresh database clock `N` and the exact equivalent
of `DELETE ... WHERE deletion_id IN (SELECT deletion_id ... WHERE block_until
< :N ORDER BY block_until,deletion_id LIMIT 256)`, with that index
forced/verified and `changes()` in `0..256`. Equality remains blocked; an
unordered, offset, caller-sized, or 257-row batch refuses. The exact exclusive
`tombstone_key_retirement_controller_v1` owner with a matching
`deletion_tombstone_drain` operation and cross-equal `draining` barrier is the
sole exception to this batch's fresh-clock read: the operation-bound native
role binds the barrier's immutable `frozen_database_clock` to the otherwise
identical statement, excludes the ordinary janitor and every producer, and
repeats observer-classified batches to a zero result. Any stale owner or other
supplied/reused clock refuses before BEGIN.
After removal the original authority is necessarily expired. Expiry and the
exact-current-instance comparison are tested as independent rejection
predicates, without forcing or promising historical instance nonreuse.
Vectors cover 255/256/257, tie ordering, stale/equal/fresh clocks, concurrent
janitors, retirement-barrier producer/janitor refusal, and crash/replay after
every batch outcome.

Those three component hashes are closed encoders, not opaque implementation
choices. Their shared scalar encoder frames a one-byte SQLite storage-class
tag (`0x00` null, `0x01` integer, `0x02` text, `0x03` blob) followed by the
section-7.5 length/value frame. Integers are canonical base-10 safe integers;
text must fatal-decode/re-encode UTF-8 and uses its exact bytes; blobs use
their exact bytes; REAL and every other storage class refuse. Each rowset
frames its canonical decimal row count before rows, each row frames the exact
declared column count and values in the stated order, and every sort is
unsigned-byte lexicographic over the framed primary-key tuple. Empty and null
remain distinct.

S28 activation also installs descriptor-generated `BEFORE INSERT` and
`BEFORE UPDATE` guards over the complete resulting row for every table named
by those deletion rowsets. They cover ordinary statements, trigger substeps,
UPSERT, and every REPLACE conflict path, not merely reviewed repository call
sites. Every snapshotted value must remain in an encoder-supported
null/integer/text/blob class, every integer must remain inside the JavaScript
safe-integer range, and every text value must remain valid byte-roundtripping
UTF-8. The descriptor supplies the exact physical column order to both guard
and encoder. A REAL, unsafe integer, invalid text value, unsupported type, or
descriptor/order drift aborts before commit; no ordinary or sealed transition
may create a row that the deletion request encoder cannot later bind.

The caller-tombstone projection uses domain
`item-deletion-caller-request-tombstones-v1`, then frames deletion ID, item ID,
item instance, the one database-clock `deleted_at`, count, and, in
caller-request-ID byte order, every source row from
`extension_capture_requests` and `item_artifact_write_requests`: exact source
class, `caller_request_id`, `authority_expires_at`,
`authority_restore_epoch`, immutable request commitment, derived keyed
authenticator, `terminal_code='item_deleted'`, exact
`block_until=max(authority_expires_at,deleted_at)+300_000`, and copied
`deleted_at`. The source classes and caller IDs are globally disjoint. The
count/set must equal every detailed caller request for that exact item
