instance, and the inserted `item_request_tombstones` set must byte-recompute
the same projection before the item delete. Source class, item identity, and
expiry are encoder inputs only and do not enter the retained tombstone.

The artifact component uses domain
`item-deletion-artifact-authority-snapshot-v1`, item ID, item instance, then
three rowsets in order:

1. every item-owned `item_artifact_write_requests` row for that instance in
   `caller_request_id` order, with every column in the section-7.10 table
   declaration order;
2. every child `item_artifact_write_operations` row in
   `(caller_request_id,artifact_index,operation_id)` order, with every column
   in declaration order; and
3. every `capture_artifacts` row for the item in artifact-ID order, with every
   exact S28 descriptor column in physical table order.

It additionally frames, per request, the exact
`item-delete-request-operations-v1` hash over its pre-cascade child rows. The
closed `item_delete_command_once` native role is the sole application route
allowed to create deletion authority. It inserts the transient permit, proves
and purges the exact bounded vec0 set at top level, marks that permit
`vectors_purged`, then executes the fixed
`INSERT INTO item_delete_commands(command_blob) VALUES (?)`. The view trigger
matches that already-proven permit and issues the sole inner
`DELETE FROM items WHERE id=<header item> AND
item_instance_id=<header instance>`. The exact parent `BEFORE DELETE` trigger
matches that one-use permit using only built-in SQL and retains it through the
cascade. From the canonical
header/map tuples, that trigger inserts exactly one
`item_deletion_requests` row, one no-FK
`item_artifact_cleanup_jobs(state='prepared')` row, and the complete
`item_request_tombstones` set; validates each inserted row by reread; performs
no vec0 access; validates the unchanged ordinary chunk/bridge snapshot against
the permit count and relational graph; and rechecks every
request/child count, state, nullable-path shape, capture projection, authority
envelope, authenticator, and absence of a live writer. It does not mutate a
caller parent into a retained shape. Only after every insertion and
validation succeeds does the same inner item-delete step cascade the newly
inserted detailed deletion request, extension/artifact requests and
operations, capture rows, recovery receipts, and rest of the item graph.
There is no standalone tombstone DML, generic HMAC UDF, schema-trigger vec0
access, or post-command vector purge. The preparatory DML is the exact
self-FK-blocked permit/vector sequence; the only post-cascade DML is the
immediately next sealed `outbox_commit_dml` phase in the same transaction.

The command-view trigger immediately requires the inner root delete's
`changes()` count to be exactly one and then performs its exact intermediate
set
proof; the driver-level change count for an `INSTEAD OF` view is not used as
authority. Before returning `SQLITE_DONE`, statements inside that same view
trigger prove the exact item instance and detailed deletion request are
absent; the marked permit remains exact; the cleanup row is `prepared` with
null `committed_at` and every other bound column unchanged; every
detailed item-owned caller, operation, capture, job, receipt, policy, source,
segment, and hold row is absent; the exact caller-request tombstones remain;
and every other permit-bound intermediate postcondition matches. This
finalized boundary is the sole executable
`deletion_after_item_cascade` coordinate.

The next and only next application statement is the exact
`outbox_commit_dml` described above. Its guarded UPDATE and built-in
`AFTER UPDATE OF state` proof trigger revalidate the surviving cleanup
deletion/fingerprint/authenticator/key-ID/expiry/root/manifest tuple, the
complete command-map/tombstone equality, and every absence proof; change only
that row `prepared -> committed` with the bound transaction clock; delete
exactly the retained permit; reread the exact committed row; and prove zero
permit. Zero or multiple matches, changed authority, an extra column mutation,
or reread drift aborts and rolls back the complete transaction.

A zero- or multiple-row inner root match, inner change count other than one,
unmatched, multiply matched, prematurely deleted, or missing permit,
command/map insertion/vector-receipt/set mismatch, or either guarded proof
mismatch
rolls back the permit insert/mark, bounded per-row top-level vec0 purge, trigger-created
detailed request, tombstones, cascades, and cleanup row together in that
transaction. No prepared outbox can commit because its retained impossible
self-FK permit blocks COMMIT. No post-cascade code pretends it can re-read
deleted child content: it proves absence plus the surviving command, permit,
tombstone, and outbox projections only.

The claim/batch component uses domain
`item-deletion-claim-batch-snapshot-v1`, item ID and instance, followed by
rowsets in this exact table order: the owning `items` row projected as
`id,item_instance_id,content_revision,enrichment_state,batch_id`, then all
owning `transcript_jobs`, `enrichment_jobs`, `embedding_jobs`,
`note_index_jobs`, and `transcript_attempts` rows. Each job/attempt row frames
every column in exact S28 physical descriptor order and is sorted by its
descriptor-declared primary key. Thus null/partial claims, raw batch BLOB/text
bytes, lease/token hashes, revisions, fingerprints, attempts, and state are
all bound without persisting their raw projection.

Independent vectors for all three components change every field and SQLite
type independently and cover null/empty, add/remove row, count, row/table
order, request-with-zero/multiple-operations, active/recovering/terminal
request shapes, every batch classification, and current-instance
substitution. The component hashes are folded into the transient detailed request's
request fingerprint and permit; raw paths, provider identifiers, claims, and
projections do not enter a tombstone or evidence.

The service first parses the immutable deletion envelope, checks the external
active restore epoch, and recomputes its request fingerprint without reading
an item. It then follows the closed order above: detailed deletion request,
cleanup outbox in every state, deletion tombstone, current item. A matching
`prepared` outbox is impossible after a supported commit and fails closed
without database, filesystem, service-store, or endpoint mutation. A matching
`committed|cleaning` outbox verifies its distinct
`stage2-deletion-cleanup-authenticator-v1` through the exact 32-slot verifier
and resumes only that cleanup; it never authorizes a new item mutation. A
matching `done` outbox requires its exact deletion tombstone and resumes only
final-key promotion, `delete_finalization_authority_v1`, or the sealed ack
transaction from the exact startup class; it cannot return success while the
row exists. Only after no cleanup outbox exists may a matching deletion
tombstone recompute the final terminal/horizon-bound authenticator through the
same 32-slot verifier and return `deleted`.
Any commitment/authenticator/request mismatch is `deletion_id_mismatch` with
no mutation. If none of those rows exists, an expired envelope refuses before
item lookup even if its authority key has retired; a potentially live envelope
must verify under a retained authority key and then pass exact current item
instance and revision before admission.

The application executes only the frozen `item_delete_command_once` phase
machine: it inserts the self-FK-blocked prepared permit, proves and purges the
bounded vec0 set at top level, reproves the vector/ordinary snapshot, marks
that permit `vectors_purged`, and only then performs the fixed one-row outer
insert into `item_delete_commands`. Its `INSTEAD OF INSERT` trigger validates
the already-proven permit without virtual-table access and issues the one
inner item delete. The `BEFORE DELETE` trigger creates the detailed request
and prepared outbox; rollback removes both. The same inner item-delete step
cascades the request, after which the view trigger proves the exact retained
marked permit, `prepared` outbox, tombstone set, and deleted graph before
`command_dml` returns and is finalized. The immediately next sealed
`outbox_commit_dml` statement changes the outbox to `committed`; its built-in
proof trigger deletes the permit and proves the committed-outbox/zero-permit
state. Final cleanup durably retains `done` with its exact tombstone until
verified signing promotion and the separate sealed ack transaction delete
that row; no statement may update its deletion ID, authenticator, authority
expiry, deletion clock, root, path, or manifest.

Create the deletion outbox:

```text
item_artifact_cleanup_jobs
deletion_id                  TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY
item_id                      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
item_instance_id             TEXT NOT NULL exact 32 lowercase hexadecimal
request_fingerprint          TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
request_authenticator        TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
request_authenticator_key_id TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
authority_expires_at         INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
authority_restore_epoch      TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
deleted_at                   INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
item_directory_relative_path TEXT NULL UNIQUE, otherwise exact safe item-ID component
artifact_root_fingerprint    TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
item_directory_device        TEXT NULL canonical unsigned decimal integer
item_directory_inode         TEXT NULL canonical unsigned decimal integer
manifest_json                TEXT NOT NULL
manifest_sha256              TEXT NOT NULL exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal
state                        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK prepared|committed|cleaning|done
attempts                     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 nonnegative
last_error_code              TEXT NULL exact 1..64-byte ASCII
                             [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}; closed enum below
created_at                   INTEGER NOT NULL nonnegative
committed_at                 INTEGER NULL nonnegative
completed_at                 INTEGER NULL nonnegative
```

The exact outbox tuple authority is
`stage2-deletion-cleanup-outbox-row-v1`. Its SHA-256 preimage is that ASCII
domain, one `0x00`, then all 21 table columns above in declaration order:
`deletion_id,item_id,item_instance_id,request_fingerprint,
request_authenticator,request_authenticator_key_id,authority_expires_at,
authority_restore_epoch,deleted_at,item_directory_relative_path,
artifact_root_fingerprint,item_directory_device,item_directory_inode,
manifest_json,manifest_sha256,state,attempts,last_error_code,created_at,
committed_at,completed_at`. Each value uses one storage-class tag (`0x00`
null, `0x01` integer, `0x02` text, `0x03` blob) followed by the section-7.5
length/value frame; integers are canonical base-10 safe-integer ASCII, text is
fatal UTF-8 roundtripped exact bytes, null uses the null frame, and REAL or
any other storage class refuses. The state field therefore distinguishes the
initial `committed` and final `done` hashes without an unnamed projection.
Independent vectors mutate every value, storage-class tag, field order,
null/empty distinction, state, and domain and require a different hash or
refusal.

The post-cascade survivors are this outbox plus the bounded five-field caller
tombstones. Of those survivors, this is the only item-identifying unparented
cleanup-work row; the caller tombstones are replay guards, not cleanup work. The narrow
deletion-ID-scoped outbox is not a backup engine or product record. It has no
foreign key to the cascading detailed deletion request. It contains
only the item ID/instance needed to block recreation and fence stale cleanup,
the request fingerprint plus cleanup authenticator, expiry, and restore epoch
needed to reconcile `deletion_id`, the authenticator key ID, deletion clock, the exact
item-directory relative
component, the minimum
root/path identity and manifest needed for cleanup, bounded state/error/times,
and no revision, content body, provider field, or result
detail. It is
absent from ordinary reads, diagnostics, logs, exports, analytics, and product
backup manifests. The root fingerprint is
SHA-256 under domain `artifact-root-v1` over the exact fatal-roundtripped
native canonical-realpath Buffer bytes from section 5.1 and filesystem
device/inode encoded as canonical unsigned decimal strings, using the framing
in section 7.5. Cleanup refuses if the configured root no
longer has that identity.

`item_directory_relative_path IS NULL` if and only if the exact compact
`manifest_json` bytes are `[]`, `manifest_sha256` is
`4f53cda18c2baa0c0354bb5f9a3ecbe5ed12ab4d8e3f36b27ca1f511821d299`,
both item-directory identity fields are null, and the writer-lock-held
projections prove zero `capture_artifacts`, zero
`item_artifact_write_requests`, and zero `item_artifact_write_operations` for
that item. A non-24-lowercase-hexadecimal `item_id` must use this null branch
and is never passed to path construction. A nonnull path requires
`item_id` to be exactly 24 lowercase hexadecimal, path bytes to equal that
item ID exactly, and the item-directory identity pair to be both null when the
directory is absent or both nonnull and manifest-equal when present.
`item_id UNIQUE` remains the recreation fence in both branches, and every
guard/finalizer locates the outbox by `item_id`, never by a nullable-path
equality.

The closed cleanup-error enum is
`artifact_root_unavailable|artifact_root_mismatch|cleanup_manifest_mismatch|
cleanup_namespace_unsafe|cleanup_scan_limit_exceeded|file_unlink_failed|
directory_rmdir_failed|directory_fsync_failed|cleanup_state_mismatch`.
Every non-null value must satisfy the declared ASCII grammar and be exactly one
of those codes. `prepared` and durable ack-pending `done` require null;
`committed` and `cleaning` may carry only this enum, and a successful later
cleanup transition clears an earlier code before advancing. Raw `errno`,
exception, SQLite,
filesystem, path, filename, or manifest text is never persisted in
`last_error_code`. At every attempted cleanup transition, the exact first
applicable predicate in this order supplies the code:
`cleanup_state_mismatch` for a wrong state/permit/outbox tuple;
`artifact_root_unavailable` when the configured root cannot be safely opened;
`artifact_root_mismatch` for opened-root identity drift;
`cleanup_manifest_mismatch` for outbox/hash/schema/path-set drift;
`cleanup_scan_limit_exceeded` for any frozen enumeration bound excess;
`cleanup_namespace_unsafe` for a new, changed, unsupported, or alien entry;
`file_unlink_failed`, `directory_rmdir_failed`, or
`directory_fsync_failed` for a mapped failure of that exact already-authorized
operation. Later predicates do not replace the first code; a retry recomputes
from the beginning and clears a prior code only after the previously failing
predicate and all earlier predicates pass. Independent negatives mutate every
enum member and state pairing, simultaneous-predicate combination and
precedence edge, and reject empty, 65-byte, uppercase, hyphenated, control,
non-ASCII, unknown, raw-OS-message, absolute-path, and filename-derived
values.

For a nonnull-path deletion, admission first performs a read-only pre-scan
outside the writer transaction. It refuses more than 512 total manifest
entries, 256 directories, nesting deeper than 16 components below the item
directory, any relative path longer than 1,024 UTF-8 bytes, more than 65,536
cumulative relative-path UTF-8 bytes, more than 268,435,456 cumulative bytes of present
regular files to hash, or a compact manifest larger than 262,144 bytes. It
also refuses when the exact empty-manifest deletion header exceeds 65,536
bytes or the complete section-7.8 command-envelope projection exceeds its
958,529-byte derived maximum or 1,048,576-byte transport cap.
Inside the later `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, the service recomputes the entire exact
tree and all hashes under the same limits and requires equality with the
pre-scan token before inserting the cleanup row or deleting anything. A
boundary-equal tree is accepted; every `+1` dimension refuses without DML or
filesystem mutation. Thus the authoritative locked scan is finite and
bounded; paging or higher limits require a separately reviewed protocol.
For a null-path candidate, the outside pre-scan and locked recomputation both
produce the exact empty manifest and the locked database projections prove the
three artifact rowsets empty; no item-ID bytes enter a path API.

The seven filesystem limits are mutually satisfiable, not merely independent
numbers. A checked-in descriptor-bound solver constructs seven distinct real
tree witnesses, one for equality on each axis while all six other dimensions
remain legal, then emits each exact compact manifest, measured dimension
tuple, and SHA-256. The 262,144-byte manifest witness uses at most 512 safe
regular-file objects and a deterministic mix of ordinary ASCII and
backslash-bearing path components so JSON escaping can tune the exact byte
length while decoded cumulative path bytes remain at most 65,536; it never
uses an invalid/dot/slash component. The 65,536 cumulative-path witness stays
within 512 entries, and the 512-entry/256-directory/16-depth/1,024-single-path/
268,435,456-file-byte witnesses each stay below the manifest cap. The
acceptance validator independently regenerates every witness, verifies real
filesystem metadata and all seven measured values, accepts equality, and
mutates only the selected dimension to `+1` while keeping a valid witness for
the other six. If any equality witness cannot be generated on a supported
platform, the descriptor is unsatisfiable and activation refuses.

The nonnull-path manifest is a bytewise-relative-path-sorted compact JSON array over the
union of every capture-artifact row path, every on-disk regular file, the
exact item directory when present, and every nested directory below it. There
is exactly one entry per relative path; the item directory's path is the
exact item ID. The null-path manifest is exactly `[]` and contains no object.
Each nonempty-manifest object has this exact key order and scalar shape:

```text
relative_path    JSON string
entry_type       "file"|"directory"
artifact_id      JSON string for a row, otherwise null
source           "row"|"disk"|"row_and_disk"
present          JSON Boolean
device           canonical unsigned decimal JSON string when present, else null
inode            canonical unsigned decimal JSON string when present, else null
size_bytes       canonical unsigned decimal JSON string when present, else null
link_count       canonical unsigned decimal JSON string when present, else null
content_sha256   exact lowercase hexadecimal when present, else null
```

A row-only missing file uses `entry_type='file'`, `source='row'`,
`present=false`, and null filesystem fields. A disk-only file uses null
`artifact_id`, `entry_type='file'`, `source='disk'`, `present=true`, and all
non-null filesystem fields. A matched row/file uses
`source='row_and_disk'`. A directory always has null `artifact_id`,
`entry_type='directory'`, `source='disk'`, `present=true`, non-null
device/inode, and null size/link-count/content hash; the separately stored
item-directory pair must equal its directory entry. The 256-directory limit
includes that item directory: 256 total directories passes and a 257th
refuses before DML or filesystem mutation. Empty nested directories are therefore bound
before database commit and cannot be confused with a later unmanifested
shape during crash resume.

Nonnull paths use `/`, contain no empty/dot/dot-dot component, begin with the exact
safe item-ID component, and are globally unique. Symlinks, non-regular
non-directory entries, file link count other than one, duplicate normalized
paths, duplicate present device/inode identities, row/hash/size mismatch, and
cross-item aliases refuse before mutation. Every cleanup resume revalidates
the complete still-present file/directory identity projection against the
persisted manifest and refuses any new or changed entry before unlink or
`rmdir`. The manifest contains no body, title, URL, artifact bytes, absolute
path, or raw error. Its SHA-256 uses the exact compact UTF-8 JSON bytes, and
independent vectors cover all three file source shapes, absent item
directory, empty and multilevel directories, quarantined safe regular files,
directory identity drift/new entry, and maximum platform-width device/inode
values. A safe disk-only or quarantined regular file may be removed only by
this explicit item-root deletion protocol; routine reconciliation never
claims or removes it.

The cleanup row is immutable except for
`prepared -> committed -> cleaning -> done`, attempts, stable error, and
timestamps. The sole `prepared -> committed` transition is the exact
immediately-post-cascade `outbox_commit_dml` phase and its built-in
`AFTER UPDATE OF state` transactional-permit proof trigger described above;
it consumes the matching permit and is impossible outside the still-held
seven-phase native role and transaction. Every other
state/attempt/error change and row deletion requires the FULL-durable
connection and its named cleanup permit. Every filesystem `lstat`, path-based unlink under the
section-6.4 threat model, directory enumeration, `rmdir`, and directory
`fsync` occurs synchronously with no `await` inside a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` batch.
Each cleaning batch arms `transaction_outcome_observer_v1` before BEGIN. An
exact `begin_refused` retains the unchanged outbox and cleanup pin, admits no
filesystem or service-store action, and enters bounded retry. After successful
BEGIN a manifested `commit_not_attempted` sentinel remains set through every
pre-COMMIT fault. The batch then handles at most 32 bytewise-first
still-present manifest files, revalidates every outbox/root/path identity,
unlinks them, and fsyncs every affected containing directory. Only then does it install the
exact native cleanup-batch prepared role, binding/row-count contract, and
authorizer trace and execute the guarded state/attempt update before commit.
Every cleanup-batch COMMIT uses the same armed
`transaction_outcome_observer_v1` and exact
`open|committed|rolled_back|indeterminate` classifier. Every post-BEGIN,
pre-COMMIT fault must retain the exact `commit_not_attempted` pair and apply
the observer classifier; only `open|rolled_back|indeterminate` are legal and
`committed` is impossible without raw COMMIT `SQLITE_DONE`. `open` alone
executes the hard-coded rollback and must become the exact
`rolled_back` tuple. `rolled_back` prepares no SQL, retains the unchanged
outbox/pin and reconciles any manifest-authorized filesystem lead.
`committed` closes and reopens before any later file action and proves the
exact advanced outbox plus manifest-authorized filesystem absence.
`indeterminate` prepares no SQL, closes/quarantines, performs no
service-store mutation, and admits no later unlink, database transition, or
success until closed-image outbox and filesystem reconciliation is
definitive.
An abrupt stop may leave the filesystem ahead of rolled-back database state;
replay accepts exact absence, fsyncs again, and installs a fresh exact
prepared role. No
worker retains authority or performs a filesystem action after releasing that
writer lock, so concurrent startup and retry workers cannot become stale
unlinkers.

For a null-path outbox, each cleanup attempt revalidates root identity, the
exact empty manifest/hash, null directory identities, unchanged item/instance
fence, and absence of the three artifact rowsets. It performs no path
construction, `lstat`, enumeration, unlink, `rmdir`, or path-parent fsync and
proceeds directly to the same sealed atomic tombstone finalization.

After all nonnull-path files are durably absent, finalization first acquires
and durably verifies the fresh `purpose='finalization_commit'` signing
reservation under its bounded 5,000-ms deadline. Only then does it enter the
one FULL `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` after arming
`transaction_outcome_observer_v1`. An exact `begin_refused` atomically
deletes the held final reservation plus empty action array through
`delete_reservation_bundle_v1`, admits no namespace/database/keystore
mutation, releases the transient gate, and enters bounded retry. After
successful BEGIN a manifested `commit_not_attempted` sentinel remains set
through every pre-COMMIT fault. While that writer lock remains held it revalidates
that no new namespace entry exists, removes only empty validated nested
subdirectories deepest-first and the item directory with `rmdir`, and fsyncs
the containing parent immediately after each removal through the artifact
root. After the final root fsync it executes and finalizes the one sealed
`final_completion_clock_read`, freezes that exact INTEGER, computes and
durably appends the exact final signing action through the already-held
nonblocking capability, then installs the exact native cleanup-finalization
prepared role with that same completion-clock binding,
expected one-row outer change, dependent tombstone/outbox change counts, and
authorizer trace.

One guarded outer cleanup transition changes the exact matching row only
`cleaning -> done`, thereby consuming its one reserved terminal-capacity
slot. Its built-in relational trigger chain uses only the bound completion
clock, inserts the exact bounded `item_deletion_request_tombstones` row into
that same slot, proves the full capacity sum is unchanged and at most 65,536,
and deliberately retains the durable null-error `done` row. The first FULL
commit therefore publishes one exact `done+tombstone` closed image. Its
`outcome_control` finalizes every statement exactly once and classifies
`open|committed|rolled_back|indeterminate` through
`transaction_outcome_observer_v1`. Every post-BEGIN, pre-COMMIT fault retains
the exact `commit_not_attempted` pair and applies that classifier; only
`open|rolled_back|indeterminate` are legal and `committed` is impossible
without raw COMMIT `SQLITE_DONE`. Only `open` executes the exact rollback
route and must become the exact `rolled_back` tuple;
`rolled_back` prepares no SQL, restores `cleaning`, and atomically deletes the
exact held final bundle only after the frozen namespace/outbox preimage proof;
`committed`, including COMMIT `SQLITE_DONE` followed by a finalize or driver
error, never rolls back and enters promotion recovery; `indeterminate`
prepares no SQL, closes/quarantines, performs no service-store mutation, and
preserves the reservation, barrier, and store quarantine until closed-image
reconciliation is definitive.

After definitive first commit and writer-lock release, the service verifies
the exact reservation/action/`done+tombstone` tuple, raises final-key retention
to `block_until`, and durably promotes the reservation. While `done` retains
the complete promotion preimage, it atomically compare-deletes the old cleanup
pin plus promoted reservation/action bundle through
`delete_finalization_authority_v1`, verifies `ack_ready`, and only then runs
the second sealed FULL ack transaction that deletes `done` as the final
mutation. Failures before the first commit restore `cleaning`; failures after
it retain a recoverable `done+tombstone` plus either all finalization
authority or exact `ack_ready`; failures after ack require no service-store
cleanup. Replay re-verifies exact
namespace absence and repeats every required directory fsync when the first
commit did not occur. `prepared` is transaction-internal and cannot commit
with a live item. If corruption or unsupported external SQL nevertheless
exposes it after restart, startup fails closed without filesystem mutation;
“quarantine” is not a persisted cleanup state. Direct SQL cannot advance,
complete, or forget cleanup because it lacks the exact native prepared role
and allowed authorizer source/action trace.

After SQLite WAL recovery and before endpoint admission, key rotation or
retirement, janitor, backup, restore, or a new deletion, startup acquires one
per-logical-store service-private startup/recovery controller latch. The latch
closes endpoint admission and makes this process the sole startup/recovery
database actor, but it is not a mutable keystore mutex and no such mutex is
held during SQLite work. Before `S1`, the latch performs the sole
fresh-process-generation absent-runtime materialization defined above. An
inactive exact durable tuple becomes `startup_closed`; an active exact
barrier/controller tuple becomes `retirement_recovery_closed` with its
byte-exact bound hash. Lost materialization response, durable movement, an
already-present exact poststate, and an invalid preexisting slot follow that
closed rule and cannot be mistaken for ordinary snapshot drift.
If an exact `ordinary/unclaimed|claimed` slot already exists when this startup
latch is acquired, one expected-tuple CAS first changes it to
`startup_closed`, invalidates its authority/channel/claim, and keeps admission
closed; a stale ordinary frame cannot survive a new startup handoff.
Under one service-linearizable read, snapshot `S1`
contains the complete nonrollbackable retirement control record, exact
barrier and exclusive controller/operation record, the complete runtime
authority projection with ordinary authority/owner/channel/state/claim or
controller capability/owner/channel/state/claim bindings, each resume state,
and the bound-tuple hash plus its exact preimage components, receipt
count/head and nonnull head receipt plus hash index, global create-only
candidate receipt lookup for each of at most 32 live ring keys, complete live
ring and current-role map, active-store binding, and every referenced
key/receipt absence or presence proof. Startup uses no individual durable or
runtime read from that tuple to admit, recover, resume, or quarantine.

With endpoint admission still closed and the controller latch still held, the
sole startup actor performs the exact SQLite closed-image and eight-class
matrix reads bound to `S1`; no other startup/recovery actor may mutate that
database projection. It then takes a second complete service-linearizable
snapshot `S2`. If `S2` is not byte-equal to `S1`, it discards the database
observation and restarts from a fresh `S1` without admission, mutation, or
quarantine. If they are equal, one service-linearizable compare-and-handoff
requires that tuple still byte-equal `S2` and atomically transfers the
controller latch either to the exact barrier/controller owner (or its
definitively authorized crash takeover) under the retirement fence, or to
ordinary admission only when both barrier and controller are absent. There is
no gap between the final equality test and that handoff. The
barrier/controller-absent branch produces the exact nonexportable
ordinary-admission authority used by normal admission and by the initial
retirement-creation bootstrap: the handoff invalidates every prior ordinary
authority and atomically changes `startup_closed -> ordinary` on the startup
actor's established service-held channel with fresh
authority/owner/channel IDs and a fresh request-bound resume claim proposed
on that channel before the CAS,
`ordinary_channel_state=live`, `ordinary_resume_state=unclaimed`, and a hash
bound to the complete `S2` tuple. The handoff then executes the general
same-channel compare-and-resume and opens ordinary admission only after
`claimed`; a lost response recovers that same authority on that same channel,
while channel invalidation returns to `startup_closed` for a fresh handoff. The
barrier-present branch requires an exact claimed live controller runtime
binding or performs the definitive takeover plus compare-and-resume before
handoff. Creation atomically transfers that same ordinary authority from the
ordinary gate to the retirement fence and installs the epoch-one capability,
never in a later step. A legal retirement creation,
controller takeover/operation transition, abort, proof append, receipt append,
clearance, key creation/import, rotation, role change, restore, or binding
change before the handoff therefore forces a retry; one after the handoff
serializes after the selected state, observes its admission gate and
controller authority, and follows the ordinary barrier/quiescence rules.
Snapshot drift alone never quarantines.

Within either byte-equal snapshot, control `active_retirement_id` is null iff
both barrier and controller are absent. When a barrier is present, control
`generation,active_retirement_id` exactly equal barrier
`retirement_generation,retirement_id`, the controller cross-equals that same
identity/binding, and the state-specific prior/current receipt count/head
formulas above hold. A no-barrier baseline is normal only with null active ID,
controller absence, a valid completed tuple/head, and either exact
`startup_closed` while the startup latch remains held or one exact
tuple-bound `ordinary` authority with `unclaimed|claimed` while handoff
recovery remains fenced. Ordinary admission requires the latter to be
`claimed`. `quiescing` permits only
the matrix actions and exact internal continuation needed to finish all
preexisting logical-store deletion work and then the ordered double-collect
complete-store producer/authority zero proof.
`draining|database_proved|retired` permits only the next retirement-state
action with the frozen `N`; ordinary janitors and producers remain blocked.
The candidate key remains present through every state that can leave one of
its tombstones, while retirement occurs only after the complete two-table
drain and sealed zero proof. Only one internally consistent, byte-equal
`S1`/database/`S2` projection that proves an absent, rolled-back, partial, or
mismatched required counterpart within the
control/barrier/receipt/key/database/role-map/runtime-authority tuple
quarantines before the matrix or any service admission.

Acceptance injects creation, controller takeover and every operation phase,
abort, database-proof persistence, receipt append, clearance, key
creation/import, rotation, role-map change, restore, and active-binding change
before and after every `S1`, database-read, `S2`, and compare-and-handoff edge.
It also exercises absent-runtime inactive/active materialization, its lost
response and durable drift, every bound-preimage nullable/set/order mutation,
ordinary and controller authority/channel liveness and resume claim/state
before and after every snapshot and compare-and-resume, duplicate same-channel
resume and different-channel/claim substitution, and abort/clear reverse
handoff with channel invalidation immediately before the CAS, immediately
after the CAS, and before/after claim. Response loss, stale-authority replay,
later retirement without restart, and startup/successor races are crossed
with each state. Each
drift interleaving retries without false quarantine, while a mutation
serialized after handoff sees the selected exact ordinary-admission authority
or controller-owned retirement-fence state.

Subject to that barrier recovery, startup applies this exact eight-class
matrix. Every row requires byte/storage-class-exact present-or-absent
projections and cross-equality for the reservation, ordered action array,
active record, outbox, tombstone, key pin, and retention state; the named
action is the only permitted next mutation.

| Class | Closed recovered shape | Sole startup action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Initial `held` reservation plus exact committed outbox and complete caller-tombstone/action projection | Classify committed, raise retention, install the cleanup pin, promote, verify, and atomically delete that reservation bundle before cleanup admission. |
| 2 | Initial `held` reservation, no outbox or deletion tombstone, and the exact unchanged item/vector/caller preimage with zero permit or new caller tombstone | Classify rolled back and atomically delete that held reservation bundle without installing a pin. |
| 3 | Initial `promoted` reservation plus exact `committed` outbox, action projection, retention floor, and cleanup pin | Verify the already-promoted action and atomically delete that reservation bundle; then admit normal cleanup. An initial promoted reservation with `cleaning` is class 8. |
| 4 | Final `held` reservation plus exact durable `done+tombstone` and final signing action | Classify committed, raise final-key retention, promote, and continue at atomic finalization-authority deletion before ack. |
| 5 | Final `held` reservation plus exact `committed|cleaning` outbox, no deletion tombstone, and an unchanged reserved capacity unit | Classify rolled back, atomically delete the held final reservation bundle, and resume namespace cleanup from that outbox. |
| 6 | Final `promoted` reservation plus exact durable `done+tombstone`, complete final action, final retention floor, and the old cleanup pin | Reconstruct and verify promotion while `done` exists, then execute or reconcile atomic `delete_finalization_authority_v1`. |
| 7 | Either exact `ack_ready`: no reservation/actions, exact durable `done+tombstone`, no old cleanup pin, and the internal constant-time proof that a matching retained HMAC key has retention floor at or above `block_until`; or exact `ack_committed`: no reservation/actions, no cleanup outbox, the unchanged exact tombstone, no old cleanup pin, and the same matching-key retention-floor proof | From `ack_ready`, execute or recover the sealed ack deletion as the final mutation. From `ack_committed`, perform no database, filesystem, or service-store mutation; finish the post-ack response only when the same live controller/caller channel still exists, otherwise release only the deletion-recovery latch and let a later identical authenticated request receive replay. Admit ordinary service only when retirement-control active ID, barrier, and exclusive retirement controller are all absent and the runtime projection is exact tuple-bound `ordinary` with `ordinary_channel_state=live`, `ordinary_resume_state=claimed`, and no controller capability/channel/claim; under `quiescing`, continue the retirement state machine with ordinary service still fenced. |
| 8 | Any mixed, duplicate, missing, noncontiguous, orphan, partial, or cross-unequal reservation/action/outbox/tombstone/pin/retention shape, including parent-only or action-only reservation state, initial promoted plus `cleaning`, held-final tombstone without `done`, `done` without its tombstone outside exact class 4, 6, or 7, or DB state requiring a reservation with none | Classify indeterminate and quarantine the logical store without SQL, filesystem, keystore, or endpoint mutation. |

Outside those seven valid recovery classes, no-reservation
`committed|cleaning` is a normal cleanup state only with its one exact
`(logical_store_id,deletion_id,request_authenticator_key_id)` cleanup pin; it
resumes only ordinary batch or final cleanup and never recreates the item or
mints replacement authority. A missing or multiply mapped normal pin, an
initial `cleaning` outbox with a promoted reservation, an initial outbox with
no matching initial action, item absence without its
initial committed outbox, or any identity/hash/state mismatch enters matrix
class 8.

An `items` insert guard rejects an ID while any cleanup outbox has that exact
`item_id`, including a null-path row. Every artifact-operation insert rejects
an existing cleanup outbox for its item ID. The final
cleanup transaction holds the writer lock until durable namespace absence and
the first `done+tombstone` commit complete together, so a new item cannot
enter the namespace between the last check, directory fsync, and release of
ownership. The durable `done` row continues to block recreation until verified
promotion and ack deletion. Before physical completion, an exact old deletion
request resumes only through the cleanup outbox. After completion, it resolves
only through the bounded keyed-authenticator tombstone. Once that tombstone is
strictly expired and removed, no historical identity or request detail
remains. A newly created item uses the section-7.1 live-unique bounded CSPRNG
allocator; stale queued and non-queued work must still match its exact current
instance and revision, while authority expiry remains an independent fence.

## 8. Trigger replacement and backfill

### 8.1 Exact recovery eligibility

Drop and recreate only `items_enqueue_youtube_transcript_recovery`. Preserve
the complete migration-021 predicate:

```text
(source_platform IN ('youtube','youtube_short') OR source_type='youtube')
AND
(capture_quality='metadata_only' OR extraction_warning IN (
  'no_transcript',
  'youtube_transcript_fetch_metadata_only',
  'youtube_antibot_metadata_only'
))
```

Add only:

```text
COALESCE(extraction_method,'') <> 'browser_link_only_v1'
AND no status='active' transcript source exists for the item
```

The new insert stamps both
`expected_item_instance_id=NEW.item_instance_id` and
`expected_content_revision=NEW.content_revision`.
The application eligibility, requeue, and backfill predicates use the same
shared contract. Automatic YouTube Short recovery remains included.

### 8.2 Enrichment and embedding enqueue triggers

Recreate `items_enqueue_enrichment` and `items_enqueue_embedding` only as
needed to stamp the current item instance and `content_revision` on newly
created singleton jobs. Preserve their historical event and state predicates. Do not add
manual-generation semantics or remove the legacy embedding trigger.

Every other item trigger and index, including FTS and workflow objects, must
remain byte-identical to the preflight snapshot.

### 8.3 Data mapping

- Every existing item receives one live-unique immutable CSPRNG 128-bit
  instance through the section-7.1 bounded retry and starts at
  `content_revision=1`.
- Every existing transcript, enrichment, embedding, and note-index job and
  every existing transcript attempt receives its owning item's instance; the
  applicable jobs also receive its revision.
- Before schema verification or commit, the locked migration reasserts zero
  null/non-text/empty `items.id`, `capture_artifacts.id`, and
  `note_index_jobs.item_id` values, fatally decodes and byte-for-byte
  re-encodes every one of those UTF-8 identities, and proves every note-index
  owner joins its exact item instance. While retaining the migration writer
  lock, a validation-only invocation of all three exact deletion component
  encoders runs for every item against the actual S28 descriptor and stored
  values. It uses a frozen nonpersisted legal header sentinel—43 ASCII `A`
  bytes for `deletion_id` and integer zero for `deleted_at`—constructs
  caller-tombstone projections without DML using a fixture-only keyed
  authenticator service, discards the resulting digests, and requires complete
  success. No deletion tombstone is synthesized because no deletion has
  completed. The transition binary repeats the
  storage-class, nonempty, fatal UTF-8 roundtrip, ownership, descriptor, and
  full encoder-success assertions immediately before S28 activation.
- New input/mutation fingerprints, claim hashes, renewal timestamps, and leases
  start null across transcript, enrichment, embedding, and note queues.
  Preflight guarantees no live claim; each transition claimant computes both
  fingerprints before it can dispatch.
- Every historical policy row receives
  `processing_mode='not_applicable'`.
- Historical source revision/delete-by fields remain null.
- Every policy, source, segment, job, attempt, item, and workflow ID and every
  historical state/counter/timestamp remains unchanged.
- Every `batch_id`, including opaque binding and reservation strings, remains
  byte-identical. Migration 028 neither parses nor reclassifies it.
- Revision-event rows, holds, extension requests, caller-request tombstones,
  recovery receipts, artifact-write operations, item-owned deletion requests,
  deletion-request tombstones, artifact-write request bindings, and
  artifact-cleanup jobs start empty.
- Every validated legacy capture-artifact absolute path receives its frozen
  canonical root-relative key; the absolute `path` bytes and artifact/file
  contents remain unchanged.
- The eligibility backfill inserts only a missing job. It never resets or
  rewrites an existing job.
- No `legacy_unproven`, blanket client-storage classification, source
  inference, or automatic supersession is created.

### 8.4 Universal title and vector reset authority

Every current title-mutating path is moved through one reviewed helper inside
its owning immediate transaction: ordinary manual item update, existing-item
URL upgrade/repair, realtime enrichment, batch result apply, automatic
recovery, and synthetic attachment. A static SQL inventory fails if any other
application statement can update `items.title`.

Before any body, title, note, enrichment, batch, recovery, attachment,
embedding, repair, or deletion path removes/replaces chunks or vectors, it
runs the exact global `auditVectorIndex(db)` under the same writer lock and
requires `safeToEnableWriters=true`. Any anomaly causes zero mutation. After a
successful reset it reruns the audit and proves the exact expected
rowid/chunk/source-kind delta.

When title bytes change, the helper first invalidates every generic
body/summary embedding whose frozen input includes title: it removes those
vectors before their bridges/chunks and rearms the singleton embedding job at
the same content revision with the new exact input/mutation fingerprints. A
title-only edit therefore cannot leave a searchable vector built from the old
title.

When a manual-note state also exists, the same helper binds the exact note
epoch/generation and title/note input, removes every old `manual_note` vector
before its bridge/chunk, and makes the indexed pointer non-current. It rearms
only an independently authorized standard-mode `include_in_ai=1` note at that
same epoch/generation. An AI-off note remains purged, and
`manual-transcript-lab` starts no note worker. Both generic and manual-note
rules apply even when body bytes do not change.

## 9. Required transaction contracts

### 9.1 Fixture-only synthetic attachment

Stage 2 includes an internal service or test harness with no route, UI,
extension, live URL, or network capability. It accepts only a packaged
no-network fixture and fails before body or database access in production.

One immediate transaction:

1. reconciles the random `caller_request_id`; the same hash returns the stored
   terminal result while authority remains current, while a changed hash
   returns `caller_request_id_mismatch` with no mutation;
2. resolves the exact item/current revision and computes the complete mutation
   preimage under the writer lock, including the immutable item instance;
3. for an existing target, evaluates the exact section-7.7 first-match
   conflict order—item instance, content revision, different active source,
   transcript-bearing unproved legacy item, different existing note,
   processing hold, then unresolved batch binding—and persists only that
   same-named immutable code;
4. recognizes the same active source text hash as a duplicate without another
   source, policy, or hold;
5. inserts a new item or updates one eligible weak item, allowing the revision
   trigger to establish revision 1 or `expected + 1`;
6. removes only stale body-derived vectors before their chunks, clears body
   summary/quotes/category/enrichment timestamps, removes auto tags and
   AI/system item-topic links, removes stale embedding work, and preserves
   manual note content and manual tags. If title changes, it also removes
   `manual_note` vectors/chunks, sets their indexed pointer non-current, and
   rearms the exact existing note epoch/generation according to D-015:
   independently authorized standard-mode notes may reindex, while AI-off
   notes remain purged and `manual-transcript-lab` starts no note worker;
7. rearms the legacy enrichment singleton with the applied content revision
   but leaves it nonclaimable because the hold is inserted before commit;
8. inserts the exact browser policy, active source, and ordered segments;
9. inserts the opaque held-attachment identity and processing hold;
10. resolves any transcript job to done, clears its claim hash/lease/claim
    time and retry time, preserves attempt history, and records
    `last_provider='browser_visible_transcript'`;
11. applies the reviewed optional note behavior with `include_in_ai=0`;
12. inserts one immutable extension-request receipt with its bounded authority
    expiry after proving the exact source/segment/hold graph;
13. commits and constructs the response from committed rows.

The executed failpoints must equal the 21 names in the
`synthetic_attachment` registry in the acceptance JSON. Its midpoint cases use
at least two vectors and at least three segments. Each injected pre-commit
failure restores the exact prior database and vector state.
Commit-before-response replay returns the one receipt. A fresh
`existing`-mode request targeting the same item, immutable item instance, and
current revision with the same content records `duplicate` without a second
active source. A fresh `new`-mode request retains its three null target
precondition frames and follows new-target creation semantics; it is not
covered by that existing-target duplicate shape. Different active content
conflicts without mutation.

Inside the transaction before mutation and again before commit,
vector/bridge/chunk counts and ownership are compared against the safe graph.
Every removed vector rowid and chunk ID must match the exact source-kind reset
set; no anomaly is tolerated.

This harness proves the schema can represent a future attachment. It is not
permission to ship or exercise browser capture.

### 9.2 Atomic automatic-recovery success

Provider fetch remains outside SQLite. Claim creates a fresh raw token, stores
only its hash, stamps the current item instance/revision and exact
`youtube-recovery-input-v1` plus mutation-preimage fingerprints, and uses the
exact lease contract in section 9.5. Before claim, the worker performs the
durable job-ID receipt reconciliation from section 7.9.

One immediate apply/finalize transaction:

1. reconciles an existing receipt by unique job ID; a complete terminal graph
   returns the committed result and a mismatch fails closed;
2. re-reads job and item and requires the exact item, `running` state, attempt
   number, claim hash, unexpired lease, expected/current item instance and
   revision, historical
   weak eligibility, exact recomputed provider input and mutation preimage, no
   link-only marker, no active source, no hold, and the exact batch
   classification in section 9.4. A safe stale binding remains eligible and
   is cleared atomically; its late result is fenced by the new revision;
3. removes stale body-derived vectors before chunks, deletes stale embedding
   work, auto tags, and item-topic links, and clears stale body-derived fields
   while preserving manual note content and manual tags. A title change purges
   stale manual-note vectors/chunks and rearms the exact current note
   epoch/generation under D-015;
4. updates item body and reviewed capture metadata exactly once and reads the
   trigger-produced `expected + 1` revision;
5. rearms the legacy enrichment singleton with that applied revision and
   clears claim/lease state;
6. inserts no policy, source, or segment;
7. inserts one immutable success attempt carrying the exact input/mutation,
   claim, provider-contact, and revision identity and null
   source/artifact/error fields;
8. reduces the provider-health outcome through the same transaction handle;
9. inserts one immutable recovery receipt;
10. compare-and-swaps the exact job to done, records the attempt/provider,
    clears claim/lease/retry state, and preserves unrelated history;
11. commits and constructs the response from committed rows.

Automatic recovery does not call `saveCaptureArtifacts` and creates no file or
capture-artifact row. Existing artifact rows and files remain byte-for-byte
unchanged.

The executed failpoints must equal the 18 `recovery_success` names and five
`recovery_non_success` names in the acceptance registry. Midpoint cases use at
least two vectors. Every pre-commit failure restores the exact database and
vector state. Commit-before-response loss reconciles the same receipt without
another provider request, body apply, revision advance, attempt, health
reduction, artifact write, or job transition.

Every current non-success claim is also finalized by one immediate transaction:

1. reconcile an attempt by exact job and claim hash; an exact immutable match
   returns its stored terminal/retry result, while a mismatch fails closed;
2. recheck the complete claim, lease, revision, input/mutation fingerprints,
   item, hold/source, and batch authority without mutating body-derived state;
3. insert exactly one immutable `retryable_error` attempt with `retryable=1`
   or one `terminal_error` attempt with `retryable=0`, recording
   `provider_contacted` as exact 0/1; only reviewed stable error/status fields
   may be non-null and source/artifact/result fields are null;
4. apply the closed provider-health row below in the same transaction;
5. for retryable results, set `retryable_error` and
   `next_run_at = finished_at + 1_800_000 * max(1,min(8,2^(attempt_number-1)))`;
   a throttling result instead uses the later of that value and the committed
   provider cooldown and preserves the existing three-additional-attempt
   window; exhausted non-throttled retries become `manual_needed`;
6. for terminal results set `manual_needed`, null `next_run_at`, and set the
   completion time; in all cases bind `last_attempt_id`/provider/stable error
   and clear claimed-at, token, renewal, and lease fields by exact CAS.

The unique attempt claim key and exact replay lookup make the attempt, health
reduction, and job transition at most once. A stale/lost claim writes none of
them and is handled only by the exact sweep contract.

Provider-health reduction follows this closed matrix:

| Provider contacted | Claim current at finalization | Normalized result | Health mutation |
|---|---|---|---|
| No | Any | skipped/pre-dispatch error | none |
| Yes | No | any result | none |
| Yes | Yes | success | one success reduction in the success transaction |
| Yes | Yes | retryable error | one retryable reduction with its attempt/job transaction |
| Yes | Yes | terminal error | one terminal reduction with its attempt/job transaction |

An expired, swept, lost, deleted, held, input-drifted, or revision-stale claim
is not current. The unique attempt/claim identity makes each contacted
reduction at most once. Replay first reconciles terminal state and never
reduces health again.

### 9.3 Shared stale-result and hold fence

All current body-derived writers are audited:

- existing-item URL upgrade;
- automatic transcript recovery;
- realtime enrichment;
- batch selection, dispatch reconciliation, and result apply;
- embedding;
- note indexing's independently authorized title/note input under D-015.

Before any provider/network await, a queued claimant records current revision,
immutable item instance, exact provider-ready input and mutation-preimage
fingerprints, fresh token hash, and lease. A non-queued URL upgrade records
the item instance/current revision, both fingerprints, and a fresh
process-local operation identity.
Immediately before dispatch and apply, the writer rebuilds and compares both
fingerprints and rechecks the same item instance, current revision,
claim/operation identity, lease, hold or D-015 note policy, item existence, and
source eligibility. Apply uses a conditional write inside one immediate
transaction. Item absence or any mismatch with the exact current live
instance therefore fences even a non-queued result whose revision and content
bytes otherwise coincide.

A mismatch returns a stable stale/blocked result and writes no body, summary,
quotes, category, tags, topics, chunks, vectors, terminal success, or
success-attributed provider usage. Held source/body work is excluded
independently at claim, immediately before dispatch, and immediately before
apply. An independently authorized standard-mode note uses its epoch,
generation, fresh token, exact input/mutation fingerprints, consent, lease,
and D-015 mode checks instead of the transcript hold;
`manual-transcript-lab` never starts that worker.

The Stage 1 compatibility wrappers remain safe on schema 027. The Stage 2
transition binary prepares 028-only SQL only after exact schema attestation.

### 9.4 Batch reservation state machine

Generic claim leases never reinterpret or clear Stage 1 batch authority.

The only valid encodings are:

- unresolved: `opaque-reservation-v1:` plus exactly 43 base64url characters
  matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}`;
- resolved: `opaque-v1:` plus the unpadded base64url encoding of exact UTF-8
  `JSON.stringify([providerBatchId,alias])`; decode then re-encode must equal
  the stored bytes, the alias uses the rule above, and provider ID is 1..512
  UTF-8 bytes with no control character;
- legacy resolved: a 1..512-byte control-free provider ID that starts with
  neither reserved prefix; it has no alias and retains the current read-only
  custom-ID compatibility.

Any reserved-prefix string that fails its canonical rule is malformed and
blocks; it is never treated as a legacy provider ID.

The generic claim fields are `claimed_at`, `claim_token_hash`,
`lease_last_renewed_at`, and `lease_expires_at`. `idle-claim` means all four
are null. `current-live-claim` means all four are non-null and well formed,
the lease is current, and the stored item instance/revision/input/mutation
tuple is complete and equals the current item and recomputation.
`well-formed-idle-expected` means the item instance is present and current,
the revision is positive, and the two fingerprints are either both null
(migration-backfilled or never claimed) or both valid lowercase SHA-256;
partial fingerprint shape is never valid.

The exact local classifications are the following precedence-free,
disjoint, exhaustive predicates:

- `none-idle`: `batch_id IS NULL`; the exact item/job pair is
  `(pending,pending)`, `(done,done)`, or `(error,error)`; the claim is exactly
  `idle-claim`; and the expected tuple is
  `well-formed-idle-expected`.
- `none-running`: `batch_id IS NULL`; the exact pair is
  `(running,running)`; and the row has exactly `current-live-claim`.
- `unresolved`: the canonical reservation exists; the exact pair is
  `(batched,batched)`; the claim is exactly `idle-claim`; and the expected
  item instance/revision/input/mutation tuple is complete and current. It is
  quarantined, nonpollable, and nonresubmittable.
- `live resolved`: a canonical resolved or legacy value exists; the exact
  pair is `(batched,batched)`; the claim is exactly `idle-claim`; and that same
  complete expected tuple is current.
- `safe stale`: a canonical resolved or legacy value exists; the exact pair is
  `(pending,pending)`, `(done,done)`, or `(error,error)`; the claim is exactly
  `idle-claim`; and the expected tuple is
  `well-formed-idle-expected` without requiring its revision/fingerprints to
  match current content.
- `integrity block`: the Boolean negation of the union of those five
  predicates. This includes every malformed encoding, mismatched state pair,
  one-sided running/batched state, partial or extra claim shape, missing or
  wrong item instance, partial fingerprints, missing/expired live authority,
  and claim fields on any batched or safe-stale row.

The public `none` classification is exactly the union of `none-idle` and
`none-running`; no precedence rule is used.

The state machine is:

1. selection CAS requires exact `none-idle` pending state, current item
   instance/revision, exact newly computed input/mutation fingerprints, no
   hold/deletion, and no generic claim; it changes both states to `batched`
   and persists a fresh unresolved alias before provider contact;
2. dispatch rereads that exact tuple and request bytes. A valid provider
   response CAS changes only the exact reservation to the canonical resolved
   binding. Timeout, exception, invalid response, lost response, or process
   loss leaves it unresolved;
3. generic renew/sweep skips every non-null reservation or binding;
4. poll/result apply accepts only the exact live resolved tuple, provider ID,
   alias/custom ID, item, job, revision, input/mutation fingerprints, and
   current hold/deletion state. Hold arrival, any drift, or deletion makes the
   result inert without authorizing resend;
5. an independently authoritative body replacement may clear only `safe
   stale` in its own apply transaction. It never clears `unresolved`, `live
   resolved`, or `integrity block`;
6. explicit item deletion is the sole exception: it may delete an item in any
   batch classification without polling, clearing, resubmitting, or declaring
   the provider outcome. The sealed deletion permit binds the exact stored
   batch bytes/state before the item-root cascade, and item absence makes every
   late dispatch reconciliation or result apply inert.

Tests cover timeout after provider acceptance, invalid/lost response, generic
lease expiry, hold arrival, item deletion, polling races, stale result apply,
all malformed/state-mismatch cells, and recovery of a safe legacy/resolved
stale binding.

### 9.5 Lease and sweep contract

Each claim transaction reads database time once as
`CAST(unixepoch('subsec')*1000 AS INTEGER)`. Apply/renew requires
`now_ms < lease_expires_at`; sweep requires
`now_ms >= lease_expires_at`. Equality belongs only to sweep.

Lease durations preserve the current operational windows: transcript recovery
10 minutes, realtime enrichment 90 seconds, generic embedding 10 minutes, and
D-015 note indexing 60 seconds. Artifact-write operations use the separately
frozen 10-minute window in section 7.10. Claim sets
`lease_last_renewed_at=now_ms` and
`lease_expires_at=now_ms+duration`. Long-running work must renew by
`lease_last_renewed_at + floor(duration/3)`; the renewal CAS rejects after that
boundary even if nominal expiry is later. It matches job/item, running state,
fresh token hash, expected item instance/revision, input/mutation fingerprints,
current hold/deletion authority, and prior renewal/expiry. Note renewal also matches
target epoch/generation, consent and D-015 mode; `claimed_by` is diagnostic,
not authority. Each accepted renewal sets both timestamps from the one
database-clock read with safe-integer overflow rejection. A failed or missed
renewal makes the result inert.

Sweep matches that same identity and atomically clears token, renewal, lease,
and claim time:

- transcript becomes `retryable_error` with the exact section-9.2 backoff when
  attempts remain, otherwise `manual_needed`;
- realtime enrichment becomes `pending` when attempts are below 3, otherwise
  `error`, with the owning item state changed by the same CAS;
- generic embedding becomes `pending` when attempts are below 3, otherwise
  `error`;
- note indexing becomes `error` with stable `lease_expired`, remains
  re-claimable only while attempts are below 5, and preserves exact desired
  action/epoch/generation.

Sweep never touches any non-null batch reservation or binding. Every new claim
uses a fresh random 256-bit token and partial-unique hash, including note
claims; a prior raw token or reused process/claimed-by identity cannot become
current again.

## 10. Retention, deletion, and backup truth

`source_delete_by` is the latest approved live-use boundary for a future
browser-visible source. It is not a promise that all ordinary backups erase at
that instant.

Migration 028 adds no deadline scheduler and authorizes no live capture.
Packaged fixture rows are deleted by their hermetic test cleanup.

A routine backup:

- does not update source status, hold state, receipt state, or delete-by;
- does not delete a live source or segment;
- holds one explicit source snapshot through copy and, for S28, admits it only
  when all cleanup-outbox and transient item-delete-permit rows are absent;
- permits bounded content-free tombstones inside the database image but never
  separately catalogs or joins them; supported restore keeps all endpoints
  fenced, publishes a fresh nonrollbackable external restore epoch, and
  disposition-deletes copied old-epoch tombstones before activation, without
  depending on retired keys;
- reproves zero cleanup-outbox and transient-permit rows on the candidate after VACUUM and before
  listing or restore; a stuck outbox defers backup with a content-free
  incident alert;
- follows the existing configured snapshot and pruning behavior and is
  database-only, with no artifact-file completeness claim;
- makes no stronger erasure claim.

Explicit item deletion is recoverable across SQLite and the filesystem:

1. before reading a current item, parse the immutable envelope and require its
   restore epoch to equal the external active epoch, then reconcile
   `deletion_id` in this exact order: detailed deletion request, committed or
   cleaning outbox, deletion tombstone, current item. An externally visible
   detailed deletion row is an integrity failure; an exact outbox cleanup
   authenticator resumes only mandatory cleanup; an exact final
   terminal/horizon-bound tombstone authenticator returns only `deleted` and
   starts no work. If none exists, expiry refuses before item lookup even if
   the authority key retired, while a potentially live envelope must verify
   under a retained key and match the exact current item instance and
   revision. An authenticator, authority, instance, or revision mismatch
   refuses without item or filesystem mutation.
2. before the database transaction, resume only an owned current
   `reconciling` operation. Any unexpired `writing` or `reconciling` operation
   owned by another token makes deletion retryable with no file or database
   mutation. An expired operation is taken over and reconciled by the exact
   section-7.10 protocol. Terminal committed/failed/quarantined rows and their
   deterministic stage/final shapes must be consistent.
3. the service first completes the exact 60,000-ms reader-drain barrier, then
   acquires the bounded tombstone-key signing reservation. One FULL-durable
   `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` revalidates the authority envelope, item instance/root,
   exact row-plus-disk or exact null-path empty manifest, the at-most-4,096
   one-to-one vector graph, and complete bounded caller set. Under that writer
   lock it precomputes one bounded canonical
   command/header/tombstone-map value over every exact detailed
   request/outbox/caller-tombstone tuple and authenticator, item
   instance/root/manifest/caller-request/artifact-request/operation/batch/
   claim snapshot. Under the closed native phase machine, the application
   inserts the self-FK-blocked `prepared` permit, runs the exact top-level
   vector preproof/bounded per-row delete/postproof, marks the same permit
   `vectors_purged`, and only then inserts the byte-identical command into the
   zero-row `item_delete_commands` view. That view trigger matches the
   already-proven transaction-local permit and issues the inner item delete.
   Its `BEFORE` trigger uses no virtual table, matches the exact permit and
   canonical map, inserts the item-owned detailed deletion request, prepared
   no-FK cleanup outbox, and exact bounded caller tombstones, and validates
   every still-present ordinary detailed row, operation child, chunk/bridge
   snapshot, authority, path/null-path shape, and absence of a live writer. The
   item delete then cascades the policy/source/segment/hold/extension-request/
   recovery-receipt/artifact-request/operation/capture/job/detailed-deletion-
   request graph while retaining the permit. The outer view trigger requires
   the inner delete count one, item/detail absence, the exact marked permit,
   the prepared outbox, and complete caller-tombstone equality before
   returning `SQLITE_DONE`; driver-level INSTEAD-OF-view change count is not
   authority. After that statement is finalized, the sole executable
   post-cascade coordinate occurs. The immediately next
   `outbox_commit_dml` phase changes only that outbox
   `prepared -> committed` with the bound transaction clock; its built-in
   proof trigger revalidates the surviving command/permit/outbox/tombstone
   projections and all deleted-row absence, deletes exactly the permit, and
   proves the final committed-outbox/zero-permit shape. No other post-command
   query or DML exists and no file is removed in this transaction.
   Ordinary queued/running claims and any batch classification are
   intentionally invalidated by item absence rather than allowed to block
   user deletion.
4. the permit insert/mark, bounded per-row top-level vec0 purge, trigger-created
   detailed deletion-request/outbox/tombstone rows, ordinary child cascades,
   the immediately-next `prepared -> committed` outbox phase, exact
   intermediate/final permit/map proofs, and item deletion commit together.
   The permit's
   impossible deferred self-FK makes any early or surviving permit fail
   COMMIT. A successful FULL commit cannot leave a permit, prepared row, or
   live item beside that outbox. Any pre-COMMIT phase failure or zero match
   enters `outcome_control` with the exact two-slot `commit_not_attempted`
   pair; `committed` is impossible, `open` alone executes the complete
   rollback including vec0, `rolled_back` prepares no SQL, and
   `indeterminate` closes/quarantines without service-store mutation. Every
   statement is finalized exactly once. For an attempted COMMIT,
   `outcome_control` applies all four
   `open|committed|rolled_back|indeterminate` classes; COMMIT `SQLITE_DONE` is
   committed even if later finalize or driver handling reports an error.
   After definitive commit and writer-lock
   release, the service cross-verifies the committed outbox, ordered signing
   actions, and complete caller-tombstone projection, raises key retention,
   installs the exact cleanup pin, promotes and verifies the initial
   reservation, and only then atomically deletes its reservation bundle and
   admits cleanup. Exact rollback atomically deletes the held parent plus its
   exact prefix action array through `delete_reservation_bundle_v1` only after
   unchanged-preimage proof and the both-present/both-absent timeout rule;
   indeterminate or mixed state keeps the reservation and logical-store fence;
5. only after that durable database commit do the bounded
   immediate-transaction cleanup batches from section 7.10 revalidate
   identities, unlink exact entries, and fsync affected directories.
   Finalization then follows this fixed order: acquire and durably verify a
   fresh bounded `finalization_commit` signing reservation; enter the one FULL
   `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; under its continuously held writer lock revalidate the
   namespace, remove empty directories, and fsync through the root; read and
   freeze the one exact final completion clock; durably append the
   terminal/horizon signing action and bind that same clock into the DML;
   publish exact durable
   `done+tombstone` in the first FULL commit; outside the lock raise final-key
   retention and promote the reservation; while `done` remains, execute or
   reconcile atomic `delete_finalization_authority_v1` over the old cleanup
   pin plus exact promoted reservation/action bundle; prove exact
   `ack_ready`; execute the second sealed FULL ack commit that deletes only
   `done` as the final mutation; then respond;
6. startup and explicit retry apply the exact eight-class matrix in section
   7.10. `committed|cleaning` resumes filesystem work only with the exact
   cleanup pin, `done+tombstone` resumes only
   promotion/finalization-authority-GC/ack work, and the exact
   tombstone/no-outbox/no-service-authority `ack_committed` shape performs no
   mutation: it finishes a response only for a still-live original channel,
   otherwise releases only the deletion-recovery latch, while a later
   identical authenticated request receives the replay response. Ordinary
   service is admitted only with null retirement-control active ID, no
   barrier or exclusive retirement controller, and an exact tuple-bound
   `ordinary` runtime projection with a live ordinary channel, claimed
   ordinary resume state, and no controller capability/channel/claim; under `quiescing` the
   controller-owned retirement state machine continues with ordinary service
   fenced.
   `prepared` is transaction-internal; observing it after restart is a
   content-free invariant refusal with no filesystem mutation. A cleanup
   outbox never recreates an item, and its unique `item_id` blocks recreation
   through durable `done` until ack deletion. A null-path row revalidates the
   exact empty manifest and zero artifact projections, performs no path
   operation, and follows the same reservation, durable receipt, promotion,
   and ack sequence.

A `BEFORE DELETE ON items` authority trigger, the command-view trigger's
post-cascade proof, and the separate built-in outbox-commit proof trigger
enforce the repository runtime boundary. The
service performs the filesystem recomputation synchronously under the writer
lock before building the canonical deletion command; the trigger itself does not
pretend SQLite can enumerate a filesystem. It requires, for that exact item
under the same transaction:

- trigger insertion of exactly one `prepared` cleanup row whose root
  fingerprint, nullable path, canonical manifest, authority expiry, request
  fingerprint, cleanup authenticator/key ID, item, and deletion ID equal the
  permit-bound tuple, followed by an exact reread;
- trigger insertion of exactly one item-owned deletion request with the exact
  deletion ID, item/instance/revision, request fingerprint, complete authority
  envelope, cleanup authenticator/key ID, root, and manifest, plus exact
  reread before its later cascade;
- zero `writing` or `reconciling` artifact operations; every nonpending
  operation has a consistent terminal committed/failed/quarantined
  operation/capture-artifact graph;
- every item-owned artifact caller binding for the item instance is internally
  consistent; an active or recovering binding has only pending or terminal
  operations after the zero-active-writer check. Before any child cascade the
  SQL authority trigger recomputes the exact child count/set and matches the
  deletion-wide and per-request snapshots without mutating a retained parent;
- trigger insertion and reread of an exact five-field caller tombstone for
  every extension or artifact request with the random caller ID, precomputed
  keyed request authenticator,
  `terminal_code='item_deleted'`, deletion time, and
  `max(authority_expires_at,deleted_at)+300_000` block boundary;
- one exact native-role `prepared` permit insert, top-level bounded
  vector preproof/delete/postproof, and one-row `vectors_purged` receipt mark,
  with equality at 4,096 and refusal at 4,097; zero main-schema trigger reads
  or writes `chunks_vec`; rollback after purge restores vec0 and removes the
  permit;
- one command-view insertion matching that exact transactional permit,
  followed by a `BEFORE` trigger match on exact item, deletion ID, statement nonce, item
  instance, root fingerprint, manifest hash, request-tombstone map, and exact
  vector receipt, artifact-request/operation, and claim/batch snapshots; child
  cascade guards require that same retained permit and authorizer source;
- before that outer `sqlite3_step` returns, one inner root row, the marked
  permit retained, no item, the exact `prepared` outbox, exact
  canonical-map/tombstone equality, and the fixed in-trigger proof of
  detailed-row absence plus all caller-tombstone state; and
- after `command_dml` returns `SQLITE_DONE` and is finalized, exactly one
  immediately following `outbox_commit_dml` UPDATE that revalidates the same
  tuple and proofs, changes only that cleanup row `prepared -> committed` with
  its bound transaction clock, and invokes the built-in
  `AFTER UPDATE OF state` proof trigger to delete exactly the retained permit
  and prove it absent before that second statement returns.

Without every predicate the delete aborts before any cascade. Direct SQL on a
supported B28 connection cannot insert or retain the main-schema permit
outside the exact authorizer source/command trigger, and its self-FK blocks
commit if the command fails to delete it; a
disposable `NORMAL` negative-control clone is refused before attachment and
lacks every admitted native durable prepared role; and an old binary lacks
the required bridge-presence function and role/authorizer. This is a sealed
repository-runtime guard, not a claim that SQLite
alone can inspect files or defend against replacement of the attested runtime.

The delete call returns success only after synchronous cleanup verifies
durable namespace absence, the first FULL immediate transaction commits the
content-free `done+tombstone` pair, the final key reservation is promoted and
verified, `delete_finalization_authority_v1` atomically removes and rereads
absent the old cleanup pin plus promoted reservation/action bundle while
`done` remains, exact `ack_ready` is proved, and the second sealed FULL ack
commit deletes `done` as the final mutation. An abrupt stop
after the initial database commit may temporarily leave files, but the durable
committed cleanup outbox makes them discoverable and mandatory on the next
startup/retry. An abrupt stop after finalization leaves the exact recoverable
receipt, service-side promotion, atomic finalization-authority-GC, or
`ack_ready`/ack state
named by the startup matrix. Root drift, identity mismatch, an unsafe
unmanifested entry, or unlink/rmdir failure retains the cleanup outbox and a
stable error without pretending deletion is physically complete.

The executed deletion failpoint array must byte-equal this exact compact
`JSON.stringify(item_deletion)` value, once, in registry order:

```json
["deletion_after_cleanup_intent","deletion_mid_vector_purge","deletion_after_vector_purge","deletion_after_item_cascade","deletion_before_database_commit","deletion_after_database_commit_before_file_cleanup","deletion_mid_file_unlink","deletion_after_file_unlink_before_parent_fsync","deletion_after_parent_fsync_before_batch_permit","deletion_after_cleanup_batch_permit_before_commit","deletion_after_nested_directory_rmdir_before_parent_fsync","deletion_after_item_directory_rmdir_before_root_fsync","deletion_after_root_fsync_before_finalize_permit","deletion_after_cleanup_finalize_permit_before_receipt_completed","deletion_after_receipt_completed_before_cleanup_row_delete","deletion_after_cleanup_row_delete_commit_before_response","deletion_cleanup_replay"]
```

Each name has exactly one injection coordinate:

| Ordinal and immutable name | Exact injection boundary |
|---|---|
| 1. `deletion_after_cleanup_intent` | After all locked pre-DML validation succeeds and the canonical command, header, tombstone map, cleanup/caller signing actions, and their hashes are completely precomputed and service-durable, but before permit insertion or vector preproof. |
| 2. `deletion_mid_vector_purge` | After the fresh no-cache per-row purge statement for canonical vector ordinal `ceil(N/2)` has returned `SQLITE_DONE` and been finalized exactly once, where this coordinate's fixture requires `N>=2`, and before preparation of the next ordinal's purge statement. |
