| 3. `deletion_after_vector_purge` | After the fresh no-cache per-row purge statement for canonical vector ordinal `N` has returned `SQLITE_DONE` and been finalized exactly once, but before `vector_postproof` or the `vectors_purged` permit mark. |
| 4. `deletion_after_item_cascade` | After `command_dml` has returned `SQLITE_DONE`, been finalized exactly once, and proved the item cascade, retained marked permit, exact `prepared` outbox, and tombstone map, but before preparation of the immediately next `outbox_commit_dml` statement. |
| 5. `deletion_before_database_commit` | After `outbox_commit_dml` is `SQLITE_DONE`, every statement is finalized, and all item/permit/outbox/map/final proofs hold, but before the initial COMMIT call. |
| 6. `deletion_after_database_commit_before_file_cleanup` | Immediately after initial COMMIT is definitively classified `committed` and the writer lock is released, but before initial reservation retention/pin promotion and therefore before the first filesystem cleanup action. |
| 7. `deletion_mid_file_unlink` | Let `F` be the initial manifest's total count of present regular-file entries across all deterministic cleanup batches before any unlink. The coordinate fixture has exactly `F=65`, and its first deterministic nonempty batch contains exact global canonical bytewise ordinals 1 through 32; therefore this coordinate is uniquely after unlink and required containing-directory fsync for global ordinal `ceil(F/2)=33` in the second batch and before ordinal 34, while coordinate 9 is uniquely after ordinal 32. Independent limit vectors still cover the general `2<=F<=512` legal range. |
| 8. `deletion_after_file_unlink_before_parent_fsync` | After the deterministic first bytewise file unlink in the first nonempty batch and before its required containing-directory fsync. |
| 9. `deletion_after_parent_fsync_before_batch_permit` | After the required containing-directory fsync following the last unlink in that nonempty batch and before cleanup-batch role installation. |
| 10. `deletion_after_cleanup_batch_permit_before_commit` | After the exact cleanup-batch role, guarded DML, row-count/reread proof, and statement finalization, but before that batch COMMIT; the same `transaction_outcome_observer_v1` four-way classifier governs this COMMIT and every cleanup-batch COMMIT. |
| 11. `deletion_after_nested_directory_rmdir_before_parent_fsync` | After the deterministic first deepest-first nested-directory `rmdir` and before fsync of its containing parent; the fixture requires at least one nested directory. |
| 12. `deletion_after_item_directory_rmdir_before_root_fsync` | After the item-directory `rmdir` and before the required artifact-root fsync. |
| 13. `deletion_after_root_fsync_before_finalize_permit` | After the final root fsync, the exact sealed `final_completion_clock_read`, and durable final signing-action append bound to that frozen completion clock under the already-held final reservation, but before cleanup-finalization role installation. |
| 14. `deletion_after_cleanup_finalize_permit_before_receipt_completed` | After the exact cleanup-finalization role and bindings are installed, but before the guarded `cleaning -> done` plus tombstone step. |
| 15. `deletion_after_receipt_completed_before_cleanup_row_delete` | After the first FULL COMMIT is definitively `committed` with exact durable `done+tombstone`, but before the first final-key retention/promotion action, atomic finalization-authority deletion, `ack_ready` proof, or ack deletion of `done`. |
| 16. `deletion_after_cleanup_row_delete_commit_before_response` | After the sealed ack COMMIT is definitively `committed`, `done` is absent, and all finalization authority was already atomically removed under coordinate 15, but before response. |
| 17. `deletion_cleanup_replay` | After startup/retry transaction-outcome classification and complete root, namespace, outbox, tombstone, reservation, action, key-pin, and identity revalidation, but before the first resumed filesystem, database, or service-recovery mutation. |

Coordinates 1 through 5 either leave the exact unchanged preimage or recover
through the four-way initial COMMIT classifier; they never infer rollback
from an error. Coordinate 2 stops between finalized per-row statements and
rolls back the transaction, so all `N` vector rows return. Coordinate 4 stops
between finalized `command_dml` and preparation of `outbox_commit_dml`; its
rollback restores the item graph and removes the prepared outbox and
tombstones. Coordinates 6 through 17 never resurrect the item. At coordinates
7 through 14 the filesystem may be ahead of rolled-back batch/finalization
database state; replay accepts only the exact manifest-proved absence,
repeats required fsyncs, and advances from the retained
`committed|cleaning` outbox. Coordinate 15 resumes final promotion and ack
from `done+tombstone`, including atomic finalization-authority deletion and
`ack_ready`; coordinate 16 classifies exact `ack_committed`, mutates nothing,
finishes the response only for a still-live original channel, otherwise
releases only the deletion-recovery latch, and leaves any later identical
authenticated request to the normal replay path. It admits ordinary service
   only with null retirement-control active ID, no barrier or exclusive
   retirement controller, and an exact tuple-bound `ordinary` runtime
   projection with a live ordinary channel, claimed ordinary resume state,
   and no controller capability/channel/claim; under `quiescing` it continues controller-owned
   retirement with ordinary service fenced. Coordinate
17 proves the selected matrix row without mutating before injection.

For both initial and final transactions, vectors exercise all four
`open|committed|rolled_back|indeterminate` observations, including COMMIT
`SQLITE_DONE` followed independently by finalize failure and driver error;
definitive commit always wins. Within coordinates 15 and 16, additional
deterministic crash vectors cover every postcommit edge: before/after final-key
retention raise, promoted-record commit, promotion reread,
`delete_finalization_authority_v1` all-present/all-absent classification,
`ack_ready` proof, ack BEGIN/step/COMMIT classification, and response. These are
subcoordinates of the existing
immutable names, not new runtime failpoint names.
Initial, every cleanup-batch, finalization, and ack transaction independently
exercise exact `begin_refused` finalize propagation, the
exact two-slot `commit_not_attempted` pair at every post-BEGIN/pre-COMMIT
fault, all three legal not-attempted observer outcomes, all four COMMIT
outcomes, open-only rollback, definitive COMMIT `SQLITE_DONE` despite finalize
or driver error, and indeterminate closed-image reconciliation with no
service-store mutation.

Tests also cover root drift, every path/alias/link anomaly, concurrent artifact
writes, response loss, delayed request replay, queued/running and every batch
classification, every vector anomaly class, caller/deletion HMAC mismatch,
authority issuance-before-persist crash/rotation, creation/admission/expiry
equality, post-purge expired new-target replay before item lookup,
eight-candidate deletion-ID collision/exhaustion, 32-slot key
capacity/loss/rotation/reservation, strict tombstone cleanup equality/`+1`,
256/257 janitor order, arbitrary UTF-8 and 24-hex item IDs, nullable-path
empty-manifest/projection mutations, proof that a non-24-hex ID never reaches
a path API, same-ID recreation fencing in both path branches, and
read/log/export exclusion. Before physical completion an exact deletion ID
resumes only its outbox; after completion it returns only `deleted` from the
bounded tombstone. After the tombstone horizon, authority expiry and a
different exact current live instance are exercised as independent refusal
controls. No forced deleted-instance collision or historical nonreuse
assertion exists. A worker that loses the item instance or claim cannot
recreate it or apply late. The immutable failpoint object, order, digest, and
145-name count do not change.

A retained pre-delete snapshot may still contain deleted content until the
configured normal pruning policy expires it. The current default is
approximately one week, not a hard seven-day guarantee. Migration 028 does not
rewrite or selectively purge historical backups.

Live lab enablement remains blocked until a separately reviewed cleanup
command, owner, scheduling mechanism, target manifest, and evidence prove the
approved live deletion lifecycle.

| Binary/schema pair | Supported behavior |

The release launcher/compatibility checker refuses the target before application startup and before any writable database open, checkpoint, or close because B27 lacks S28 connection/checkpoint authority. The sole writable non-WAL exception is the private unattached single-handle `isolated_backup_scrub` candidate: DELETE+FULL under its exact native prepared role/authorizer trace; it cannot attach to, checkpoint, reset, last-close, or obtain any authoritative active-database role. |

Forward recovery keeps S28 and deploys a prebuilt, reviewed, S28-aware disabled

No migration-030 cleanup, old-column removal, old-state removal, or

The machine-readable registry at

`S2-AC-01` through `S2-AC-17`.

checked-in insertion order and hashes to
`6b3aa6da2dd37dae9e5435426b2ca6937ac83fc9dffb3f75a6b20d858df0b12b`.
Every evidence file's `failpoint_registry_sha256` always equals that immutable
rule-set hash. The generated migration names are bound separately as described
below; they do not mutate this accepted registry or addendum.

Every case emits one content-free JSON evidence file as UTF-8 compact JSON
with keys in the following order, no extra keys or BOM, and exactly one
trailing LF:

- `case_id`;

`host_control_oracle_bundle_sha256` is nonnull and equals the exact protected

`host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity.sha256`—only for S2-AC-01 and

Every artifact hash covers the exact bytes and scope named by the registry's
machine-readable field schema, shared pre-run binding, aggregation binding,
and selected platform descriptor.
Unless a formula explicitly excludes the final LF, every Stage 2 manifest
below is serialized as ASCII-only UTF-8 compact JSON with keys in the stated
order, no insignificant whitespace, extra key, duplicate key, BOM, CR, or
alternate escape, and exactly one trailing LF; SHA-256 covers those exact
bytes. Strings contain bytes `0x20..0x7e`, are bounded where stated, and JSON
escaping is the exact ECMAScript `JSON.stringify` result. Integers are safe
nonnegative JSON integers unless a schema explicitly requires a decimal
string. Every hash is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal and every Git commit is
exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal.

The accepted package topology is federated because no one host can truthfully
execute both Linux-only AC13 and Darwin-only AC17. The canonical platform
partition is exactly:

```json
[{"platform":"linux","case_ids":["S2-AC-01","S2-AC-02","S2-AC-03","S2-AC-04","S2-AC-05","S2-AC-06","S2-AC-07","S2-AC-08","S2-AC-09","S2-AC-10","S2-AC-11","S2-AC-12","S2-AC-13","S2-AC-14","S2-AC-15","S2-AC-16"]},{"platform":"darwin","case_ids":["S2-AC-17"]}]
```

SHA-256 over exact ASCII `stage2-platform-partition-v1`, one `0x00`, and
exact no-LF `JSON.stringify(partition)` is
`4aef20f3dd0e59d16c0ecee0693be9328f01a9ce98793420ca5bed687a9f2bfe`.
The arrays are disjoint, their union is every registry case exactly once, and
their concatenation is registry order. A one-host run, SKIP, platform

The fixed pre-run locators are:

The acyclic build/run order is exact:
`immutable common files and each platform's capsule static-entry projection P
-> independently pre-pin one two-host attestation-trust manifest T outside S
and the federation assembler -> construct each complete capsule manifest M
by the exact field transform from P, T's locator, and the five existing
reserved-slot descriptors -> construct the initial kernel-read-only capsules -> choose one
fresh run ID/challenge -> start each independently pinned host supervisor and
pass its initial capsule, with Linux first placed in its closed cgroup and
passing through the static helper/one-broker seal before same-PID zero-
capability Node exec and Darwin passing through the native suspended spawn
gate -> each supervisor authenticates its T-bound keystore service-control
endpoint and creates one exact persistent platform-local launcher behind a
post-exec pre-key/commitment barrier -> validate each supervisor launch offer
-> each controller authority durably consumes the unique run and offer
latches and issues its controller-signed run request -> release each exact
launcher, validate its locked/noninheritable key commitment, and use the
service-control channel to partially issue then observer-bind and final-ready
bind one keystore session -> obtain the matching durability-committed,
host-root-signed run attestation with exact response/EOF delivery -> shared
binding S ->
Linux descriptor D_L + Darwin descriptor D_D -> aggregation binding
A(S,D_L,D_D) -> fill and kernel-freeze both capsule reserved slots -> each
supervisor invokes its T-bound host-kernel oracle observer with the exact six
read-only request rights, validates the protected result bundle and EOF, and
retains one read-only bundle description -> live Linux and Darwin platform
activation with that bundle as the exact seventh right -> platform runs ->
externally gated platform
archives/expectations -> signed post-gate platform admissions -> final Linux
aggregation -> signed scratch-destruction receipt -> aggregate catalog/marker
-> signed post-exit package admission -> Linux host-supervisor out-of-band-pin
revalidation -> controller-read/supervisor-sole-write control-plane
direct-validation acceptance frame -> supervisor/broker/launcher/descendant
exit ->
controller/provisioner double-empty cgroup proof and exact leaf removal`.
Both live platform runs positionally read and bind the already
frozen `A`; the oracle bundles are live post-A values and never alter it.
Neither output, platform catalog, platform result, archive,
expectation, platform admission, scratch receipt, aggregate catalog, marker,
nor package admission enters any pre-run hash.

`session_ready`, `request_frame_latched`, and `signing_started`, each to
`consumed_failure`, in that order. Terminal states are exactly
`["signature_committed","consumed_failure"]`.

Canonical `stage2-authority-ledger-recovery-policy-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,role,reopen_policy,integrity_policy,
wal_autocheckpoint,checkpoint_mode,uncertain_commit_policy,
crash_state_policy,terminal_policy,forbidden_actions`. Values require reopening
only the same filesystem identity, native WAL recovery,
`PRAGMA integrity_check(1)` returning exactly `ok`, `wal_autocheckpoint=0`,
and `checkpoint_mode=FULL`. An uncertain transaction is resolved on a fresh
connection by reading its complete unique-key set: all-present remains
consumed, all-absent fails the original caller without resume/retry, and a
partial set or I/O ambiguity quarantines the service. Controller recovery
never signs from a recovered latch. Keystore recovery changes every
pre-signature terminal or `signing_started` state to `consumed_failure`;
`signature_committed` preserves stored bytes without retransmission.
`forbidden_actions` is exactly
`["delete_row","reset_state","replace_database","alternate_ledger",
"vacuum_into","reissue","replay","resend_committed_signature"]`.

Each mutation uses one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. Controller reservation
atomically inserts both latch rows and the complete immutable
consumed-before-signature receipt before validation or signing. Keystore
`issue_session_request` chooses one fresh nonce and atomically inserts the
run, request, and session latches plus `issued_unbound` before transferring
an endpoint; any collision returns no endpoint and consumes the run. Request
latching atomically inserts the replay latch and retained complete frame
hash; result bytes/hash commit with `signing_started ->
signature_committed` before transport. `COMMIT` return under the frozen
settings is the only durability boundary. WAL/SHM first creation and every
recovery checkpoint are followed by final-parent fsync or the service is
quarantined.

The four subordinate and enclosing digests each use the nested object's
exact ASCII domain, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF JSON. Static subordinate
objects contain only filesystem identities, literal key shapes, states, and
recovery rules—not authorization IDs, T/M/S, a live request, session, replay
value, or row—so the graph remains acyclic.
The controller record uses this schema as
`controller_request_latch_policy`; the keystore record uses it as
`keystore_ledger_policy`. Each nested service identity's
nonnull `durable_state_policy_sha256` cross-equals the corresponding complete
policy.
Replacing a service, manager, ledger root, durability setting, unique-key
schema, state graph, or recovery rule invalidates T and both authorization
IDs.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-endpoint-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,path,parent_chain,parent_device,parent_inode,
socket_device,socket_inode,
owner_uid,owner_gid,mode,transport,peer_authentication`. Its absolute
nonsymlink path, root/admin-owned nonwritable parent chain, owner/mode, and
socket identity are T-bound. Linux uses
`unix_seqpacket_connect` plus `SO_PEERCRED+SO_COOKIE+pidfd`; Darwin uses
`unix_stream_connect` plus `LOCAL_PEERPID+LOCAL_PEERTOKEN+kqueue`. The
observer reopens/fstats before and after accept; the supervisor connects once
beneath a retained parent and validates the service's complete T-bound
executable/start token and manager-retained original observer.
`parent_chain` has `1..32` root-to-direct-parent records in traversal order,
each with keys exactly `path,device,inode,owner_uid,owner_gid,mode`; paths are
absolute, component-unique, nonsymlink printable ASCII, and all numeric
identities/modes use the authority-ledger forms above. Its last
device/inode byte-equal `parent_device,parent_inode`. Every parent is
root/admin-owned and unwritable by the repository, assembler, supervisor,
launcher, wrapper, payload, or oracle subject. A missing ancestor, writable
ancestor, alias, replacement, or last-record mismatch invalidates T.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-protocol-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,transport,frame_cap,supervisor_states,observer_states,
request_rights,result_rights,zero_right_states`. Transport is
`unix_seqpacket_connect` on Linux and `unix_stream_connect` on Darwin;
`frame_cap` is `131072`; states are exactly
`["control_init","oracle_request","SHUT_WR/EOF"]` and
`["channel_init","oracle_result","SHUT_WR/EOF"]`, respectively. Request
rights are exactly
`["supervisor_run_request","host_attestation_trust","execution_capsule",
"shared_binding","platform_descriptor","aggregation_binding"]`; result
rights are exactly `["host_control_oracle_bundle"]`; and zero-right states
are exactly `["channel_init","control_init"]`.
Every payload-bearing state is one cap-bounded uint32be-prefixed frame in its
declared direction. After authenticated accept, the observer sends
`channel_init`; the supervisor validates it, sends `control_init` then the
single oracle request, and performs `SHUT_WR`; the observer receives request
EOF before executing the plan, sends the single result only after complete
bundle construction, and performs `SHUT_WR`; the supervisor accepts only
result plus EOF. A wrong direction or state, repeated/skipped frame,
premature half-close, extra byte/right, held EOF, or retained sender
description consumes the request and refuses. The protocol digest is
SHA-256 over its exact domain, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF `JSON.stringify`.

The exact static oracle authoring inventory is
`implementation/fixtures/
stage2-host-control-oracle-authoring-inventory-v1.json` inside the immutable
capsule and
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/implementation/
fixtures/stage2-host-control-oracle-authoring-inventory-v1.json` in the
repository. Canonical
`stage2-host-control-oracle-authoring-inventory-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,assertion_manifest_path,platforms`; `assertion_manifest_path` is
exactly `implementation/fixtures/stage2-assertion-manifest-v1.json`, and
`platforms` is Linux then Darwin. Each platform record
has keys exactly
`platform,scenario_plan_path,observation_schema_registry_path,
observation_schemas,assertion_bindings,subject_profiles`.
Each `observation_schemas` record has keys exactly
`event_kind,observation_domain,observer_capability_kind,
observation_schema_path`; records are unique and unsigned-byte sorted by
`(observation_domain,event_kind)`. Each `subject_profiles` record has keys
exactly
`subject_profile,subject_entrypoint_path,system_runtime_manifest_path,
import_manifest_path,native_observer_adapter_path,observer_kind`; records
are unique and unsigned-byte sorted by `subject_profile`.
The observer kind is `linux_host_control_oracle_v1` for Linux and
`darwin_host_control_oracle_v1` for Darwin. Every ID/domain token follows its
closed grammar below. Every path is a unique printable-ASCII
capsule-relative ordinary-file path beginning `implementation/`, contains no
empty/dot/dot-dot component, percent escape, backslash, or case folding, and
maps one-to-one to a P/M entry.

Each `assertion_bindings` record has keys exactly
`assertion_id,event_kind,observation_domain,required_json_pointers`.
Records are unique and unsigned-byte sorted by `assertion_id`.
`assertion_id` selects one record in the checked-in assertion manifest whose
source is `host_control_oracle_bundle`; the Linux projection byte-equals the
complete ordered S2-AC-01 oracle subset and the Darwin projection byte-equals
the complete ordered S2-AC-17 oracle subset. Event kind/domain select exactly
one record in the same platform's `observation_schemas`.
`required_json_pointers` is nonempty, unique, unsigned-byte sorted, and each
exact RFC6901 pointer resolves through explicit `properties` in that
record's closed raw schema. No binding may point only to `phase`, a
subject-reported status, or an observer-supplied assertion result.

The Linux schema set is exactly `cgroup_snapshot` from `cgroupfs_fd`,
`deadline_snapshot` from `clock_monotonic`, `pidfd_identity` from `pidfd`,
`procfs_snapshot` from `procfs_fd`, `socket_probe` from `socket_probe`,
`subject_exit` from `pidfd`, and `subject_launch` from `procfs_fd`. The
Darwin set is exactly `deadline_snapshot` from `clock_monotonic`,
`kqueue_exit` from `kqueue`, `proc_pidinfo_snapshot` from `proc_pidinfo`,
`subject_exit` from `kqueue`, `subject_launch` from `proc_pidinfo`,
`subject_process_snapshot` from `sysctl_snapshot`, and
`vm_region_snapshot` from `mach_vm_region`. Their checked-in raw schemas are
the complete evidence surface: Linux includes boot ID, broker task list,
cgroup double-empty/removal samples, child-gate process/image identity,
key-region noninheritance scan, post-exec seals, complete FD table, pidfd
identity/wait result, bounded decimal-string monotonic deadline endpoints,
seqpacket cap probe, and socket cookies; Darwin includes boot time/backend
APIs, complete sysctl process snapshot, executable vnode/VM-region equality,
complete FD table, process group, socket objects, suspended-spawn
flags/mutex/release count, kqueue registration/NOTE_EXIT, bounded
decimal-string monotonic deadline endpoints, and complete VM-region
inheritance observations. Arrays are complete observer
enumerations, not subject-selected samples. Count fields byte-equal their
corresponding array lengths, elapsed times equal finish minus start without
underflow, endpoint/process identities cross-equal the bundle process and
capability graph, and duplicate or nonmonotonic records refuse before
predicate evaluation.

The domain validators apply these exact relations before any plan predicate:

- Linux `procfs_snapshot.boot_id` equals both selected process tokens'
  `boot_identity`; `broker_thread_ids` is the complete numeric-ascending
  `/proc/<broker_pid>/task` enumeration and its count; the four child-gate
  fields equal the selected child process token, direct parent, and P/M gate
  executable; the key-region start/length equal the P/M key-memory record and
  `child_matching_key_regions` is the complete numeric-address-ascending
  overlap scan; post-exec device/inode/seals equal the retained artifact and
  exact seal policy; and `fd_table` is the complete numeric-FD-ascending
  procfs enumeration cross-equal to the role's retained FD plan.
- Linux `pidfd_identity` PID/start/device/inode equal the subject token and
  selected pidfd capability; signal-zero result is `0`; and its `waitid`
  triple equals the sole subject-exit observation. Linux `cgroup_snapshot`
  path/device/inode equal the run's retained leaf identity; each process
  array is a complete numeric-ascending `cgroup.procs` sample; and the two
  populated values, process arrays, and final `ENOENT` are sampled in that
  order. Linux `socket_probe` buffer, byte, right, return, and flag fields
  equal the frozen seqpacket probe; endpoint records are complete and
  unsigned-byte role then numeric device/inode ordered, and cross-equal the
  retained socket identities/cookies.
- Darwin `proc_pidinfo_snapshot` PID/start/group equal the subject token;
  group members are complete numeric ascending; executable FD/path/hash,
  vnode triple, and every start-address-ordered executable-region vnode are
  equal; `fd_table` is the complete numeric-FD-ascending
  `PROC_PIDLISTFDS`/`PROC_PIDFDINFO` projection; socket endpoints are complete
  role/device/inode ordered and cross-equal retained `soi_so` identities; and
  spawn flags, mutex scope, suspended-before-instruction state, and sole
  `SIGCONT` count equal the native spawn-gate trace.
- Darwin `kqueue_exit` device/inode equal the selected kqueue capability,
  registered and exit identities equal the subject PID, registration returns
  zero, and the exact flags plus sole `NOTE_EXIT` event are retained.
  `subject_process_snapshot` boot time equals both process tokens, kernel name
  is `Darwin`, API set is exact, and its role/PID/start/group array is the
  complete numeric-PID-ascending sysctl process projection.
  `vm_region_snapshot.region_count` equals the complete strictly
  start-address-ordered region array length, every region has
  `VM_INHERIT_NONE`, and `non_none_inheritance_region_count` is zero.
- On both platforms, `startup_started_monotonic_ns`,
  `startup_finished_monotonic_ns`, `run_started_monotonic_ns`, and
  `run_finished_monotonic_ns` are observer `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` nanosecond
  samples encoded as canonical unsigned-decimal strings with length `1..19`
  and pattern `^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,18})$`. This is an explicitly bounded subset
  of uint64; a JSON number, leading zero, sign, exponent, whitespace, or
  `20`-digit value is invalid. Validators parse these four fields only as
  exact base-10 `BigInt` values and never coerce them through a JavaScript
  `Number`. For each startup/run pair, finish is not earlier than start; the
  exact difference is in `0..9007199254740991` and equals
  `BigInt` of the corresponding safe unsigned JSON-integer
  `startup_elapsed_ns|run_elapsed_ns`. Each
  `startup_limit_ns|run_limit_ns` is a positive safe unsigned JSON integer
  that byte-equals the signed request, and exact comparison proves
  `BigInt(elapsed) <= BigInt(limit)`.

These are closed domain relations, not subject claims or implementation
defaults. The bundle validator must prove them before predicate evaluation.
For an assertion-bound pointer, `present|absent` alone is insufficient unless
one of these relations or a singleton raw-schema constraint already fixes the
complete selected value; otherwise its required plan predicate must use the
applicable value-comparing operator and exact operand. Schema validity,
pointer presence, or a top-level PASS never substitutes for the relation.

The inventory contains no file hash, argv, scenario, predicate, mutation,
policy, T/P/M/S/D/A value, cap-profile hash, or live-bundle value. Its
assertion IDs and pointers only close the static evidence-to-claim
projection. Its exact compact JSON plus one LF is the checked-in file.
`authoring_inventory_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-host-control-oracle-authoring-inventory-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact
no-LF `JSON.stringify(authoring_inventory)`. The exact construction order is
`assertion manifest + static authoring inventory -> raw schema and
subject/runtime/import/adapter closure bytes -> observation registry and
scenario plan ->
oracle policy -> P/T/M -> live request/bundle`. No closure leaf embeds the
inventory, plan, registry, policy, cap profile, P, T, M, S, D, A, or a live
bundle digest, so this order has no back-edge.
For Contract GO, the required checked-in oracle authorities stop at the
assertion manifest, authoring inventory, raw schemas, derived observation
registries, and their verifier. Those exact 19 ordinary-file leaves are the
oracle projection of the header-pinned 39-leaf contract static-authority
index; path, size, or physical-byte hash drift changes or invalidates that
root. Scenario plans, subject/runtime/import
manifests, native adapters, policies, and live bundle fixtures are
Implementation-GO evidence: their final bytes and hashes cannot exist until
the implementation closures they bind exist. Contract GO neither requires
nor permits placeholder plan, adapter, closure, policy, or bundle hashes;
Implementation GO requires every one of those downstream leaves and all
projection checks below.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-policy-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,endpoint,endpoint_sha256,observer_identity_sha256,
channel_protocol,channel_protocol_sha256,
authoring_inventory_path,authoring_inventory_sha256,
scenario_plan_path,scenario_plan_sha256,observation_schema_registry_path,
observation_schema_registry_sha256,request_frame_cap,result_frame_cap,
bundle_byte_cap,process_count_cap,event_count_cap,observation_byte_cap,
scenario_count_cap,
bundle_artifact_profile,request_rights,result_rights`. Fixed caps are
`131072`, `131072`, `16777216`, `256`, `2048`, `262144`, and `512`.
Request rights are
exactly
the selected protocol's request rights; result rights equal the selected
protocol's result rights. Artifact profile is
`linux_sealed_memfd_readonly` or
`darwin_unlinked_fsynced_readonly_vnode`. Static plan/registry paths are
respectively
`implementation/fixtures/oracle-plan-<platform>-v1.json` and
`implementation/fixtures/oracle-schema-registry-<platform>-v1.json`,
resolved beneath the immutable capsule. The authoring-inventory path is the
exact shared path above. The selected platform record's two fixed paths and
both complete ordered path projections byte-equal the plan and registry
described below. The
complete service identity, policy, endpoint, plan, registry, native subject/
observer closures, authoring inventory, protocol, and their digests are exact
P/M/T entries.
`endpoint_sha256`, `authoring_inventory_sha256`, `scenario_plan_sha256`,
`observation_schema_registry_sha256`, and
`channel_protocol_sha256` each use the selected complete object's exact
domain, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF `JSON.stringify` preimage.
`host_control_oracle_policy_sha256` uses the complete policy's
exact ASCII domain, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF `JSON.stringify` preimage.
The policy hash is computed only after the endpoint, protocol, authoring
inventory, plan, and registry objects/hashes are final.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-scenario-plan-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,authoring_inventory_sha256,subject_profiles,mutations,
predicates,scenario_count,scenarios`.
`subject_profiles` is a nonempty unsigned-byte-`subject_profile`-sorted,
profile-unique array. Each record has keys exactly
`subject_profile,subject_entrypoint_path,subject_entrypoint_sha256,
system_runtime_manifest_path,system_runtime_manifest_sha256,
import_manifest_path,import_manifest_sha256,native_observer_adapter_path,
native_observer_adapter_sha256,observer_kind,argv,argv_sha256`.
`observer_kind` is exactly `linux_host_control_oracle_v1` for Linux or
`darwin_host_control_oracle_v1` for Darwin. `argv` is a nonempty
printable-ASCII token array whose first token is the exact subject
entrypoint; it contains no shell/eval/ambient-resolution token.
`subject_profile` matches `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,127}`.
`argv_sha256` hashes exact no-LF `JSON.stringify(argv)`. Paths/hashes map one-to-one to
exact P/M entries and close every executable, loader, import, native addon,
observer adapter, and argv byte the disposable subject can use. A scenario's
`subject_profile` selects exactly one record; no ambient lookup, wildcard,
implementation default, or unlisted profile is legal.
The selected inventory platform record's `subject_profiles` byte-equals the
plan array projected to
`subject_profile,subject_entrypoint_path,system_runtime_manifest_path,
import_manifest_path,native_observer_adapter_path,observer_kind` in that
order. Its `scenario_plan_path` equals the checked-in plan path, and
`authoring_inventory_sha256` equals the complete shared inventory digest.

`mutations` is an unsigned-byte-`mutation_id`-sorted, mutation-ID-unique
array. Each record has keys exactly
`mutation_id,subject_profile,operation,selector,operand_json`; operation is
exactly
`omit|replace|duplicate|reorder|truncate|append|hold_eof|wrong_right|
wrong_process|wrong_identity|wrong_state|wrong_deadline|fault_boundary`,
selector is a nonempty printable-ASCII value in the closed grammar below, and
`operand_json` is either JSON null or a JSON string containing the exact
canonical no-LF UTF-8 JSON bytes required by the operation. A nonnull string
is parsed once as a complete JSON value with no BOM, LF, trailing byte,
duplicate key, unsafe integer, or noncanonical encoding; the parsed value,
not the containing string, is the mutation operand. Every negative scenario
selects one record for its exact subject profile; an unused mutation or
implementation-defined mutation refuses.
Every mutation ID matches `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,127}`.
Every negative scenario starts from a fresh byte-identical execution of its
profile's positive baseline and applies exactly one mutation. Selectors use
only these closed ASCII grammars, where every direction, state, role, field,
deadline, and boundary token resolves exactly once in that profile's static
protocol/observation closure:

| Operation | Selector | Operand | Exact mutation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `omit` | `json:<state>:<RFC6901>` | null | remove the one existing selected member or array element before serialization |
| `replace` | `json:<state>:<RFC6901>` | any nonnull canonical JSON value | replace the one existing selected value, preserving every other value |
| `duplicate` | `json:<state>:<RFC6901>` | null | copy the selected encoded member/element immediately after itself, including its key for an object member |
| `reorder` | `json:<state>:<RFC6901>` selecting an array | two distinct in-range safe unsigned indices | swap exactly those two encoded elements |
| `truncate` | `carrier:<direction>:<state>` | safe unsigned integer below baseline wire length | emit exactly that many leading carrier bytes, then close |
| `append` | `carrier:<direction>:<state>` | nonempty even-length lowercase hex string of at most 4,096 decoded bytes | emit the baseline carrier followed by those decoded bytes before half-close |
| `hold_eof` | `direction:<direction>` | null | retain only that direction's final writer until one monotonic deadline tick after refusal |
| `wrong_right` | `rights:<direction>:<state>:<index>` | one closed descriptor-role JSON string different from baseline | replace exactly that right with a harmless independently created descriptor of the named wrong role |
| `wrong_process` | `process:<role>` | null | perform the selected baseline action from one fresh observer-created PID/start identity not named by the baseline |
| `wrong_identity` | `identity:<field>` | one same-JSON-type nonnull sentinel unequal to baseline | replace exactly the selected complete identity field |
| `wrong_state` | `state:<direction>:<state>` | one different closed state JSON string in that direction | send the baseline state's carrier at the selected wrong transition |
| `wrong_deadline` | `deadline:<name>` | null | complete the selected boundary at exactly the frozen deadline plus one monotonic tick |
| `fault_boundary` | `fault:<boundary_id>` | JSON string `before` or `after` | terminate at the named side of the one P/M-bound fault boundary before any later effect |

For `truncate`, the declared uint32be length remains the positive baseline
length when the prefix is present. Duplicate object keys intentionally create
noncanonical JSON bytes. A missing/multiple selector, illegal pointer/index,
operand mismatch, mutation of an unselected byte/effect, second mutation, or
unlisted selector/operation combination refuses before subject launch.

`predicates` is a nonempty unsigned-byte-`predicate_id`-sorted,
predicate-ID-unique array. Each record has keys exactly
`predicate_id,event_kind,observation_domain,json_pointer,operator,
operand_json,minimum_match_count,maximum_match_count,
after_predicate_ids`. Event kind/domain select exactly one observation-schema
record; `json_pointer` is an exact RFC6901 pointer valid for that closed
schema. Operator is exactly
`equals|not_equals|present|absent|uint_equals|uint_at_most|
array_equals|set_equals|bytes_equals|errno_equals`;
`operand_json` uses the same JSON-null-or-canonical-JSON-byte-string
representation as mutation operands and is parsed once before evaluation;
the closed operator table is:

| Operator | Operand / selected value | Match |
|---|---|---|
| `equals` | nonnull operand containing any JSON value / present value | exact equality of canonical no-LF JSON bytes |
| `not_equals` | nonnull operand containing any JSON value / present value | canonical no-LF JSON bytes differ |
| `present` | null / any value or missing | pointer resolves |
| `absent` | null / any value or missing | pointer does not resolve |
| `uint_equals` | nonnull safe unsigned JSON integer / present safe unsigned JSON integer | integer equality |
| `uint_at_most` | nonnull safe unsigned JSON integer / present safe unsigned JSON integer | selected integer is at most operand |
| `array_equals` | nonnull JSON array / present JSON array | same length and exact canonical element bytes in the same order |
| `set_equals` | nonnull duplicate-free JSON array / present duplicate-free JSON array | unsigned-byte-sorted canonical element-byte sets are equal |
| `bytes_equals` | nonnull even-length lowercase-hex JSON string / present even-length lowercase-hex JSON string | decoded bytes are equal |
| `errno_equals` | nonnull JSON string matching `E[A-Z0-9_]{1,63}` / present string with that pattern | ASCII strings are equal |

An absent pointer matches only `absent`; an illegal operand, selected type,
duplicate set element, noncanonical encoding, or unlisted operator/type pair
refuses the plan or bundle rather than contributing a match.
Counts are safe integers with `0 <= minimum <= maximum <= event_count_cap`.
`after_predicate_ids` is unique, unsigned-byte sorted, references only
earlier acyclic predicates whose minimum match count is at least one, and is
the sole cross-event ordering mechanism. An operator first produces the
predicate's raw match-event set. For every referenced predecessor, that set
and the predecessor's validated match-event set must be nonempty and every
current sequence must be greater than the predecessor set's maximum
sequence; otherwise the predicate fails. The raw set size is the declared
match count checked against the minimum/maximum bounds.
The validator evaluates only these declarative predicates over the bundle's
validated event range; a hard-coded, default, inferred, or subject-reported
predicate is forbidden.
Every predicate ID matches `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,127}`.

Each scenario has keys exactly
`scenario_id,polarity,mutation_id,subject_profile,event_domains,
expected_terminal,terminal_predicate_id,subject_launch_predicate_id,
subject_exit_predicate_id,forbidden_effects,assertion_ids,assertion_rules`.
`scenario_id` is a unique printable-ASCII
`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,127}` string and scenario array order is execution
order. Polarity is `positive` iff `mutation_id` is JSON null; each negative has
one nonnull exact mutation selector. Event domains are nonempty, unique,
ordered selectors into the registry. `expected_terminal` is a nonempty
printable-ASCII closed value named by the exact
`terminal_predicate_id`; that predicate uses `equals`, a nonnull
printable-ASCII JSON-string operand byte-equal to `expected_terminal`, and
minimum/maximum match count one. `observed_terminal` is the unique matched
event's selected string value.
`subject_launch_predicate_id` selects exact event kind `subject_launch`, uses
`equals` at `/argv_sha256` with the selected profile's hash, and has
minimum/maximum one. Its closed observation schema requires top-level keys
exactly `phase,executable_path,executable_sha256,argv_sha256`.
`subject_exit_predicate_id` selects exact event kind `subject_exit`, has
operator `present` at `/subject_exit_kind`, minimum/maximum one, and its
closed observation schema requires top-level
keys exactly `phase,subject_exit_kind,subject_exit_status_text`.
`subject_exit_status_text` is `none` for `timeout|observer_refusal`, decimal
`0..255` without a leading zero for `exit_code`, and decimal `1..127` without
a leading zero for `signal`; those values come only from the retained
pidfd/kqueue/wait observation. `forbidden_effects` is a unique unsigned-byte-sorted array of
predicate IDs whose evaluated match count must be zero.
`assertion_rules` has exactly one record per `assertion_ids` element in the
same order, with keys exactly `assertion_id,required_predicate_ids`; the
predicate list is nonempty, unique, unsigned-byte sorted, and every member
must satisfy its declared count/order bounds for that assertion to pass.
For each assertion, the selected inventory `assertion_bindings` record is
authoritative: the rule's predicates collectively select its exact
event-kind/domain pair and cover every `required_json_pointers` member at
least once with minimum match count at least one. No predicate over another
schema, top-level scenario status, phase alone, or a proper subset of the
required pointers can substitute. Predicates may add ordering and
negative-effect constraints but may not erase, widen, or remap this required
evidence projection.
Assertion arrays are nonempty and assertion-manifest ordered; across
scenarios they are disjoint and their union is exactly the
host-oracle-sourced AC01 set on Linux or AC17 set on Darwin.
`scenario_count` equals `scenarios.length` and is in `1..512`. The checked-in
Implementation-GO plan enumerates every live oracle claim; no wildcard, “including”,
schema-only surrogate, top-level status, or exit-zero shortcut supplies
coverage.
The selected platform policy names and hashes this plan; the plan never names
the enclosing policy, T, P, M, S, D, A, or a live bundle, so no static
policy/plan hash cycle exists.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-observation-schema-registry-v1` has keys
exactly `domain,platform,authoring_inventory_sha256,schema_count,schemas`;
records are unique and
unsigned-byte sorted by `(observation_domain,event_kind)` and have keys exactly
`event_kind,observation_domain,observer_capability_kind,
observation_schema_path,observation_schema,observation_schema_sha256,
required_keys`.
`observation_schema_path` is the unique P/M-inventoried capsule-relative
ordinary-file path. Canonical
`stage2-host-control-oracle-observation-schema-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,schema_dialect,schema_json`; dialect is
`stage2-closed-json-schema-subset-v1`, and `schema_json` is the complete
canonical JSON value from that path. The subset permits only explicit
objects with keys exactly
`type,properties,required,additionalProperties`, every property required in
insertion order, and `additionalProperties:false`; arrays with keys exactly
`type,items,minItems,maxItems,uniqueItems`, safe
`0 <= minItems <= maxItems <= 256`, `uniqueItems:true`, and one closed item
schema; strings whose keys are an insertion-ordered subset of
`type,minLength,maxLength,pattern,enum` and that have either a nonempty
duplicate-free string enum or complete
`0 <= minLength <= maxLength <= 4096` plus compilable `pattern`
bounds; safe unsigned integers with keys exactly
`type,minimum,maximum`; and boolean/null leaves with only `type`.
Unbounded recursion, references, unions,
implicit defaults, coercion, nonfinite numbers, unevaluated keys, remote
resolution, and implementation extensions are forbidden. Required-key arrays
are insertion ordered, exact, nonempty, and byte-equal the top-level
`schema_json.required`. The nested schema hash uses its exact
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimage; the registry hash covers every complete
schema record. Every event selects one record and validates its complete
no-LF observation JSON against those exact bytes. A path/hash-only,
required-key-only, or validator-selected schema is invalid.
`schema_count=schemas.length`, is positive, and does not exceed the policy's
event-count cap. Every event's `(observation_domain,event_kind)` resolves
exactly one record and its selected observer capability kind byte-equals that
record; a duplicate, ambiguous, missing, or differently ordered pair refuses.
The selected inventory platform record's `observation_schemas` byte-equals
the registry array projected to
`event_kind,observation_domain,observer_capability_kind,
observation_schema_path` in that order. Its
`observation_schema_registry_path` equals the checked-in registry path, and
`authoring_inventory_sha256` equals the complete shared inventory digest.
The checked-in static verifier/generator is
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/implementation/
fixtures/generate-stage2-host-control-oracle-static-fixtures.mjs`. From
repository root,
`node <generator_path> --verify-registries` with an empty injection
environment recursively validates the complete closed schema subset,
the exact raw-schema-tree ordinary-file set, platform and subject-profile
records, both fixed scenario-plan paths, each exact seven-record ordered
schema projection, globally unique safe inventory paths, assertion-manifest
subset equality, assertion-binding pointer resolution and rejection of
phase/status/result-only evidence,
registry path/projection, every domain-separated schema digest, and exact
derived registry bytes. It emits only
`stage2-host-control-oracle-schema-registries-v1:PASS:
<authoring_inventory_sha256>\n` on stdout, empty stderr, and exit zero.
`--generate-registries` is the sole checked-in derivation path for the two
registry files. Scenario plans are deliberately not generated by this
static tool: after the implementation closure bytes exist, their separate
validator must additionally prove the subject-profile and assertion-binding
projection rules above.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-socket-identity-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,channel_nonce,endpoint_role,device,inode,
kernel_socket_object_kind,kernel_socket_object_value`. Endpoint role is
`supervisor|observer`; device, inode, and object value are nonzero canonical
uint64 decimals. Linux kind is `so_cookie` and value is the endpoint's
nonce-bound `SO_COOKIE`; Darwin kind is `soi_so` and value is the endpoint's
nonce-bound `PROC_PIDFDSOCKETINFO.psi.soi_so` after the frozen signed-device
normalization. The endpoint values differ. Both endpoints are fstat twice
with exact equality, and the manager-retained pidfd/kqueue observation binds
the final holder; a pathname, inherited peer credential, raw persisted
Darwin object value, or `soi_stat` substitution is invalid. Each socket
digest uses the complete object's exact domain, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` preimage.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-channel-identity-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,channel_nonce,endpoint_identity,
endpoint_identity_sha256,supervisor_pid,supervisor_start_token,
observer_pid,observer_start_token,supervisor_socket_identity,
supervisor_socket_identity_sha256,observer_socket_identity,
observer_socket_identity_sha256,transport_profile_sha256,
supervisor_sndbuf,observer_sndbuf,observer_identity_sha256,
host_control_oracle_policy_sha256,channel_protocol_sha256`. Start tokens and
endpoint/socket objects
are complete. Linux uses the frozen seqpacket-buffer policy and both observed
send buffers are at least `524288`; Darwin uses the stream policy and both
send-buffer values are null. `channel_nonce` is fresh 64-lowercase-hex;
endpoint and protocol hashes cross-equal the complete policy; every nested
digest and the channel digest uses its object's exact domain/`0x00`/no-LF
JSON.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-channel-init-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,package_run_id,challenge,channel_identity,
channel_identity_sha256,host_control_oracle_policy_sha256,
channel_protocol_sha256,status`; status is `observer_ready`. The complete
identity and all hashes recompute from the accepted endpoint/policy/protocol
and current run. Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-control-init-v1` has
keys exactly
`domain,platform,package_run_id,challenge,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
channel_identity_sha256,host_control_oracle_policy_sha256,
channel_protocol_sha256,scenario_plan_sha256,
observation_schema_registry_sha256,status`; status is `request_pending`.
Both frames are compact no-LF JSON beneath the protocol cap, carry zero
rights, and their frame hashes cover exact uint32be prefix plus payload. The
supervisor completely consumes and validates channel-init before sending
control-init; the observer completely consumes and validates control-init
before accepting the oracle request. A hash-only identity, wrong run,
duplicate init, right, trailing byte, or missing directional state refuses.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-request-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,package_run_id,challenge,
supervisor_run_request_sha256,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
approved_launcher_capsule_policy_sha256,
execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,shared_run_binding_sha256,
platform_descriptor_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,
host_control_oracle_policy_sha256,channel_protocol_sha256,
scenario_plan_sha256,observation_schema_registry_sha256,request_nonce,
channel_identity_sha256,fd_roles,status`. Request nonce is fresh
64-lowercase-hex; roles equal the policy; and status is
`authorize_disposable_live_oracles`. One authenticated service-control frame
carries those six rights. The observer positionally validates exact
T/M/S/D/A, signed request, live supervisor, P/M plan/registry/subject/
observer closures, then runs only the enumerated isolated disposable
subjects. These subruns finish before platform activation and may exercise
later-lifecycle mechanisms in disposable runs; they never claim that the
still-future main package teardown occurred.
`request_sha256` is SHA-256 over the exact accepted request carrier bytes:
the four-byte uint32be payload length followed by the exact compact no-LF
request JSON. A payload-only, one-LF, reserialized, or alternate-prefix hash
is invalid.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-bundle-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,package_run_id,challenge,
supervisor_run_request_sha256,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
approved_launcher_capsule_policy_sha256,
execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,shared_run_binding_sha256,
platform_descriptor_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,
host_control_oracle_policy_sha256,channel_protocol_sha256,
scenario_plan_sha256,
observation_schema_registry_sha256,channel_identity_sha256,request_sha256,
oracle_run_nonce,started_monotonic_ns,
finished_monotonic_ns,process_count,processes,event_count,events,
scenario_count,scenarios,event_chain_sha256,status`. Times are canonical
uint64 decimals, end is not earlier than start,
`oracle_run_nonce` is 64-lowercase-hex and byte-equals the accepted current
request's `request_nonce`; `channel_identity_sha256` byte-equals the one
authenticated live channel; and `request_sha256` hashes the exact accepted
current request carrier,
`process_count=processes.length`, `event_count=events.length`, and
`scenario_count=scenarios.length=plan.scenario_count`; all three counts are
positive and obey the policy caps.
Bundle `platform,package_run_id,challenge,
supervisor_run_request_sha256,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
approved_launcher_capsule_policy_sha256,
execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,shared_run_binding_sha256,
platform_descriptor_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,
host_control_oracle_policy_sha256,channel_protocol_sha256,
scenario_plan_sha256,observation_schema_registry_sha256,
channel_identity_sha256,request_sha256` byte-equal the accepted current
request or the exact endpoint/policy-selected object that request names.
Every digest independently recomputes; an omitted, replayed, hash-only, or
same-run-but-different provenance value refuses.
Each process record has keys exactly
`role,pid,start_token,start_token_sha256,observer_kind,
observer_capability_identities,observer_capability_identity_set_sha256`; full
tokens occur once, hashes recompute, and `(pid,start_token)` pairs are unique.
Role is `subject|observer`. Subject records have all three observer fields
JSON null; observer records have all three nonnull and bind one exact
plan-selected subject process. The capability array is unique and
unsigned-byte sorted by `(kernel_object_kind,
kernel_object_identity.identifier)`. Canonical
`stage2-host-control-oracle-observer-capability-identity-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,role,observer_kind,observer_pid,observer_start_token,
subject_pid,subject_start_token,kernel_object_kind,kernel_object_identity,
access_mode,retention_phase`. Kernel-object kind is exactly
`cgroupfs_fd|clock_monotonic|kqueue|mach_vm_region|pidfd|proc_pidinfo|
procfs_fd|socket_probe|sysctl_snapshot`. Canonical
`stage2-host-control-oracle-kernel-object-identity-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,kind,device,inode,identifier,registration_flags,
observation_source_sha256`; kind cross-equals the enclosing field,
device/inode are canonical uint64 decimals or the schema-declared null for an
API without an fstat identity, identifier is the exact canonical kernel
cookie/ident/pathless token, flags are a unique ordered array from the
plan-selected observer API, and source hash selects the exact P/M observer
adapter. The complete kernel-object identity object is embedded as
`kernel_object_identity` and is covered by the enclosing observer-capability
digest; it is never replaced by a digest string or unconstrained value.
Capability `role` is exactly `observer`, `platform` byte-equals the bundle
platform, and `observer_kind` byte-equals both the enclosing observer process
and its selected subject profile's closed `observer_kind`.
The closed kind table is:

| Observer kind | Required capability kinds, in array order | Device/inode | Exact identifier form | Exact registration flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `linux_host_control_oracle_v1` | `cgroupfs_fd,clock_monotonic,pidfd,procfs_fd,socket_probe` | nonnull for `cgroupfs_fd,pidfd,procfs_fd,socket_probe`; null for `clock_monotonic` | `<kind>:<subject_pid>:<subject_start_token_sha256>` | `cgroupfs_fd=["O_CLOEXEC","O_DIRECTORY","O_RDONLY"]`; `clock_monotonic=["CLOCK_MONOTONIC"]`; `pidfd=[]`; `procfs_fd=["O_CLOEXEC","O_DIRECTORY","O_RDONLY"]`; `socket_probe=["SOCK_CLOEXEC","SOCK_SEQPACKET"]` |
| `darwin_host_control_oracle_v1` | `clock_monotonic,kqueue,mach_vm_region,proc_pidinfo,sysctl_snapshot` | nonnull for `kqueue`; null for the four API snapshots | `<kind>:<subject_pid>:<subject_start_token_sha256>` | `clock_monotonic=["CLOCK_MONOTONIC"]`; `kqueue=["EV_ADD","EV_ENABLE","EV_ONESHOT","NOTE_EXIT"]`; `mach_vm_region=["MACH_VM_REGION_RECURSE"]`; `proc_pidinfo=["PROC_PIDFDINFO","PROC_PIDLISTFDS","PROC_PIDREGIONPATHINFO"]`; `sysctl_snapshot=["KERN_BOOTTIME","KERN_PROC","KERN_PROC_PID"]` |

The array contains exactly one identity for every required kind and no other
kind. Canonical
`stage2-host-control-oracle-observer-capability-set-v1` is the complete
array; `observer_capability_identity_set_sha256` is SHA-256 over that exact
ASCII domain, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF `JSON.stringify(array)`.
Access is `read_observe_only`, and retention is
`through_subject_exit_and_final_event`. PID/start values cross-equal the
process table and cannot come from the subject. The capability digest uses
the complete object's exact domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimage.

Each event has keys exactly
`sequence,scenario_id,phase,event_kind,monotonic_ns,subject_process_index,
observer_process_index,observer_capability_index,observation_domain,
observation_schema_sha256,observation_json,observation_sha256,
previous_event_sha256,event_sha256`.
Sequence is `1..event_count`; `monotonic_ns` is a canonical uint64 decimal
within the inclusive bundle `[started_monotonic_ns,finished_monotonic_ns]`
range and is nondecreasing; the first previous hash is null, and each later
one equals the prior event hash. `phase` is a nonempty printable-ASCII string
that byte-equals the parsed observation's required top-level `phase` value;
the uniquely selected closed observation schema supplies its complete enum,
so an unlisted phase refuses. `observation_json`
is a JSON string containing `1..262144` exact canonical no-LF UTF-8 JSON bytes
selected by the P/M registry; `262144` byte-equals the selected policy's
`observation_byte_cap`. It is parsed once as a complete value with no
BOM, LF, trailing byte, duplicate key, unsafe integer, or noncanonical
encoding; predicates and schema validation operate on that parsed value.
`observation_sha256` is SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 bytes contained in the
string, never over the enclosing JSON string encoding. Both process
indices are safe integers in `0..process_count-1`, select the declared
subject/observer roles. `observer_capability_index` is a safe integer within
the selected observer's complete capability array; that identity binds the
selected subject and its kind byte-equals the resolved registry record.
`event_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-host-control-oracle-event-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` of the insertion-ordered projection through
`previous_event_sha256`, excluding `event_sha256`. Because event count is
positive, `event_chain_sha256` equals the last event hash; a zero-event or
alternate empty-chain rule refuses.

Each scenario result has keys exactly
`scenario_id,polarity,mutation_id,first_sequence,last_sequence,
expected_terminal,observed_terminal,subject_exit_kind,subject_exit_status,
forbidden_effect_count,status`. There is exactly one record per plan scenario
in plan order. First/last sequence are safe integers with
`1 <= first_sequence <= last_sequence <= event_count`; ordered
nonoverlapping ranges cover every event. Each result's
`scenario_id,polarity,mutation_id,expected_terminal` byte-equal its plan
record. Every event inside that result's inclusive range has exactly that
`scenario_id` and one fixed `(subject_process_index,observer_process_index)`
pair whose complete observer-capability set binds that subject, an
`observation_domain` listed by the plan record's `event_domains`, and an
`observation_schema_sha256` equal to the unique registry record resolved by
that domain and event kind. The range selects every required capability kind
at least once. The fixed subject token's executable path and
hash byte-equal the selected profile's
`subject_entrypoint_path,subject_entrypoint_sha256`. The range contains one
observer-derived `subject_launch` event selected by
`subject_launch_predicate_id`; its executable path/hash and `argv_sha256`
byte-equal that profile. No matching-scenario event lies outside the range. Each
scenario range contains every and only the events used to evaluate its plan
predicates.
`subject_exit_kind` is exactly
`exit_code|signal|timeout|observer_refusal`; `subject_exit_status` is a safe integer
`0..255` for `exit_code`, `1..127` for `signal`, and null for
`timeout|observer_refusal`. Positive status is `PASS`; negative status is
`EXPECTED_REFUSAL`; observed/expected terminals equal and forbidden-effect
count is zero. The unique event selected by `subject_exit_predicate_id`
supplies `subject_exit_kind,subject_exit_status_text`; the validator derives
the result's status integer or null from that closed string, enforces the
kind-dependent range/nullability above, and byte-compares both derived fields
to the scenario result. The
unique terminal match supplies `observed_terminal`. The validator recomputes
terminal, both exit fields, forbidden-effect count, and status from the exact
plan predicates/events and requires those values to byte-equal the scenario
record. It separately recomputes every assertion rule
and requires all true; no observer-supplied assertion-result field exists.
Bundle status `PASS` means the independent observer proved the complete plan,
never that a subject printed or emitted PASS.

Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-bundle-file-identity-v1` has keys
exactly
`domain,platform,protection_profile,device,inode,size,mode,link_count,seals,
access_mode,descriptor_flags,sha256`. Device, inode, size, and link count are
canonical uint64 decimals; size is `1..16777216`, mode is `"0400"`, link
count is `"0"`, access is `read_only`, descriptor flags are
`["FD_CLOEXEC"]`, and `sha256` hashes exact compact bundle plus one LF.
Linux uses `memfd_create(MFD_CLOEXEC|MFD_ALLOW_SEALING)`, `seals` exactly
`["F_SEAL_WRITE","F_SEAL_GROW","F_SEAL_SHRINK","F_SEAL_SEAL"]`, a
complete write, `fchmod(writer_fd,0400)`, exact writer `fstat`, all four
seals, a read-only procfd reopen with exact identity/mode/seal revalidation,
and writer close. Darwin uses `seals:null`, an
exclusive private file, complete write,
fchmod-`0400`, file/parent fsync, read-only reopen, writer close, unlink plus
parent fsync, link-count zero, and no writable alias. Canonical
`stage2-host-control-oracle-result-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,status,request_sha256,bundle_file_identity,
bundle_file_identity_sha256,event_chain_sha256,process_count,event_count,
scenario_count,fd_roles`; status is `PASS` and roles equal the policy. The
observer sends one bounded result with exactly one read-only bundle right,
then closes all its bundle descriptions. The supervisor validates exact
bytes, identity/protection, bundle graph, authenticated channel/service, and
result EOF before accepting.
`bundle_file_identity_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-host-control-oracle-bundle-file-identity-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact
no-LF `JSON.stringify` of the complete identity. It is distinct from the
nested `identity.sha256`, which hashes the bundle's exact one-LF bytes.
`request_sha256` byte-equals the SHA-256 of the exact accepted current request
carrier, including its four-byte uint32be prefix, and byte-equals the
validated bundle's `request_sha256`; the bundle's `oracle_run_nonce` and
`channel_identity_sha256` byte-equal that request's nonce and live channel.
The result's three counts and `event_chain_sha256` byte-equal the validated
bundle; `bundle_file_identity.sha256` recomputes from those exact one-LF
bundle bytes, and the complete identity digest recomputes before the one
returned right is accepted.

Oracle subjects possess no observer endpoint, output writer, T/S/D/A
authority, package-output authority, or bundle writer. The observer derives
facts only from retained pidfd/kqueue, proc/sysctl/proc_pidinfo, FD-table,
syscall return/errno, stream EOF, and process-tree observations. Subject
stdout, structured events, claimed status, exit zero, and the bundle's own
top-level status are insufficient. Only static identity/policy/plan/registry/
validator hashes enter T/P/M/S/D/A. The live bundle is created after D/A,
enters only activation, AC01/AC17 evidence, and the later signed admission/
catalog graph, and never enters T/P/M/S/D/A, the signed request, commitment,
or its own plan. This is the exact acyclic anti-self-attestation boundary.

Canonical `supervisor_identity` is
`stage2-host-supervisor-identity-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,platform,runtime_path,runtime_sha256,source_path,source_sha256,
system_runtime_manifest_path,system_runtime_manifest_sha256,
import_manifest_path,import_manifest_sha256,argv_sha256`. Domain and platform
are exact. Every path is canonical absolute and nonsymlink beneath the

The import manifest uses `stage2-attestation-import-closure-v1` with keys
exactly `domain,platform,entrypoint_path,entrypoint_sha256,builtin_modules,
files`. Built-in names are unique unsigned-byte sorted. Files are unique by
unsigned-byte-sorted `specifier` and have keys exactly
`specifier,resolved_path,sha256,kind`, where kind is
`source|json|native_addon`; no unlisted import, addon, filesystem resolution,
eval, loader, framework, or shared object is legal.
`import_manifest_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-attestation-import-closure-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` of that manifest.
`supervisor_identity_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-host-supervisor-identity-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify(supervisor_identity)`.

Canonical `attestation_execution_closure` is
`stage2-attestation-execution-closure-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,platform,runtime_path,runtime_sha256,bootstrap_path,
bootstrap_sha256,system_runtime_manifest_path,
system_runtime_manifest_sha256,import_manifest_path,
import_manifest_sha256`. Its system-runtime and import manifests obey the

`attestation_execution_closure_sha256` uses its exact domain/`0x00`/no-LF

Canonical `approved_launcher_capsule_policy` is
`stage2-approved-launcher-capsule-policy-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,platform,git_commit,contract_sha256,registry_sha256,

linux_node_post_exec_reseal_addon_sha256,
linux_node_post_exec_reseal_policy,
linux_node_post_exec_reseal_policy_sha256,

linux_scratch_transition_helper_argv_sha256,

linux_scratch_privilege_policy_sha256,export_policy_sha256`. Domain/platform,
commit, contract, registry, manifest locator/profile, runtime, launcher, FD

The key provider is a P/M-inventoried native addon that exposes only opaque
key generation, public-key export, domain-specific signing, and the exact

Darwin's aggregate-role digest and all Linux helper/broker/scratch/reseal
fields are null. Both platforms' native spawn gate fields are nonnull exact P/M entries
and their complete policy object/digest fields are nonnull and exact: Darwin
uses the suspended native gate frozen below, while Linux
uses the static key-free direct-child gate frozen below. Linux's aggregate-
role digest is the digest of the exact aggregate role array frozen below, and
its transition helper is the exact statically
linked PIE in P/M, with no `PT_INTERP`, `DT_NEEDED`, dynamic loader, or
second executable. That helper remains as exactly one single-threaded broker
child while its original PID execs the zero-capability Node supervisor; no
other transition-helper process or exec is legal. The separate Linux child
spawn gate is never used for the supervisor, helper, or broker. The helper
argv and every complete broker policy object/digest are frozen below.
`platform_activation_fd_roles_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-platform-activation-fd-roles-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` of the seven-role array; the nonnull
`aggregate_activation_fd_roles_sha256` uses exact ASCII
`stage2-aggregate-activation-fd-roles-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` of the fifteen-role array.
`approved_launcher_capsule_policy_sha256` uses its exact
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimage.

Canonical `stage2-linux-scratch-privilege-policy-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,user_namespace_creation,mount_namespace_creation,
outer_identity_policy,uid_map_policy,gid_map_policy,setgroups_policy,
supplementary_groups_policy,mount_propagation_policy,cap_last_cap_max,
cap_setpcap_number,cap_sys_ptrace_number,cap_sys_admin_number,
helper_prefork_capabilities,node_zero_capabilities,
broker_active_capabilities,broker_post_teardown_capabilities`. Its fixed
scalar values are respectively `same_pid_static_helper_with_one_broker`,
`after_fresh_user_namespace`,
`nonroot_no_outer_capabilities`, `single_id_outer_euid_to_namespace_zero`,

Before filter load the one-threaded broker occupies every guarded slot with
an independently verified CLOEXEC eventfd guard. Immediately before one
declared receive/socketpair/open/memfd operation it closes only that
operation's exact ordered slot or slots; the return/received FDs must equal

slot is restored only by exact

before continuing. The frozen
one-way ledger accounts for every close/transfer/reuse; generic

Each `argument_rules` record has keys exactly
`syscall,variant,conditions`; each condition has keys exactly
`argument_index,operation,value,mask`, with operation
`eq|masked_eq|range`. The complete array has at least one exhaustive variant
for every allowed syscall and no variant for another syscall. Scalar
kernel-visible arguments are enforced by cBPF; `pointer_argument_policy` is
exactly
`pinned_static_binary_validates_all_pointer_bytes_and_syscall_postconditions`.
The P/M-bound broker validates every pathname, `open_how`, `msghdr`, iovec,
control message, buffer byte/length, returned FD, and syscall postcondition
because classic BPF cannot inspect pointed-to bytes or return values. The
FD-plan and seccomp-policy digests each use their exact domain/`0x00`/no-LF
JSON preimages.
A filter load without `TSYNC`, a second TID, an
unknown architecture, a permissive default, or filter-byte drift refuses

The Linux controller invokes exactly
`[linux_scratch_transition_helper_path,"--",
supervisor_runtime_path,"--no-warnings","--require",
linux_node_post_exec_reseal_prelude_path,supervisor_source_path,
"--platform","linux","--host-attestation-trust-fd","3",
"--execution-root-fd","4","--controller-channel-fd","5",
"--scratch-broker-fd","6","--scratch-broker-pidfd","7",
"--process-domain-fd","8","--scratch-parent-fd","9",
"--controller-placement-release-fd","10"]`; the no-LF
JSON-array hash is `linux_scratch_transition_helper_argv_sha256`. The helper
runs single-threaded in the future supervisor PID. Before executing any
namespace, capability, mount, pipe, socket, or fork operation, its first
static-gate action validates FD 10 and blocks for exactly one byte `0x01`
plus EOF. The controller releases that barrier only after the T-bound
provisioner has placed the pidfd-bound future supervisor in the fresh leaf,
sealed all join/move authority, returned the independent read-only leaf
descriptions, and the controller has cross-validated PID/start token,
leased UID/GID, leaf identity, membership, and helper FD 8. The helper
closes FD 10 immediately after accepting the release.
It starts with the final supervisor's exact
empty environment, source-directory cwd, umask `0077`, new process group,
stdio, FDs 3..5, the independently provisioned read-only cgroup leaf at FD 8,
and the independently provisioned scratch parent at FD 9. It requires outer
effective UID/GID both in
`1..4294967294`, outer effective/permitted/inheritable/ambient capability sets
empty, and `getgroups(0,NULL)==0`. It executes, in order:
`unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)`; writes exact `0 <outer_euid> 1\n` to
`/proc/self/uid_map`; rechecks the still-empty supplementary-group set;
writes exact `deny\n` to `/proc/self/setgroups`; writes exact
`0 <outer_egid> 1\n` to `/proc/self/gid_map`; sets all
real/effective/saved/filesystem IDs to namespace zero;
`unshare(CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWCGROUP)`; mounts root recursively private;
binds a cgroup2 view rooted at the already joined leaf read-only inside the
private mount namespace; closes every outside cgroup path; and verifies the
fresh cgroup namespace exposes exactly that leaf. While namespace-local
`CAP_SETPCAP` remains effective, it drops every bounding bit except
`[8,19,21]`, clears every effective/permitted bit except `[8,19,21]`, clears
inheritable/ambient, requires `no_new_privs=0`, and fixed-point verifies the
exact one-thread `helper_prefork_capabilities` profile. It validates FD 8,
membership, FD 9, and both policies; creates one private
`socketpair(AF_UNIX,SOCK_SEQPACKET|SOCK_CLOEXEC,0,sv)`; creates and verifies a
zero-count `eventfd(0,EFD_CLOEXEC|EFD_NONBLOCK)` guard; creates one
parent-to-child observer-release `pipe2(O_CLOEXEC)` and one independent
child-to-parent seal `pipe2(O_CLOEXEC)`; normalizes their per-process live
ends to FD 11 and FD 12 respectively; and calls `fork`
exactly once while still single-threaded. No callback, signal handler, or
other thread can run across this sequence.

The child's first post-fork operation is
`prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG,SIGKILL)`, followed immediately by
`getppid()==<expected-supervisor-pid>`; either failure refuses, closing the
parent-death race. It then closes the parent ends and blocks on FD 11. The
parent closes the child ends, opens and validates the child's original
pidfd/PID/full start token, installs the broker observer, writes exactly one
byte `0x01` to FD 11, and closes it; the child requires that byte plus EOF
before continuing and closes FD 11.
In the child, exact file actions first place the eventfd guard at FD 19 and
verify it, then
atomically `dup3` the independently provisioned scratch-parent FD over that
guard at 19, place a pidfd for its parent at FD 20, open trusted `/proc` at FD
21, and close every other description except empty captured stdio, T FD 3,
broker endpoint FD 6, process-domain FD 8, seal writer FD 12, and FDs 19..21.
It then performs
one exact-path `execve` of the same static helper bytes with the frozen
`--scratch-broker` argv and empty environment. The parent attached the broker
observer before this release. The final broker revalidates executable, argv,
FD table, `PR_GET_PDEATHSIG==SIGKILL`,
`getppid()==<expected-supervisor-pid>`, parent start token, namespaces,
process domain, and one TID before sending ready. While
`CAP_SETPCAP` is effective it drops every bounding bit `0..cap_last_cap`,
then clears SETPCAP and retains only effective/permitted capabilities
`[19,21]`, empty inheritable/ambient/bounding sets, `no_new_privs=1`, and
`PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0`. It installs the exact seccomp filter and requires
`/proc/self/task` to contain only its PID before and after every privileged
operation. After that one broker exec it never execs, forks, clones, creates
a network endpoint other than the exact session socketpair, or loads another
byte. `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` is exactly `SIGKILL`; loss of the supervisor can
never yield success and disposal of the private namespace is the recovery.
After the final capability/seccomp/one-TID checks, the broker writes exactly
one byte `0x01` to helper-only FD 12 and closes it. The parent
requires that byte plus EOF and closes its reader before it may drop its own
profiles or exec Node. The barrier survives in neither final process.

The original parent opens and retains the broker pidfd at FD 7, places its
control endpoint at FD 6, retains the read-only process-domain FD 8, and
closes FD 9 and every helper-only description. While SETPCAP remains
effective it drops every bounding bit, then clears every effective,
permitted, inheritable, and ambient capability and sets `no_new_privs=1` and

frozen post-exec reseal prelude inserted before the repository entrypoint,

crosses the role's independently observed ready barrier. The launcher and
every bootstrap, gate, coordinator, aggregate, validator, and verifier child

application-action reseal; no zero-capability descendant invokes
`capset`, `PR_CAPBSET_DROP`, or another privileged transition.

observation refuses. Darwin never uses this helper or broker.

  `{"path":"fixtures/stage2-host-attestation-trust-v1.json",

match M's profile; P's `contract_sha256` and `registry_sha256` cross-equal

equally exact: first require complete equality of all eight inserted fields,
then remove that sole exact path from M.entries, decrement the count by one,
project the four shared top-level values above, and restore only
P.domain/platform/contract/registry from the already selected T policy. The
result must byte-equal P. `regular_file`, `data_only`, and
`independently_pinned_manifest` are legal in this combination only for this
one T entry. Link count is not an entry key: the image-tree object at this
path is separately required to be ordinary, nonsymlink, mode `0400`, and
link-count one. An alternate kind/load/source/locator, an extra/missing/
reordered entry, a same-path unequal record, a second T entry, a reserved
descriptor in entries, another excluded/generated field, a count mismatch,
or any alternate forward/inverse mapping refuses. Thus T never hashes the
full manifest that contains T, and the graph has no T/capsule cycle.

The concrete T-bound authority first parses enough canonical bytes to derive
both keys, then in one durable transaction inserts both unique rows and the
complete receipt. It durability-confirms that transaction before semantic
validation can produce a signature. A collision, failed validation, failed
signing, or crash after confirmed commit leaves both keys permanently
consumed. An uncertain commit produces no signature and blocks that authority
until the T-bound recovery policy proves the committed outcome; it never
retries with another nonce. The complete receipt and digest enter the signed
request. No volatile latch, crash-reset state, alternate ledger, or
`sign(bytes)` operation exists.

Before the run ID or challenge is chosen, both acceptance-host supervisors
independently pin the same exact T bytes and expected digest through
configuration whose write/selection authority is unavailable to the
federation assembler, S constructor, launchers, gates, aggregators,
repository worktree, argv, or environment. Each directly compares its local
T FD and verifies the controller/attestation public keys, supervisor and
bootstrap closures, authorization IDs, approved static projection, runtime,
launcher, activation roles, and export policy. The deterministic S/D/A
constructor is explicitly untrusted: it receives only public T, the exact
launch offers, signed requests, commitments, and attestations through offset-independent
read-only copies, may not claim an external pin, and cannot nominate any
value. Both launchers and both supervisors revalidate the constructor's

The full-duplex per-direction state sequences are exact. For

`launcher_activation`, supervisor-to-launcher is

omitted on Darwin, and launcher-to-supervisor is
`launcher_exec_ready -> SHUT_WR/EOF`. For `keystore_session`,
keystore-to-bootstrap is
`channel_init -> signed_result -> SHUT_WR/EOF`, while
bootstrap-to-keystore is `attestation_request -> SHUT_WR/EOF`. A frame in the
wrong direction/state, a repeated/skipped state, premature half-close, byte or
right between states, or final held/missing EOF is fatal. The generic
one-frame parser rule is therefore per declared state, never a claim that a
multi-state channel carries only one frame in its lifetime.
