Linux attaches exactly one ordered `SCM_RIGHTS` description,
`acceptance_reader`; Darwin attaches zero rights and both pipe hashes are
null. After successful Linux `sendmsg`, the supervisor closes its
acceptance-reader copy immediately and may not retry; the controller receives,
validates, and retains the sole reader while the supervisor retains the sole
writer. No controller, assembler, constructor, launcher, bootstrap, gate,
aggregate, validator, or descendant ever owns another acceptance writer.
After the sole offer packet on either platform, the supervisor performs
`shutdown(FD5,SHUT_WR)`; the controller must observe that directional EOF and
no second supervisor byte/right before it may sign.
The supervisor retains the context read end as final observer and the context
write end only as request-authorized transfer escrow; neither endpoint ever
enters the controller, assembler, or constructor. Before the aggregate
transfer the escrow writer is never written, duplicated, or polled by another
process and no other process can successfully open or duplicate it.
`ioctl(FIONREAD)` on the retained reader must report exactly zero, but that
proves only byte emptiness, never ownership. Sole-writer closure derives from
creation by the nondumpable dedicated-UID supervisor inside the closed
process domain, exact CLOEXEC/default child tables, broker fixed-point scans
of every run-domain FD table, one recorded role-15 transfer, immediate sender
close, and eventual reader EOF. The ordinary fact that the supervisor's own
FD appears in `/proc/<supervisor>/fd` is not called exposure. Any successful
proc-FD open/duplication, pre-transfer byte, duplicate, inherited description,
unreadable run-domain entry, or nonzero readable count consumes the run.

Canonical `stage2-one-shot-pipe-identity-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,purpose,platform,pipe_device,pipe_inode,channel_nonce,reader_pid,
reader_start_token,writer_pid,writer_start_token`; purpose is
`package_acceptance`, device/inode are canonical uint64 decimals, and nonce
is fresh 64-lowercase-hex. Canonical
`stage2-supervisor-context-channel-identity-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,pipe_device,pipe_inode,channel_nonce,reader_pid,
reader_start_token,escrow_pid,escrow_start_token,writer_pid,
writer_start_token,launcher_activation_channel_identity_sha256,
activation_mode,activation_fd_role_index`. On Linux, reader and escrow are
the exact supervisor, final writer is the original launcher,
`activation_mode` is `aggregate`, and `activation_fd_role_index` is `15`;
on Darwin the record and hash are null. Both pipe hashes use their exact
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimages.

The controller independently validates the launch offer, attached Linux
reader, T/P/M delta, live supervisor and launcher observers, all channel
identities, and policy before invoking its request-only signing handle. It
sends exactly one signed-request packet on FD 5 with the same uint32be/
compact-JSON `1..262144` framing, then performs write shutdown. The supervisor
requires that packet, peer EOF, and no other byte/right; validates and retains
the exact request; creates fresh offset-independent request bytes for the
bootstrap; and closes FD 5. The controller observes its own completed request
packet and write shutdown as `supervisor_request_frame_eof`, which starts the
encompassing external timeout. Offer/request reversal, a second frame in
either offer or request state,
attached request right, missing peer shutdown, alternate bytes, or a
controller/supervisor-channel duplicate refuses before launcher release.

Each controller-signed `stage2-host-supervisor-run-request-v1` envelope has
top-level keys exactly `domain,payload,controller_key_id,signature_hex`.
Payload keys are exactly
`package_run_id,challenge,request_nonce,
controller_request_authorization_id,
controller_request_authority_identity_sha256,
controller_request_latch_policy_sha256,
controller_request_latch_receipt,
controller_request_latch_receipt_sha256,
platform,issued_at,expires_at,
host_attestation_trust_sha256,approved_launcher_capsule_policy_sha256,
execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,host_attestation_key_id,
keystore_service_identity_sha256,keystore_ledger_policy_sha256,
supervisor_pid,supervisor_start_token,supervisor_process_group,launcher_pid,
launcher_start_token,launcher_process_group,launcher_argv_sha256,
launcher_source_sha256,node_executable_sha256,
system_runtime_manifest_sha256,attestation_execution_closure_sha256,
keystore_authorization_id,launcher_exec_ready_sha256,launch_offer_sha256,
linux_seqpacket_transport_probe_sha256,
linux_cgroup_provisioner_channel_identity_sha256,
linux_cgroup_domain_ready_sha256,
linux_scratch_privilege_policy_sha256,
linux_scratch_namespace_identity_sha256,
linux_scratch_setup_privilege_state_sha256,
linux_fd19_guard_identity_sha256,
controller_channel_identity_sha256,
launcher_activation_channel_identity_sha256,
keystore_service_control_channel_identity_sha256,
acceptance_pipe_identity_sha256,
supervisor_context_sink_identity_sha256,
supervisor_startup_timeout_start_event,
supervisor_startup_timeout_end_event,supervisor_startup_timeout_ms,
supervisor_run_timeout_start_event,supervisor_run_timeout_ms`.
`issued_at`/`expires_at` are Unix-epoch
milliseconds, `expires_at-issued_at` is exactly `300000`, the start event is
`controller_channel_creation_call_entry`, the startup end and run start are
both `supervisor_request_frame_eof`, and both timeout values equal the export
policy.
Every offer, policy, manifest, process, launcher, runtime, channel, pipe, and
key value cross-equals T and live kernel observations.
The Linux transport-probe digest recomputes under T's buffer policy; the five
cgroup/scratch digests and guard digest equal the complete launch-offer
objects and T policy. All seven are null on Darwin. Both service and
controller authority/ledger hashes cross-equal T and the live control
channel. The complete latch receipt recomputes and its two unique keys are
already durability-confirmed.
`controller_key_id` equals T;
the signature is 128 lowercase hexadecimal Ed25519 over exact ASCII domain,
one `0x00`, and exact no-LF `JSON.stringify(payload)`.
`supervisor_run_request_sha256` hashes the exact compact envelope plus one LF.
`supervisor_run_request_set_sha256` hashes exact ASCII
`stage2-host-supervisor-run-request-set-v1`, one `0x00`, and no-LF JSON of
Linux-then-Darwin records with keys
`platform,controller_key_id,supervisor_run_request_sha256`.

The supervisor preserves the exact received signed-envelope payload bytes and
frame length in two separately sealed offset-independent read-only
descriptions: one retained by the supervisor and one starting at offset zero
for the bootstrap. It never shares an open-file-description offset and never
reserializes the request.

Only after request acceptance, the supervisor sends exactly one no-rights
`stage2-launcher-request-release-v1` packet on the retained launcher
activation channel, with uint32be `N` plus `N` compact JSON bytes without LF
for `N` in `1..4096`. Keys are exactly
`domain,platform,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
launcher_exec_ready_sha256,launcher_activation_channel_identity_sha256`.
The launcher validates the packet against T, its exact ready state, live
supervisor peer, and channel, retains both hashes, and only then generates
its ephemeral key and writes its commitment. A second/replayed/reordered/
rights-bearing release, activation before release, or key/commitment before
release refuses the run.

Wrong/expired/replayed/cross-platform requests, alternate bytes,
trailing/duplicate/held frames, a wrong controller key, offer mismatch, or any
policy, manifest, process, channel, or closure mismatch refuses before
commitment.

Each exact host-root-signed envelope has top-level keys
`domain,payload,attestation_key_id,signature_hex`; domain is
`stage2-launcher-host-attestation-v1`. Its payload keys are exactly
`package_run_id,challenge,platform,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
approved_launcher_capsule_policy_sha256,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
attestation_execution_closure_sha256,keystore_authorization_id,
keystore_service_identity_sha256,keystore_ledger_policy_sha256,
keystore_service_control_channel_identity_sha256,
keystore_session_identity,keystore_session_identity_sha256,
bootstrap_pid,bootstrap_start_token,
bootstrap_process_group,
execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,node_path,node_executable_sha256,
system_runtime_manifest_sha256,federation_launcher_path,
federation_launcher_sha256,launcher_argv_sha256,launcher_pid,
launcher_start_token,launcher_process_group,launcher_nonce,
launcher_commitment_sha256,launcher_commitment_frame_sha256,key_id,
public_key_hex`. Every value cross-equals T, the signed request, live process,
the complete commitment, and the measured capsule/launcher. Signature key ID
must equal the independently pinned record for that platform. `signature_hex` is
exactly 128 lowercase hexadecimal encoding the Ed25519 signature over exact
ASCII `domain`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF `JSON.stringify(payload)`.
`launcher_commitment_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-launcher-public-key-commitment-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify(launcher_commitment)`.
`launcher_commitment_frame_sha256` hashes the exact four-byte uint32be length
plus commitment JSON bytes. Each bootstrap refuses a reused run/challenge,
wrong-host key, stale commitment, unmeasured byte, alternate preimage, or
signing before the complete commitment frame and EOF.

`host_attestation_set_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-launcher-host-attestation-set-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` of Linux-then-Darwin records with keys exactly
`platform,attestation_key_id,host_attestation_sha256`, where each SHA covers
the exact compact signed-envelope JSON plus one LF. S embeds the exact two
requests, commitments, and attestations in the launcher-trust records and
verifies their public graph; the untrusted constructor does not claim the
external pin. The controllers, supervisors, registered bootstraps/keystores,
and persistent launchers directly compare T through their independently
provisioned capabilities. Every gate, aggregate, admission/receipt validator,
and package validator instead receives exact `Ht,Hat` values transitively
from its host-attested live launcher context, reopens the immutable capsule T
copy, requires equality with S/D/A, and reverifies both requests and host
signatures without claiming a child-local external pin.

`launcher_trust` is canonical
`stage2-federation-launcher-trust-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,algorithm,signature_encoding,platforms`. Domain is exact, algorithm
is `Ed25519`, signature encoding is `lowercase_hex`, and platforms is Linux
then Darwin. Each platform record has keys exactly
`platform,launch_offer,launch_offer_sha256,supervisor_run_request,
supervisor_run_request_sha256,key_id,
public_key_hex,node_path,node_executable_sha256,
system_runtime_manifest_sha256,federation_launcher_path,
federation_launcher_sha256,launcher_commitment,
launcher_commitment_frame_sha256,host_attestation`.
`launch_offer` is that platform's exact retained canonical offer and its hash
cross-equals the controller-signed request. `host_attestation` is that
platform's exact validated signed envelope and its
hash participates in `host_attestation_set_sha256`. `public_key_hex` is
exactly 64 lowercase
hexadecimal encoding the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key; `key_id` is SHA-256
over those raw 32 bytes. Node, system-runtime, launcher path, and launcher
hash cross-equal the selected capsule/runtime and the shared launcher source.
`launcher_commitment` is canonical
`stage2-launcher-public-key-commitment-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,platform,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
launcher_exec_ready_sha256,execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,node_path,
node_executable_sha256,system_runtime_manifest_sha256,
federation_launcher_path,federation_launcher_sha256,launcher_argv_sha256,
launcher_pid,launcher_start_token,launcher_process_group,launcher_nonce,
launcher_key_isolation_state,launcher_key_isolation_state_sha256,
host_attestation_trust_sha256,key_id,public_key_hex`; domain is exact and
every duplicated value
cross-equals its enclosing record. The two key IDs and launcher nonces are
distinct. `launcher_trust_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact
ASCII `stage2-federation-launcher-trust-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify(launcher_trust)`.

Before S serialization, each host-root-attested platform-local launcher
generates exactly one independent Ed25519 keypair inside its own process and
exports only the public-key commitment used by `launcher_trust`. No bootstrap,
federator, transport process, other host, sibling launcher, or child ever
receives private bytes, and no process may possess both private keys. The same
launcher process and start token persist from that commitment through its
platform gate; the Linux launcher additionally persists through aggregation
and final package admission. After `S,D_L,D_D,A` fill the reserved slots, each
launcher revalidates the finalized capsule, externally pinned host-trust
digest, both host attestations, and its own public key/key ID against
`S.launcher_trust` before any lock or output.

Canonical `stage2-launcher-ephemeral-key-memory-policy-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,algorithm,private_key_storage,private_region_lock,
private_region_dump,private_region_fork,temporary_copy_policy,
spawn_serialization_policy,child_absence_probe,zeroization_policy`.
Common values are `Ed25519`, `dedicated_anonymous_locked_mapping`,
`mlock_required`, `no_private_stack_or_heap_copy`,
`process_wide_spawn_lock`, and
`explicit_bzero_before_munlock_and_munmap`. Linux dump/fork/probe values are
`madvise_dontdump_and_dumpable_zero`, `madvise_dontfork`, and
`static_gate_parent_proc_maps_between_0x01_and_release_then_0x02_reseal`;
Darwin values are
`rlimit_core_zero_and_pt_deny_attach`, `vm_inherit_none`, and
`child_suspended_vm_region_absence`. The native key provider holds every
private-bearing temporary in that same arena, exposes only an opaque handle,
and serializes signing against child creation.
`launcher_key_memory_policy_sha256` uses the complete platform record's exact
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimage.

Canonical `stage2-launcher-key-isolation-state-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,launcher_pid,launcher_start_token_sha256,policy_sha256,
private_region_count,private_region_locked,private_region_nondumpable,
private_region_noninheritable,core_dump_disabled,
ptrace_or_task_access_denied,temporary_private_copy_count,status`. Values are
one region, all booleans true, zero copies, and `PASS`. The complete state and
digest enter the public-key commitment; the host keystore independently
validates it before signing.
`launcher_key_isolation_state_sha256` uses the complete state's exact
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimage.

Canonical `stage2-launcher-child-key-absence-proof-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,platform,launcher_pid,launcher_start_token_sha256,child_role,
child_pid,child_start_token_sha256,policy_sha256,probe_mechanism,
observed_private_region_count,status`. `probe_mechanism` exactly equals the
platform policy. Linux uses the exact static-gate `0x01` blocked/dumpable
window for parent `/proc/<gate>/maps` observation after the DONTFORK boundary,
then requires release, final exact exec, the final Node prelude's post-exec
reseal and `0x02`, nondumpable final state, and the same PID/start identity
before constructing the proof.
Darwin's native gate inspects the suspended child VM map after
`VM_INHERIT_NONE`. Count is zero and status is `PASS`. Each phase launcher
context carries the complete proof/digest for its direct gate or aggregate
child. A missing lock,
swappable/dumpable/inheritable region, temporary copy, unlocked spawn,
private mapping in a child, or unverifiable probe refuses before child
context release.
`launcher_child_key_absence_proof_sha256` uses the complete proof's exact
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimage.
Its `policy_sha256` is exactly `launcher_key_memory_policy_sha256`; an
implementation-selected child-probe policy hash is invalid.

Before key generation, the launcher applies the exact memory policy, core/
task-access denial, and process nondumpability. Private bytes are held only
by the nonexportable provider and every child is created after the explicit
absence proof.
Private bytes never enter argv, environment, filesystem, capsule, transport,
log, receipt, evidence, archive, or child FD and are zeroized when the
launcher terminates. A restarted launcher, commitment replay, key import,
exportable handle, cross-host key reuse, wrong derived key, or failed
memory/process isolation refuses the whole package run; a new run uses new
launchers, run ID, challenge, and keys.

For every exact Node argv below, `linux_node_prefix` is exactly
`[node_linux,"--no-warnings","--require",
linux_node_post_exec_reseal_prelude_path]`, `darwin_node_prefix` is exactly
`[node_darwin,"--no-warnings"]`, and `node_prefix_p` selects the one matching
platform `p`. Array-spread notation below means literal insertion of every
selected prefix element in order; it is not a runtime-expansion permission.

The two launchers' immutable initial argv values are respectively
`[...linux_node_prefix,"scripts/run-stage2-federation-launcher.mjs",
"--host-role","linux_federation","--execution-root-fd","3",
"--activation-fd","4","--public-key-commitment-fd","5",
"--host-attestation-trust-fd","6"]` and
`[...darwin_node_prefix,"scripts/run-stage2-federation-launcher.mjs",
"--host-role","darwin_platform","--execution-root-fd","3",
"--activation-fd","4","--public-key-commitment-fd","5",
"--host-attestation-trust-fd","6"]`. Darwin has only stdio and FDs 3..6. Linux additionally
starts with the exact eventfd guard at FD 19; no other FD survives.
environment is empty, cwd is capsule FD 3, umask is `0077`, and each launcher
owns a new process group. FD 4 is the request-bound
`stage2-local-control-channel-identity-v1` launcher-activation endpoint using
the exact platform transport and logical-frame parser above. Each activation
has `N` in `1..262144` and exactly the ordered `SCM_RIGHTS` vector declared by
`fd_roles`; a short sender return, second application send, trailing,
zero-length, oversized, credential-bearing, wrong-state, or other ancillary
value refuses. FD 5 is a one-shot commitment pipe containing exactly uint32be
`N`, then `N` compact canonical JSON bytes without LF for `N` in `1..65536`,
then EOF; no second frame or trailing byte is legal. FD 6 is the positional
read-only independently pinned host-attestation-trust value; the launcher
hashes it before key generation, never accepts its expected digest from S,
and closes the child-visible duplicate after its initial check while
retaining a private read-only description through termination.

For this operation `attestation_node_prefix_p` is exactly
`[attestation_runtime_path,"--no-warnings","--require",
linux_node_post_exec_reseal_prelude_path]` on Linux and exactly
`[attestation_runtime_path,"--no-warnings"]` on Darwin. The host supervisor
invokes that bootstrap exactly
`[...attestation_node_prefix_p,attestation_bootstrap_path,
"--platform",p,"--request-fd","3","--host-attestation-trust-fd","4",
"--launcher-commitment-fd","5","--bootstrap-result-fd","6",
"--keystore-session-fd","7"]`, where `p` is `linux` or `darwin` and every
path/hash/key/policy value cross-equals T. Stdin is `/dev/null`;
stdout/stderr are privately captured and must both reach EOF with empty
stdout/stderr; environment is empty; cwd is the nonsymlink directory
containing `attestation_bootstrap_path`; umask is `0077`; a new process group
is used; and only stdio plus FDs 3..7 survive. FD 3 is the fresh
offset-independent exact signed-request frame (`N=1..262144`) and EOF. FD 4 is
a fresh read-only T description. FD 5 is the sole read end paired directly
with launcher commitment FD 5; no supervisor, controller, or assembler owns
another read. FD 6 is the sole bootstrap-result write end. FD 7 is the sole
bootstrap endpoint of a one-shot
`stage2-local-control-channel-identity-v1` keystore session using the exact
platform transport above. The independently registered keystore service
creates the pair, retains the sole service endpoint, and returns the sole
client endpoint in the exact service-control `issuance` state. The preceding
`issue_session_request` is the sole request-authorized operation. It durably
in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction inserts the complete run, request, and
session unique-key rows plus the `issued_unbound` state, durability-confirms
the commit before exposing any endpoint, and returns canonical
`stage2-keystore-session-issuance-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,platform,keystore_authorization_id,
supervisor_run_request_sha256,session_nonce,service_endpoint_device,
service_endpoint_inode,service_endpoint_socket_object_sha256,
client_endpoint_device,client_endpoint_inode,
client_endpoint_socket_object_sha256`;
`session_nonce` is the channel nonce, endpoint values are canonical uint64
decimals, Linux socket-object fields are null, Darwin fields use the exact
nonce-bound rules above, and `issuance_sha256` uses the exact
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimage. No full keystore-session identity or digest
exists yet because the bootstrap PID has not been created. The typed result
is capped at 131,072 canonical JSON bytes and
carries exactly one ordered client-endpoint right and no other ancillary
value; failure returns no endpoint.

The supervisor then creates the bootstrap behind the platform barrier with
the client endpoint reserved for FD 7 and sends the only allowed
`bind_bootstrap_request` before release. Its canonical
`stage2-keystore-bootstrap-registration-v1` argument has keys exactly
`domain,issuance_sha256,platform,keystore_authorization_id,
supervisor_run_request_sha256,supervisor_pid,supervisor_start_token,
bootstrap_base_identity,bootstrap_process_group,fd7_target`;
`fd7_target` is exactly `7`. On Linux this operation carries exactly one
duplicated bootstrap pidfd right; on Darwin it carries zero rights and the
service installs its own exact kqueue `NOTE_EXIT` registration while the
final image remains suspended. The service samples parent/PID/start/group
twice, requires the bootstrap's parent to be the authorized live supervisor,
retains that observer through exit, and returns canonical
`stage2-keystore-bootstrap-observer-bound-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,status,registration_sha256,bootstrap_base_identity,
keystore_observer_identity,keystore_observer_identity_sha256`;
status is `observer_bound`, the observer is the complete canonical record,
and both digests use their exact domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimages.

Only after that exact observer-bound ACK does the supervisor perform the one
Linux pre-exec release or Darwin `SIGCONT`, close its client-endpoint copy,
and send `bootstrap_release_notice`. After final exec/release, the service
cross-equals PID/start/group, executable/closure, and final bootstrap FD-7
identity against the registration and retained observer. It then atomically
binds the issued row, completes the full self-contained bootstrap start token
and keystore-session channel identity, sends that channel's init frame to the
bootstrap, and sends canonical `stage2-keystore-bootstrap-ready-v1` to the
supervisor with keys exactly
`domain,status,registration_sha256,bootstrap_start_token,
keystore_session_identity,keystore_session_identity_sha256,
keystore_service_control_channel_identity_sha256`; status is `ready`.
Observer-bound and ready frames are each capped at 131,072 canonical JSON
bytes and carry no rights. The bootstrap learns its complete token from the
session init; neither registration nor issuance can circularly nominate it.
No generic issue/register/spawn operation exists. No supervisor, controller,
launcher, assembler, or other process retains a session endpoint. Missing/
wrong registration, ACK, ready, pidfd/kqueue, parent, holder, double sample,
or premature release consumes the issued session.

The bootstrap constructs exactly one
`stage2-host-attestation-keystore-request-v1` with keys
`domain,session_nonce,keystore_authorization_id,
keystore_session_identity,keystore_session_identity_sha256,
supervisor_run_request,
supervisor_run_request_sha256,launcher_commitment,
launcher_commitment_sha256,launcher_commitment_frame_sha256,
host_attestation_payload`. `session_nonce` is exactly the fresh
64-lowercase-hex `channel_nonce` issued by the keystore service in the
validated channel-init identity; the bootstrap cannot nominate another
session.
The two nested objects serialize byte-for-byte to the already validated FD-3
and FD-5 payloads. `host_attestation_payload` is the exact ordered payload
schema frozen above; the bootstrap constructs it, but the keystore
independently reconstructs it from T, the signed request, commitment, channel
identity, and live supervisor/bootstrap/launcher/runtime/import/loader
measurements and requires byte equality.

Only after receiving and validating the keystore-service channel-init frame
does the bootstrap send the request as one no-rights logical frame with N in
`1..262144`, followed by bootstrap `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` and
keystore-observed EOF. The service sent init only after validating the exact
bootstrap executable, group, start token, channel holder, and closure.
Wrong peer, right, framing, EOF, closure, or payload consumes the issued
session without a success response.

The durable replay tuple is canonical
`stage2-host-attestation-replay-tuple-v1` with keys exactly
`platform,keystore_authorization_id,package_run_id,challenge,request_nonce,
launcher_pid,launcher_start_identity,launcher_nonce,session_nonce`. Its
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON digest indexes the independently durable keystore
ledger's replay index. Before transferring the client endpoint, the service
durably inserts exactly one session row keyed by
`platform,keystore_authorization_id,session_nonce` in state
`issued_unbound`, with the issuance digest and no full channel identity or
request tuple; collision refuses and no caller can recreate a row. Successful
observer binding changes exactly `issued_unbound -> bootstrap_bound`;
successful final executable/FD-7/session completion changes exactly
`bootstrap_bound -> session_ready`. After the complete request frame and EOF,
one atomic durable transaction compares `session_ready`, stores the exact
frame hash, replay tuple and tuple digest, inserts that tuple digest into a
unique global replay index, and changes state to `request_frame_latched`.

After complete semantic/live-process validation, one atomic durable CAS
changes exactly `request_frame_latched -> signing_started` before the sole
private-handle signing call. `signing_started` is replay-terminal and
authorizes exactly one signing attempt. On successful signing, the service
constructs the exact result frame bytes and in one durable transaction stores
those bytes and their hash while changing exactly
`signing_started -> signature_committed`; only then may transport begin.
`signature_committed` is terminal and transport failure never demotes,
deletes, or retries it. Complete response frame plus EOF, not a ledger claim,
is the receiver's delivery proof.

Any failure before `signature_committed` durably changes the current row to
terminal `consumed_failure`; if no complete tuple exists, the session key
alone is consumed. A crash in `signing_started` recovers to failure without a
second signing attempt. Thus the only success path is
`issued_unbound -> bootstrap_bound -> session_ready ->
request_frame_latched -> signing_started -> signature_committed`, with
`consumed_failure` reachable from every earlier state. No jump, rollback,
success-to-failure rewrite, response-delivery fiction, or retry is legal.

Only after the `signing_started` transition may the keystore sign the exact
`stage2-launcher-host-attestation-v1` payload. It returns exactly one
no-rights `stage2-host-attestation-keystore-result-v1` logical frame with N
in `1..131072` and keys exactly
`domain,status,session_nonce,keystore_authorization_id,
keystore_session_identity,keystore_session_identity_sha256,
host_attestation`; status is `signed`.
It then performs `shutdown(SHUT_WR)`; the bootstrap requires exact response
EOF and closes FD 7. On any failure the service sends no `signed` result,
shuts down/closes, and the bootstrap fails; a transport failure after
`signature_committed` remains committed and is never resent. A second use, another domain,
generic preimage, different commitment, re-registration, missing EOF,
ancillary right, replay tuple, or transport substitution refuses. Private
key bytes and a generic signing oracle never enter the bootstrap.

FD 6 carries one uint32be `N`, `N` compact canonical JSON bytes without LF
for `N` in `1..262144`, then EOF. The value is
`stage2-host-attestation-bootstrap-result-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,supervisor_run_request,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
launcher_commitment,launcher_commitment_sha256,
launcher_commitment_frame_sha256,keystore_session_identity,
keystore_session_identity_sha256,host_attestation,
host_attestation_sha256`. The exact compact serialization of nested
`supervisor_run_request` equals the FD-3 frame payload byte-for-byte, its
recomputed byte length equals that frame's uint32be prefix, and its one-LF
hash equals `supervisor_run_request_sha256`. The exact compact serialization
of nested `launcher_commitment` similarly equals the FD-5 payload
byte-for-byte, while `launcher_commitment_frame_sha256` additionally binds
its original uint32be prefix. The attestation binds both plus the exact
retained bootstrap kernel identity.
The supervisor validates and retains the exact result, then supplies its
exact retained launch-offer payload plus those public result bytes through an
untrusted transport to the deterministic S constructor. No second launch-
offer, raw-commitment, or reconstructed-request path exists.
Truncation, trailing/duplicate frame, held EOF, cap `+1`, nonempty bootstrap
stream, nonzero/signal exit, surviving descendant/open pipe, wrong closure,
request, key, process, policy, commitment, or result refuses before S.

The launcher state machine is exact: Linux is
`exec_ready -> request_release -> commitment -> host attestation accepted in
S -> platform_gate activation ->
signed platform admission final -> aggregate activation -> signed scratch
receipt -> aggregate exit -> signed package-admission final -> terminate`;
Darwin is
`exec_ready -> request_release -> commitment -> host attestation accepted in
S -> platform_gate activation -> signed platform admission final ->
terminate`. A duplicate, skipped,
reordered, concurrent, or post-termination activation or signing operation
refuses the whole run. Final supervisor acceptance is deliberately not a
launcher state and has no ACK path back to the launcher.

The controller arms one monotonic `supervisor_startup_timeout_ms` deadline
immediately before `controller_channel_creation_call_entry`. It spans channel
creation, process-domain placement, helper/broker transition, observer setup,
supervisor exec/suspended release, service-control connection, launcher
exec-ready, launch offer frame plus EOF, durable request latching/signing,
request delivery, and controller-observed `supervisor_request_frame_eof`.
Exact equality passes and one millisecond over refuses. Expiry irreversibly
fails acceptance and applies the frozen graceful/forced closure bounds to
the supervisor group, broker, launcher, services' per-run connections,
streams, and rights. The encompassing run deadline starts at the identical
end event, so no pre-request or inter-deadline interval is unbounded.

For the Linux acceptance pipe, the controller retains the sole read end
received in the launch offer and the exact live pinned supervisor retains the
sole write end it created. The supervisor closed its reader immediately after
the one successful offer send; the controller never possessed a writer. No
launcher, bootstrap, constructor, assembler, broker, gate, aggregate,
validator, or descendant inherits a writer. The signed request binds the
offer and that pipe identity.
The controller's external `supervisor_run_timeout_ms` starts at its observed
signed-request frame EOF and spans the complete platform/aggregate run,
acceptance frame/EOF, supervisor exit, empty streams, zero descendants, and
closure of every supervisor-owned capability plus the controller/provisioner
double-empty cgroup observation, leaf removal, and controller-observed
`ENOENT`. It does not start from an
unobservable launcher event and no payload attests its own timing.
For Darwin, the same request-bound timeout starts at the same observed
signed-request frame EOF and spans signed platform-admission final
validation, launcher and supervisor exit, empty captured streams, zero
descendants/open pipes, and closure of every supervisor-owned capability;
Darwin has no acceptance frame. Exact equality passes and one millisecond
over refuses on both platforms, and no phase restarts or extends the
encompassing timeout.

The Linux supervisor retains exact T, launch offer, signed request, bootstrap
result, launcher observer, acceptance writer, supervisor-context bytes, all
channel identities, and, once delivered, both validated sealed process-domain
snapshot readers through final validation. After the original launcher publishes
the package admission and terminates, it reopens the final, S, T, both full
requests/commitments/attestations, and its retained aggregate launcher
context; requires every policy, run/challenge, process, channel, context,
snapshot byte/identity/seal, signature, deadline, and hash equality; and
accepts no hash-only shortcut.
Only on success it writes uint32be `N`, exactly `N` compact canonical JSON
bytes without LF for `N` in `1..262144`, then EOF. The JSON is
`stage2-linux-host-supervisor-acceptance-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,challenge,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
host_attestation_trust_sha256,approved_launcher_capsule_policy_sha256,
host_attestation_set_sha256,launcher_trust_sha256,
launcher_commitment_sha256,launcher_pid,launcher_start_token,
launcher_context_sha256,acceptance_pipe_identity_sha256,
supervisor_context_sink_identity_sha256,
scratch_broker_teardown_result_sha256,broker_pid,broker_start_token,
broker_wait_status,broker_wait_status_sha256,
package_admission_sha256,status`.
Domain is exact, status is `PASS`, and every other value cross-equals the
retained request/context, its byte-exact broker-control result, original
broker pidfd, complete direct-parent wait-status proof with exit status zero,
and revalidated final. The supervisor then exits
zero with empty captured stdout/stderr, zero descendants, and zero open
pipes. The controller accepts only that one frame plus EOF and successful
supervisor termination within the external timeout. A retained controller
writer, missing/oversized/truncated/trailing/duplicate/held frame, wrong
channel or process, late exit, nonempty stream, descendant/open FD, package
file, child-validator PASS line, bare hash, or substituted observation is not
external PASS. The frame and supervisor-context copy are nonpersisted
control-plane observations, are not package artifacts, and enter no S/D/A,
catalog, marker, receipt, admission, or package hash.

The initial FD 3 is a kernel-read-only key-commit capsule image containing the
exact final manifest-governed entries and empty reserved slots. The later
final capsule is a separately built kernel-read-only image with the same
manifest hash and byte-identical nonreserved tree; only the manifest-excluded
reserved-slot contents differ. Final activation carries that final capsule as
the `execution_capsule` authority. Before accepting it, the still-live
launcher proves one-to-one equality of every nonreserved entry, runtime,
loader map, launcher source, device-independent manifest field, and its own
already loaded executable/source hashes, then validates all filled reserved
slots. A writable provisional image, mutation after initial exec, different
nonreserved inode content, remount/alias, or activation without the final
read-only image refuses. Thus no launcher executes from a capsule being
mutated to fill `S,D_L,D_D,A`.

The pinned supervisor, not the controller, assembler, constructor, or a
relay, is the sole activation sender. After S/D/A and each phase's exact
run-scoped authorities become durable, it opens them through their frozen
local locators, independently validates their complete bytes, identities,
mount/root profiles, request/attestation graph, and phase preconditions, and
constructs the canonical activation packet itself. It sends exactly one
seven-right platform packet on each host. On Linux only, after direct
platform-admission validation it later constructs exactly one fifteen-right
aggregate packet; rights 1..14 are its directly validated phase authorities
and right 15 is the original never-relayed context-writer escrow. The
Linux transition helper already created the fresh user/mount namespaces
before final supervisor exec. Before the aggregate send, the zero-capability
supervisor sends the exact broker `create_request` with four ordered
read-only/observer rights: the exact signed request bytes, S, A, and a
duplicated launcher pidfd. The one-thread broker independently validates T,
the signed request, S, A, process domain, namespace, parent FD 19, launcher,
and static A scratch profile; creates the disposable mount; creates one fresh
broker/launcher seqpacket session; and returns exactly two rights in
`create_result`:
`scratch_root` and `scratch_privilege_broker_session`. The supervisor
independently validates the complete setup object and uses those exact two
rights as aggregate roles 13 and 14. No Node process mounts, unmounts, or
holds a capability.

Canonical `stage2-linux-scratch-broker-setup-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,challenge,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,linux_run_process_domain_sha256,
broker_pid,broker_start_token,broker_control_channel_identity_sha256,
linux_scratch_mount_policy_sha256,parent_control_identity,
covered_directory_identity,scratch_mount_identity,scratch_root_identity,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,status`.
Status is `ready`. Parent, covered-directory, root, and mount identities are
complete canonical device/inode/mount-ID/profile records. The session
identity is the full local-control identity with purpose
`scratch_privilege_broker_session`, broker endpoint, expected original
launcher endpoint, and fresh nonce; it contains no activation hash. Static
policy/profile fields cross-equal T and the request; run/challenge/request/
aggregation fields cross-equal the request and A. Dynamic parent, covered inode,
mount ID, root, endpoint, and nonce values do not claim to preexist in or
cross-equal A. The setup digest uses exact domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON.

Canonical `stage2-linux-scratch-broker-create-request-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,challenge,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
shared_run_binding_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,
linux_scratch_privilege_policy_sha256,
linux_scratch_namespace_identity_sha256,
linux_scratch_setup_privilege_state_sha256,
linux_run_process_domain_sha256,launcher_pid,launcher_start_token,
launcher_process_group,fd_roles,status`. `fd_roles` is exactly
`["supervisor_run_request","shared_binding","aggregation_binding",
"launcher_pidfd"]` and status is `authorize_create`. One control packet
carries those four nonduplicate rights in that order. The first three are
independent read-only descriptions whose complete canonical bytes and hashes
equal the retained request, S, and A; the fourth is a duplicate of the
supervisor's original launcher pidfd and cross-equals the complete launcher
start token. The broker positionally reads, validates, and retains the first
three descriptions through teardown and uses the pidfd only for live process
equality. Writable, offset-shared, short, extra, reordered, relayed, or
hash-only authority refuses. `create_request_sha256` hashes the exact compact
payload plus one LF.

Canonical `stage2-linux-scratch-broker-create-result-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,status,create_request_sha256,linux_scratch_broker_setup,
linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,fd_roles`. Status is `ready`; `fd_roles` is
exactly `["scratch_root","scratch_privilege_broker_session"]`; and one control
packet carries exactly those two rights in that order. Both descriptions
cross-equal the complete nested setup and no broker duplicate is exposed
through another channel. Because `SCM_RIGHTS` transfer does not consume the
sender's description, immediately after the successful one-shot send the
broker closes its sender copy of the launcher/client session endpoint before
accepting `handoff_commit`; only the broker/service session endpoint remains.
It retains the separately declared scratch-root authority solely until the
pre-teardown alias check and closes it at the exact teardown step below.
Both close events enter the one-way authority ledger.
`create_result_sha256` hashes the exact compact payload plus one LF.

Canonical `stage2-linux-scratch-broker-handoff-commit-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,challenge,create_request_sha256,
create_result_sha256,activation_frame_sha256,
linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,launcher_pid,
launcher_start_token,launcher_target_fd,status`. The target FD is `19` and
status is `activation_delivered_and_sender_rights_closed`. It carries zero
rights and can be sent only after the exact aggregate activation `sendmsg`
and closure of every sender description for roles 1..15.
`handoff_commit_sha256` hashes the exact compact payload plus one LF.

Canonical `stage2-linux-scratch-broker-session-init-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,status,package_run_id,challenge,create_result_sha256,
handoff_commit_sha256,activation_frame_sha256,
linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,launcher_pid,
launcher_start_token,launcher_target_fd`. Status is `channel_ready`; the
target is `19`; every value cross-equals the retained create/handoff/activation
bytes and complete session/launcher identities. The frame carries zero
rights. `scratch_privilege_broker_session_init_frame_sha256` hashes the exact
uint32be prefix plus compact payload bytes.

Canonical `stage2-linux-scratch-broker-session-init-ack-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,status,session_init_frame_sha256,activation_frame_sha256,
linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,launcher_pid,
launcher_start_token,launcher_target_fd`. Status is `accepted`; target is
`19`; it carries zero rights; and `session_init_ack_sha256` hashes the exact
uint32be prefix plus compact payload bytes. The original launcher sends it
only after accepting aggregate activation, atomically replacing the FD-19
eventfd guard with the received session description, closing the received
source description, independently validating its live FD table and the
session-init frame, and retaining its write direction for the later destroy
request and result ACK.

Canonical `stage2-linux-launcher-fd19-observation-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,launcher_pid,launcher_start_token,target_fd,device,inode,
fd_descriptor_flags,open_file_status_flags,
matching_run_domain_description_count`. Target FD is `19`; device/inode
cross-equal the launcher endpoint of the broker/launcher session; descriptor flags are
`FD_CLOEXEC`; status flags are `O_RDWR`; and the count is `1`. The broker
derives the record from the retained launcher pidfd/start token and two
fixed-point-equal closed-domain `/proc/<launcher>/fd` plus `fdinfo` samples;
it never opens or duplicates the endpoint.

Canonical `stage2-linux-scratch-broker-handoff-ack-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,status,handoff_commit_sha256,activation_frame_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_init_frame_sha256,
session_init_ack_sha256,
launcher_fd19_observation,launcher_fd19_observation_sha256`. Status is
`handoff_complete`; the init-frame digest covers its exact uint32be prefix
plus payload; and the observation digest uses its exact
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimage. `handoff_ack_sha256` hashes the exact
compact ACK payload plus one LF. The ACK carries zero rights and is sent
only after the broker has validated the exact launcher init ACK and then
independently produced the pidfd-bound FD-19 observation. Missing, premature,
duplicate, self-reported, wrong-FD, non-CLOEXEC, aliased, or unequal handoff
consumes the run.

Scratch creation is exact: verify trusted procfs and `/proc/self`; atomically
replace the broker's still-verified eventfd guard at FD 19 with the
independently provisioned scratch-parent description; require the parent
identity from the launch offer/request; exclusive
`mkdirat(19,package_run_id,0700)`; `fsync(19)`; sample the covered directory;
invoke exactly
`mount("stage2-scratch","/proc/self/fd/19/<package_run_id>","tmpfs",
MS_NOSUID|MS_NODEV|MS_NOEXEC,
"mode=0700,uid=0,gid=0,size=268435456,nr_inodes=65536")`; verify mountinfo,
`fstatfs`, `statx(...,STATX_MNT_ID)`, options, owner/mode, and disjoint mount
identity; then open the root only with the policy's `openat2` flags. Any
symlink/magic link, preexisting basename, alternate source/fstype/flag/data,
missing parent fsync, retry, path fallback, wrong mount ID, or mutable
identity refuses.

Each `sendmsg` is one-shot: failure or partial/short/ambiguous delivery is
fatal and is never retried. After Darwin's successful platform activation the
supervisor performs `shutdown(activation_fd,SHUT_WR)`. Linux keeps that
direction open, with no intervening frame, between its platform and aggregate
activation states. Linux aggregate finalization is ordered exactly:
successful `sendmsg` -> close every sender description for roles 1..15 ->
send broker `handoff_commit` binding the exact activation and session hashes
-> broker observes the original launcher at FD 19 and sends its session-init
frame -> launcher returns the exact session-init ACK -> broker independently
observes the original launcher at FD 19 -> broker sends `handoff_ack` -> prove
zero supervisor scratch-root,
session, context-writer, cwd, root, map, or mount-internal alias -> sample the
exact all-thread-zero supervisor state twice -> perform
`shutdown(activation_fd,SHUT_WR)`. The supervisor retains only separately
opened T, launch offer, request, bootstrap-result, process observers,
broker-control reader/original pidfd, context reader, final-acceptance, and
captured-stream authorities. It receives and retains the broker's later
byte-exact teardown result and its two ordered sealed read-only snapshot
descriptions before broker EOF/exit.

The launcher requires the final frame plus directional EOF with no undeclared
byte/right, validates the live supervisor and broker handoff, and
byte-reconstructs the all-thread-zero supervisor state before releasing any
aggregate context or child. Its own every-TID state was zero/bounding-empty/
no-new-privileges from first instruction and remains so. The aggregate child
inherits that irreversible state, passes the launcher key-region absence
probe, has every TID all-zero after exec, and remains behind the context
barrier until the launcher samples exact `aggregate_child` state twice. The
broker remains exactly one TID with only effective/permitted
`CAP_SYS_PTRACE|CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, empty bounding/inheritable/ambient sets,
no-new-privileges, and the exact seccomp filter. Any ordering, thread,
profile, alias, handoff, EOF, or sample mismatch refuses.

Only then does the launcher adopt the already received sink writer without
duplicating it; it validates the request-bound supervisor peer and
activation-channel identity, never sends the sink to a child, writes the
single frozen context frame, and closes it. Thus by aggregate execution the
original supervisor is the sole reader and the original persistent launcher
is the sole writer; the controller and every other process own neither end.

Each activation frame is canonical `stage2-launcher-activation-v1` with keys
exactly `domain,mode,platform,package_run_id,challenge,
shared_run_binding_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,
platform_descriptor_sha256,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
host_attestation_set_sha256,launcher_trust_sha256,
launcher_activation_channel_identity_sha256,
host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity,
host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity_sha256,
linux_scratch_privilege_policy_sha256,
linux_scratch_namespace_identity_sha256,
linux_scratch_setup_privilege_state_sha256,
linux_scratch_broker_setup,linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,
supervisor_context_sink_identity_sha256,fd_roles`; mode is
`platform_gate|aggregate` and aggregate is Linux-only. Platform-gate
`fd_roles` is exactly
`["execution_capsule","platform_output_root","platform_descriptor",
"shared_binding","aggregation_binding","transfer_root",
"host_control_oracle_bundle"]`; both oracle-bundle fields are the complete
validated platform bundle identity/digest. Its
four runtime broker/session fields and
`supervisor_context_sink_identity_sha256` are
null. Aggregate oracle-bundle fields are null. Aggregate
`fd_roles` is exactly
`["execution_capsule","aggregate_output_root","aggregation_binding",
"shared_binding","linux_archive","linux_expectation","darwin_archive",
"darwin_expectation","linux_descriptor","darwin_descriptor",
"linux_admission","darwin_admission","scratch_root",
"scratch_privilege_broker_session","supervisor_context_sink"]`; its context-sink hash
exactly equals the Linux controller-signed request and the received pipe
identity.
The aggregate setup/session objects and hashes are complete canonical records
frozen above and match roles 13/14; neither may be reconstructed from a path.
The three Linux scratch digests equal the signed request and retained live
namespace/setup state on both Linux activation modes; all three are null on
Darwin.
Every activation-channel hash equals the request and the retained
supervisor/launcher endpoint pair.
One frame carries exactly one matching nonduplicate ordinary-file,
directory/mount, socket, or pipe FD per role, no credential ancillary data,
no undeclared bytes, and no unknown ancillary data.
`activation_frame_sha256` is SHA-256 over the exact four-byte uint32be
payload length followed by the exact compact activation JSON bytes.
After the reserved slots are final and kernel-read-only, the persistent
launcher positionally revalidates every received authority and exact
`S,D_L,D_D,A`, the independently pinned host-trust digest, and both host
attestations, requires its original commitment in `S`, and creates distinct
launcher-owned and child-owned descriptor-table entries by duplicating each
validated activation description that a child is allowed to receive, with
`CLOEXEC` set until the exact child remap.
`scratch_privilege_broker_session` and
`supervisor_context_sink` are exceptions: neither is ever child-owned. The
launcher requires the exact eventfd guard still occupy FD 19. Because 19 was
occupied throughout `recvmsg`, no incoming right can have been allocated
there. Only after validating the complete 15-right vector does it invoke
`dup3(received_session,19,O_CLOEXEC)` directly over the guard without an
intervening close, immediately closes the received source number, and retains
no duplicate. The sink is adopted without duplication, written, and closed
as frozen below, while session FD 19 survives through broker teardown.
All reads are positional and no phase depends on a shared mutable file
offset. The launcher then closes every other received activation-message
description. For
platform mode the launcher retains
private read-only descriptions of the final capsule, S, A, selected
descriptor, platform-output root, transfer root, and original oracle bundle
through signed platform-admission final validation; the gate receives
separate duplicates and the supervisor closes its sent bundle duplicate
immediately after the successful activation send.
For aggregate mode the Linux launcher retains private descriptions of the
final capsule, S, A, both descriptors, both archives, both expectations, both
admissions, aggregate-output root, scratch root, and the launcher-only
`scratch_privilege_broker_session` through their last post-exit use. It becomes the sole
writer of `supervisor_context_sink`, validates that pipe against the signed
request and activation identity, writes the exact context protocol frozen
below, closes it, and retains no writer duplicate. The aggregate child
receives separate duplicates of every declared child FD except
`scratch_privilege_broker_session` and `supervisor_context_sink`. Role 14 is
a request-bound launcher-only control channel to the exact one-thread broker,
not a directory and not mount authority in Node. It carries exactly the
broker channel-init and later signed destroy-request/result-plus-snapshot
protocol. The
broker privately retains the outside-parent FD 19, scratch-root description,
mount identity, process-domain view, and original supervisor pidfd. The
launcher separately retains its scratch-root description only until the
pre-teardown alias boundary, then closes it before requesting destruction.
A lost/substituted session, guard drift, session at the wrong FD, broker/
launcher endpoint mismatch, duplicate into a child, wrong setup/mount/
namespace/run, or payload before the declared state refuses before scratch
ready can be accepted.
Missing/extra/reordered rights, wrong rights count, truncation, multiple
messages for one phase, cross-run activation, mutable slot, premature close,
missing launcher or child duplicate, inherited wrong descriptor-table entry,
or any identity/hash/access mismatch refuses before child or lock.

Every launcher-signed frame or artifact has top-level keys exactly
`domain,payload,signature_key_id,signature_hex`. `payload` has its
domain-specific exact schema; key ID selects the matching platform record;
and `signature_hex` is exactly 128 lowercase hexadecimal encoding the
64-byte Ed25519 signature over exact ASCII `domain`, one `0x00`, and exact
no-LF `JSON.stringify(payload)`. Verification rejects a noncanonical public
key, key substitution, nonexact signature length/case, invalid signature,
unknown algorithm, alternate preimage/encoding, cross-platform key,
cross-domain replay, or any payload byte drift.
For platform phase ACK and platform admission, `signature_key_id` must equal
that platform's host-attested ephemeral key and the live launcher-context
key. For scratch-destruction and package admission it must equal the
host-attested Linux key and the live aggregate launcher-context key; a valid
Darwin signature is invalid for either Linux-only domain.

Canonical `stage2-federation-launcher-context-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,mode,platform,package_run_id,challenge,
shared_run_binding_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,
platform_descriptor_sha256,execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,
host_attestation_trust_sha256,host_attestation_set_sha256,
launcher_trust_sha256,host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity,
host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity_sha256,
node_path,node_executable_sha256,
system_runtime_manifest_sha256,federation_launcher_path,
federation_launcher_sha256,launcher_argv_sha256,launcher_pid,
launcher_start_token,launcher_process_group,launcher_nonce,
signature_key_id,launcher_child_key_absence_proof,
launcher_child_key_absence_proof_sha256,
linux_scratch_privilege_policy_sha256,
linux_scratch_namespace_identity,linux_scratch_namespace_identity_sha256,
linux_scratch_setup_privilege_state,
linux_scratch_setup_privilege_state_sha256,
linux_aggregate_privilege_state,linux_aggregate_privilege_state_sha256,
scratch_nonce,linux_scratch_broker_setup,
linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,
launcher_activation_channel_identity_sha256,activation_frame_sha256,
supervisor_context_sink_identity_sha256`.
Domain is exact; `mode` is
`platform_gate|aggregate`;
platform is the executing host, and aggregate mode is necessarily Linux with
the Linux descriptor. Every hash/path/key value cross-equals `S`, `A`, the
selected descriptor, capsule, runtime, launcher-trust record, and exact
launcher argv. PID, start token, and process group identify the live direct
parent; `launcher_nonce` is a fresh 64-lowercase-hex value; and
`launcher_argv_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact no-LF `JSON.stringify` of the
launcher argv token array. The complete child-key absence proof names the
exact blocked direct gate/aggregate child and policy and is verified before
context release. `scratch_nonce`, both broker-setup fields, both broker-
session fields, and
`supervisor_context_sink_identity_sha256` are all null in platform-gate
mode. All seven Linux scratch
policy/namespace/setup/aggregate fields are null on Darwin. In Linux
platform-gate mode the policy hash, complete namespace/setup objects, and
their hashes equal the signed request/offer/activation while the two
aggregate-privilege fields are null. In Linux aggregate mode all seven are
nonnull, and the aggregate privilege record is formed only after the
supervisor and launcher all-thread-zero samples, broker-active sample, and
aggregate child's post-exec zero-capability measurement.
The complete oracle-bundle identity/hash are nonnull and byte-equal activation
in platform-gate mode and null in aggregate mode; their presence never
depends on child output.
In aggregate mode `scratch_nonce` is the fresh 64-lowercase-hex value and
the complete broker setup/session objects and hashes byte-equal aggregate
activation. The launcher endpoint is the exact FD-19 session after atomic
guard replacement; the broker endpoint and privately retained parent FD 19
match the broker setup. Only the static run ID/profile/policy constraints
cross-equal A. Dynamic parent/covered inode, mount ID, root, endpoint, and
nonce values are created after A and are instead bound by setup, activation,
this context, the ready frame, broker result, and signed receipt. The
activation-channel hash equals the request and
retained supervisor/launcher channel; the context-sink hash equals the exact
pipe identity in the controller-signed Linux request and aggregate
activation. `activation_frame_sha256` recomputes from the exact accepted
activation prefix/payload and, in aggregate mode, cross-equals the broker
handoff and later destroy request/result. Only
`host_attestation_trust_sha256` equals the immutable capsule
T copy. The run-specific `host_attestation_set_sha256` is recomputed from the
two exact signed attestations and cross-equals S/D/A and the live launcher
context; it never equals T. The child context verifier receives both values
transitively from the live host-attested launcher and reverifies both signed
host attestations without claiming an independent external pin. The
launcher serializes the context once into one immutable byte buffer of exact
compact JSON plus one LF with total length in `1..262144`. It writes those exact bytes and EOF to the fresh
read-only child context FD. In aggregate mode it also writes uint32be `N`,
the same exact `N` bytes for `N` in `1..262144`, and EOF to
`supervisor_context_sink`; the Linux supervisor is the sole reader, validates
the frame, request-bound pipe identity, activation, context, and EOF, and
retains the exact bytes through final package acceptance. There is no
context ACK and no context-derived timing claim. `launcher_context_sha256`
is SHA-256 over the identical one-LF bytes on both paths. A gate or
aggregator independently validates the context, exact parent
executable/source/argv, PID/start token/process group, capsule/runtime
closure, selected public-key ID, and one-shot context FD/EOF before creating
a lock. The supervisor performs the same validation against its retained
out-of-band trust and signed request. Direct child launch, a self-created or
nonidentical supervisor copy, context replay, a second writer, held EOF, or a
parent that does not byte-equal the frozen launcher refuses.

`max_import_index_bytes` is the exact conservative derivation
`max_header_bytes + 128*max_binding_count + 128*max_object_count + 65536 =

than 128 compact-JSON bytes to each binding and object record, and has less

The gate enforces `archive_stream_timeout_ms` as one monotonic export-phase
deadline from coordinator spawn through archive FD-10 EOF, candidate/final
framing and native source-receipt validation, durable final publication, and
ACK EOF, with the narrower ACK subdeadline below. Independently, the trusted
launcher enforces `archive_stream_timeout_ms` from gate-process spawn through
its consumption of the exact launcher-phase frame and that pipe's EOF, so a
gate that never exposes the transition cannot wait without bound. The trusted
launcher is the sole enforcer of `coordinator_exit_timeout_ms` as one
monotonic deadline from that observable phase EOF, which precedes ACK
emission, through launcher phase-ACK EOF, coordinator ACK EOF, coordinator
process-tree exit/stdout/stderr EOF,
expectation final validation, gate-lock removal, gate marker, gate process
exit, gate stdout/stderr EOF, zero descendants/open pipes, and the final
gate-lock-absence observation. That observation freezes
`gate_completion_before_deadline=true` before any signed platform-admission
bytes are constructed; the gate cannot self-attest or extend the deadline.
The launcher then enforces `post_exit_admission_timeout_ms` from that frozen
observation through signed platform-admission candidate/final validation.
The admission payload does not claim its own publication completed; final
validation within this external timeout is an acceptance condition. The
trusted launcher also enforces
`aggregate_import_timeout_ms`
as one monotonic deadline from aggregate process spawn
through context/lock publication, both ordered imports, all imported
validation/replay, scratch ready/signed receipt and destruction, durable
scratch-receipt publication, aggregate-catalog final validation,
aggregate-lock removal, final marker, process-tree exit, stdout/stderr EOF,
zero descendants/open pipes, and the final aggregate-lock-absence
observation. That observation freezes
`aggregate_completion_before_deadline=true` before any package-admission
bytes are constructed. The launcher then enforces
`post_exit_admission_timeout_ms` from that frozen observation through signed
package-admission candidate/final validation; the payload does not attest its
own publication. `ack_timeout_ms` is the exact archive ACK deadline below;
the scratch ready-frame EOF through signed-receipt EOF subdeadline is exactly
`scratch_receipt_timeout_ms` and is enforced by the receiving aggregate
coordinator, not asserted inside the receipt. Independently of all launcher
subdeadlines, the Linux supervisor enforces
`supervisor_acceptance_timeout_ms` from its direct observation that the
original launcher has exited through reopening and directly validating every
required final input, writing the one acceptance frame and EOF, and closing
all supervisor-owned capabilities. The controller enforces the encompassing
`supervisor_run_timeout_ms` of exactly 259,200,000 milliseconds from its
observed signed-request frame EOF through the entire platform and aggregate
run, acceptance frame and EOF, supervisor exit, empty captured streams, zero
descendants, zero remaining supervisor capability descriptions, the
controller and provisioner independent double `populated 0`/empty-membership
samples, exact leaf removal, controller-observed `ENOENT`, and closure of the
provisioner-control channel. Neither
deadline is derived from a payload timestamp or reset by progress.
On gate or
aggregate failure, descendant termination and complete pipe drain receive at
most `graceful_cleanup_ms` followed by at most `forced_cleanup_ms`; expiration
is final and never restores PASS. Every numeric export-policy cap/deadline is
tested at equality and one unit beyond without allocating an overflow.

Each fixed `stage2-execution-capsule-v1` manifest has keys exactly

five reserved descriptors remain M's exact top-level array and are never

Capsule `entries` has exactly `entry_count` records, both in 1..65,536 and

The prior complete-tree, regular/directory, loader-class, source-locator,

The manifest excludes only its five reserved slots. It requires a
kernel-enforced read-only SquashFS image or APFS snapshot and no writable
alias. Create, write, truncate, chmod, link, unlink, rename, remount, and
alternate-mount probes fail before coordinator entry and throughout the run.
A read-only bind of mutable bytes, mode bits, or hash-then-reopen fallback is
NO-GO.

root_inode,readonly,immutable_generation`. Domain is
`stage2-mount-identity-v1`; filesystem ID is 16 lowercase hexadecimal from

Every context mount record has keys exactly
`logical_prefix,mount_identity,mount_identity_sha256`.
`logical_prefix` is the canonical descriptor- or binding-bound logical root;

defined immediately above; and `mount_identity_sha256` is its exact digest.
Every context authority snapshot has keys exactly

count are canonical uint64 decimal strings; mode is exactly four octal digits;

records and three authority snapshots; the platform context uses two and

`domain,package_run_id,shared_binding_sha256,aggregation_binding_sha256,
platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,case_id,global_sequence,
platform_sequence,coordinator_pid,coordinator_start_token,nonce`; global
sequence is 1..17 and platform sequence is 1..16 or 1. FD 9 is the exact
context. The control carrier is exactly one uint32be `N` followed by `N`
compact no-LF JSON bytes for `N` in `1..65536`, then EOF; it selects
`local_channel_init`, carries zero rights, and its frame digest hashes the
complete prefix plus payload. Missing, extra, reused, trailing, reordered, early-EOF, HUP,
reparented, or self-created authority refuses.

Only for the descriptor-selected oracle case—S2-AC-01 on Linux or S2-AC-17
on Darwin—the coordinator opens a separate positional read-only duplicate of
its still-validated FD 12 and includes the frozen spawn file action
`dup2(oracle_source_fd,74)`. The parent source remains `FD_CLOEXEC`; the
wrapper receives exactly FD 74 at offset zero, makes it `FD_CLOEXEC` as its
first built-ins-only operation, cross-equals its `fstat` identity and bytes to
the platform context, and separately cross-equals role/policy/plan/cap to the
descriptor binding before any import, output mutation, thread, or payload
spawn. The coordinator closes its per-wrapper source
immediately after successful spawn and retains only its original FD 12.
Every non-oracle case starts with FD 74 absent. A missing, extra, inheritable
after-wrapper-entry, wrong-offset, wrong-identity, case-swapped, or
coordinator-self-created bundle refuses before payload execution.

FD 4 is coordinator/wrapper publication authority and never crosses the
acceptance-payload boundary. Descriptor-bound root/blob supervisors remain
inside the trusted wrapper role. Payload inherited FDs are exactly:
FD 0 `/dev/null`; FDs 1/2 capture; immutable read-only FD 3; private scratch
FD 6; structured-event write FD 7; and zero to 64 increasing
descriptor-listed case-data FDs 10..73. FDs 4/5/8/9 and every other FD are
closed and must return `EBADF` under `F_GETFD`; for S2-AC-01 and S2-AC-17
this explicitly includes the already consumed wrapper-only FD 74.

Scratch profile is exact `stage2-private-scratch-v1`: an empty
current-child-owned mode-`0700` root on a disposable `noexec,nosuid,nodev`
substrate, mount-disjoint from execution and output, capped at 65,536 entries
and 8,589,934,592 bytes with equality passing and `+1` failing. Case
descriptor records add `child_scratch_profile,child_data_fds`.
Each data-FD record has keys
`fd,role,access,type,device,inode,size,sha256`; access is
`read|read_write`, type/nullable size/hash match the descriptor type, and no
identity aliases capsule, output, lock/context, prior output, or blob
authority. QA and ancestors are absent from the child namespace. After drain
and descriptor closure the wrapper destroys the complete scratch substrate
before publication. AC01 covers inherited/open FD4, `/proc/self/fd/4`,
`/dev/fd/4`, openat/fchdir/unlinkat, absolute QA, `..` escape, lock/prior
evidence/blob mutation, extra/reused/writable data FD, scratch metadata/
mount/alias/quota, survivor/open-FD/residue, and failed disposal, always
requiring unchanged lock/prior-output identities.

Registry commands have exact prefix
`node scripts/run-stage2-acceptance.mjs --platform <platform>
--execution-root-fd 3 --output-root-fd 4 --platform-descriptor-fd 5
--shared-binding-fd 6 --aggregation-binding-fd 7 --package-control-fd 8
--package-context-fd 9 --case <case-id> --`.
The platform value equals the case record and descriptor. Commands remain
logical display/provenance strings; actual Node and source bytes come only
from the selected capsule.

Each platform streams one canonical binary `stage2-platform-export-v1`
archive through FD 10 while retaining its lock. Framing is exact 26-byte
prefix: the 25-byte ASCII literal `stage2-platform-export-v1` plus one
`0x00`, followed by uint64be header length, exact
compact-JSON header, then for every object in raw-SHA order:
32 raw SHA-256 bytes, uint64be size, exact bytes, then EOF. Archive size is
`34 + header_length + sum(40 + object_size)`.
Header keys are exactly
`domain,package_run_id,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,
host_control_oracle_bundle_sha256,
platform_result_sha256,platform_catalog_sha256,case_ids,binding_count,
object_count,payload_set_sha256,host_binding_set_sha256,
source_receipt_count,source_receipt_set_sha256,source_receipts,
bindings,objects`.
Domain is exactly `stage2-platform-export-v1`. `objects` records have keys
exactly `sha256,size`, are unique and sorted by raw 32-byte SHA, and match the
binary payload sequence one-to-one. `payload_set_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact
ASCII `stage2-platform-export-payload-set-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify(objects)`. Bindings are unique `(role,logical_path)`
records with exact `role,logical_path,locator_kind,original_locator,
original_type,original_owner,original_mode,original_device,original_inode,
sha256,size`, sorted by unsigned-byte `(role,logical_path)`.
For `original_type=regular_file`, `original_locator` is nonnull;
`original_owner`, `original_device`, and `original_inode` are canonical
uint64 decimal strings; and `original_mode` is four octal digits. For
`original_type=captured_stream|generated_bytes`, all five fields
`original_locator,original_owner,original_mode,original_device,
original_inode` are null. No other type/nullability combination is legal.
`host_binding_set_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-imported-host-binding-set-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` of `bindings` projected, in binding order, to exact keys
`role,logical_path,locator_kind,original_locator,original_type,
original_owner,original_mode,original_device,original_inode,sha256,size`.

`source_receipts` contains exactly one record for every selected case's
fixture/binary entry whose locator kind is `host_path|guest_image_path`, in
descriptor case order, fixture before binary, then manifest entry order. Each
record has keys exactly
`case_id,manifest_kind,entry_index,entry_role,locator_kind,locator,sha256,
size,validation_kind,original_owner,original_mode,original_device,
original_inode,source_container_role,source_container_sha256`.
`manifest_kind` is `fixture|binary`; index is the safe-integer one-based
manifest position; size is a canonical uint64 decimal string. For
`host_path`, validation kind is `host_regular_file`, owner/mode/device/inode
have the exact regular-file forms above, and both source-container fields are
null. For `guest_image_path`, validation kind is
`guest_image_extraction`, the four original-host metadata fields are null,
and source-container role/hash identify the exact descriptor-bound image
artifact parsed from the locator. No other combination is legal.
`source_receipt_count` is the exact array length in `0..1024*n`.
`source_receipt_set_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-platform-source-receipt-set-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify(source_receipts)`.
`case_ids` is the selected descriptor partition in registry order;
`host_control_oracle_bundle_sha256` equals the selected platform context's
`host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity.sha256`,
oracle-bearing case evidence/fixture entry, platform catalog, and result;
`locator_kind` is `platform_export_object`. Darwin performs all
original `host_path` checks; the gate repeats every nonnull original-path
identity/hash check on its original host while validating the seekable
archive final. Header and expectation cross-equal
`host_binding_set_sha256` and `source_receipt_set_sha256`. Linux later validates transport bytes and the
signed platform admission plus expectation and never applies Darwin path semantics or pretends to
reopen a Darwin path. Duplicate path,
duplicate object, missing/extra/unreferenced payload, wrong order/count/size/
hash, truncation, or trailing bytes refuses.

Transport closure is exactly context snapshot, platform catalog/result, three
fixed finals per selected case, every distinct referenced evidence blob, and
the exact two raw outer stdout/stderr replay objects per case needed for
independent verification. Host/guest source leaves are intentionally not
payload objects: they may exceed the per-object cap and are represented only
by the exact source-receipt array in the header. For both candidate and final
archive validations, the gate independently reopens/revalidates every host
regular file and reruns the immutable descriptor-bound guest extractor over
the exact source-container image, then cross-equals each receipt's
identity/locator/hash/size. The expectation and later signed platform
admission bind that validated receipt-set digest. Linux import treats these
leaves only as signed-admission-bound gate-validated external-source receipts:
it reruns manifest structure, order, role/hash, container, and
downstream evidence checks but never claims to rehash an unavailable Darwin
path or multi-gigabyte image. Repository-path inputs remain immutable FD-3
bytes and are neither transported nor receipt leaves.

With case count `n` and distinct state-4 evidence-blob-final count `B`, exact
`binding_count K=5*n+B+3`;
`object_count O` is in `1..K` because byte-identical bindings may share one
object. Every object is `0..16,777,216` bytes, header length is in
`1..67,108,864`, and total archive size is in `1..1,099,511,627,776`; each
bound is tested at equality and `+1` without allocating the overflow.
Pre-run `S,D_L,D_D,A`, capsule manifests, contract, registry, migration,
validators, and static inputs are never trusted from transport.

Under transfer FD 8, the launcher and gate provision exactly `archives/`,
`expectations/`, `admissions/`, and the gate lock. The archive
candidate/final are exactly
`archives/.<platform>.<package_run_id>.stage2x.candidate` and
`archives/<platform>.<archive_sha256>.stage2x`. The gate exclusively creates
the candidate with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, current UID/GID,
`umask 0177`, and requested mode `0600`, drains FD 10 into it while hashing and enforcing
the exact framing/caps, file-fsyncs it, fchmods it `0400`, file-fsyncs again,
closes, and reopens read-only. It invokes the immutable `platform_export`
validator with the seekable candidate on target FD 12, hard-links no-replace
to the content-addressed final, parent-fsyncs, unlinks the candidate,
parent-fsyncs, reopens the final, requires the recorded identity/hash/size,
mode `0400`, and link count one, and invokes `platform_export` again. Only a
fresh exact final validation permits ACK.

Immediately after that final validation and before any ACK byte, the gate
writes exactly one launcher-phase frame to its FD 9: uint32be payload length,
then exact UTF-8 compact JSON without LF of length `1..4096`, then closes the
pipe so the launcher observes EOF. Keys are exactly
`domain,package_run_id,challenge,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,
launcher_trust_sha256,launcher_context_sha256,gate_context_sha256,
sink_nonce,archive_sha256,archive_size,archive_device,
archive_inode,platform_export_validator_result_sha256,phase`. Domain is
`stage2-platform-gate-phase-v1`; `phase` is exactly
`archive_final_validated_ack_pending`; every other value cross-equals the
pinned context and reopened validated archive final. This frame write/close
is the gate's next operation after final validation. The trusted launcher
validates the exact
frame, cross-equalities, length, and EOF, records the monotonic completion
time as the sole `coordinator_exit_timeout_ms` start.
`phase_frame_sha256` is SHA-256 over the exact four-byte uint32be length plus
the exact JSON payload bytes. All values represented in the later signed ACK,
expectation, gate marker, or admission must cross-equal their corresponding
fields.

Only after arming that deadline, the launcher writes exactly one FD-10
phase-ACK frame: uint32be payload length, then exact UTF-8 compact JSON
without LF of length `1..8192`, then EOF. Its JSON value is the exact
launcher-signed envelope with domain `stage2-platform-gate-phase-ack-v1`.
Its payload keys are exactly
`package_run_id,challenge,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,
launcher_trust_sha256,launcher_context_sha256,gate_context_sha256,
sink_nonce,archive_sha256,archive_size,phase_frame_sha256,deadline_armed`;
`deadline_armed` is true and every other value cross-equals the accepted phase
frame and launcher context. Signature key ID is the selected platform key.
`phase_ack_sha256` is SHA-256 over the exact four-byte uint32be length plus the
exact signed-envelope JSON bytes. The gate verifies the signature through
`S.launcher_trust`, reads the complete frame and EOF, and records both frame
hashes before its first coordinator ACK byte; the coordinator ACK write is
its next operation after phase-ACK EOF. Thus the exact launcher's observable
phase EOF, deadline arming, and authenticated ACK happen-before coordinator
ACK emission. Missing,
malformed, duplicate, reordered, extra, trailing, wrong-run/hash/identity/
phase/deadline/key/signature bytes, a held writer, or no EOF on either
direction refuses;
the launcher's independent export-phase deadline bounds phase-frame arrival,
the already armed coordinator-exit deadline bounds the reverse ACK and all
later work, and cleanup remains irreversible. AC01's immutable gate-envelope
suite covers both directions' exact argv/FD/access/order, phase
4,096/4,097-byte and signed-ACK 8,192/8,193-byte
boundary, missing/duplicate/truncated/trailing/held frames and EOFs,
wrong-field/hash/nonce/deadline/key/signature values, domain/cross-platform/
cross-run replay, coordinator ACK before phase-ACK, each timeout edge,
descendant drain, and uncertain-cleanup refusal.

After that exact launcher handshake, the gate sends the coordinator exactly
one FD-11 ACK: one uint32be length,
compact JSON without LF of length `1..4096`, then EOF. Its keys are exactly
`domain,package_run_id,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,
gate_context_sha256,sink_nonce,archive_sha256,archive_size,archive_device,
archive_inode,platform_export_validator_result_sha256`. Domain is
