`stage2-platform-export-ack-v1`; all values cross-equal the pinned context and
reopened final. The ACK deadline after final validation is exactly 300,000
milliseconds and includes phase-frame publication, launcher phase-ACK EOF,
and coordinator ACK EOF. Malformed, duplicate, extra, trailing, reordered,
wrong-length, nonce/context/identity/hash mismatch, timeout, or early EOF on
either handshake fails.

`platform_export_validator_result_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-platform-export-validator-result-set-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact
no-LF `JSON.stringify` of a record with keys exactly
`domain,candidate_stdout_sha256,candidate_stderr_sha256,
candidate_exit_status,final_stdout_sha256,final_stderr_sha256,
final_exit_status`. Domain is exactly
`stage2-platform-export-validator-result-set-v1`; each stdout hash covers the exact
one-LF `stage2-validator-v1:platform_export:PASS:<archive_sha256>` bytes;
both stderr hashes cover empty bytes; and both statuses are zero. The
expectation's `archive_validator_result_sha256` equals this exact digest.

Only that exact ACK permits the coordinator to remove/fsync its platform lock
and emit exact coordinator marker
`stage2-platform-result-v1:PASS:<platform>:<package_run_id>:<Hs>:<Ha>:<Hd>:<platform_result_sha256>:<platform_catalog_sha256>:<archive_sha256>:<archive_size>\n`.
The gate requires this exact marker, empty coordinator stderr, stdout/stderr
EOF, exit zero, zero descendants/open pipes, and confirmed absence of the
exact platform lock.

The gate then constructs canonical `stage2-platform-expectation-v1` with
keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,
launcher_trust_sha256,launcher_context_sha256,phase_frame_sha256,
phase_ack_sha256,gate_context,gate_context_sha256,platform_context_sha256,
execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,host_binding_set_sha256,
source_receipt_set_sha256,host_control_oracle_bundle_sha256,
platform_result_sha256,platform_catalog_sha256,archive_sha256,archive_size,
archive_source_final,archive_validator_result_sha256,sink_nonce,
coordinator_marker_sha256,coordinator_stdout_sha256,
coordinator_stderr_sha256,coordinator_exit_status,descendant_count,
open_pipe_count,platform_lock_path,platform_lock_removed`.
`archive_source_final` has keys exactly
`path,device,inode,size,mode,link_count,sha256`. `gate_context` is the exact
canonical value retained after gate-lock removal; `gate_context_sha256`
covers its exact one-LF bytes. The four launcher/phase fields cross-equal the
validated context and handshake. Header and expectation cross-equal
`host_binding_set_sha256` and `source_receipt_set_sha256`. Exit/count values are zero, coordinator stderr is
the empty hash, `platform_lock_removed` is true, and every other value comes
from pinned context, reopened platform finals, retained streams, or the
validated archive final. The oracle-bundle hash cross-equals
`host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity.sha256` inside the launcher, gate,
and platform contexts, the archive header, catalog/result, and the
oracle-bearing case's evidence/fixture blob.

The expectation candidate/final are exactly
`expectations/.<platform>.<package_run_id>.expectation.candidate` and
`expectations/<platform>.<expectation_sha256>.expectation.json`. The gate
uses the same exclusive candidate, fchmod `0400`, file-fsync, reopen,
canonical-byte/hash validation, no-replace hard-link, parent-fsync, candidate
unlink, parent-fsync, final reopen, and final validation protocol, with exact
65,536-byte cap. After that final validation it removes/fsyncs the exact gate
lock, retains the context value, and emits as its final stdout operation
`stage2-platform-gate-v1:PASS:<platform>:<package_run_id>:<Hs>:<Ha>:<Hd>:<archive_sha256>:<expectation_sha256>\n`.
The external launcher may place the expectation hash into its signed
admission only after
the exact launcher-phase frame/EOF and phase-ACK under both launcher
deadlines, that exact gate marker, empty gate stderr, EOF, exit zero, zero
descendants/open pipes, and confirmed gate-lock absence. Those facts are not
authority until the launcher publishes the signed platform admission below.
An expectation, archive-contained expectation, coordinator/gate marker,
unsigned receipt, or gate crash before complete exit is never cross-host
authority.

For platform `p`, `Hg_p` is SHA-256 over the exact accepted one-LF gate
marker bytes
`stage2-platform-gate-v1:PASS:<p>:<package_run_id>:<Hs>:<Ha>:<Hd_p>:<archive_sha256>:<expectation_sha256>\n`.
The launcher recomputes it only after the complete gate-exit conditions
above; neither the gate nor an archive may self-declare an accepted `Hg_p`.

After the gate has fully exited and all those observations are final, the
same live platform launcher constructs a signed envelope with domain
`stage2-platform-gate-admission-v1`. Its payload keys are exactly
`package_run_id,challenge,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,
host_attestation_trust_sha256,host_attestation_set_sha256,
launcher_trust_sha256,launcher_context_sha256,
federation_launcher_sha256,gate_context_sha256,phase_frame_sha256,
phase_ack_sha256,archive_sha256,archive_size,expectation_sha256,
host_control_oracle_bundle_sha256,
gate_marker_sha256,gate_stdout_sha256,gate_stderr_sha256,gate_exit_status,
gate_stdout_eof,gate_stderr_eof,descendant_count,open_pipe_count,
gate_lock_removed,archive_deadline_met,gate_completion_before_deadline,status`.
All identifiers and hashes cross-equal `S,A,D_p`, the validated launcher/gate
contexts, handshake, reopened archive/expectation, and exact retained streams.
Before signing, the live launcher directly reverifies both host attestations
against its retained independently provisioned T description and positionally
revalidates its retained protected oracle-bundle description, exact bytes, and
hash against the launcher/gate/platform contexts, archive header,
expectation, catalog/result, and oracle-bearing case evidence/fixture blob.
Candidate and
final child validators instead receive exact transitive `Ht,Hat` through the
host-attested launcher context, reopen the immutable capsule T copy,
cross-equal it with S/D/A, and reverify both controller requests and host
signatures without claiming an independent child-local pin.
Both EOF fields, lock removal, archive-deadline, and
gate-completion-before-deadline fields are true; status/counts are
respectively `PASS` and zero; stderr is empty; and `gate_stdout_sha256` and
`gate_marker_sha256` cover the same sole exact gate-marker line.

The signed admission's exact compact JSON plus one LF is capped at 262,144
bytes. Its candidate/final paths are
`admissions/.<platform>.<package_run_id>.admission.candidate` and
`admissions/<platform>.<admission_sha256>.admission.json`, where
`admission_sha256` covers the exact one-LF envelope bytes. The launcher uses
the exact exclusive mode-`0600`, complete write, fchmod-`0400`, file-fsync,
read-only reopen, `platform_gate_admission` candidate validation, no-replace
hard link, parent-fsync, candidate unlink, parent-fsync, final reopen, and
final validation protocol. Publication begins only after gate exit and never
reuses an earlier candidate/final; it must finish within the separately
enforced `post_exit_admission_timeout_ms` and the payload makes no claim about
its own publication. Only after final admission validation may the launcher
close its last oracle-bundle description. An unsigned, forged, replayed, wrong-key,
cross-platform, cross-domain, cross-run/challenge, premature, self-declared,
or post-validation-replaced admission refuses. Only the final validated
signed admission hash is admitted to Linux aggregation; naked archive,
expectation, or marker hashes are never cross-host acceptance authority.

Exact Linux aggregation argv is
`[...linux_node_prefix,"scripts/run-stage2-aggregate.mjs",
"--execution-root-fd","3","--output-root-fd","4",
"--aggregation-binding-fd","5","--shared-binding-fd","6",
"--linux-export-fd","7","--linux-expectation-fd","8",
"--darwin-export-fd","9","--darwin-expectation-fd","10",
"--linux-descriptor-fd","11","--darwin-descriptor-fd","12",
"--linux-admission-fd","13","--darwin-admission-fd","14",
"--scratch-root-fd","15","--scratch-ready-fd","16",
"--scratch-receipt-fd","17","--launcher-context-fd","18",
"--scratch-nonce",Ns,
"--aggregation-binding-sha256",Ha,"--shared-binding-sha256",Hs,
"--linux-expectation-sha256",HeL,"--darwin-expectation-sha256",HeD,
"--linux-archive-sha256",HxL,"--linux-archive-size",ZL,
"--darwin-archive-sha256",HxD,"--darwin-archive-size",ZD,
"--linux-admission-sha256",HpaL,"--darwin-admission-sha256",HpaD,
"--launcher-context-sha256",Hl]`.
Only stdio and FDs 3..18 survive; environment is empty, cwd is immutable
Linux capsule FD 3, umask is `0077`, and the aggregator owns a new process
group. FDs 13 and 14 are the pinned read-only final signed platform
admissions. FD 15 is the already-empty, current-owned mode-`0700`,
`noexec,nosuid,nodev`, mount-disjoint scratch root bound by
`A.aggregate_scratch_profile`; it is a child-only duplicate and is not
aggregate publication authority. The launcher retains its distinct
scratch-root description plus the launcher-only
`scratch_privilege_broker_session`;
neither is counted as a child alias after the aggregate closes FD 15.
FD 16 is the coordinator's write-only scratch-ready pipe and FD 17 its
read-only signed scratch-receipt pipe; the launcher retains only the opposite
ends. FD 18 is the exact one-shot read-only aggregate launcher-context pipe.
The aggregator consumes/validates its bytes and EOF, checks the live parent,
and closes FD 18 before creating the aggregate lock. FDs 13..18 never survive
into a validator or outer-verifier child.
The launcher supplies each archive hash/size, expectation hash, and signed
admission hash only after canonical candidate/final admission validation and
signature verification against `S.launcher_trust`. For each platform,
`Hx_p`, `Z_p`, `He_p`, descriptor/run/challenge hashes, and the gate-marker
hash derived inside the aggregator equal the signed admission, expectation,
and pinned input FD values. No naked gate-marker argv value exists.
`Ns` is the launcher's fresh 64-lowercase-hex scratch nonce and equals the
context's `scratch_nonce`.

Canonical `stage2-aggregate-context-v1` keys are exactly
`domain,package_run_id,challenge,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
host_attestation_set_sha256,launcher_trust_sha256,
federation_launcher_sha256,launcher_context,launcher_context_sha256,
linux_descriptor_sha256,darwin_descriptor_sha256,git_commit,
execution_capsule,output_root,scratch_root,
shared_binding_snapshot,aggregation_binding_snapshot,
linux_descriptor_snapshot,darwin_descriptor_snapshot,linux_archive_input,
linux_expectation_input,linux_admission_input,darwin_archive_input,
darwin_expectation_input,darwin_admission_input,
platform_admission_set_sha256,
aggregation_coordinator_path,aggregation_coordinator_sha256,coordinator_pid,
coordinator_start_token,coordinator_process_group,scratch_nonce,
linux_scratch_privilege_policy_sha256,
linux_scratch_namespace_identity_sha256,
linux_aggregate_privilege_state_sha256,
linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,
aggregate_lock_path,
lock_device,lock_inode`. Each of the six input records has keys exactly
`device,inode,size,mode,link_count,expected_sha256`; archive input
`expected_sha256`/size equal `HxL/ZL` or `HxD/ZD`, and expectation input
`expected_sha256` equals `HeL` or `HeD`; admission input equals `HpaL` or
`HpaD` and is at most 262,144 bytes. Device, inode, size, and link count are
canonical uint64 decimal strings, mode is `"0400"`, link count is `"1"`, and
SHA is 64 lowercase hexadecimal. `launcher_context` is the exact value read
from FD 18 and cross-equals the live persistent Linux launcher, its original
commitment, both host-root attestations, the immutable capsule T copy and
transitive `Ht,Hat`, source/runtime/capsule closure, and aggregate activation;
the aggregate child does not claim an independent external pin.
`scratch_nonce` is a fresh 64-lowercase-hex launcher value.
The three Linux scratch privilege hashes equal the complete nested launcher
context records, the signed request/activation, and live supervisor/launcher/
aggregate-child observations.
The broker setup/session hashes equal the aggregate launcher-context fields
and are validated by the launcher against FD 19, the retained broker
endpoint/process observer, and activation before and after child spawn.
`platform_admission_set_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-platform-admission-set-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` of Linux-then-Darwin records with keys exactly
`platform,platform_gate_admission_sha256`. `execution_capsule`, `output_root`,
and `scratch_root` are the three exact shared-schema mount records; the four
binding/descriptor snapshots are the shared-schema authority snapshots. The exact aggregate lock
contains canonical one-LF context bytes and uses the same exclusive
mode-`0600`, fchmod-`0400`, file-fsync, parent-fsync, read-only-reopen,
identity/bytes/hash validation protocol as the platform context.

Import order is exact: Linux expectation, Linux signed admission, Linux
archive, Darwin expectation, Darwin signed admission, Darwin archive,
imported-object validation/replay, signed scratch destruction, then aggregate
catalog. The launcher's pre-exec checks derive argv/context values but publish
nothing and are not import steps; the coordinator revalidates and durably
imports the same pinned FD identities and bytes in that exact order.
Expectation candidate/final names are
`exports/.<platform>.<package_run_id>.expectation.candidate` and
`exports/<platform>.<expectation_sha256>.expectation.json`; archive
candidate/final names are
`exports/.<platform>.<package_run_id>.stage2x.candidate` and
`exports/<platform>.<archive_sha256>.stage2x`; admission candidate/final names
are `exports/.<platform>.<package_run_id>.admission.candidate` and
`exports/<platform>.<admission_sha256>.admission.json`. Expectation import
copies the exact input bytes within the 65,536-byte cap, canonical-validates
and hash-checks them, and uses the standard candidate/no-replace/final
protocol. Admission import does the same within 262,144 bytes and invokes
`platform_gate_admission` over both candidate and final; it verifies the
signature, key/platform/run/challenge/context/phase/expectation cross-hashes,
and all true/zero post-exit facts before any archive byte is imported.
Archive import streams exactly
the independently expected size into an exclusively created
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` mode-`0600` candidate, requires EOF and no
trailing bytes, hashes and framing-validates while streaming, file-fsyncs,
fchmods `0400`, file-fsyncs again, closes, reopens read-only, and invokes
`platform_export` over the candidate. It then hard-links no-replace to the
exact final, parent-fsyncs, unlinks the candidate, parent-fsyncs again,
reopens the final, requires the recorded identity/hash/size, mode `0400`, and
link count one, and invokes `platform_export` over the final.

Aggregation validates independently supplied signed admissions and
expectations, exact partition union/no overlap, descriptors/bindings,
archives, catalogs/results, every
fixed manifest/evidence/blob, and reruns the correct descriptor-bound outer
verifier from raw replay bytes. Imported AC17 is verified against `D_D`; the
Linux aggregator retains separate `A` and Linux runtime authority and never
rewrites AC17 evidence to claim `D_L` or executes a Darwin Node/Mach-O byte.

Platform failure, missing expectation, differing run/challenge/S/A/descriptor/
commit/contract/registry/partition, replay, archive collision, equal Linux
and Darwin archive hashes, case overlap/omission/reorder, third archive,
transport path collision, or import cleanup uncertainty yields no aggregate
catalog, package marker, or package admission. Exact run-owned imports alone may be removed;
uncertain cleanup retains the aggregate lock.

For each validated imported archive, the aggregator constructs private
canonical `stage2-platform-export-index-v1` with keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,
platform_descriptor_sha256,archive_sha256,header_sha256,
host_binding_set_sha256,source_receipt_count,source_receipt_set_sha256,
source_receipts,binding_count,object_count,bindings,objects`.
Each object record has keys exactly
`sha256,size,record_offset,payload_offset,payload_end`; offsets are canonical
uint64 decimal strings. Each index binding copies the exact canonical header
binding and appends key `object_index`, a zero-based safe integer selecting
the one matching object record. The index copies the exact canonical
source-receipt array and digest without reinterpretation. The index is compact JSON without LF,
at most 83,951,616 bytes. Its sole temporary name beneath retained scratch FD
15 is `.<platform>.<package_run_id>.stage2-index.tmp`. The aggregator creates
it with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, current UID/GID, `umask 0177`, and mode
`0600`; writes exact bytes; file-fsyncs; fchmods `0400`; file-fsyncs again;
closes; reopens read-only; validates exact identity/bytes/hash/mode/link
count; unlinks; parent-fsyncs; and retains only the read-only FD.

For an imported dynamic target, only that target's at-most 16,777,216 exact
bytes are materialized under FD 15 as
`.<platform>.<package_run_id>.<slot>.<target_sha256>.stage2-target.tmp`,
where slot is exactly
`target|context|evidence|fixture|binary|outer_stdout|outer_stderr`, using the
same protocol, then unlinked while its read-only FD is retained. Related
blobs remain addressable only by positional reads through archive plus index.
Targets are created/unlinked serially, so visible-name states are exactly
zero, one exact index temp, zero, one exact target temp, zero; one visible
name passes and a second refuses. Up to seven unlinked read-only objects may
be retained simultaneously: one index plus context, evidence, fixture,
binary, stdout replay, and stderr replay; seven passes and eight refuses.
Open-byte accounting passes exactly 184,614,912 and refuses `+1`. The
aggregator requires a zero-name scan, closes every scratch/object FD plus FD
15, and—after all imported validation/replay but before constructing the
aggregate catalog and while retaining the aggregate lock—sends one FD-16
scratch-ready frame. Framing is exactly one
uint32be length, compact JSON without LF of length `1..4096`, then EOF. Keys
are exactly
`domain,package_run_id,challenge,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
host_attestation_set_sha256,launcher_trust_sha256,launcher_context_sha256,
aggregate_context_sha256,platform_admission_set_sha256,
linux_aggregate_privilege_state_sha256,
scratch_mount_identity_sha256,linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,
scratch_nonce,visible_name_count,
retained_object_count,open_byte_count`; domain is
`stage2-aggregate-scratch-ready-v1`, the privilege, mount, and nonce values
equal context,
all binding/context/admission hashes cross-equal validated authorities, and
all three counts are safe-integer zero. `aggregate_context_sha256` covers the
exact one-LF aggregate-context bytes pinned in the lock.
`ready_frame_sha256` is SHA-256 over the exact four-byte uint32be length plus
the exact ready JSON bytes.

The trusted Linux launcher permits the one live aggregate direct child to
await FD 17 only after that child closed FD 15 and every scratch/object
description. It verifies the ready frame, rescans its own retained root to
zero names, proves the live child has no scratch FD/map/cwd/root alias, closes
its own scratch-root description, and opens a pidfd for the exact broker
start token. It never claims a host-global scan. The broker's retained
CAP_SYS_PTRACE and read-only cgroup/proc roots instead produce two
fixed-point snapshots of the closed process domain.

Canonical `stage2-linux-process-domain-snapshot-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,phase,linux_run_process_domain_sha256,scratch_mount_observation,
scratch_logical_prefix_observation,process_count,
total_thread_count,fd_alias_count,map_alias_count,cgroup_procs,cgroup_threads,
processes,alias_count,unreadable_count`. Phase is exactly
`pre_teardown|post_remove`. Canonical
`stage2-linux-scratch-mount-observation-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,phase,scratch_mount_id,mountinfo_match_count,present`; the mount ID is
the exact frozen canonical uint64-decimal tmpfs mount ID. Pre-teardown values
are `pre_teardown`, `1`, and `true`; post-remove values are `post_remove`,
`0`, and `false`. Canonical
`stage2-linux-scratch-logical-prefix-observation-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,phase,parent_device,parent_inode,basename,lookup_flags,result,
mount_id`. It uses the frozen parent identity and package-run basename;
`lookup_flags` is exactly
`AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW|AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT|STATX_BASIC_STATS|STATX_MNT_ID`.
Pre-teardown values are `pre_teardown`, `present`, and the frozen scratch
mount ID; post-remove values are `post_remove`, `ENOENT`, and JSON null.
Each nested observation's phase equals the enclosing phase. PID/TID arrays
are unique ascending safe integers.
`process_count` is in `1..64` and equals both `processes.length` and
`cgroup_procs.length`; `total_thread_count` is in `1..512` and equals
`cgroup_threads.length`; and the two aggregate alias counts are each in
`0..1024` and equal the sums of their named arrays. Each PID record has keys
exactly
`pid,start_token,process_group,process_role,tids,thread_states,
thread_set_state_sha256,fd_aliases,map_aliases,cwd_alias,root_alias,
mount_namespace_id`; `start_token` is the complete canonical
`stage2-kernel-process-identity-v1` object and its PID/process-group values
cross-equal the duplicated scalars. `process_role` is exactly
`supervisor|broker|launcher|aggregate_child|declared_descendant`; `tids` is
a nonempty unique ascending safe-integer array, the PID arrays partition
`cgroup_threads`, and `thread_states` is a TID-sorted, count-equal array of
complete `stage2-linux-thread-privilege-state-v1` objects whose TIDs exactly
equal `tids`. `thread_set_state_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-linux-process-thread-set-v2`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify(thread_states)`, not over a TID-only projection. Every
supervisor, launcher, aggregate-child, and declared-descendant thread equals
the zero-capability/no-new-privileges profile; every broker thread equals
`broker_active_capabilities` in `pre_teardown` and
`broker_post_teardown_capabilities` in `post_remove`. PID and process-group
values are safe integers and mount-namespace IDs are canonical uint64
decimals.

Each FD-alias record has keys exactly
`fd,device,inode,mount_id,access_mode,cloexec`; FD is a safe integer in
`0..1048575`, device/inode/mount ID are canonical uint64 decimals,
`access_mode` is exactly `read_only|write_only|read_write`, and `cloexec` is a
boolean. Each map-alias record has keys exactly
`start_address,end_address,permissions,offset,device,inode,mount_id`;
addresses and offset are 1..16 lowercase hexadecimal digits without `0x`,
the numeric start is below the numeric end, permissions are exactly four
ASCII characters matching `[r-][w-][x-][ps]`, and the three identity values
are canonical uint64 decimals. FD aliases are numerically FD-sorted and map
aliases are numerically start/end-sorted; both contain only descriptions or
file-backed mappings whose independently resolved mount ID equals the frozen
scratch mount. `cwd_alias` and `root_alias` are booleans indicating that the
respective independently resolved mount ID equals the scratch mount.
`map_aliases` are derived by parsing canonical `/proc/<pid>/maps`
device/inode pairs and joining each pair to exactly one canonical
`/proc/<pid>/mountinfo` entry whose major/minor and mount ID equal the frozen
scratch mount. A missing or nonunique join refuses; `/proc/<pid>/map_files`
is never opened and no inaccessible child-user-namespace path is assumed.
`alias_count` equals
`fd_alias_count + map_alias_count +` the number of true cwd/root aliases and
is in `0..2050`; `unreadable_count` is exactly zero. The snapshot repeats complete
`cgroup.procs`/`cgroup.threads` and every
`/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/{fd,maps,mountinfo,cwd,root,ns/mnt,status}`
enumeration until the before/after sets byte-equal. Every entry must be
readable. Only the
pidfd-bound supervisor, broker, launcher, live aggregate child, and exact
declared descendants may occur. The dedicated UID, closed cgroup leaf,
nondumpability, namespace construction, and one-way FD ledger exclude a
foreign entrant; host-global absence outside that trust boundary is not
asserted. Exact compact JSON plus one LF is the snapshot artifact and must be
in `1..4194304` bytes. For each phase the acceptance generator records and
independently regenerates the exact length/hash of the deterministic
schema-valid fixture with maximum legal aggregate counts and scalar widths
and deterministic distinct values where uniqueness/order requires; that
fixture must fit even though lifecycle acceptance separately requires zero
aliases. Separately, a canonical-JSON size-gate body at
exactly 4,194,304 bytes reaches ordinary schema validation, while byte
4,194,305 refuses before a snapshot file is created; size-gate equality does
not make an otherwise schema-invalid filler object valid.

Canonical `stage2-sealed-process-domain-snapshot-file-identity-v1` has keys
exactly `domain,role,device,inode,size,seals,sha256`. Role is exactly
`pre_teardown_process_domain_snapshot|post_remove_process_domain_snapshot`;
device and inode are canonical uint64 decimals; size is a canonical uint64
decimal in `"1".."4194304"` and equals the exact one-LF snapshot byte length;
`seals` is exactly
`["F_SEAL_SEAL","F_SEAL_SHRINK","F_SEAL_GROW","F_SEAL_WRITE"]`; and `sha256`
hashes those complete one-LF bytes. The identity digest uses exact
domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON.

The broker constructs exactly two such artifacts, one immediately after each
accepted fixed-point snapshot. For each it calls exactly
`memfd_create("stage2-process-domain-snapshot",
MFD_CLOEXEC|MFD_ALLOW_SEALING)`, completely writes the bounded one-LF bytes
from offset zero, truncates to the exact final size, applies in one
`F_ADD_SEALS` call
`F_SEAL_SEAL|F_SEAL_SHRINK|F_SEAL_GROW|F_SEAL_WRITE`, and requires
`F_GET_SEALS` to return exactly that set. Through its already trusted procfs
authority it then reopens that exact memfd description once with
`O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC`, cross-equals device/inode/size/seals, closes the
writable creation description, and uses only bounded `pread` to byte-validate
the read-only description. The two artifacts have distinct inodes; no
writable descriptor or mapping survives sealing, and no alternate name,
flags, seal sequence, reopen path, mutable alias, or third snapshot is legal.

The launcher sends canonical signed
`stage2-linux-scratch-broker-destroy-request-v1` on session FD 19 with one
exact aggregate pidfd right. Its envelope uses the frozen launcher-signed
four-key schema; its payload keys are exactly
`package_run_id,challenge,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,launcher_context_sha256,
aggregate_context_sha256,ready_frame_sha256,
activation_frame_sha256,
linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,
linux_run_process_domain_sha256,scratch_nonce,aggregate_pid,
aggregate_start_token,status`; status is `authorize_normal_teardown`. The
single packet is uint32be `N` followed by exactly `N` compact envelope bytes,
with no LF. `destroy_request_sha256` is SHA-256 over that exact four-byte
prefix followed by those exact envelope bytes. A payload-only, LF-appended,
re-encoded, or signature-excluding hash is invalid. The launcher retains its
write direction after this request for the later typed result ACK; it
performs `SHUT_WR` only after that ACK and sends no intervening frame.
The
broker verifies the signature against the exact host-attested launcher key
and complete T/S/attestation bytes retained from the supervisor's create
request, validates the pidfd and every hash, and accepts no generic command.

The broker destruction sequence is exact and has no alternative success
path:

1. It validates the ready frame and signed request; takes the exact
   `pre_teardown` fixed-point process-domain snapshot; requires the live
   aggregate child, launcher, and supervisor all-thread-zero; and requires
   no scratch alias except the broker's own scratch root and outside-parent
   FD 19. It closes its scratch-root description and repeats the snapshot
   with `alias_count=0`, freezes that repeated snapshot as the canonical
   `pre_teardown_process_domain_snapshot`, and constructs and validates its
   sealed read-only artifact.
2. It verifies `fstatfs` on `/proc` has exact `PROC_SUPER_MAGIC`,
   `/proc/self` resolves to its broker PID/start token, and `fstat(19)` still
   equals the frozen outside parent. It invokes exactly
   `statx(AT_FDCWD,"/proc/self/fd/19/<package_run_id>",
   AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW|AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT,
   STATX_BASIC_STATS|STATX_MNT_ID,&before)` and requires the frozen mounted
   root and mount ID. It calls exactly once
   `umount2("/proc/self/fd/19/<package_run_id>",0)`. `MNT_DETACH`,
   `MNT_FORCE`, lazy/forced unmount, retry after `EBUSY`, cwd/logical/other-
   PID fallback, another FD/basename/namespace, or any nonzero flag fails.
   It requires the frozen mount ID absent from canonical mountinfo.
3. It invokes exactly `statx(19,package_run_id,
   AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW|AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT,
   STATX_BASIC_STATS|STATX_MNT_ID,&covered)` and requires the frozen covered
   directory on the parent mount; calls
   `unlinkat(19,package_run_id,AT_REMOVEDIR)` and `fsync(19)`; and requires
   `openat2(19,package_run_id,O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC,
   RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS|
   RESOLVE_NO_XDEV)` to fail with `ENOENT`. It closes FD 19.
4. It takes the exact `post_remove` fixed-point process-domain snapshot with
   zero aliases/unreadable entries, absent logical prefix, and absent mount.
   It constructs and validates the second sealed read-only snapshot artifact.
   While still one-threaded it clears effective/permitted
   `CAP_SYS_PTRACE|CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, verifies all five capability sets and
   bounding set empty plus no-new-privileges, and freezes the exact
   `broker_post_teardown` state. It can never regain a capability.
5. It builds one immutable canonical result buffer, sends the identical
   uint32be prefix and bytes plus the same two read-only snapshot descriptions
   in exact pre/post order, first on broker-control to the supervisor and then
   on its session endpoint whose launcher peer is FD 19. Each receiver uses
   `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC`, requires exactly two rights and no other ancillary
   data, and independently cross-equals access mode, descriptor flags,
   device/inode/size/seals, positional bytes, snapshot schema/counts, and
   hashes before accepting the result. Each returns its exact typed
   `teardown_result_validated_ack`, then performs write shutdown. The broker
   remains alive in the frozen post-teardown state, requires both ACKs and
   both input EOFs, and only then performs output shutdown/EOF on both, closes
   every remaining run FD, and exits zero. A short/failed send or ACK is never
   retried and invalidates the run. The supervisor retains its original
   broker pidfd, exact result, and two snapshot readers; the launcher
   validates the result, both readers, broker EOF, and pidfd-readable broker
   exit through its fresh pidfd before signing. Only the direct-parent
   supervisor later derives the numeric exit status.

Canonical `stage2-linux-scratch-broker-teardown-result-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,challenge,supervisor_run_request_sha256,
create_request_sha256,create_result_sha256,activation_frame_sha256,
handoff_commit_sha256,handoff_ack_sha256,
linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,
launcher_context_sha256,aggregate_context_sha256,ready_frame_sha256,
destroy_request_sha256,
pre_teardown_process_domain_snapshot_file_identity,
pre_teardown_process_domain_snapshot_file_identity_sha256,
post_remove_process_domain_snapshot_file_identity,
post_remove_process_domain_snapshot_file_identity_sha256,
broker_pid,broker_start_token,
broker_parent_control_fd,umount_target_path,umount_flags,umount_call_count,
scratch_mount_id,scratch_mount_absent,covered_directory_identity,
parent_fsync_succeeded,reopen_errno,alias_count,
scratch_aliasing_descendant_count,scratch_logical_prefix_absent,
broker_post_teardown_privilege_state,
broker_post_teardown_privilege_state_sha256,status`. Fixed values are FD
`19`, exact broker `/proc/self/fd/19/<package_run_id>`, flags `0`, call count
`1`, true absence/fsync/prefix facts, `ENOENT`, zero counts, and `PASS`. Its
create/result/handoff hashes cross-equal the broker and supervisor's retained
byte-exact control frames; the activation hash also cross-equals the launcher's
destroy request and context. The two complete nested file identities and
their digests cross-equal the exact two ordered SCM_RIGHTS descriptions and
their validated snapshot bytes; the result contains neither full snapshot.
`broker_post_teardown_privilege_state` is the complete canonical
`stage2-linux-broker-post-teardown-privilege-state-v1` object and its digest
recomputes; a bare capability record or hash-only claim is invalid. Its
digest uses exact domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON. Both recipients require byte-
identical result frames, byte-identical snapshot artifacts, and the same
device/inode identities in the same rights order.

Canonical
`stage2-linux-scratch-broker-teardown-result-validated-ack-v1` has keys
exactly
`domain,receiver_role,status,channel_identity_sha256,destroy_request_sha256,
scratch_broker_teardown_result_sha256,
pre_teardown_process_domain_snapshot_file_identity_sha256,
post_remove_process_domain_snapshot_file_identity_sha256,
broker_post_teardown_privilege_state_sha256`. `receiver_role` is
`supervisor|launcher`, status is `validated`, and the channel identity selects
the original broker-control or broker-session channel respectively. Each ACK
is one zero-right framed packet; its digest hashes the exact uint32be prefix
plus compact payload bytes. The broker cross-equals every field against its
immutable result and the receiver's exact channel before accepting it.

Canonical `stage2-linux-pidfd-observation-identity-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,holder_pid,holder_start_token,subject_pid,subject_start_token,
device,inode,fd_descriptor_flags,fdinfo_pid,fdinfo_nspid`. Both start tokens
are complete kernel process identities; device/inode are canonical uint64
decimals; descriptor flags are exactly `FD_CLOEXEC`; and the parsed pidfd
`Pid`/`NSpid` values cross-equal the broker's subject identities. The digest
uses exact domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON.

Canonical `stage2-linux-broker-exit-observation-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,observer_role,broker_pid,broker_start_token,
observer_identity_sha256,pidfd_identity,pidfd_identity_sha256,
pidfd_readable,status`. The launcher is the only `observer_role`; the
complete pidfd identity names the original launcher and broker; readable is
true; and status is `exit_observed`. This record proves that the pidfd became
readable after both broker EOFs, but deliberately contains no numeric wait
status because the launcher is not the broker's parent.

Canonical `stage2-linux-broker-wait-status-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,broker_pid,broker_start_token,supervisor_pid,supervisor_start_token,
wait_api,si_code,exit_status,status`. The complete tokens name the broker and
its direct-parent supervisor; fixed values are `waitid_P_PIDFD`,
`CLD_EXITED`, safe-integer `0`, and `PASS`. Only the supervisor invokes
`waitid(P_PIDFD)` through its original broker pidfd after both result ACKs,
both directional EOFs, and pidfd readiness. Both exit-record
digests use their exact domain/`0x00`/no-LF JSON preimages. External PASS
requires both records to name the same broker/result lifecycle.

Only after all broker steps, both validated-result ACKs, both-direction EOFs,
and pidfd-readable broker exit succeed does the launcher send one FD-17
signed receipt frame using uint32be
length, exact compact JSON of length `1..262144`, and EOF. The envelope domain is
`stage2-aggregate-scratch-destruction-receipt-v1`; its payload keys are
exactly
`package_run_id,challenge,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
host_attestation_set_sha256,launcher_trust_sha256,signer_platform,
launcher_context_sha256,
aggregate_context_sha256,ready_frame_sha256,platform_admission_set_sha256,
linux_scratch_privilege_policy_sha256,
linux_scratch_namespace_identity_sha256,
linux_aggregate_privilege_state_sha256,
launcher_post_teardown_privilege_state,
launcher_post_teardown_privilege_state_sha256,
scratch_mount_identity_sha256,linux_scratch_broker_setup_sha256,
scratch_privilege_broker_session_identity_sha256,
scratch_broker_teardown_result,
scratch_broker_teardown_result_sha256,broker_exit_observation,
broker_exit_observation_sha256,
scratch_nonce,visible_name_count,
retained_object_count,open_byte_count,alias_count,
scratch_aliasing_descendant_count,
scratch_logical_prefix_absent,scratch_mount_absent,status`.
`signer_platform` is exactly `linux`; the five counts are safe-integer zero,
the two booleans are true, status is
`PASS`, and all other fields cross-equal the ready frame, aggregate context,
signed input-admission set, complete privilege records, and the final
twice-sampled all-zero launcher/broker state, byte-exact broker result, and
complete pidfd-readable broker exit observation. It never claims the
non-child broker's numeric exit code. Before signing, the live Linux launcher validates both
ordered snapshot readers exactly as above and retains them through signature
construction; it closes them before receipt delivery. The live Linux launcher
reverifies both host attestations against its retained out-of-band trust
description. The signature key must equal the Linux host-attested launcher
key and aggregate launcher-context key. The exact
deadline from ready-frame EOF through signed-receipt EOF is
`scratch_receipt_timeout_ms`; the receiving aggregator enforces it and the
receipt contains no self-asserted deadline fact.

The aggregator verifies the complete envelope/signature/EOF against
`S.launcher_trust`, both host attestations, the immutable capsule T copy
through `Ht`, and the independently recomputed transitive `Hat` before the
external scratch-receipt deadline, then
publishes those exact
compact JSON bytes plus one LF.
Candidate/final paths are
`.stage2-aggregate-scratch-destruction-receipt.<package_run_id>.candidate`
and
`stage2-aggregate-scratch-destruction-receipt.<receipt_sha256>.json`, where
`receipt_sha256` covers the exact one-LF envelope. Publication uses exclusive
mode `0600`, complete write, fchmod `0400`, file-fsync, read-only reopen,
`aggregate_scratch_destruction` candidate validation, no-replace hard link,
parent-fsync, candidate unlink, parent-fsync, final reopen, and final
validation. Only that durable final may be referenced by the later aggregate
catalog. Malformed/duplicate/extra/trailing/wrong-nonce/context/count/
identity/key/signature frames, early EOF, timeout, incomplete destruction,
remaining alias, forged/replayed receipt, or candidate/final failure leaves
the aggregate lock and yields no catalog or package marker. The coordinator
never derives a parent with `..`. Ambient `/tmp`, aggregate FD 4, a transfer
root, and capsule FD 3 are never scratch authority.

In the imported-validator argv below, `validator_body` is exactly the
selected role's `D_L.validators[role].command` array after removal of the
four-element Linux runtime/reseal prefix. It begins with the validator path.
For an imported Darwin role it must byte-equal the corresponding `D_D`
command after removal of the two-element Darwin runtime prefix, and its
source hash cross-equals `S`, both descriptors, `A`, and the Linux capsule
inventory.

Exact imported-validator invocation is
`[...linux_node_prefix,...validator_body,"--execution-root-fd","3",
"--output-root-fd","4","--platform-descriptor-fd","5",
"--shared-binding-fd","6","--aggregation-binding-fd","7",
"--host-attestation-trust-sha256",Ht,
"--host-attestation-set-sha256",Hat,
"--import-mode","stage2-platform-export-v1","--import-archive-fd","8",
"--import-expectation-fd","9","--import-index-fd","10",
"--import-context-fd","11","--target-role",role,"--target-fd","12",
"--target",targetPath,"--target-sha256",targetSha256]`.
Only stdio and FDs 3..12 survive. In import mode, immutable repository/static
bytes resolve only under FD 3; imported dynamic logical paths, evidence blobs,
and replay objects resolve only through archive FD 8 plus index FD 10.
Original archive-binding metadata resolves through the header/index
`host_binding_set_sha256` cross-equal to expectation FD 9;
fixture/binary `host_path|guest_image_path`
external-source leaves resolve only as exact index source receipts whose
`source_receipt_set_sha256` cross-equals expectation FD 9, and are never
materialized or locally reopened. The exact imported platform context from
the archive is supplied on FD 11 and cross-equals the expectation/result
hash. The aggregator's writable aggregate FD 4 never crosses into an imported
child. Child FD 4 instead pins exact empty capsule directory
`fixtures/stage2-import-inert-output-root-v1`, inventoried mode `0555` on the
kernel-read-only capsule mount; it is an ABI placeholder on which every
create/write/link/unlink/rename probe fails `EROFS`, and is never treated as
a platform or aggregate output root.

For Darwin evidence, imported validator FD 5 is `D_D`, but `command[0]` is
the Linux aggregation Node bound by `D_L` and `A`. Import records exact
`validation_runtime_platform=linux` and `evidence_platform=darwin`, requires
shared release/source/semantic-probe equality, and never executes Darwin Node
or Mach-O evidence.

Exact imported outer-verifier invocation is
`[...linux_node_prefix,verifier_path,"--execution-root-fd","3",
"--output-root-fd","4","--platform-descriptor-fd","5",
"--shared-binding-fd","6","--aggregation-binding-fd","7",
"--host-attestation-trust-sha256",Ht,
"--host-attestation-set-sha256",Hat,
"--import-mode","stage2-platform-export-v1","--import-archive-fd","8",
"--import-expectation-fd","9","--import-index-fd","10",
"--import-context-fd","11","--case",caseId,"--evidence-fd","12",
"--fixture-fd","13","--binary-fd","14","--outer-stdout-fd","15",
"--outer-stderr-fd","16"]`.
Only stdio and FDs 3..16 survive. Every evidence/fixture/binary/replay
reference is resolved through the validated archive/index; no aggregate path
or original host path substitutes for those bytes. FDs 3 and 5..14 are
pinned read-only; FD 4 is the independently verified inert read-only capsule
directory above; authority and
target FDs begin at offset zero and use positional reads. Replay FDs 15/16
are read-only and consumed exactly once through EOF. Stdin is `/dev/null`;
stdout/stderr are independently captured; environment is empty; cwd is
immutable capsule FD 3; and every other FD is closed.
Each imported outer invocation has its own exact 300-second monotonic
deadline through process-group/descendant exit and stdout/stderr EOF, nested
within the aggregate import deadline. Verifier stdout/stderr caps are each
4,096 bytes; equality passes and `+1` fails. Success requires complete
consumption of both replay FDs through EOF, zero descendants/open pipes, exit
zero, empty stderr, and exact one-LF stdout
`stage2-case-evidence-verifier-v1:<case_id>:PASS:<output_sha256>:<evidence_sha256>\n`.
Failure is irreversible and permits at most 2,000 milliseconds graceful plus
5,000 milliseconds forced kill/drain; it accepts no imported case, catalog,
package marker, or package admission. AC01 import vectors exercise every argv/FD/mode/offset,
replay cap/order/truncation/trailing/early-EOF, timeout, signal/nonzero,
stdout/stderr, descendant, held-pipe, inert-FD4, and cleanup failure.


`validators` has exactly these unsigned-byte-role-sorted unique roles:
`aggregate_catalog,aggregate_scratch_destruction,aggregation_binding,
assertion_manifest,b27_admission,
binary_artifacts,case_evidence,clean_admission,darwin_fixture_template,
evidence_catalog,evidence_runner,execution_capsule,fixture_bundle,
generated_migration_failpoints,host_control_oracle_bundle,
operation_matrix,package_admission,
platform_descriptor,platform_export,
platform_gate_admission,platform_result,qemu_inputs,s28_schema_manifest,
shared_run_binding,tool_transition`. Each entry has keys
exactly `role,path,sha256,command,timeout_seconds`; path is a canonical
repository-relative ordinary validator source, SHA covers its bytes,
`timeout_seconds` is a safe integer in `1..300`, and `command` is the exact
five-element Linux or three-element Darwin printable-ASCII argv prefix
frozen above, not a shell string.

No transient-control-only role is added. Validation ownership within those
25 roles is exact: `execution_capsule` owns P/M/T-entry/reserved-delta and
complete runtime/import/loader closure; `shared_run_binding` owns T,
controller and keystore authorization schemas, both signed requests, combined
bootstrap results, commitments/attestations, the request-set and attestation-
set hashes, and the public S trust graph; `platform_descriptor` owns canonical
kernel process identities, pipe identities, activation schemas/role arrays,
and platform-specific request equality; `platform_gate_admission` owns the
platform launcher/gate context and transitive `Ht,Hat` checks;
`aggregation_binding` owns A plus the fifteen-right Linux activation and
supervisor-context identity; `aggregate_scratch_destruction` owns aggregate
context identity, the receipt's bounded pre/post process-domain snapshot
identities/hashes, and the exact normal-unmount/result/receipt sequence. The
two sealed snapshot files themselves are nonpersistent live control-plane
evidence owned and byte-validated only by the broker, launcher, and final
Linux supervisor; they are not validator inputs or package artifacts; and
`package_admission` owns the terminal launcher context, file/hash/signature/
deadline graph consumed by direct supervisor acceptance.
`host_control_oracle_bundle` owns the complete policy/plan/registry,
protected file identity, chronological event chain, exact scenario set, and
AC01/AC17 route. S2-AC-01 owns platform-neutral child events plus the
independently sourced Linux oracle assertion projection; S2-AC-17 owns its
platform-neutral child events plus the independently sourced Darwin
projection. Neither payload child fabricates, receives, or duplicates the
host observer's live proof. `assertion_manifest` owns every record's exact
source split. `fixture_bundle` requires the one exact oracle evidence-blob
role only for AC01/AC17. `case_evidence` and the outer verifier recompute the
full manifest-order union, require the evidence oracle hash to equal that
fixture blob and the platform context, and reject a child-event/oracle-source
substitution even when the final ID set is unchanged.

`Ht` and `Hat` below are respectively the exact
`host_attestation_trust_sha256` and `host_attestation_set_sha256` from S and
the live host-attested launcher/gate or aggregate context; every validator
reopens the fixed trust bytes under immutable FD 3, compares `Ht`, and
reverifies both host attestations plus `Hat` before its target-specific work.
Live-platform and post-gate platform-launcher invocation is exactly
the selected-platform prefix followed by
`["--execution-root-fd","3","--output-root-fd","4",
"--platform-descriptor-fd","5","--shared-binding-fd","6",
"--aggregation-binding-fd","7","--host-attestation-trust-sha256",Ht,
"--host-attestation-set-sha256",Hat,
"--target-role",role,"--target-fd","12",
"--target",targetPath,"--target-sha256",targetSha256]`, or the aggregation
invocation used for aggregate-static/imported-control/scratch/catalog and
post-exit package-admission targets is exactly the Linux prefix followed by
`["--execution-root-fd","3","--output-root-fd","4",
"--aggregation-binding-fd","5","--shared-binding-fd","6",
"--linux-descriptor-fd","11","--darwin-descriptor-fd","12",
"--host-attestation-trust-sha256",Ht,
"--host-attestation-set-sha256",Hat,
"--target-role",role,"--target-fd","13","--target",targetPath,
"--target-sha256",targetSha256]`. A platform admission imported as a control
artifact uses that aggregation invocation; dynamic targets inside an archive
use only the exact import-mode invocation frozen above. Before each child, the
parent closes/remaps all unrelated admission/scratch/context/transport FDs so
only the enumerated child envelope survives.

No validator child inherits a parent's writable output-root description.
For a live-platform, post-gate launcher, aggregate, or post-exit launcher role
that needs related output traversal, child FD 4 is a fresh
`stage2-validator-output-view-v1`
kernel-read-only, `noexec,nosuid,nodev` snapshot/view of the exact paused
source root. Its shared-schema mount record, complete allowed-name inventory,
and every source device/inode/size/mode/hash are frozen before spawn; no
writable alias is present in the child namespace; every create/write/link/
unlink/rename probe fails `EROFS`; and the parent revalidates unchanged source
identities after child EOF before destroying the view. For a role needing no
related output traversal, child FD 4 is the exact inert capsule directory
defined above. The writable parent FD 4 never survives either route.

The caller pins every authority and target
read-only at offset zero and gives the validator only the enumerated FDs.
Binding, descriptor, and target reads use positional I/O; paths are
provenance only. The wrapper
independently verifies the capsule runtime/validator entries before shell-free
execution. Success is only exit zero,
empty stderr, and exact stdout
`stage2-validator-v1:<role>:PASS:<target-sha256>\n`; failure emits no such
prefix and cannot create or accept evidence/catalog output. Binding and
descriptor validators receive bytes from separate caller-pinned read-only
descriptions and caller-supplied expected hashes, never self-hash fields.
That object pinning is not an independently provisioned trust-root claim:
every validator child receives `Ht,Hat` transitively through its
host-attested launcher context, reopens capsule T, and reverifies the signed
requests and attestations. The `execution_capsule` validator independently
rescans the selected FD-3 root, mount/read-only profile, reserved slots,
system loader map, and complete entry inventory under that transitive
binding.

Every dynamic fixture manifest, binary manifest, case-evidence file, and
catalog uses one exact candidate path
`<final-path>.candidate.<package_run_id>`. Its publisher exclusively creates
the same-directory candidate through the retained directory description with
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, current UID/GID, `umask 0177`, and requested
first-visible mode `0600`; it writes complete canonical bytes, `fchmod`s to
current-owned read-only mode `0400`, file-fsyncs after that metadata change,
closes, and reopens/hashes it.
Write, pre-fsync `fchmod`, post-`fchmod` file fsync, reopen, candidate
validation, no-replace link, first parent fsync, candidate unlink, second
parent fsync, final reopen, and final validation are separate crash-tested
boundaries for fixture, binary, evidence, and catalog candidates. The
descriptor-bound role validator must emit exact PASS over that
candidate. Only then may the publisher create a no-replace same-filesystem
hard link at the fixed final path, parent-fsync, unlink the candidate,
parent-fsync again, reopen the final, and require the recorded inode/hash,
mode `0400`, and link count one. The same role validator must then emit exact
PASS over the final before the case or package can advance. A preexisting
candidate or final, even byte-identical, is a hard failure; replacement,
rename-over, or accept-existing publication is forbidden.

For every live-platform validator, `command[0]` is the selected platform
descriptor's canonical capsule Node executable and satisfies the shared
runtime policy. For aggregate import mode, `command[0]` is instead the
canonical Linux aggregation Node frozen above, while FD 5 still supplies the
evidence platform's descriptor and the shared runtime policy must cross-equal;
the final command-prefix token is byte-equal to the validator entry's `path`.
The complete prefix is exactly
`[node_linux,"--no-warnings","--require",
linux_node_post_exec_reseal_prelude_path,validator_path]` on Linux and
`[node_darwin,"--no-warnings",validator_path]` on Darwin. Any other
`-e`, `-p`, loader, import/require hook, shell evaluation, environment
interpolation, or ambient executable resolution is forbidden. The exact
target map is:
`aggregate_catalog -> aggregate catalog candidate and final`,
`aggregate_scratch_destruction -> signed aggregate scratch-destruction
receipt candidate and final`,
`aggregation_binding -> A`,
`assertion_manifest -> static assertions`,
`b27_admission -> static b27_admission`,
`clean_admission -> static clean_admission`,
`darwin_fixture_template -> static darwin_fixture_template`,
`evidence_runner -> static evidence_runner`,
`execution_capsule -> selected execution_capsule_linux or
execution_capsule_darwin`,
`generated_migration_failpoints -> static generated_migration_failpoints`,
`host_control_oracle_bundle -> the live protected FD-74 bundle before the
oracle-bearing payload and the exact transported evidence-blob bytes during
aggregate import`,
`operation_matrix -> static operation_matrix`,
`package_admission -> signed final package-admission candidate and final`,
`qemu_inputs -> static qemu_inputs`,
`binary_artifacts -> each exact run-derived candidate and fixed final
completed case binary manifest in its phase`,
`s28_schema_manifest -> static schema`,
`tool_transition -> static tool_transition`,
`fixture_bundle -> each exact run-derived candidate and fixed final completed
case fixture in its phase`,
`case_evidence -> each exact run-derived candidate and fixed final completed
case evidence in its phase`,
`platform_descriptor -> D_L and D_D`,
`platform_export -> each externally gated platform archive`,
`platform_gate_admission -> each signed platform gate-admission candidate and
final`,
`platform_result -> each platform result`,
`shared_run_binding -> S`, and
`evidence_catalog -> each selected platform catalog in its phase`. Before any
child, `S`, `A`, both descriptors, the selected capsule, and all eleven
applicable static targets must emit exact PASS. Before a case
is accepted, both candidate and final validations for its completed fixture,
binary manifest, and evidence must emit exact PASS. Each platform catalog,
result, and archive is validated before its marker; each signed platform
admission validates after its complete gate exit and before aggregate import;
the signed scratch-destruction receipt validates after imported replay; the
final aggregate catalog validates only after both admissions, expectations,
archives, and that receipt pass; and terminal package admission validates only
after aggregate exit.
A missing invocation, target/hash/path substitution, nonexact
stdout/stderr/status, or validator source/runtime mismatch is NO-GO.

The global static-manifest union has exactly twelve
unsigned-byte-role-sorted, role-unique entries with keys `role,path,sha256`;
its exact role set is
`assertions,b27_admission,clean_admission,darwin_fixture_template,
evidence_runner,execution_capsule_darwin,execution_capsule_linux,
generated_migration_failpoints,operation_matrix,qemu_inputs,schema,
tool_transition`. Each platform descriptor has exactly the ten common roles
plus its selected capsule, hence eleven applicable static targets. Every role
has the exact section-12 domain/filename. Across both descriptors, `cases`
has exactly S2-AC-01..17 in registry order and each has
keys exactly
`case_id,platform,global_sequence,platform_sequence,command,timeout_seconds,
evidence_path,fixture_manifest_path,binary_artifact_manifest_path,
required_fixture_roles,required_binary_roles,child_scratch_profile,
child_data_fds,host_control_oracle_binding`. ID, platform, sequences, command,
timeout, and evidence path
equal the exact partition/registry values except that each registry
`evidence_path` is a logical template containing exactly one literal
`<package_run_id>` token and the descriptor replaces exactly that token with
its own run ID. No other template expansion is legal; the platform and case
suffix must already equal the registry record. The two sequence fields are
derived, not stored in the registry:
`global_sequence = 1 + the zero-based index of the case in registry.cases`
and
`platform_sequence = 1 + the zero-based index in registry.cases filtered by
case.platform`. Descriptors store both, and validators recompute both from
registry order.
Fixture and binary paths are respectively exact
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/qa/stage2/runs/<package_run_id>/platforms/<platform>/manifests/<case-id>/stage2-fixture-bundle-v1.json`
and the sibling `stage2-binary-artifacts-v1.json`, with every notation token
replaced by the descriptor's exact run/platform/case values. Required-role arrays are
nonempty, respectively bounded at 512 and 512, unsigned-byte sorted, unique,
and use the role grammar below. They freeze the exact allowed entry-role set
before execution even when a generated artifact hash is not available until
the case closes. Scratch/data records obey the exact payload-capability
contract above. Canonical `stage2-host-control-oracle-case-binding-v1` has
keys exactly
`required,fd,role,policy_sha256,scenario_plan_sha256,bundle_byte_cap`.
Only S2-AC-01/Linux and S2-AC-17/Darwin have a nonnull object: required is
true, FD is `74`, role is `host_control_oracle_bundle`, the two digests equal
the selected T policy/plan, and the cap is `16777216`; every other case stores
JSON null. The corresponding `required_fixture_roles` array contains exactly
one oracle bundle role—`ac01/host_control_oracle_bundle` or
`ac17/host_control_oracle_bundle`—and no other case's fixture-role array may
contain either role. Neither platform descriptor contains an evidence, platform
catalog/result, archive, expectation, platform admission, scratch receipt,
aggregate-catalog, package admission, or final-result hash.

The `qemu_inputs` static role is exactly canonical
`stage2-ac13-qemu-inputs-v1` at
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/implementation/fixtures/stage2-ac13-qemu-inputs-v1.json`.
Its key order and nested artifact/dependency schemas are exactly section 6.1.
Before spawn, only the `qemu_inputs` validator targets these reopened static
bytes. It independently reruns the host runtime and guest system-`flock`
loader/dependency derivations, networkless image rebuild/extraction, v2 launch
config, QMP-plan, expected runtime-envelope, nested role/hash, and exact
`R+I+T+16 <= 512` preflight checks and requires the input hash to equal the
descriptor static role. It neither opens nor predicts the absent completed
binary manifest. After child exit, `binary_artifacts` targets only the
completed manifest and then requires its isolation input hash to equal that
same static role. A phase substitution or generated-output dependency in
preflight refuses.

Every persisted path is printable ASCII and 1..1024 bytes. Every
`repository_path`, `host_path`, or `evidence_blob` locator is 1..1024 bytes;
`guest_image_path` is 1..1153 bytes including its image-role prefix and colon.
No path or locator has a backslash, NUL, control, glob, percent-encoded
separator, or component over 255 bytes. A repository path is slash-separated
and relative with no empty, `.` or `..` component. The one exact selected
logical
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/qa/stage2/runs/<package_run_id>/platforms/<platform>`
prefix is stripped and resolved beneath that platform's output FD 4; every
other repository path is resolved beneath immutable execution FD 3. Both routes
lstat/open/fstat-verify every component and refuse aliasing between roots. An
absolute host path is normalized and receives the same path/descriptor checks
before spawn and after child closure on its original platform, but is
data/provenance only; executable,
import, native-addon, compiler, or non-system library use maps to its exact
capsule entry and never executes the host pathname. Imported Darwin bytes use
only `platform_export_object` transport bindings; nontransported host/guest
source leaves use only the signed-admission-bound source-receipt-set
authority. Linux
never applies local `host_path` semantics to either. Role is
1..128 bytes and
matches `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/-]{0,127}`.

Every `evidence_blob` producer uses one global protocol. For expected bytes
`B` of length `0..16,777,216` and `H=SHA-256(B)`, the only names are final
`blobs/H` and candidate `blobs/.H.tmp`; publication is serialized so at most
one candidate exists. Before its first create the live platform coordinator
records `H`, expected length, producer/case/role, and later every created
device/inode. A nested root recovery may instead derive that same authority
only from its reopened exact external intent or destruction journal. No
unrecorded or merely hash-shaped name is owned evidence.

Creation uses the retained blob-directory description, current UID/GID,
`umask 0177`, requested mode `0600`, and
`O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`. The producer writes only an exact prefix of `B`,
completes it, file-fsyncs, closes the writable description, reopens read-only,
and requires ordinary-file type, exact owner/mode/device/inode/size/bytes/hash,
and link count one. It then makes a same-filesystem no-replace hard link at
the final name, parent-fsyncs, unlinks the candidate, parent-fsyncs again, and
reopens the final read-only with the recorded inode, exact bytes/hash, mode
`0600`, and link count one. Each create, write completion, file fsync,
read-only validation, link, first parent fsync, unlink, second parent fsync,
and final validation is a distinct failure boundary.

Recovery admits exactly four name states:

1. neither name exists;
2. only one ordinary current-owned mode-`0600`, link-count-one candidate with
   size at most the expected length and bytes equal to that exact prefix;
3. candidate and final are ordinary current-owned mode-`0600` names for the
   same recorded device/inode, both report link count two, and contain the
   complete exact `B` and hash `H`; or
4. only the ordinary current-owned mode-`0600`, link-count-one exact final
   exists.

State 1 restarts creation. State 2 unlinks the candidate by its recorded
identity and restarts. State 3 file-fsyncs the shared inode, parent-fsyncs,
unlinks only the candidate, and proceeds. State 4 proceeds. After every state
2/3 reconciliation—and conservatively in states 1/4 before accepting or
creating a final—the producer performs an unconditional blob-parent fsync;
this is a distinct restart-observable operation even when the candidate was
already absent. It then requires the state-4 final by a fresh
`lstat`/read-only-open/`fstat`/byte/hash check. A different-inode pair, third
link, oversize or nonprefix candidate, unsafe metadata, symlink, unexpected
name, byte/hash mismatch, or final not registered to this package/root
authority preserves and refuses. Reuse for a second role is allowed only for
that already recorded exact state-4 final. Failure cleanup removes only
recorded candidate/final identities created by the package and fsyncs the
parent; it never accepts or deletes a preflight-existing or orphan blob.

`fixture_sha256` hashes a `stage2-fixture-bundle-v1` manifest with keys exactly
`domain,case_id,entries`; domain is exactly `stage2-fixture-bundle-v1` and
case ID matches the containing case. `entries` has 1..512 role-unique entries
in the exact order of the descriptor's `required_fixture_roles`, with keys
exactly
`role,locator_kind,locator,sha256,packaging_scope`. Role matches
`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/-]{0,127}`. `locator_kind` is exactly
`repository_path|host_path|guest_image_path|evidence_blob`:

- `repository_path` is resolved beneath the exact immutable `git_commit`
  capsule root;
- `host_path` is a canonical absolute nonsymlink file that is
  lstat/open/fstat/hash-verified before child spawn and again before evidence;
  if its bytes are ever executed or loaded, that action uses only the
  one-to-one immutable capsule copy;
- `guest_image_path` is `<image-role>:/<canonical-absolute-guest-path>`,
  totals at most 1153 bytes, and is independently
  reopened through the descriptor-bound read-only image extractor against the
  one same-manifest image role before launch;
- `evidence_blob` is the canonical repository-relative
  `docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/qa/stage2/runs/<package_run_id>/platforms/<platform>/blobs/<sha256>`
  final from the global protocol above, durably completed before evidence and
  reopened as an ordinary current-owned mode-`0600`, link-count-one file whose
  content hash equals both basename and entry hash.

`packaging_scope` is exactly `production|evidence_only` and denotes authority,
not mere physical colocation. Entry roles equal the descriptor array exactly,
so omitted, extra, duplicate, reordered, orphan, or unreviewed fixtures fail.
The bundle includes every checked-in or generated case fixture, all applicable
admission/tool/Darwin-expanded/operation manifests, destruction receipts, and
every nested negative fixture. No unresolved generated label or
post-destruction guest path is a legal locator.

`schema_manifest_sha256` hashes
`stage2-s28-schema-manifest-v1`. Its top-level insertion order is exactly
`contract_version,source_commit,sqlite_version,canonicalizer,runtime,
verification_inputs,canonicalization,canonical_descriptor_sha256,
migration_ledger_sha256,object_counts,critical_relations,migrations`, with the
exact audited S27 nested key order/types unless changed below.
`contract_version` is exactly
`youtube-item-recovery-stage2-s28-schema-v1`; `source_commit` equals the
shared binding and both platform descriptors' common commit. `canonicalizer` keeps keys
`path,sha256,command`; its path is exactly
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/implementation/fixtures/verify-stage2-s28-schema-manifest.mjs`,
its SHA hashes those bytes and equals the descriptor
`s28_schema_manifest` validator hash, and command is exactly
`node --no-warnings --experimental-strip-types docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/implementation/fixtures/verify-stage2-s28-schema-manifest.mjs`.
That `canonicalizer.command` value is the canonical display/provenance string
retained by the S27 manifest schema; it grants no ambient executable-resolution
authority. Every actual S28 canonicalizer/validator invocation uses the
descriptor's shell-free absolute Node runtime, reviewed flags, and validator
path required above.

`runtime` and `verification_inputs` retain the S27 schema/formulas but every
scalar, list, tree/executable/shared-object digest, resolved entry, launch
environment, source-commit blob, runtime capability, and migration input is
freshly recomputed at the descriptor commit. `canonicalization` retains the
S27 structure/formulas with version exactly
`stage2-s28-schema-canonical-v1`. `migrations` has exactly the S27 29-record
array byte-for-byte followed by
`{name:"028_youtube_browser_transcript.sql",sha256:<descriptor migration
sha256>}` and admits no 029/030 file.
`migration_ledger_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify(migrations)`.

The verifier builds the complete canonical descriptor from the actual
normalized S28 `sqlite_master`, relation envelopes, and 30-row ledger.
`canonical_descriptor_sha256` hashes exact no-LF `JSON.stringify(descriptor)`;
`object_counts` keeps keys `tables,indexes,triggers,views` and freshly counts
that same master array. `critical_relations` has exactly these 26
unsigned-byte-ordered keys:
`_migrations,capture_artifacts,capture_policy_decisions,chunks,chunks_rowid,
chunks_vec,content_processing_holds,embedding_jobs,enrichment_jobs,
extension_capture_requests,
item_artifact_cleanup_jobs,item_artifact_write_operations,
item_artifact_write_requests,item_body_revision_events,
item_delete_commands,item_delete_permits,
item_deletion_request_tombstones,item_deletion_requests,
item_request_tombstones,items,note_index_jobs,
transcript_attempts,transcript_jobs,
transcript_recovery_apply_receipts,transcript_segments,transcript_sources`.
This is the S27 14 plus the exact twelve new relations defined in section 7:
eleven tables and the zero-row `item_delete_commands` view.
Each value keeps keys `sha256,columns,foreign_keys,indexes,triggers`; SHA
hashes the actual no-LF relation-envelope JSON and counts equal the actual
arrays. All 14 old summaries are recomputed from S28 bytes, not inherited.
The S28-minus-S27 table-name set equals exactly the eleven new table names,
the S28-minus-S27 view-name set equals exactly
`item_delete_commands`, and both reverse differences are empty.

Two independent construction paths—fresh database plus exact 001..028, and
an independently verified S27 database plus exact 028—must each pass
`quick_check`, have zero FK violations and the exact 30-row ledger, and
produce byte-identical full descriptors, object counts, 26 summaries, and
one-LF manifest bytes. The descriptor `schema` entry, every case evidence
field, and both paths equal one hash. Carry-forward assumptions, relation
omission/addition/reorder, count drift, or construction-path drift fails.

`binary_artifact_sha256` hashes `stage2-binary-artifacts-v1`, with top-level
keys exactly `domain,environment,artifacts` and domain exactly
`stage2-binary-artifacts-v1`.
`environment` has keys exactly
`platform,os_release,kernel_release,filesystem_type,euid,egid,identities,
compiler,isolation`. Platform is `linux|darwin`;
the next three strings are respectively 1..256, 1..256, and 1..64 printable
ASCII bytes. EUID/EGID are safe integers. `identities` has 1..8 entries
bytewise sorted by unique `name`; each has keys `name,uid,gid`, name matches
`[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`, and IDs are safe integers.

`compiler` is null or has keys exactly
`executable_path,executable_role,executable_sha256,version,flags,
output_role,output_sha256,self_test_role,self_test_sha256`.
Path is canonical absolute/nonsymlink; version is 1..256 printable ASCII;
flags is an ordered array of 0..64 strings each 0..256 bytes. The executable,
output, and self-test role/hash pairs each equal exactly one artifact and vice
versa. AC17 roles are exactly
`ac17/flock_adapter/compiler_executable`,
`ac17/flock_adapter/output`, and `ac17/flock_adapter/self_test`; its adapter
source is the separate required role `ac17/flock_adapter/source`.

`isolation` is null except AC13, where it has keys exactly
`profile,qemu_inputs_role,qemu_inputs_sha256,launcher_role,launcher_sha256,
runtime_role,runtime_sha256,runtime_dependency_roles,base_image_role,
base_image_sha256,firmware_role,firmware_sha256,image_build_manifest_role,
image_build_manifest_sha256,image_build_input_roles,system_flock_role,
system_flock_sha256,
expected_runtime_envelope_role,expected_runtime_envelope_sha256,
launch_config_role,launch_config_sha256,qmp_transcript_role,
qmp_transcript_sha256,serial_transcript_role,serial_transcript_sha256,
diagnostic_stderr_role,diagnostic_stderr_sha256,
observed_runtime_envelope_role,
observed_runtime_envelope_sha256,destruction_receipt_role,
destruction_receipt_sha256,root_runtime_authority_role,
root_runtime_authority_sha256,root_destruction_journal_role,
root_destruction_journal_sha256,instance_id,writable_root_id`. Profile is exactly
`stage2-ac13-qemu-tcg-vm-v2`; `qemu_inputs_role` is
`ac13/qemu_inputs`, its hash equals the descriptor static `qemu_inputs` hash,
and it maps to that same manifest as one binary artifact. Remaining scalar
role/hash pairs are respectively exact
`ac13/launcher`, `ac13/qemu_runtime`, `ac13/base_image`, `ac13/firmware`,
`ac13/image_build_manifest`, `ac13/system_flock`,
`ac13/runtime_envelope_expected`, `ac13/launch_config`,
`ac13/qmp_transcript`, `ac13/serial_transcript`,
`ac13/diagnostic_stderr`, `ac13/runtime_envelope_observed`,
`ac13/root_destruction_receipt`, `ac13/root_runtime_authority`, and
`ac13/root_destruction_journal`, each mapping one-to-one to an artifact.
`runtime_dependency_roles` is the exact 1..256 role array from `qemu_inputs`;
every role is `ac13/runtime_dependency/<three-decimal-index>` and maps
one-to-one to the reopened dependency artifact. `image_build_input_roles` is
the exact 1..128 role array from the nested image-build manifest; every role
is `ac13/image_build_input/<three-decimal-index>` and maps one-to-one to the
reopened build input. `instance_id` is a lowercase RFC4122 UUID;
`writable_root_id` is a 64-lowercase-hex content-free identifier. No launch
config, input/image-build manifest, expected/observed envelope, raw transcript,
root authority, destruction journal, compiler record, or receipt contains the encompassing
binary-manifest hash.

`artifacts` has 1..512 role-unique entries in the exact descriptor
`required_binary_roles` order, using the fixture-entry key schema and locator
rules. Environment role/hash references, every transition `source.role`, and
every artifact entry are one-to-one; an orphan, duplicate, wrong hash/scope,
or extra role fails. For AC13 let `R`, `I`, and `T` be respectively the exact
runtime-dependency, image-build-input, and production tool-source counts.
Its required role set is exactly the 16 scalar isolation roles, all `R`
runtime dependencies, all `I` image-build inputs, and all `T` production tool
sources, so both required-role and artifact lengths equal exactly
`R+I+T+16`. The independent bounds `R<=256`, `I<=128`, and `T<=64` imply a
maximum of 464 and the explicit joint check requires `R+I+T+16 <= 512`.
It requires guest Linux
EUID zero, exact root/`brain` identities, null compiler, and nonnull isolation.
Its required fixture roles include exact role `ac13/root_intent` for the
canonical root-intent evidence blob.
AC17 requires Darwin, its declared identity, null isolation, nonnull compiler,
the four exact adapter/compiler roles, every private tool source, and its root
destruction journal and receipt; its required fixture roles include the template,
expanded, cleanup, provisioning-intent, and root-intent manifests. Its
five manifest roles are exactly `ac17/template`, `ac17/expanded_manifest`,
`ac17/cleanup_manifest`, `ac17/provisioning_intent`, and
`ac17/root_intent`.
Its
destruction receipt domain is exactly
`stage2-ac17-root-destruction-receipt-v2`. VM/launcher and Darwin adapter
artifacts are
`evidence_only`; no evidence-only artifact has production authority.
For AC17, `compiler.output_sha256` equals the Darwin descriptor
`ac17_adapter_prebuild.output.sha256`, the immutable capsule output entry, and
artifact `ac17/flock_adapter/output`; the same four-way equality applies to
source, compiler, and self-test roles where applicable. The runtime compiler
writes only FD-6 noexec scratch, the completed comparison bytes must hash
equal to that prebuilt output, and neither those bytes nor any writable alias
is loaded, mapped executable, or executed. The self-test and adapter execution
use only immutable FD-3 capsule entries. Source/compiler/version/flag/
environment drift, nondeterministic output, equality/`+1`, scratch execution
or load, capsule substitution, and role/hash mismatch all fail before AC17
acceptance.

For each selected outer invocation the platform coordinator concurrently
captures exact stdout and stderr, each bounded at 16,777,216 bytes, and
retains both through platform export. Acceptance requires outer exit zero,
EOF, zero descendants/open pipes, one exact final case marker, and reopened
final-validated evidence. It recomputes `stage2-command-output-v1` and invokes
the immutable selected-platform evidence-runner `verifier` with exact argv
`[...node_prefix_p,verifier_path,"--execution-root-fd","3",
"--output-root-fd","4","--platform-descriptor-fd","5",
"--shared-binding-fd","6","--aggregation-binding-fd","7",
"--host-attestation-trust-sha256",Ht,
"--host-attestation-set-sha256",Hat,
"--case",caseId,"--evidence-fd","12","--evidence-path",evidencePath,
"--evidence-sha256",evidenceSha256,"--outer-stdout-fd","13",
"--outer-stderr-fd","14"]`.
The writable platform-output description never enters this child: FD 4 is a
fresh kernel-read-only `stage2-validator-output-view-v1` containing exactly
the paused case's validated evidence/fixture/binary/blob closure, with the
same mount/inventory/EROFS/source-revalidation contract frozen above.
FD 12 is the pinned evidence; FDs 13/14 are private replay reads. Paths are
provenance only. Environment is empty, cwd is capsule root, stdin is
`/dev/null`, and only stdio plus FDs 3/4/5/6/7/12/13/14 survive.

The coordinator writes each retained stream exactly once concurrently and
closes its writer; early close, partial/extra write, or missing EOF fails. The
verifier has an exact 300-second monotonic deadline through process-group/
descendant exit and stdout/stderr EOF. Verifier stdout/stderr caps are each
4,096 bytes; equality passes and `+1` fails. Failure cleanup is at most 2,000
milliseconds graceful plus 5,000 milliseconds forced kill/drain and never
restores PASS. Success requires every replay byte consumed, zero descendants/
open pipes, exit zero, empty stderr, and exact one-line stdout
`stage2-case-evidence-verifier-v1:<case_id>:PASS:<output_sha256>:
<evidence_sha256>\n`. AC01 covers every argv/FD/order/hash/path/replay cap,
truncation/trailing/early-EOF, timeout, signal/nonzero, wrong stdout/stderr,
descendant, and held-pipe negative.

Each canonical `stage2-platform-evidence-catalog-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,shared_binding,aggregation_binding,platform,
platform_descriptor,execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,
platform_coordinator_sha256,package_lock_path,
host_control_oracle_bundle_sha256,git_commit,migration,contract,
registry,failpoint_registry_sha256,static_manifests,cases`. Binding and
descriptor records have exact `path,sha256`; all fields equal reopened
pre-run/context bytes. Cases are exactly that platform partition in registry
order, each with keys
`case_id,platform,evidence_path,evidence_sha256,fixture_manifest_path,
fixture_sha256,binary_artifact_manifest_path,binary_artifact_sha256,
schema_manifest_sha256,generated_migration_failpoints_sha256,
assertion_manifest_sha256,evidence_runner_sha256,operation_matrix_sha256,
command,timeout_seconds,output_sha256,run_binding_sha256,result_marker,
outer_stdout_sha256,outer_stderr_sha256`. Every value is recomputed from
reopened finals and retained streams. The catalog has no self/result/archive
hash. Its oracle-bundle hash equals the platform context's
`host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity.sha256`, the one
oracle-bearing case evidence field, and that case's required fixture
evidence-blob entry; no child-reported value supplies it.

Canonical `stage2-platform-result-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,
execution_capsule_manifest_sha256,platform_context_sha256,package_lock_path,
host_control_oracle_bundle_sha256,git_commit,platform_catalog_path,
platform_catalog_sha256,case_count,case_ids,
