case_result_set_sha256,catalog_output_set_sha256,freshness_response_sha256,
status`. Status is `ready_for_external_gate`.
`freshness_response_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-platform-freshness-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF compact JSON with
keys `challenge,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform_context_sha256,case_result_set_sha256`.
Every value comes from `S`, `A`, the live context, or reopened catalog.
The oracle-bundle hash cross-equals the live platform context's
`host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity.sha256` and catalog and
is deliberately excluded from the freshness preimage because
`platform_context_sha256` plus `case_result_set_sha256` already bind it.

`case_result_set_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-platform-case-result-set-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` of case records in descriptor order. Each record has keys
exactly
`case_id,evidence_sha256,fixture_sha256,binary_artifact_sha256,
output_sha256,run_binding_sha256,result_marker,outer_stdout_sha256,
outer_stderr_sha256`.

`catalog_output_set_sha256` is SHA-256 over exact ASCII
`stage2-platform-catalog-output-set-v1`, one `0x00`, and exact no-LF
`JSON.stringify` of records in unsigned-byte `logical_path` order. Each
record has keys exactly
`logical_path,role,sha256,size,device,inode,mode,link_count`. The set is
exactly the `3*n+B` persistent case-triple/blob finals referenced by the
platform catalog. It excludes context/lock, catalog, result, raw replay
streams, archive, expectation, admission, and aggregate artifacts, preventing a
back-edge.

Platform catalog and result each use candidate validation, no-replace
publication, final validation, and exact fixed paths. The archive includes
their finals and all transport closure bytes but no lock or candidate. It is
streamed while the lock remains. An exact external ACK permits removal/fsync
of the selected lock and the platform marker defined above; any later
status/EOF/descendant/lock mismatch prevents an expectation. A platform
marker, catalog, result, archive, or ACK alone is never package completion.

The aggregate coordinator receives archive bytes only after independently
pinned expectation records and signed platform admissions validate. It
validates signatures, launcher/gate/phase/post-exit facts, framing, hashes,
partition, `S`, `A`, `D_L`, `D_D`, capsule manifests, platform
contexts/catalogs/results, fixed finals, evidence blobs, and raw replay
streams. It reruns every
platform-independent fixture/binary/evidence/catalog/result validator and
the exact outer verifier over each imported case; within fixture/binary
import mode, host/guest leaf byte checks are the explicit platform-dependent
exception and consume only the immutable source receipts whose digest is
bound by the signed post-exit platform admission, while all structural/
downstream checks rerun. For AC17, verifier FD 5 is
the immutable Darwin descriptor `D_D`; for Linux cases it is `D_L`. Original
Darwin `host_path` records are validated only through the Darwin execution
receipt plus exact source-receipt-set digest, never by false Linux reopen.
For each oracle-bearing case it additionally invokes the imported
`host_control_oracle_bundle` validator over the exact transported
evidence-blob bytes and static plan/registry. Import mode revalidates canonical
bundle bytes, chronological event/scenario graph, assertion projection, and
the original protection identity/hash against the supplied expectation and
platform context. The aggregate coordinator and
`platform_gate_admission` validator—not this imported child—establish the
signed-admission binding. Import mode does not claim that the imported blob
still has the original platform's memfd or vnode protection, nor rerun a
completed host-kernel observation.

Canonical `stage2-aggregate-catalog-v1` has keys exactly
`domain,package_run_id,shared_binding,aggregation_binding,git_commit,
migration,contract,registry,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
host_attestation_set_sha256,launcher_trust_sha256,platforms,
scratch_destruction_receipt_path,scratch_destruction_receipt_sha256,cases`.
`host_attestation_trust_sha256` alone cross-equals immutable capsule T;
`host_attestation_set_sha256` is independently recomputed from both signed
attestations and cross-equals the transitive `Hat` graph. Launcher-trust and
scratch-receipt fields cross-equal both verified controller requests/
signatures and the exact durable signed receipt final;
the aggregate catalog validator claims no independent external pin;
`scratch_destruction_receipt_path` is the exact run-scoped aggregate logical
path to
`stage2-aggregate-scratch-destruction-receipt.<receipt_sha256>.json`.
`platforms` is exactly
Linux then Darwin and each record has keys
`platform,descriptor_sha256,capsule_manifest_sha256,expectation_path,
expectation_sha256,platform_gate_admission_path,
platform_gate_admission_sha256,gate_marker_sha256,archive_path,
archive_sha256,archive_size,platform_catalog_sha256,
platform_result_sha256,host_control_oracle_bundle_sha256,
case_count,case_ids`. `cases` is all 17 entries in
registry order. Each record has the exact platform-catalog case keys in their
existing order, followed only by `archive_sha256,expectation_sha256`;
`platform` already exists in the platform-catalog record and is not
duplicated. Every platform path names its exact content-addressed final under
the aggregate `exports` directory and cross-equals the imported final
identity/hash. The aggregate catalog has no self hash or marker.
Each platform oracle-bundle hash cross-equals its signed admission,
expectation, export header, platform catalog/result, imported platform
context's `host_control_oracle_bundle_file_identity.sha256`,
oracle-bearing case evidence, fixture entry, and transported blob; it does
not equal the context's file-identity object digest.

Only after both signed admissions, archives, expectations, platform
catalogs/results, all 17 case triples, replay verification, partition union,
durable signed scratch-destruction receipt, and exact aggregate-catalog
candidate/final validation pass does the coordinator remove/fsync its exact
aggregate lock and emit as its final stdout operation
`stage2-package-result-v2:PASS:<package_run_id>:<aggregation_binding_sha256>:<aggregate_catalog_sha256>\n`.
The line occurs once, is outside every case/run binding, and is only an
internal aggregate marker. No platform coordinator or payload may emit it.

Only after the aggregate process and its complete process tree exit, both
stdout/stderr reach EOF, stderr is empty, stdout is exactly the sole marker
with no post-marker byte, exit status is zero, descendants/open pipes are
zero, the aggregate lock is absent, and aggregate completion has been
observed before the aggregate deadline
does the same persistent Linux launcher construct the terminal signed
envelope with domain `stage2-package-admission-v1`. Its payload keys are
exactly
`package_run_id,challenge,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,host_attestation_trust_sha256,
host_attestation_set_sha256,launcher_trust_sha256,signer_platform,
launcher_context_sha256,
federation_launcher_sha256,linux_platform_gate_admission_sha256,
darwin_platform_gate_admission_sha256,
scratch_destruction_receipt_sha256,aggregate_catalog_sha256,
package_marker_sha256,aggregate_stdout_sha256,aggregate_stderr_sha256,
aggregate_exit_status,aggregate_stdout_eof,aggregate_stderr_eof,
descendant_count,open_pipe_count,aggregate_lock_removed,
aggregate_completion_before_deadline,status`. `signer_platform` is exactly
`linux`. Every hash cross-equals the validated inputs,
aggregate context/catalog/receipt, and retained streams. Both EOF/lock/
completion-before-deadline booleans are true, status is `PASS`, exit/counts
are zero, stderr is empty, and marker/stdout hashes cover the same exact
one-LF line. Before signing, the live Linux launcher directly reverifies both
host attestations against its retained independently provisioned T
description. Candidate and final child validators instead reopen immutable
capsule T, consume transitive `Ht,Hat`, and reverify both controller requests
and host signatures without claiming an independent child-local pin;
`signature_key_id` must equal the Linux host-attested launcher key and the
aggregate launcher-context key.

The exact compact signed envelope plus one LF is capped at 262,144 bytes.
Candidate/final paths are
`.stage2-package-admission.<package_run_id>.candidate` and
`stage2-package-admission.<package_admission_sha256>.json`. The launcher uses
the exclusive complete-write/fchmod-`0400`/file-fsync/read-only-reopen,
`package_admission` candidate validation, no-replace hard-link, both parent
fsyncs, candidate unlink, final reopen, and final validation protocol. The
candidate/final publication must complete within the separately enforced
`post_exit_admission_timeout_ms`; the payload does not attest its own
publication. A
candidate/final crash, forged/unsigned/wrong-key/replayed/cross-run receipt,
premature publication, marker-only success, exit/EOF/descendant/pipe/lock/
deadline mismatch, or post-validation replacement yields no accepted
package. The exact final `package_admission_sha256`, not the aggregate marker,
catalog, expectation, or platform admission alone, becomes the sole external
PASS authority only after the still-live Linux host supervisor repeats the
out-of-band-pin and final-file validation and releases that exact hash through
the original controller-read/supervisor-sole-write acceptance pipe frozen
above. The terminal package
admission is intentionally absent from the
aggregate catalog.

The graph is acyclic: independently pinned host roots precede the run;
fresh host-signed launcher commitments/attestations precede `S,D,A`; pre-run
bindings contain no platform output; each live oracle bundle is created only
after D/A and flows forward through activation/context, its one
oracle-bearing case evidence/fixture blob, platform catalog/result/export/
expectation, signed platform admission, and aggregate replay/catalog;
neither the bundle nor any derived assertion/output hash enters T/P/M/S/D/A
or its own policy/plan. Evidence contains no platform
catalog/result/archive/expectation/admission/aggregate hash; platform catalogs
contain no result/archive/expectation/admission; platform results contain the
catalog hash but no archive/expectation/admission; archives contain no
expectation/admission; expectations bind completed archives and pre-gate-exit
facts; signed platform admissions bind post-gate-exit facts; the signed
scratch receipt binds only prior admissions/context/ready/destruction facts;
the aggregate catalog binds prior admissions and scratch receipt but neither
its own hash nor marker; and the post-aggregate-exit package admission binds
the catalog/marker/exit facts but never enters an earlier artifact.


The common static `operation_matrix` role is

Its hash is SHA-256 over exact no-LF `JSON.stringify` of the coordinate array.
This submatrix exercises each phase-artifact publication boundary inside root

At every coordinate the nested root supervisor receives uncatchable

The two root-operation arrays are respectively the exact 76 AC13 and
77 AC17 section-6.1 root IDs. `ac13_root_coordinates` is the exact 152-element

and every value is exactly
`setup_replay|prejournal_fail_closed|journal_publication_repair|

the section-6.1 dispositions below. No separate oracle hash is needed because
the complete operation-matrix bytes are descriptor-hashed.

Every operation number is the 1-based position in that case's exact root
operation array. For each record, `after(candidate_file_fsync_operation)` is
immediately before candidate read-only validation; exact validator PASS is
required before `before(no_replace_link_operation)`.
`after(cleanup_parent_fsync_operation)` is immediately before final
validation; exact validator PASS is required before
`before(next_operation)`. No mutation occurs within either edge pair.
For every record, `recovered_state3_source_operation` equals its
`no_replace_link_operation`, `recovered_state4_source_operation` equals its
`cleanup_parent_fsync_operation`, and `recovered_final_validation_edge` is
exactly
`after_recovery_unconditional_parent_fsync_before_state4_accept_or_next_mutation`.
The recovered-state vector has two mandatory subruns: one begins from the
exact state-3 source and one from the exact state-4 source; each runs the
global recovery classifier through its unconditional blob-parent fsync, then
injects final-validator failure at that exact edge before state-4 acceptance
or any next mutation. Its disposition is the table's exact
`recovered_failure_disposition`, separate from the live
`failure_disposition`.
`validation_failure_vectors` is exactly
`candidate_readonly_validation_failure,fresh_final_validation_failure,
recovered_state3_or_state4_final_validation_failure` in that order. These
inject a validator failure over otherwise exact bytes and accept no evidence
or PASS; unsafe metadata or byte drift still preserves and refuses. They are
assertion vectors, not root coordinates or fixed runtime failpoint names.
For each record/vector pair, the exact assertion ID is
`<case_id>/root_blob_validation.<role-with-slash-replaced-by-dot>.<vector>`;
record order then vector order is authoritative. These IDs satisfy the global
assertion grammar; a recovered-state assertion passes only when both mandatory
subruns pass. They give the AC13 and AC17 assertion manifests exactly 12
and 18 corresponding IDs. Root-operation counts, root-coordinate formulas, and the fixed
145-failpoint count do not change.

The descriptor's `generated_migration_failpoints` role is
`stage2-generated-migration-failpoints-v1`, with keys exactly
`domain,migration_sha256,parser_path,parser_sha256,statement_count,names`.
Domain is exactly `stage2-generated-migration-failpoints-v1`; the parser path
is repository-relative; the manifest path is exactly
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/implementation/fixtures/stage2-generated-migration-failpoints-v1.json`;
count is a positive safe integer; and
`names` has exactly that many ordered unique strings
`migration_after_sql_statement_%03d` for `1..statement_count`. AC01
independently reruns the exact parser and requires byte-for-byte equality.

After exclusively publishing its platform context but before any acceptance
child, each platform coordinator performs one selected-partition preflight by
traversing only retained directory descriptions in unsigned-byte name order
without following links. For partition size `n`, its exact skeleton is
`manifests`, `blobs`, and `n` manifest case directories: `n+2` entries.
The fixed finals are one evidence file plus one fixture and one binary
manifest per case, then one platform catalog and one platform result:
`3*n+2` finals. Each final has at most its one exact current-run candidate,
so the fixed final/candidate-name bound is `6*n+4`.
`blobs` admits only 64-lowercase-hex content-addressed finals plus at most one
serialized current-run `.H.tmp` candidate. Because each case has at most 512
fixture and 512 binary roles, the blob final/candidate-name bound is
`1024*n+1`. One exact platform lock is the only other admitted name. No deeper
directory, symlink, socket, device, FIFO, unknown hard link, alternate
candidate, malformed prefix-bearing basename, or unmatched name is accepted.

With `B` distinct state-4 blob finals, exact success-state entry counts are
`4*n+5+B` while the lock remains and `4*n+4+B` after its durable removal.
Maximum enumeration including all legal candidate names is `1031*n+8`;
the next total, fixed-name, or blob-name entry refuses. Exact boundaries are:

| Platform | `n` | Fixed finals | Success while/after lock | Total pass/fail | Fixed names pass/fail | Blob names pass/fail |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Linux | 16 | 50 | `69+B_L` / `68+B_L` | 16,504 / 16,505 | 100 / 101 | 16,385 / 16,386 |
| Darwin | 1 | 5 | `9+B_D` / `8+B_D` | 1,039 / 1,040 | 10 / 11 | 1,025 / 1,026 |

`B_L` is in `0..16384`; `B_D` is in `0..1024`. Preflight requires exactly
the selected skeleton plus its one lock and zero fixed output/blob names.
Every fixed evidence, fixture, binary, platform-catalog, platform-result,
current-run candidate, and blob path must be absent. A preexisting output is
never trusted or deleted, even if byte-identical. The platform coordinator
positionally hashes FDs 5/6/7, hashes contract, registry, migration, its own
source, every validator, and every applicable static manifest through
immutable FD 3; rescans the selected capsule/system-loader closure; validates
the shared binding, aggregation binding, selected platform descriptor,
execution capsule, and all applicable static roles through pinned target FDs;
and requires every graph, partition, role set, command, path, hash, key order,
bound, FD route, and cross-hash to close exactly.

Only after that preflight does the platform coordinator invoke exactly its
partition once in registry order—Linux AC01..AC16 or Darwin AC17—with fresh
FD-8/FD-9 authority per case. It retains an open description of its exact lock
through every case, dynamic validation, catalog/result validation, final
referenced-output recheck, archive stream, and external ACK. A pristine
preflight failure removes/fsyncs only its exact lock. A later failure may
remove only candidate/final/blob inodes whose identities that platform run
recorded as created, fsyncs every affected parent, and removes its lock only
after the scanner proves the selected skeleton plus lock and zero generated
output. Uncertain ownership or cleanup retains the lock and fails closed.
A crash therefore leaves its never-reused run-scoped lock and/or partial
output quarantined and permanently non-acceptable; that same run ID is never
restarted or cleaned automatically. A fresh run provisions a distinct absent
root under a new run ID and is neither blocked nor satisfied by the abandoned
root. Destructive reclamation of abandoned roots remains separately reviewed
and is not an acceptance prerequisite.

The immutable gate separately scans only its selected transfer FD-8 root.
Its exact skeleton is `archives`, `expectations`, and `admissions`; admitted
generated names are one archive final and its at-most-one exact candidate, one
expectation final and its at-most-one exact candidate, one signed
platform-admission final and its at-most-one exact candidate, and the one gate
lock. Phase ordering makes maximum enumeration seven names; the eighth
refuses. Exact success is six names while the gate lock remains, five after
durable lock removal but before admission publication, and six after the
signed admission final replaces its candidate. Preflight accepts exactly the
three freshly provisioned empty skeleton directories plus the gate lock and
no archive/expectation/admission name. A preexisting candidate/final, third
object of a class, malformed prefix-bearing name, symlink, or foreign inode is
never accepted or removed.

The aggregate coordinator and post-exit launcher separately scan only the
aggregate FD-4 root under the same closed grammar. Admitted names are one
`exports` directory; exact Linux and Darwin archive, expectation, and signed
platform-admission finals; one signed scratch-destruction-receipt final; one
aggregate-catalog final; one terminal signed package-admission final; each
final's at-most-one exact candidate; and one aggregate lock. Phase ordering
makes maximum enumeration eleven names; the twelfth refuses. Candidate
accumulation across classes is invalid: a phase cannot advance until its one
candidate is unlinked and the second parent fsync completes, so any
simultaneous candidates from different classes refuse even below the numeric
cap. Exact
success is ten names while the lock remains, nine after removal but before
package admission publication, and ten after the package-admission final
replaces its candidate.
No case manifest, evidence file, or evidence blob is copied into the aggregate
tree: those bytes remain inside the two validated archive finals and are
reopened through archive-object FDs. A preexisting candidate/final or third
archive is never accepted or removed. Aggregate failure removes only exact
run-owned identities and retains the lock whenever cleanup is uncertain.

It also covers direct

Each negative

AC01 also constructs S28 through both exact section-12 paths and reruns the
`s28_schema_manifest` validator over each; mutates every top-level manifest
field, migration record, object count, critical-relation membership/order,
relation digest/count, canonical descriptor digest, ledger digest, runtime
input, and canonicalizer binding one at a time; and requires every mutation
to fail. It then uses descriptor-bound synthetic artifacts to exercise
positive and one-at-a-time negative `fixture_bundle`, `binary_artifacts`,
`case_evidence`, platform `evidence_catalog`, `platform_result`,
`platform_export`, `platform_gate_admission`,
`aggregate_scratch_destruction`, `aggregate_catalog`, and
`package_admission` validation, including role-set, locator, packaging-scope,
generated-artifact, result-marker, signature/trust, run-binding, and cross-
case/platform substitutions. Its Darwin, export, gate/admission, aggregate
catalog/scratch-receipt, and package-admission vectors are synthetic only:
AC01 never claims that its Linux child ran AC17, never opens the actual Darwin
archive/expectation/admission, and never validates or binds an actual
aggregate catalog, package marker, or terminal admission. Actual completion
remains the external signed two-platform federation gate.

After each platform's selected `case_evidence` validators have passed and all
of its outer invocations have been accepted, that platform coordinator,
outside every acceptance case and run binding, publishes and validates its
actual catalog and result, rechecks the complete referenced output set, and
streams its archive under the lock. Only the external gate may create its
expectation after ACK/marker/EOF/exit/descendant/lock checks. Only after both
post-exit signed admissions, expectations, and archives independently validate
may the Linux aggregate coordinator complete replay, receive/publish the
signed scratch receipt, publish the actual aggregate catalog, and emit its
nonterminal package marker. Only the persistent Linux launcher may publish the
terminal signed package admission after aggregate exit. These completion
gates are not AC01 assertions or outputs. Any failure invalidates the package
even when every individual case command exited zero.

The common static assertions role is canonical
The exact assertion-manifest source path is
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/implementation/
fixtures/stage2-assertion-manifest-v1.json`; its capsule path is
`implementation/fixtures/stage2-assertion-manifest-v1.json`. Canonical
`stage2-assertion-manifest-v1` has keys exactly `domain,cases`; domain is
exact. `cases` has exactly S2-AC-01 through S2-AC-17 in registry order. Each
value is an array of `1..10000` records with keys exactly
`assertion_id,source`, ordered by unsigned bytes of `assertion_id`.
Assertion IDs are globally unique, match
`^S2-AC-[0-9]{2}/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`, and have the containing case
prefix. `source` is exactly
`child_event|host_control_oracle_bundle`. Only S2-AC-01 and S2-AC-17 may
contain oracle-sourced records; each contains a nonempty oracle subset whose
ordered ID projection byte-equals the disjoint scenario-plan assertion-ID
union for its platform. Every other record is child-event sourced, and every
case has a nonempty child-event subset. `assertion_count` is the case-array
length; `assertion_ids_sha256` hashes exact no-LF `JSON.stringify` of the
array's `assertion_id` projection, not the record array. Missing, extra,
duplicate, reordered, unknown-source, wrong-case, or plan-divergent records
make the static assertion-manifest validator fail.

Before spawning the S2-AC-01 or S2-AC-17 payload, the wrapper independently
revalidates FD 74's complete file identity and bytes against the platform
context and separately cross-equals role/policy/plan/cap against the
descriptor binding, reads
the exact canonical one-LF bundle bytes within `16777216`, and invokes the
selected descriptor's `host_control_oracle_bundle` validator. It gives that
validator only the standard live-platform authority envelope and a fresh
read-only duplicate remapped to target FD 12, with exact arguments
`--target-role host_control_oracle_bundle --target-fd 12 --target
host-control-oracle-bundle/<platform>/<package_run_id> --target-sha256
<bundle_sha256>`; the target string is printable-ASCII provenance only.
Success requires exit zero, empty stderr, the exact role PASS line, target
consumption through EOF, and post-validation unchanged file identity and
bytes. The wrapper then publishes those same bytes through the global
four-state evidence-blob protocol and adds exactly one descriptor-required
fixture entry: role `ac01/host_control_oracle_bundle` for S2-AC-01 or
`ac17/host_control_oracle_bundle` for S2-AC-17, locator kind
`evidence_blob`, locator
`docs/feature-council/youtube-item-recovery-implementation/qa/stage2/runs/<package_run_id>/platforms/<platform>/blobs/<bundle_sha256>`,
`sha256` equal to the exact bundle hash, and `packaging_scope` exactly
`evidence_only`. No other case or role may reference the bundle.
The live protected description is not itself persisted or transported.

The wrapper derives the oracle-observed ID set only from the validated static
scenario plan plus the validated bundle's exact ordered scenario results. It
requires every planned positive scenario to be `PASS`, every planned
negative scenario to be `EXPECTED_REFUSAL`, all expected/observed terminals
equal, every forbidden-effect count zero, and the derived ID projection to
equal exactly the manifest's oracle-sourced subset. An ID is derived only
when its complete plan `assertion_rules` predicate set recomputes true over
the validated event range; scenario status or exit alone derives no ID. It
then closes FD 74,
every validator duplicate, and every bundle description before payload spawn
and verifies `F_GETFD(74)` returns `EBADF`. The payload never receives bundle
bytes, an observer channel, an oracle assertion list, or any bundle-derived
authority.

The frozen wrapper—not the child command or test module—is the sole emitter of a
`stage2-assertion-result-v1` or `stage2-case-result-v1` line. It rejects any
child stdout or stderr line beginning `stage2-platform-result-v1:` or
`stage2-package-result-v2:`; only a platform coordinator may emit its platform
marker and only the aggregate coordinator may emit the package marker.

From child spawn through child/process-tree exit and EOF on stdout, stderr,
and the structured-event channel, the wrapper enforces the registry timeout
with a monotonic clock while draining all three channels concurrently. Exact
caps are 16,777,216 bytes for final stdout, 16,777,216 bytes for child stderr,
8,388,608 event bytes, 10,000 terminal events, and 4,096 bytes per event. The
structured-event channel is a dedicated inherited binary pipe, never stdout or
stderr. Each event frame is a four-byte unsigned big-endian payload length
`N`, followed by exactly `N` bytes. `N` is in `1..4096`; the 4,096-byte limit
applies to the payload, while the 8,388,608-byte total counts every four-byte
prefix plus payload. A payload is exact compact UTF-8 JSON with no BOM or LF,
keys exactly `case_id,assertion_id,status` in that order, no extra key, and a
status exactly `PASS`, `SKIP`, `TODO`, `CANCELLED`, or `FAIL`. Zero-length,
oversize, invalid UTF-8/JSON, wrong-key/order, unknown-status, truncated-frame,
or trailing bytes are protocol errors. EOF is valid only on a frame boundary.

Before spawn the wrapper reserves the invariant exact assertion/result
protocol length from the frozen assertion IDs, manifest-derived count/hash,
fixed grammar, and the fixed-width 64-hex run-binding slot; it does not need or
invent a run-binding value at that point. It additionally reserves a
conditional one-byte stdout separator: exactly one `0x0a` is inserted before
the first assertion line iff child stdout is nonempty and its last byte is not
`0x0a`. After child status zero, complete three-channel EOF, zero surviving
descendants, the wrapper finalizes the fixture and binary manifests, invokes
their descriptor-bound validators over the reopened finalized bytes, requires
exact PASS, constructs the exact run binding, and only then materializes the
protocol bytes. Final stdout is exact child
stdout, that conditional separator, the ordered assertion lines, and the
result line. The separator is included in the reserve and `output_sha256`.
Child stdout plus the actual separator and appended protocol bytes must be at
most 16,777,216, so the child cannot consume the protocol reserve. Equality
passes and `+1` fails.

Timeout is the acceptance deadline. At that deadline, cap breach, child exit
with a descendant-held pipe, or protocol error, the case is irreversibly
failed; cleanup may then consume at most an additional 2,000-millisecond
graceful termination interval plus a 5,000-millisecond forced-kill/drain
interval. The wrapper emits no PASS/evidence and exits nonzero even if cleanup
later succeeds. An environment without the reviewed descendant-control
adapter refuses rather than weakening this rule.

Only after child status zero, complete three-channel EOF, zero surviving
descendants, and successful finalization and validation of the exact
descriptor-required fixture/binary role sets does the wrapper evaluate the
structured terminal events and construct the run binding. It requires the
positive child-event set to equal exactly the containing case's manifest
records whose source is `child_event`, every such ID exactly once with PASS,
and no missing, extra, duplicate, foreign-case, oracle-sourced, skipped, todo,
cancelled, failed, or unknown event. For S2-AC-01 and S2-AC-17 it then forms
the disjoint union of that set and the already validated
`host_control_oracle_bundle` set; for every other case the oracle set is
empty. Before case PASS, that union must equal the full manifest ID projection
exactly in manifest order.

The wrapper emits on stdout one exact
`stage2-assertion-result-v1:<case_id>:PASS:<assertion_id>` line per ID in that
validated full union, in manifest order, then the exact final protocol line
`stage2-case-result-v1:<case_id>:PASS:<observed_assertion_count>:<observed_assertion_ids_sha256>:<run_binding_sha256>`.
It first emits the conditional separator defined above when required; it never
rewrites, decodes, or otherwise normalizes child stdout.
The evidence verifier accepts protocol lines only as complete
`0x0a`-terminated ASCII stdout lines with no prefix or `0x0d`, rejects every
protocol-prefixed stderr byte and every malformed, duplicate, foreign, or
post-marker protocol line, reconstructs the positive observed count/hash from
the assertion lines, and requires equality to the expected fields and frozen
manifest. `nonpass_assertion_count` is exactly zero.

The wrapper buffers only those bounded exact bytes, constructs the assertion
and final protocol lines as the end of stdout, computes the binary output
hash, and constructs the ordered evidence JSON. It publishes the evidence only
through the exact candidate validation, no-replace final link, and final
validation protocol above while all protocol output remains buffered. Only
after exact final `case_evidence` PASS does it write child stderr completely
and final stdout as its last fallible operation. A stream, output,
fixture/binary/evidence write, publication, or validation failure exits
nonzero; it durably removes every exact candidate/final fixture, binary, and
evidence inode recorded as created for that case and leaves no accepted case
output or complete PASS marker. If exact owned cleanup fails, the selected
platform lock is retained and that platform package fails closed. The frozen runner manifest binds the
wrapper, structured reporter, descendant-control adapter, and evidence
verifier; no child-controlled aggregate marker is trusted. Runner conformance
is an executable nested suite owned by the S2-AC-01 child command and frozen
assertion IDs. It spawns descriptor-bound nested runner helpers and covers
stdout protocol-reserve equality/`+1`, child stdout that is empty,
LF-terminated, or nonempty without a final LF, 10,000/10,001 assertions,
4,096/4,097-byte event payloads, exact total-event-cap equality/`+1`, zero,
truncated, malformed, wrong-key/order, unknown-status, and trailing frames,
timeout, the 2,000-millisecond graceful and 5,000-millisecond force/drain
limits, stuck descendants, descendant-held pipes, missing descendant control,
missing/substituted/malformed FD 9, every missing/malformed/reused/extra/
trailing/EOF/HUP/reparented FD-8 control case, a valid-looking self-created
context without the live coordinator, child package-marker injection, candidate
and final `fixture_bundle`, `binary_artifacts`, and `case_evidence` validator
failures, preexisting candidate/final, no-replace promotion collision,
between-phase replacement, stale run-binding fields, output-write and
evidence-write failures, late cleanup success, and output/evidence cap breach.
Every negative execution
must leave no accepted evidence or PASS marker even if its child exits zero or
cleanup later succeeds.

`run_binding_sha256` is SHA-256 over ASCII domain
`stage2-run-binding-v2`, one `0x00`, then compact UTF-8 JSON without LF and
keys exactly
`case_id,contract_sha256,registry_sha256,shared_run_binding_sha256,
aggregation_binding_sha256,platform,platform_descriptor_sha256,
host_control_oracle_bundle_sha256,git_commit,
migration_sha256,fixture_sha256,schema_manifest_sha256,
failpoint_registry_sha256,generated_migration_failpoints_sha256,
binary_artifact_sha256,assertion_manifest_sha256,evidence_runner_sha256,
operation_matrix_sha256,command,timeout_seconds` in that order. The exact
result marker binds that hash. Empty, zero-match, all-skipped, partially
matched, renamed, stale-output, or exit-zero-with-nonpass execution fails.

## 13. Review and release gates

### 13.1 Contract GO

Before migration SQL is authored, one exact hash of this candidate requires:

- successful read-only verification of the exact header-pinned 39-leaf
  contract static-authority index and all nested cap/oracle derivations;
- focused migration/bootstrap/SQLite review;
- focused product, existing-item, deletion, retention, and backup review;
- focused transaction, R-032, idempotency, and worker-fence review;
- a fresh full adversarial review;
- zero unresolved P0 or P1 findings;
- explicit acceptance of the six reconciliations in section 2.

Any material edit invalidates those reviews.

### 13.3 Non-disposable, lab, and production gates

No non-disposable database may be migrated without a separately reviewed
release decision and verified backup/rehearsal evidence.

No live lab access follows from Stage 2. It still requires the exact external
platform/policy approvals, private-lab identity, manifest, target allowlist,
cleanup owner, and later-stage packaged extension evidence.

Production browser capture and held-transcript manual enrichment remain
denied. Enabling either requires its own explicit future authority; no Stage 2
row, flag, migration, or capability latch supplies that authority.
